docs.title: Supported Adapters
docs.text: The NL2SQL Platform supports a variety of datasources through specialized adapters. Each adapter is designed to handle the specific idiosyncrasies of its underlying database engine, from connection strings to catalog row estimates.

docs.title: SQL Adapters
docs.text:
We provide first-class support for the following SQL databases via SQLAlchemy.

Adapter Description Status PostgreSQL Full support including catalog row estimates, JSONB, and SSL. 🟢 Stable MySQL Support for 5.7+ and 8.0. Includes MAX_EXECUTION_TIME management. 🟢 Stable Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise support via pyodbc and T-SQL dialect. 🟡 Beta SQLite File-based local development. 🟢 Stable DuckDB In-process analytical engine over local files. 🟢 Stable

docs.title: Core Libraries
docs.text:
For developers building their own adapters, we provide detailed reference documentation for our core SDKs.

  • SDK Reference: The core interface (DatasourceAdapter, from nl2sql-sdk) that all adapters must implement.
  • SQLAlchemy Adapter Reference: The base class in the SDK (nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy.SQLAlchemyAdapter) for building SQL-based adapters.

docs.title: Missing your database?
docs.text: Can't find what you need? Check out the Building Adapters guide to see how to implement your own.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All adapters are configured in the datasources section of nl2sql.yaml, usually one file per datasource in datasources/ (see Datasources).

# datasources/sales_db.yaml   (id defaults to the file name)
type: postgres
connection:
  host: "${env:DB_HOST}"
  port: 5432
  # ... see specific adapter docs for full reference

docs.title: Plugin / Adapter Architecture
docs.text: Adapters integrate NL2SQL with external datasources. Each adapter implements a protocol contract, is found by name in the registry (nl2sql.registry, built from Python entry points), and is registered in the DatasourceRegistry.

docs.title: Discovery and registration
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Config["nl2sql.yaml: datasources"] --> Registry[DatasourceRegistry]
    Registry --> Lookup["Registry.load('adapter', type)"]
    Lookup --> EntryPoints["nl2sql.adapters entry points, or a class registered in code"]
    EntryPoints --> AdapterClass[Adapter Class]
    AdapterClass --> Validate["connection validated against connection_model"]
    Validate --> AdapterInstance["adapter_cls(id, connection, limits, folder=...)"]

docs.title: Core adapter contract
docs.text:
classDiagram
    class DatasourceAdapter {
        +interface_version 2
        +title
        +connection_model
        +capabilities() Set
        +get_dialect() str
        +default_schema() str
        +test_connection() ConnectionCheck
        +fetch_schema_snapshot(IndexScope) SchemaSnapshot
        +execute(AdapterRequest) ResultFrame
        +close()
    }
    class AdapterRequest {
        +plan_type
        +payload
        +limits
    }
    class ResultFrame {
        +success
        +columns
        +rows
        +row_count
        +error
    }

See sdk.md for the authoritative adapter interface reference and required fields/methods.

docs.title: Capability-driven routing
docs.text:
Adapters expose capabilities (supports_sql, supports_bound_parameters, enforces_read_only, enforces_timeout). The registry reads them once, at registration, and DatasourceRegistry.supports(datasource_id, *capabilities) is the one check every consumer asks. It fails closed: an unknown datasource, or an adapter whose capabilities() is missing or raises, supports nothing. These capabilities drive:

  • Subgraph selection (resolve_subgraph() in routing).
  • Executor selection (ExecutorNode._supports_sql() and SqlExecutorService.validate_request(), gating the SQL executor).
flowchart TD
    Adapter[DatasourceAdapter] --> Caps["capabilities(), read once"]
    Caps --> Check["DatasourceRegistry.supports() (fails closed)"]
    Check --> Exec[ExecutorNode capability gate]
    Check --> Subgraph[resolve_subgraph()]
    Exec --> Service[SqlExecutorService]
    Subgraph --> Graph[Subgraph Selection]

docs.title: Multi-datasource routing
docs.text: The control graph can resolve multiple datasources for a single user query. DecomposerNode produces sub-queries scoped to individual datasources. Each sub-query is then routed to a subgraph that matches its adapter capabilities.

docs.title: Extensibility model
docs.text:
To add a new adapter:

  1. Implement DatasourceAdapter (or extend a base adapter), with a connection_model.
  2. Publish the adapter class as an nl2sql.adapters entry point, or register it in code (see Adding a New Adapter).
  3. Configure the datasource in the datasources section of nl2sql.yaml, with type: set to the adapter's name.

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:
• Adapter protocol: packages/sdk/src/nl2sql_sdk/protocols.py
  • Registry: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/registry.py
  • Datasource registry: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/datasources/registry.py
  • SQLAlchemy base: packages/sdk/src/nl2sql_sdk/sqlalchemy/adapter.py
  • Example adapter: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/adapters/postgres/adapter.py

docs.title: Building Adapters Guide
docs.text: The NL2SQL Platform is designed to be extensible. You can build adapters for any datasource, from SQL databases to REST APIs.

docs.title: Implementation Path
docs.text:
There are two primary ways to build an adapter. Choose the one that fits your target:

If you are checking... Use... Reference A standard SQL Database (Postgres, Oracle, Snowflake) nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy (pip install "nl2sql-sdk[sqlalchemy]") SQLAlchemy Adapter Reference A NoSQL DB, REST API, or custom driver Core adapter protocol Adapter Interface Reference

docs.title: Option 1: The "Fast Lane" (SQLAlchemy)
docs.text:
For 95% of use cases, you are connecting to a SQL database that already has a Python SQLAlchemy dialect.

Use SQLAlchemyAdapter from the SDK. It handles:

  • Connecting on first use, with a connection pool (SQLAlchemyConnection adds pool)
  • Executing queries with bound parameters, and turning a database error into a failed result
  • Reading the schema: one reflection pass per schema, filtered by the datasource's index scope
  • Catalog row estimates, type-aware statistics, and values only when index.sample_values is on
  • Reporting what a table or column was indexed without as an IndexIssue
  • probe_overlap, the schema profiler's join check, in SQLAlchemy Core

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A complete adapter: the built-in PostgreSQL one, less its session_setup, classify and capabilities.

from typing import Dict, Literal

from pydantic import Field, SecretStr
from sqlalchemy import URL, text

from nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemyAdapter, SQLAlchemyConnection


class PostgresConnection(SQLAlchemyConnection):
    host: str = Field(title="Host", examples=["db.internal"])
    port: int = Field(5432, title="Port")
    database: str = Field(title="Database")
    user: str = Field(title="User")
    password: SecretStr = Field(title="Password")
    sslmode: Literal["disable", "prefer", "require", "verify-full"] = Field(
        "prefer", title="SSL mode", json_schema_extra={"group": "advanced"})


class PostgresAdapter(SQLAlchemyAdapter):
    title = "PostgreSQL"
    connection_model = PostgresConnection
    driver_modules = ("psycopg2",)
    install_hint = 'pip install "nl2sql-engine[postgres]"'

    def url(self, connection: PostgresConnection) -> URL:
        # URL.create escapes the credentials; an f-string breaks on a password
        # containing @ : / # or %.
        return URL.create("postgresql+psycopg2", username=connection.user,
                          password=connection.password.get_secret_value(), host=connection.host,
                          port=connection.port, database=connection.database,
                          query={"sslmode": connection.sslmode})

    def get_dialect(self) -> str:
        return "postgres"  # a sqlglot dialect name, not SQLAlchemy's "postgresql"

    def system_schemas(self) -> set[str]:
        return {"pg_catalog", "information_schema"}

    def row_estimates(self, conn, schema: str) -> Dict[str, int]:
        rows = conn.execute(text(
            "SELECT c.relname, c.reltuples FROM pg_catalog.pg_class c "
            "JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace "
            "WHERE n.nspname = :schema AND c.relkind IN ('r', 'p', 'm', 'f') AND c.reltuples >= 0"
        ), {"schema": schema})
        return {name: int(count) for name, count in rows}

Make the session read-only and enforce limits.timeout_ms in session_setup(): the base class keeps the limit but does not apply it. Then declare ENFORCES_READ_ONLY and ENFORCES_TIMEOUT for what it enforces, and override classify() to map your driver's connection errors to stages (see the reference).

docs.title: Adding estimate
docs.text:
The engine's cost rule asks an adapter for the rows a query will read before it runs it. Reading a plan is the database's own, so the base has no estimate: add one and declare ESTIMATES_COST (the contract).

  1. Ask for the plan without running the query (EXPLAIN, an estimated plan), on the adapter's own connections, so it runs read-only and under timeout_ms, with parameters bound as execute binds them.
  2. Add up the rows each scan operator reads. A full scan counts its table's row count, never the operator's own row estimate, which is its output after the filter: a scan that filters a billion rows down to ten reads a billion. An index seek counts its own estimate. Both are per execution: an operator on the inner side of a nested loop runs once per outer row, so multiply by the times it runs where the plan says.
  3. Return Estimate(rows=..., cost=..., source=...): cost is the planner's total, for display only, or None when the plan has none; source says what was read.
  4. Raise RuntimeError on every failure, the database's (with the driver's first line, driver_message) and a plan you cannot read alike: the engine's cost rule reads a RuntimeError as "no estimate", and the kit checks it. Never fall back to the operator's filtered estimate, and never report a statement the database gives no plan for as zero rows: no plan is no estimate, so raise.
  5. Leave no session setting behind. A setting that changes what a query returns (SQL Server's SHOWPLAN_XML) must be turned off before the connection is closed: a driver's own pool can hand the session on.

The built-in PostgreSQL adapter's:

def estimate(self, sql: str, parameters: Dict[str, Any]) -> Estimate:
    try:
        with self.engine.connect() as conn:
            plan = _plan(self._run(conn, f"EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE) {sql}", parameters).scalar())
            seq_scans, rows = scans(plan)  # each Seq Scan with the times it runs; index scans' rows
            sizes = {(schema, name): self._planned_size(conn, schema, name) for schema, name, _ in seq_scans}
        rows += sum(sizes[(schema, name)] * times for schema, name, times in seq_scans)
        cost = plan.get("Total Cost")
        return Estimate(rows=int(rows), cost=float(cost) if cost is not None else None,
                        source="EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) and pg_class.reltuples")
    except SQLAlchemyError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{self} could not estimate the query: {driver_message(exc)}") from None
    except _UNREADABLE as exc:  # KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError, IndexError
        raise RuntimeError(f"{self} could not estimate the query: the plan could not be read "
                           f"({type(exc).__name__})") from None

See the SQLAlchemy Adapter Reference for full API details.

docs.title: Option 2: The "Custom" Path (Protocol)
docs.text:
If you need to connect to something else (e.g., ElasticSearch, a CRM API, or a raw SQL driver), implement the core adapter protocol.

Implement DatasourceAdapter. You must manually handle:

  • Fetching and normalizing schema metadata.
  • Executing queries and formatting results.
  • Declaring a connection_model: a ConnectionModel subclass with one field per connection setting. The engine validates the datasource's connection against it (unknown keys are errors) and passes the instance to your constructor.
  • The constructor the engine builds every adapter with: adapter_cls(datasource_id, connection, limits, *, folder=None), where limits is the datasource's Limits and folder the folder of nl2sql.yaml, or None. Do not connect in the constructor: engine.check() calls test_connection(), which returns a ConnectionCheck.
  • A close() that releases connections; engine.close() calls it once.
  • Declaring interface_version = 2, a title, the driver_modules it imports to connect, and an install_hint (see Class attributes).
  • A default_schema() naming the schema an unqualified table resolves to, or returning None. Policies read a table with no schema as a table in this schema; without one, main is assumed.
  • A fetch_schema_snapshot(scope, on_table=None) that reads only what the datasource's IndexScope wants (scope.wants_table, scope.wants_column).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from pydantic import SecretStr

from nl2sql_sdk import (AdapterRequest, ConnectionCheck, ConnectionModel, IndexScope, Limits,
                        ResultFrame, SchemaSnapshot)


class MyApiConnection(ConnectionModel):
    url: str
    token: SecretStr


class MyApiAdapter:
    interface_version = 2
    title = "My API"
    connection_model = MyApiConnection
    driver_modules = ("httpx",)
    install_hint = 'pip install "nl2sql-my-api"'

    def __init__(self, datasource_id: str, connection: MyApiConnection, limits: Limits, *, folder=None):
        self.datasource_id, self.connection, self.limits = datasource_id, connection, limits

    def capabilities(self):
        return set()  # not SQL: the SQL agent does not serve it

    def test_connection(self) -> ConnectionCheck:
        ...  # call the API; return ConnectionCheck(ok=False, message=...) on failure

    def fetch_schema_snapshot(self, scope: IndexScope, on_table=None) -> SchemaSnapshot:
        ...  # call the API, return the schema of what scope.wants_table() keeps

    def execute(self, request: AdapterRequest) -> ResultFrame:
        ...  # run the request, return rows

    def get_dialect(self) -> str: ...
    def default_schema(self): return None
    def close(self): pass

See the Adapter Interface Reference for the method signatures and compliance guide.

docs.title: Running the conformance kit
docs.text:
Whichever path you choose, run the conformance kit against a real database before you publish. It is a pytest test class, AdapterConformance, in nl2sql_sdk.testing:

pip install "nl2sql-sdk[testing]"   # adds pytest and sqlglot

Subclass it in a test module (the name must start with Test) and give it four fixtures:

Fixture What it gives connection The ConnectionModel of a database the tests may write the kit's seed into adapter_factory adapter_factory(connection, limits): your adapter, built the way the engine builds it seed seed(statements): runs each SQL statement with a writable connection, outside your adapter sleep_sql sleep_sql(seconds): a query that runs at least that long 
import pytest
from sqlalchemy import create_engine

from nl2sql_sdk.testing import AdapterConformance

from my_adapter import MyAdapter, MyConnection


class TestMyAdapterConformance(AdapterConformance):

    @pytest.fixture
    def connection(self):
        return MyConnection(host="127.0.0.1", database="kit", user="kit", password="...")

    @pytest.fixture
    def adapter_factory(self):
        return lambda connection, limits: MyAdapter("kit", connection, limits)

    @pytest.fixture
    def seed(self):
        admin = create_engine("mydb://admin:...@127.0.0.1/kit")

        def run(statements):
            with admin.connect().execution_options(isolation_level="AUTOCOMMIT") as conn:
                for statement in statements:
                    conn.exec_driver_sql(statement)
        return run

    @pytest.fixture
    def sleep_sql(self):
        return lambda seconds: f"SELECT pg_sleep({seconds})"

Each test writes the kit's seed first and drops it after: two schemas (kit_a, kit_b), a view, a mixed-case table, boolean, uuid and json columns, and kit_orders, the largest table, with 100 rows. It is written once and transpiled to your get_dialect() with sqlglot. Two class attributes adapt it:

  • schemas = ("main",) for a database with one schema, such as SQLite: the seed then creates no schema, and the check that needs two is skipped.
  • column_types = {"uuid": "CHAR(36)"} for a database without one of the three types (MySQL has no uuid, SQL Server 2022 no json).

A database with logins can also give limited_login: the ConnectionModel of a second login whose password holds @ : / # % and that can read kit_a but not kit_b. It may request the seeded fixture to grant on the seed. Without it, the two checks that need it are skipped.

Check Passes when Dialect get_dialect() is a name sqlglot.Dialect.get_or_raise accepts Connection model An unknown key fails; a password with @ : / # % connects; no secret appears in repr, str, a validation error or a failed check Stages Good settings are ok; a wrong password is auth, a closed port network, a missing database database (skipped when the model has no such field) Scope System schemas stay out even when named; include and exclude rules hold; views are included; mixed-case names keep their case Odd columns Profiling the boolean, uuid and json columns gives statistics or an IndexIssue, never an exception Row estimates Every table has a row count and says where it came from Bound parameters 1; DROP TABLE kit_people passed as a parameter is a value Read-only If ENFORCES_READ_ONLY is declared, an INSERT and a CREATE TABLE through execute fail, are not retryable and change nothing Timeout If ENFORCES_TIMEOUT is declared, sleep_sql(5) with a one-second limit fails within three seconds as QUERY_TIMEOUT Errors A missing column is retryable; a permission error is not Streaming If the adapter has execute_batches, its frames match execute's result Estimates If ESTIMATES_COST is declared: estimate returns rows >= 0 and a source; an estimate of sleep_sql(5) returns or raises RuntimeError within two seconds (it does not run the statement; a statement with no plan, such as SQL Server's WAITFOR, raises); a filter on an unindexed column of kit_orders that matches no row reports at least half the table's rows; a missing table raises RuntimeError Overlap If the adapter has probe_overlap: kit_orders.person_id against kit_people.id samples 2 distinct values and matches 2; kit_people.name against KitMixedCase.DisplayName matches none

A capability you do not declare is not checked: its test is reported as skipped, with the reason, so pytest -rs shows what your adapter does not promise. The five built-in adapters run the kit: SQLite and DuckDB in packages/nl2sql/tests/adapters/unit/test_conformance.py, PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server in packages/nl2sql/tests/realdb/test_conformance.py.

docs.title: DuckDB Adapter
docs.text:
In-process analytical adapter for local files and ad-hoc analysis.

Implementation

This adapter extends SQLAlchemyAdapter. It overrides build_engine() to open a file with read_only=True and to enforce limits.timeout_ms: DuckDB runs in-process and has no statement timeout setting, so the adapter interrupts a statement that runs too long. It overrides schema_names() and reflect() to read DuckDB's own catalog (see below).

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The SQLAlchemy dialect lives in duckdb-engine, which ships in its own extra:

pip install "nl2sql-engine[duckdb]"

The adapter reads a schema from DuckDB's own catalog (duckdb_schemas(), duckdb_tables(), duckdb_views(), duckdb_columns() and duckdb_constraints()) rather than through duckdb-engine's reflection, which reuses SQLAlchemy's PostgreSQL reflection and queries pg_catalog tables DuckDB does not have. A column's type is DuckDB's own name: DECIMAL(10,2), VARCHAR[], JSON.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Type: duckdb

# datasources/warehouse.yaml
type: duckdb
connection:
  database: ./warehouse.duckdb # File path, or ":memory:"

database is the only key (DuckdbConnection); any other is an error.

Persistence

:memory: databases live for the lifetime of the process. Use a file path for anything that must survive a restart, and an absolute path under a mounted volume when running in Docker.

docs.title: Connection Details
docs.text:
• Driver: duckdb-engine (the duckdb:/// SQLAlchemy dialect) over the duckdb package.
  • URI Constructed: duckdb:///{database} — for example duckdb:///./warehouse.duckdb or duckdb:///:memory:.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Implementation Note Read-only read_only=True on the connection A file is always opened read-only, so it must exist, and declares ENFORCES_READ_ONLY. DuckDB cannot open :memory: read-only, and an in-memory database has nothing to protect, so it does not declare it. Timeout interrupt() on a timer See Statement Timeout. Declares ENFORCES_TIMEOUT. Connection stages The message A file that does not exist is database. Estimates EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON), then duckdb_tables().estimated_size estimate never runs the query. A scan of a table counts the table's size, never the operator's estimate; its name is read as DuckDB prints it (memory.main."Big Orders"), and a scanned table with no size raises. A table function (range, read_parquet) counts its own estimate. DuckDB plans hash joins, so each scan counts once. DuckDB reports no cost. Declares ESTIMATES_COST. Row counts duckdb_tables().estimated_size The catalog's count. Stats One query per column See Reading a schema.

docs.title: Statement Timeout
docs.text: When limits.timeout_ms is set, each statement starts a timer that calls the DuckDB connection's interrupt() once the limit passes. DuckDB stops the query and raises InterruptException, which the adapter reports as a timeout (QUERY_TIMEOUT) that the engine does not retry. The timer is cancelled as soon as the statement finishes or fails, so it never touches a later query. The limit covers running the statement; DuckDB materialises the result while it runs, so fetching rows afterwards is not timed.

docs.title: Schema Introspection
docs.text: DuckDB qualifies schema names with their catalog (memory.main, warehouse.main). The adapter excludes system.main, system.information_schema and temp.main, leaving the schemas of the attached database.

docs.title: Hints
docs.text:
• Analytics: DuckDB is columnar and vectorized, which suits aggregation-heavy generated SQL. It reads Parquet and CSV directly via read_parquet() / read_csv().
  • Concurrency: A DuckDB file allows a single writing process, and a process that has it open for writing keeps a read-only one out. Write to the file from another process only while the engine is not using it.

docs.title: Microsoft SQL Server (MSSQL) Adapter
docs.text:
Support for SQL Server 2017+ and Azure SQL.

This adapter extends SQLAlchemyAdapter. Its row counts are the catalog's (sys.partitions), and it enforces limits.timeout_ms through pyodbc's query timeout. It cannot make the session read-only: see Read-only.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Type: mssql

# datasources/my_db.yaml
type: mssql
connection:
  host: localhost
  port: 1433
  user: sa
  password: "${env:DB_PASS}"
  database: my_db
  driver: "ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server" # Optional: unset picks the newest one installed
  trusted_connection: false               # true: log in as the account the engine runs under
  encrypt: true                           # false: a local or test server without TLS
  trust_server_certificate: false         # true: accept a self-signed certificate

The keys are MssqlConnection's (nl2sql.adapters.mssql.adapter), and any other key is an error; see Connection.

docs.title: Connection Details
docs.text:
• Driver: pyodbc, with one of Microsoft's ODBC drivers (see Requirements).
  • ODBC driver: the driver you set, else the newest ODBC Driver N for SQL Server that pyodbc.drivers() lists, so a machine with only Driver 17 works without configuration. With none installed, nl2sql check fails at the driver stage and says where to download one.
  • Encryption: on by default (Encrypt=yes). Driver 18 encrypts by default and Driver 17 does not, so the adapter always says which it wants: the connection behaves the same whichever driver is used. A server with a self-signed certificate (a local or test server) needs trust_server_certificate: true; one without TLS at all needs encrypt: false, which sends Encrypt=no.
  • URI Constructed: mssql+pyodbc://{user}:{pass}@{host}:{port}/{db}?driver={driver}&Encrypt=yes (no with encrypt: false), plus Trusted_Connection=yes and TrustServerCertificate=yes when set. Built with SQLAlchemy's URL.create, so the user name and password are percent-escaped: a password containing @ : / # % works as written.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Implementation Note Read-only None Does not declare ENFORCES_READ_ONLY; see Read-only. Timeout pyodbc Connection.timeout Client-side query timeout, in whole seconds. Declares ENFORCES_TIMEOUT. Connection stages SQL Server's error number 18456 is auth, 4060 database, 916 permission; ODBC's 08001, 08S01 and HYT00 are network; no ODBC Driver for SQL Server installed is driver. Estimates SET SHOWPLAN_XML ON, then sys.partitions estimate never runs the query. Each Table Scan, Clustered Index Scan, Index Scan, Columnstore Index Scan, Index Seek or Clustered Index Seek counts EstimatedRowsRead where the server reports it; else a scan counts its table's catalog row count and a seek its EstimateRows. Each is per execution, so it is multiplied by 1 + EstimateRebinds + EstimateRewinds (the inner side of a nested loop). cost is StatementSubtreeCost, else the plan's top EstimatedTotalSubtreeCost, else none. Bound parameters are written into the statement as escaped literals, because SQL Server returns no plan for a statement sent with parameters (an sp_executesql call). A statement SQL Server gives no plan for (WAITFOR) raises rather than counting zero rows. SHOWPLAN is turned off again before the connection is closed, because pyodbc's ODBC pooling hands the session on to the next connection. Needs the SHOWPLAN permission: see Estimates. Declares ESTIMATES_COST. Row counts sys.partitions The row count SQL Server keeps for each table. Stats One query per column See Reading a schema.

docs.title: Read-only
docs.text:
SQL Server has no setting that makes a session read-only. ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly only routes the connection to a readable secondary replica; on a primary the session can still write. So the adapter does not declare ENFORCES_READ_ONLY, and engine.check() puts a warning on every SQL Server datasource's status:

sales: ready
  Warning: sales (mssql): this adapter cannot make the session read-only. Connect with a login that can only read.

The typed plan and the validator still block every write (see the security model). The third guard is yours: connect with a login whose only role in the database is db_datareader.

CREATE LOGIN nl2sql WITH PASSWORD = '...';
CREATE USER nl2sql FOR LOGIN nl2sql;
ALTER ROLE db_datareader ADD MEMBER nl2sql;

docs.title: Estimates
docs.text:
estimate reads SQL Server's estimated plan, which needs the SHOWPLAN permission. A db_datareader login does not have it, and its estimate raises, which a cost rule treats as unknown. To give the cost rule real numbers, grant it; it lets the login see plans, not data:

GRANT SHOWPLAN TO nl2sql;

docs.title: Statement Timeout
docs.text: SQL Server has no session setting for a statement timeout, so the adapter's session_setup sets pyodbc's query timeout (Connection.timeout) on every new pooled connection. pyodbc counts whole seconds, so limits.timeout_ms is rounded up: 1500 becomes 2 seconds, and anything from 1 to 1000 becomes 1 second. When the limit passes, the driver cancels the query and the adapter reports it as a timeout (QUERY_TIMEOUT), which the engine does not retry.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
pip install "nl2sql-engine[mssql]" installs pyodbc. You also need Microsoft's ODBC Driver for SQL Server (17 or 18) in your Docker image or local environment; the adapter uses the newest one installed.

Download ODBC Driver for SQL Server

# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt-get install unixodbc-dev

docs.title: MySQL Adapter
docs.text:
Support for MySQL 5.7+ and 8.0+.

Implementation

This adapter extends SQLAlchemyAdapter. Its session_setup makes every new pooled connection read-only and sets the MAX_EXECUTION_TIME session variable.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Type: mysql

# datasources/my_db.yaml
type: mysql
connection:
  host: localhost
  port: 3306
  user: root
  password: "${env:DB_PASS}"
  database: my_db

The keys are MysqlConnection's (nl2sql.adapters.mysql.adapter), and any other key is an error; see Connection.

docs.title: Connection Details
docs.text:
• Driver: pymysql (Pure Python), with cryptography. MySQL 8's default login, caching_sha2_password, needs cryptography on a connection without TLS. pip install "nl2sql-engine[mysql]" installs both (pymysql[rsa]); without cryptography, nl2sql check fails at the driver stage with that install command.
  • URI Constructed: mysql+pymysql://{user}:{pass}@{host}:{port}/{db}. Built with SQLAlchemy's URL.create, so the user name and password are percent-escaped: a password containing @ : / # % works as written.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Implementation Note Read-only SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY An INSERT or CREATE TABLE fails even for a login that could write. Declares ENFORCES_READ_ONLY. Timeout SET SESSION MAX_EXECUTION_TIME = {ms} Server-side. It applies to SELECT, which is all the engine runs. Declares ENFORCES_TIMEOUT. Connection stages MySQL's error number 1045 is auth, 1049 database, 1044 permission, 2003 and 2005 network; PyMySQL's "'cryptography' package is required" is driver. Estimates EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON estimate never runs the query. Each table access counts rows_examined_per_scan, MySQL's estimate of the rows one scan reads (a full scan, access_type: ALL, counts the table), times its scans: in a nested loop, once per row the tables before it produce (rows_produced_per_join), and once when it is joined through a join buffer (a hash join). A materialized derived table is not counted again; what it reads is. A dependent subquery counts one execution. cost is query_cost. Runs read-only, under MAX_EXECUTION_TIME. Declares ESTIMATES_COST. Row counts information_schema.tables.table_rows InnoDB's estimate; ANALYZE TABLE refreshes it. Stats One query per column See Reading a schema.

docs.title: PostgreSQL Adapter
docs.text:
This adapter extends SQLAlchemyAdapter, leveraging automatic schema reflection and statistics gathering. Its row counts are the catalog's estimates (pg_class.reltuples), so a table never analyzed has none.

A partitioned table is one table. PostgreSQL declares its foreign keys on the partitions (payment_p2022_01, ...), so the adapter does not list the partitions: the parent keeps the foreign keys it declares and gains the partitions' (once each), and a key that points at a partition points at its parent. A query names the parent, and the planner is sent one table instead of the parent and all its partitions. A parent never analyzed takes the sum of its partitions' row estimates. A partition is read when its top parent is in the datasource's index scope.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Type: postgres

# datasources/my_db.yaml
type: postgres
connection:
  host: localhost
  port: 5432
  user: postgres
  password: "${env:DB_PASS}"
  database: my_db
  sslmode: require # disable, prefer (default), require or verify-full

The keys are PostgresConnection's (nl2sql.adapters.postgres.adapter), and any other key is an error; see Connection.

docs.title: Connection Details
docs.text:
• Driver: psycopg2 (via sqlalchemy).
  • URI Constructed: postgresql+psycopg2://{user}:{pass}@{host}:{port}/{db}?sslmode={sslmode}. Built with SQLAlchemy's URL.create, so the user name and password are percent-escaped: a password containing @ : / # % works as written.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Implementation Note Read-only SET default_transaction_read_only = on Set on every new pooled connection (session_setup): an INSERT or CREATE TABLE fails even for a login that could write. Declares ENFORCES_READ_ONLY. Timeout SET statement_timeout = {ms} Set with the read-only flag; enforced server-side. Declares ENFORCES_TIMEOUT. Connection stages libpq's message psycopg2 has no SQLSTATE for a failed connection, so classify reads the message: a refused password is auth, a missing database database, an unreachable host or port network. Estimates EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE) estimate never runs the query. A Seq Scan counts its whole relation, not its Plan Rows (the rows left after the filter): the Plan Rows of an unfiltered scan of it, which the planner makes from pg_class.reltuples scaled to the relation's current size, so a relation never analyzed (on any version) is counted too. Index Scan, Index Only Scan and Bitmap Index Scan count their Plan Rows. A scan on the inner side of a Nested Loop counts once per outer row, unless a Materialize keeps its rows. Not counted: Foreign Scan, Function Scan, and the repeats of a correlated SubPlan. cost is the plan's Total Cost. Runs read-only, under statement_timeout. Declares ESTIMATES_COST. Row counts pg_class.reltuples The catalog's estimate; a table never analyzed has none, and is counted under profile: stats. Stats One query per column Null share, distinct count, min/max (no min/max for boolean, uuid; only the null share for jsonb, bytea, arrays). A column that fails is an index issue, rolled back so the transaction is not aborted; see Reading a schema.

docs.title: SSL Verification
docs.text: If connecting to Azure or AWS RDS with strict SSL, ensure you pass the CA certificate path through the standard libpq environment variables (PGSSLROOTCERT), or use sslmode: disable for testing.

docs.title: SDK Interface Reference
docs.text:
The SDK, nl2sql-sdk (imported as nl2sql_sdk), holds the interfaces an extension implements. Its core depends on pydantic and the standard library only.

  • Adapters: nl2sql_sdk.DatasourceAdapter (interface version 2), with the models it is built from (ConnectionModel, Limits, IndexScope) and returns (ConnectionCheck, SchemaSnapshot, ResultFrame)
  • The SQLAlchemy base: nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy.SQLAlchemyAdapter and SQLAlchemyConnection, installed with pip install "nl2sql-sdk[sqlalchemy]". The one part of the SDK that imports SQLAlchemy; see SQLAlchemy adapters.
  • The conformance kit: nl2sql_sdk.testing.AdapterConformance, installed with pip install "nl2sql-sdk[testing]", a pytest test class every adapter should pass; see the conformance kit.
  • Secret providers: nl2sql_sdk.secrets.SecretProvider
  • Stores: the four protocols in nl2sql_sdk.stores
  • Policy checks: nl2sql_sdk.policy.PolicyCheck, with UserContext and Grant
  • Knowledge sources: nl2sql_sdk.knowledge.KnowledgeSource, with the glossary's models; see below

The adapter's interfaces and models are exported from nl2sql_sdk itself; the stores, policy checks and knowledge sources are read from their modules.

docs.title: Interface: DatasourceAdapter
docs.text:
from nl2sql_sdk import (AdapterRequest, ConnectionCheck, ConnectionModel, DatasourceAdapter,
                        DatasourceCapability, IndexScope, Limits, ResultFrame, SchemaSnapshot)

The contract, version 2:

class DatasourceAdapter(Protocol):
    interface_version: ClassVar[int]   # 2
    title: ClassVar[str]               # "PostgreSQL", for people and forms
    connection_model: ClassVar[type[ConnectionModel]]
    driver_modules: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]]
    install_hint: ClassVar[str]

    def __init__(self, datasource_id: str, connection: ConnectionModel, limits: Limits,
                 *, folder: Path | None = None) -> None: ...      # never connects
    def capabilities(self) -> set[DatasourceCapability]: ...
    def get_dialect(self) -> str: ...                  # a sqlglot dialect name
    def default_schema(self) -> str | None: ...
    def test_connection(self) -> ConnectionCheck: ...
    def fetch_schema_snapshot(self, scope: IndexScope,
                              on_table: Callable[[str], None] | None = None) -> SchemaSnapshot: ...
    def execute(self, request: AdapterRequest) -> ResultFrame: ...
    def close(self) -> None: ...

docs.title: Class attributes
docs.text:
The class attributes let the engine check an adapter, and show it to people, before it builds one.

Attribute Type Description interface_version int The version of this interface the adapter was written for: 2. The engine accepts exactly the version it was built for, and any other version is a load error. title str The database's name for people, such as "PostgreSQL". connection_model type[ConnectionModel] The model the datasource's connection block is validated against. See The connection model. driver_modules tuple[str, ...] The modules the adapter needs to connect, for example ("psycopg2",). The engine looks for each one with importlib.util.find_spec before it builds the adapter. install_hint str What to install when a driver module is missing, for example pip install "nl2sql-engine[postgres]".

The adapter module must import without its driver, so import the driver where it is used and not at the top of the module. The built-in adapters declare:

Adapter title connection_model driver_modules Extra sqlite SQLite SqliteConnection ("sqlite3",) none: sqlite3 ships with Python postgres PostgreSQL PostgresConnection ("psycopg2",) nl2sql-engine[postgres] mysql MySQL MysqlConnection ("pymysql", "cryptography") nl2sql-engine[mysql] mssql SQL Server MssqlConnection ("pyodbc",) nl2sql-engine[mssql], plus Microsoft's ODBC driver duckdb DuckDB DuckdbConnection ("duckdb", "duckdb_engine") nl2sql-engine[duckdb]

Each connection model is public, next to its adapter (from nl2sql.adapters.postgres.adapter import PostgresConnection).

docs.title: The connection model
docs.text:
ConnectionModel is a pydantic model with extra="forbid" and hide_input_in_errors=True. Subclass it with one field per setting:

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import Field, SecretStr

from nl2sql_sdk import ConnectionModel


class PostgresConnection(ConnectionModel):
    host: str = Field(title="Host", examples=["db.internal"])
    port: int = Field(5432, title="Port")
    database: str = Field(title="Database")
    user: str = Field(title="User")
    password: SecretStr = Field(title="Password")
    sslmode: Literal["disable", "prefer", "require", "verify-full"] = Field(
        "prefer", title="SSL mode", json_schema_extra={"group": "advanced"})
  • Strict. An unknown key is an error that names the field it was probably meant to be: connection.hostname: unknown key 'hostname'. Did you mean 'host'?. No error message holds a value from the connection.
  • Validated when the adapter is built. The engine resolves every ${provider:key} reference in the connection block, validates it against connection_model, and passes the instance to the constructor. From Python, Datasource(connection=PostgresConnection(...)) passes an instance, which is used as given; another adapter's model is refused.
  • Secrets. Declare a credential as SecretStr: it never prints, and its JSON Schema is "format": "password", "writeOnly": true.
  • The form. connection_model.model_json_schema() describes the form for connecting a database: Field(title, description, examples) label it, and json_schema_extra={"group": "advanced"} marks a field to fold away.

docs.title: The constructor
docs.text:
adapter_cls(datasource_id, connection, limits, *, folder=None):

Argument What it is datasource_id The datasource's id. Keep it as self.datasource_id. connection The validated connection_model instance. limits The datasource's Limits: row_limit, timeout_ms, max_bytes, each None when unset. Enforce timeout_ms the way your driver allows. The engine caps a query's rows itself, from the datasource's limits. folder The folder of the nl2sql.yaml the datasource came from, or None when the config was built in code. Read a relative file path from it.

The constructor must not connect: the adapter connects on first use, and engine.check() connects through test_connection().

docs.title: capabilities() -> set[DatasourceCapability]
docs.text:
Declares what the adapter does. Declare a flag only when it holds on a real server.

Flag Meaning SUPPORTS_SQL The adapter runs SQL requests (plan_type="sql"). The SQL agent serves only a datasource that declares it. SUPPORTS_BOUND_PARAMETERS The adapter binds AdapterRequest.parameters by name to the :name placeholders in the SQL, and never pastes a value into the SQL text. The engine sends parameters (for a verified query) only to an adapter that declares it. Every built-in SQLAlchemy adapter does. ENFORCES_READ_ONLY The session cannot write: an INSERT or CREATE TABLE through execute fails. ENFORCES_TIMEOUT A statement running past limits.timeout_ms is stopped by the server or the driver. ESTIMATES_COST The adapter has estimate(sql, parameters) (below): the database's estimate of the rows a query reads, without running it. Release 0.8's cost rule reads it.

docs.title: get_dialect() -> str
docs.text: The sqlglot dialect name the engine renders SQL in: postgres, tsql, mysql, duckdb, sqlite, or any other name sqlglot.Dialect.get_or_raise accepts. It is not the SQLAlchemy dialect name (postgresql, mssql).

docs.title: default_schema() -> str | None
docs.text: The schema an unqualified table name resolves to, or None when unknown. Policies read a plan table with no schema as a table in this schema; without one, main is assumed.

docs.title: test_connection() -> ConnectionCheck
docs.text:
Connects and reports what it found. It returns a failure rather than raising it:

Field Meaning ok Whether the adapter connected. stage Which stage failed: config, driver, network, auth, database or permission; None when the adapter cannot tell. message Why, in one line, with no secret in it. fix What to do about it, when the adapter knows. server_version The server's version, when connected.

engine.check() calls it for each datasource and reports the stage, message and fix in the datasource's status.

docs.title: fetch_schema_snapshot(scope, on_table=None) -> SchemaSnapshot
docs.text:
The schema of the tables and views the datasource's index scope wants, with their metadata. scope is an IndexScope (see index): call scope.wants_table(ref) and scope.wants_column(ref, column) rather than matching its patterns yourself, and leave out your database's system schemas. on_table is called with each table's schema.table as it is read, for progress.

The snapshot's issues list holds an IndexIssue (table, column, stage, message, and error_type, the exception's class name when an exception caused it) for each table or column indexed without something, and each table's row_count_source says where its row_count came from: catalog (an estimate) or exact (a count).

docs.title: execute(request: AdapterRequest) -> ResultFrame
docs.text:
Executes a plan-specific request and returns a normalized ResultFrame.

  • Args: AdapterRequest with plan_type, payload, and parameters (values to bind; empty for generated SQL)
  • Returns: ResultFrame with columns, rows, row_count, and error metadata

A query the database rejects is a result, not an exception: return ResultFrame(success=False, error=ResultError(...)). Two fields of the ResultError decide what the engine does with it:

Field Meaning retryable True when the query itself was wrong and a different query could succeed: bad syntax, an unknown table, column or function, a type mismatch. The engine reports EXECUTION_FAILED and sends the sub-query back to the planner, with safe_message as the feedback, while retries remain. False (the default) for a refusal the engine cannot plan its way out of: permission, a timeout, a lost connection, a read-only database. The engine reports DB_EXECUTION_ERROR and ends the sub-query. safe_message Shown to the planner and the user. Keep it to one short line: no SQL echo, no stack trace, no driver dump, and for a refusal nothing that names a host or a user.

Only the adapter knows its driver, so the classification is the adapter's; the engine names no database. SQLAlchemy adapters inherit it from SQLAlchemyAdapter (see SQLAlchemy adapters). An exception that escapes execute is still caught, as a non-retryable EXECUTOR_CRASH.

docs.title: close()
docs.text: Releases the adapter's connections. The engine calls it once, from engine.close(), and when a datasource is removed.

docs.title: Optional hook: render_sql(expression)
docs.text:
nl2sql_sdk.protocols.SqlRenderingAdapterProtocol. The engine builds every query as a sqlglot expression tree and, when the adapter has render_sql, passes it the finished tree and executes the text it returns. Without the hook the engine renders expression.sql(dialect=adapter.get_dialect()), so an adapter written before the hook keeps working. SQLAlchemyAdapter implements that same default.

Override it only for what sqlglot cannot express for your database. The SQLite adapter, for example, rewrites EXTRACT and date truncation with STRFTIME and DATE(x, 'start of month'). Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server and DuckDB use the default.

get_dialect() must return a sqlglot dialect name (postgres, tsql, mysql, duckdb, sqlite, ...), not the SQLAlchemy name.

docs.title: Optional hook: execute_batches(request, batch_size)
docs.text:
nl2sql_sdk.protocols.StreamingAdapterProtocol. When the adapter has execute_batches, the engine reads the result through it, RESULT_FETCH_BATCH_SIZE rows at a time (default 10,000), and writes each batch to the sub-query's result artifact as it arrives, so a large result is never held whole in memory (see Artifact Store). Without the hook the engine calls execute and writes its one ResultFrame, so an adapter written before the hook keeps working unchanged.

The contract:

  • It is a generator (or returns an iterator) of ResultFrame.
  • Every frame carries the result's columns and at most batch_size rows. An empty result is one frame with its columns and no rows.
  • A failure, before the first row or between batches, is one frame with success=False and an error, classified exactly as execute would (retryable, safe_message), and it is the last frame. The engine discards whatever it had written.
  • The request is the same AdapterRequest execute gets; refuse one you cannot run the same way.

SQLAlchemyAdapter implements it with fetchmany on a result opened with stream_results, a server-side cursor on drivers that have one (see SQLAlchemy adapters).

The hook is an optional protocol rather than a required method, so an adapter without it needs no change.

docs.title: Optional hooks: estimate and probe_overlap
docs.text:
Two optional protocols in nl2sql_sdk.protocols, added for release 0.8, found with isinstance as the two hooks above are. The adapter interface stays at version 2.

Protocol Method Contract EstimatingAdapterProtocol estimate(sql, parameters) -> Estimate The database's estimate of the rows sql reads, without executing it, under timeout_ms; raise on failure. Declare ESTIMATES_COST with it. ProfilingAdapterProtocol probe_overlap(left, right, sample_rows) -> Overlap Of up to sample_rows distinct non-null values of the column left (a ColumnRef), how many exist in right. Read-only, within the adapter's limits.

Estimate (nl2sql_sdk.models) has rows (the rows the query is expected to read, added up over the plan's scan operators: a full scan counts its table, not its filtered output), cost (the planner's own units, for display only) and source (what was read, for people). Overlap has sampled and matched.

On the built-ins:

  • probe_overlap is on the SDK's SQLAlchemyAdapter, so all five built-ins and every adapter on the base have it. It is one statement in SQLAlchemy Core (a DISTINCT sample of left with a limit, and an EXISTS on right), run on the adapter's own connections, so read-only and under timeout_ms wherever the adapter enforces them. The limit caps the sample, not the read: DISTINCT can read all of left, so on a large table the timeout is what bounds it. A failure raises RuntimeError naming the two columns and the driver's error class, never the driver's message, which can quote a value.
  • estimate is on PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and DuckDB, which declare ESTIMATES_COST. SQLite does not: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN has no row estimates. Each reads the database's plan without running the query and adds up what its scan operators read, per execution where the plan gives the executions; the four adapter pages say how and what they do not count. Every failure raises RuntimeError, which the cost rule reads as "no estimate".

docs.title: Result types every adapter returns
docs.text:
These are part of the contract, so the same plan gives the same values on every database:

Plan operation Result type Example DATE_PART(unit, date), unit year, quarter, month, day INTEGER 2011 DATE_TRUNC(unit, date), same units ISO date string YYYY-MM-DD '2011-04-01' DATE_DIFF('day', start, end) number, elapsed days with the fraction kept (negative when end is before start, NULL if either is) 3.87

The engine builds a day difference as DateDiff(end, start, SECOND) / 86400.0; the base class's render_sql fixes it for MySQL and SQL Server, and an adapter whose database sqlglot renders it wrongly for (SQLite) rewrites the DateDiff node into a fractional seconds count.

The engine already wraps a date part in CAST(... AS INT) and a truncation in a YYYY-MM-DD format; an adapter that rewrites the inner nodes keeps those wrappers.

docs.title: Interface: SecretProvider
docs.text:
A secret provider is where ${id:key} references are read from. The secrets config names one by type (see Secrets).

from typing import ClassVar, Optional, Self

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, SecretStr


class AcmeVaultConfig(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    url: str
    token: SecretStr


class AcmeVaultSecretProvider:
    interface_version: ClassVar[int] = 1
    config_model: ClassVar[type[BaseModel]] = AcmeVaultConfig

    def __init__(self, client):
        self.client = client

    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg: AcmeVaultConfig) -> Self:
        try:
            import acme_vault  # the client library, imported only here
        except ImportError:
            raise ImportError("Missing dependency 'acme-vault'. Install 'nl2sql-acme-vault'.") from None
        return cls(acme_vault.Client(cfg.url, cfg.token.get_secret_value()))

    def get_secret(self, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
        return self.client.read(key)
Member Description interface_version 1. The engine accepts exactly the version it was built for. config_model A pydantic model for the provider's entry in the secrets config, apart from id and type. Set extra="forbid", so a misspelt key fails when the config loads, and hold credentials as SecretStr, so they never print. from_config(cfg) Builds the provider from a validated config_model instance, after the engine has resolved any ${env:...} in it. Raise ImportError naming what to install when the client library is missing. get_secret(key) Returns the secret stored under key, or None when there is none.

A provider reads its settings from its entry only, never from the environment. The module that defines it must import without its client library, so the engine can validate the entry before building anything.

docs.title: Interfaces: the stores
docs.text:
A store keeps one part of the engine's data: the vector index, the state (schema snapshots, plan cache, feedback), the run traces or the results. The storage config names one per slot by type (see Storage). The four interfaces live in nl2sql_sdk.stores, which imports only pydantic and the standard library.

Every store class has the same four members, whatever its slot:

Member Description interface_version 6. The engine accepts exactly the version it was built for. Version 2 added StateStore.put_schema_diff and get_schema_diff (schema drift); version 3 the review queue's proposal methods and BuildPointer.knowledge_hash; version 4 the conversation, workspace, dashboard, stored chart result and API key methods; version 5 the approval methods; version 6 the saved-answer methods. The version is one per kind, so a store of any slot declares 6. slot "index", "state", "traces" or "results": the sub-block it fills. The engine refuses a store in another slot. config_model A pydantic model for the store's sub-block apart from type. Set extra="forbid", so a misspelt key is an error, and hold credentials as SecretStr. from_config(cfg, *, folder) Builds the store from a validated config_model instance, after the engine has resolved any ${provider:key} in it. folder is storage.path. It should write nothing: nl2sql config check builds the stores too.

The slots' methods:

Interface Methods IndexStore open(namespace, dimension), add(namespace, entries), query(namespace, vector, k, where=None, with_vectors=False), get(namespace, where, with_vectors=False), delete(namespace, where), pointers(namespace), set_pointers(namespace, updates) (atomic), namespaces(), drop(namespace), close() StateStore migrate(), put_snapshot(snapshot), get_snapshot(datasource_id, schema_version), list_versions(datasource_id) (newest first), keep_snapshots(datasource_id, keep) (also deletes the diffs of the snapshots it deletes), put_schema_diff(diff) (keyed by diff.datasource_id and diff.to_version, which it requires; replaces one stored before), get_schema_diff(datasource_id, schema_version) (or None), get_plan, put_plan, clear_plans(), add_feedback(row), list_feedback(limit=None), clear_feedback(), put_proposal(proposal) (replaces the row with its id), get_proposal(id), list_proposals(kind=None, status=None, datasource_id=None, limit=None) (newest first), decide_proposal(id, status, *, by, reason=None, wrote=None, at=None), purge_proposals(older_than) (decided rows only), the version 4 methods on JSON documents (dict; see The state store): put_conversation, get_conversation, list_conversations(tenant_id, user_id, limit), delete_conversation, purge_conversations(older_than), put_dashboard, get_dashboard, list_dashboards(tenant_id, user_id), delete_dashboard, purge_dashboards(drafts_older_than), list_scheduled_dashboards(), put_workspace, get_workspace, list_workspaces(tenant_id, user_id), delete_workspace, put_tile_runs(dashboard_id, docs), get_tile_runs(dashboard_id), delete_tile_runs(dashboard_id, tile_ids), add_api_key(row) (raises ValueError when the id exists), revoke_api_key(key_id, revoked_at), get_api_key(key_id), list_api_keys(), the version 5 methods on JSON documents: put_approval(doc), get_approval(request_id), list_approvals(status=None) (newest first), decide_approval(request_id, status, *, by, at=None) (decides a pending request atomically; one already decided is returned unchanged; None for an unknown id) and purge_approvals(older_than), the version 6 methods on JSON documents: put_saved_answer(doc), get_saved_answer(answer_id), list_saved_answers(tenant_id, user_id) (newest created_at first) and delete_saved_answer(answer_id) (False for an unknown id), then lock(name, ttl_s), close() TraceStore write(trace_id, document), get(trace_id), purge(older_than) ResultStore write(key, chunks), open(key), exists(key), purge(older_than). Bytes only: the engine writes the Parquet.

The models they exchange: Entry (id, text, vector, metadata), Hit (an entry with its distance, and its vector when asked for), Filter (eq, ne and in, all of which must hold), BuildPointer (which build of a datasource is live, the schema_version it was built from, and the curated_hash and knowledge_hash it was built with) and Proposal (one row of the review queue: its id is a hash of its kind, datasource, target and change, which Proposal.build(...) computes). The engine embeds; a store keeps the vectors it is handed.

A results store, sketched:

from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import BinaryIO, ClassVar, Iterable, Self

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class BucketConfig(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    bucket: str


class BucketResults:
    interface_version: ClassVar[int] = 6
    slot: ClassVar[str] = "results"
    config_model: ClassVar[type[BaseModel]] = BucketConfig

    def __init__(self, client, bucket: str):
        self.client, self.bucket = client, bucket

    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg: BucketConfig, *, folder: Path) -> Self:
        import acme_blob  # the client library, imported only here
        return cls(acme_blob.Client(), cfg.bucket)

    def write(self, key: str, chunks: Iterable[bytes]) -> int:
        return self.client.put(self.bucket, key, b"".join(chunks))

    def open(self, key: str) -> BinaryIO:
        return self.client.open(self.bucket, key)

    def exists(self, key: str) -> bool:
        return self.client.exists(self.bucket, key)

    def purge(self, older_than: datetime) -> int:
        return self.client.delete_before(self.bucket, older_than)

Declare it in the nl2sql.stores entry point group (bucket = "acme_nl2sql.results:BucketResults"), or register it in code with registry.add_store("bucket", BucketResults). Then results: {type: bucket, bucket: nl2sql-results}.

Built-ins only, for now

The engine moves onto these interfaces one slot at a time during 0.6 (the index, then the state, then the traces and results). Until a slot's move lands, the engine refuses a plugin store in that slot.

docs.title: Interface: PolicyCheck
docs.text:
A policy check asks an outside service what a caller may read. The policies config names one by type in its check block (see A policy check). It lives in nl2sql_sdk.policy, with UserContext (who is asking) and Grant (allow and deny patterns, written like a role's).

Member Description interface_version 1. The engine accepts exactly the version it was built for. config_model A pydantic model for the check block apart from type. Set extra="forbid", so a misspelt key is an error. from_config(cfg) Builds the check from a validated config_model instance, after the engine has resolved any ${provider:key} in it. grant(user, datasource_id) Returns the Grant for user in datasource_id. Asked once per caller and datasource per run. Intersected with the roles; any exception denies the datasource for the run.

Declare it in the nl2sql.policy_checks entry point group, or register it in code with registry.add_policy_check(name, cls) or @registry.policy_check(name). No check is built in.

docs.title: Interface: KnowledgeSource
docs.text:
A knowledge source is where a glossary comes from: what people write about their data (descriptions, synonyms, column roles, joins, business terms, prose rules, example questions). The knowledge section names one per item by type (see Configuration). It lives in nl2sql_sdk.knowledge, which imports only pydantic and the standard library, with the glossary's models (Glossary, DatasourceKnowledge, TableKnowledge, ColumnKnowledge, JoinKnowledge, Term, Rule), all strict. A source only reads.

Member Description interface_version 1. The engine accepts exactly the version it was built for. config_model A pydantic model for the source's keys apart from type. Set extra="forbid". from_config(cfg, *, folder) Builds the source from a validated config_model instance. folder is the folder of nl2sql.yaml. load() Returns the Glossary, read now. Called when the engine is built and on reload, never during a run.

Every glossary text is at most 500 characters (the engine passes settings.knowledge.item_max_chars as the validation context item_max_chars); a longer one is a load error naming the item. Declare a source in the nl2sql.knowledge_sources entry point group, or register it in code with registry.add_knowledge_source(name, cls) or @registry.knowledge_source(name). The built-in yaml source arrives with release 0.8.

docs.title: Optional: DiscoverableAdapter
docs.text:
An adapter can declare what it is found by, so engine.datasources.scan() can offer it without the engine naming any database. It lives in nl2sql_sdk.discovery, which imports only pydantic and the standard library, with Found (kind: url, file or port, and its value). The engine tests for it with isinstance, so an adapter without it is never found, only chosen by name, and the adapter interface stays at version 2. All four members are required together: leave a tuple empty for a way of being found the adapter does not use. The five built-ins declare it.

scan() hands connection_for one Found at a time: the URL the caller passed (whose scheme, up to any +driver, is in your url_schemes), a file under the scanned folder with one of your file_suffixes, or "127.0.0.1:port" for an open port in your default_ports. Return the connection fields it fills in (the keys of your connection_model), or None when it is not yours. Do not connect: read a file's first bytes at most. scan() lists the required fields you did not fill as missing.

Member Description file_suffixes File suffixes it opens, such as (".sqlite", ".sqlite3", ".db"). default_ports TCP ports it listens on by default, such as (5432,). Probed on 127.0.0.1 only. url_schemes Connection URL schemes, up to any +driver, such as ("postgresql", "postgres"). connection_for(found) A classmethod: the connection fields this Found fills in, or None when it is not this adapter's (a .db file that is not SQLite). It never connects.

docs.title: The conformance kit: nl2sql_sdk.testing
docs.text: AdapterConformance, installed with pip install "nl2sql-sdk[testing]" (adds pytest and sqlglot), is a pytest test class an adapter's own tests subclass. It checks what this page promises through DatasourceAdapter alone: the dialect, the connection model, test_connection's stages, the index scope, profiling, bound parameters, every declared capability, error classification and streaming. Like the SQLAlchemy base, it is an extra: the SDK core never imports it. How to run it, with its fixtures and the full list of checks: Running the conformance kit.

docs.title: SQLAlchemy Adapter Reference
docs.text:
nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy is the base for an adapter to any database SQLAlchemy reaches. It ships in the SDK as an extra, so an adapter author installs the SDK, not the engine:

pip install "nl2sql-sdk[sqlalchemy]"

from nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemyAdapter, SQLAlchemyConnection

The five built-in adapters (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, SQLite, DuckDB) are built on it. It is the one part of the SDK that imports SQLAlchemy; the SDK's core still imports only pydantic and the standard library.

An adapter on it implements url and get_dialect, and overrides what its database does differently. Building adapters has a complete one; the built-in PostgreSQL adapter (packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/adapters/postgres/adapter.py) is about 60 lines.

docs.title: What the base does
docs.text: Feature Description Engine on first use Building the adapter never connects. The SQLAlchemy engine, and the driver import, are made on the first query or test_connection(). Connection pool SQLAlchemyConnection adds pool (below). Execution execute and execute_batches, with AdapterRequest.parameters bound by the driver, never written into the SQL. A database error is a failed ResultFrame, not an exception. Schema reading fetch_schema_snapshot(scope): one reflection pass per schema, filtered by the datasource's index scope (below). Default schema default_schema() reports the schema an unqualified table resolves to (inspect(engine).default_schema_name); policies read a table with no schema as a table in this schema.

docs.title: pool
docs.text:
A connection model built on SQLAlchemyConnection has a pool block, in the form's advanced group:

Field Default Meaning size 5 Connections kept open max_overflow 0 Extra connections allowed under load timeout_s 30 How long a query waits for a free connection recycle_s 1800 A connection older than this is replaced

With no overflow, size is also the most queries NL2SQL runs against the database at once, so it cannot overload a production server. A file database has no server to protect: the SQLite and DuckDB connections are plain ConnectionModels, with no pool.

docs.title: Reading a schema
docs.text:
fetch_schema_snapshot(scope, on_table=None):

  1. The scope first. The database's schemas are listed (schema_names), and a schema in system_schemas() or one the scope does not want (scope.wants_schema) is dropped before any query names it. So is a table the scope does not want. An excluded schema costs nothing.
  2. Reflect once. Each remaining schema is read by reflect, by default with inspector.get_multi_columns, get_multi_pk_constraint, get_multi_foreign_keys and get_multi_table_comment, for the wanted tables and views together. A dialect whose multi-table reflection fails is read one table at a time; a table that still cannot be read is an issue (below), and is left out when its columns cannot be read.
  3. Row counts from the catalog. row_estimates(conn, schema) gives each table's estimate (row_count_source: catalog). Only a table with none is counted, with COUNT(*), and only under profile: stats (row_count_source: exact). Under profile: catalog it has no row count.
  4. Statistics, under profile: stats, one query per column: its null share, and what column_profile(type) allows: MIN/MAX and the distinct count. A table estimated above max_profile_rows is not profiled, and gets an issue saying so.
  5. Values, only with index.sample_values: true and only for a column whose profile allows them (text): every distinct value when there are 50 or fewer, otherwise the five most frequent, most frequent first and ties by value. Off by default: values reach the index, the prompts and the model provider.

on_table is called with each table's schema.table as it is profiled.

docs.title: Issues, not log lines
docs.text:
A statement that fails while reading a table (its reflection, its row count, a column's statistics or values) is rolled back, so on PostgreSQL the aborted transaction does not fail every query after it, and becomes an IndexIssue on the snapshot:

Field Value table schema.table, or schema.* when the schema's row estimates failed column the column, for a statistics or values failure stage reflect, estimate, profile or values message the driver's first line, or why the table was not profiled

The column keeps its description with statistics: None. nl2sql index prints each datasource's issues, and engine.index.build() returns them in the datasource's stats under issues.

A rollback rather than a savepoint per column: reading only reads, so it loses nothing, and it works on every dialect (pysqlite and DuckDB savepoints do not) without a round trip per column.

docs.title: url(connection) -> URL | str
docs.text: Turns the validated connection_model instance into a SQLAlchemy URL. Build it with sqlalchemy.URL.create, so a password holding @ : / # % is escaped.

docs.title: get_dialect() -> str
docs.text:
Returns the sqlglot dialect name the engine renders SQL in: postgres, tsql, mysql, duckdb, sqlite, or any other name sqlglot.Dialect.get_or_raise accepts. It is not the SQLAlchemy dialect name (postgresql, mssql), which sqlglot rejects. tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py checks every adapter registered under the nl2sql.adapters entry point.

The class attributes title, connection_model, driver_modules and install_hint are required too; the base sets interface_version = 2. See Class attributes.

docs.title: system_schemas() -> set[str]
docs.text: The database's own schemas, never indexed whatever the scope says, matched ignoring case. The default is none. The built-ins: PostgreSQL pg_catalog and information_schema; MySQL mysql, information_schema, performance_schema and sys; SQL Server sys and INFORMATION_SCHEMA; DuckDB its system and temp catalogs.

docs.title: schema_names(conn) -> list[str]
docs.text: The database's schemas, as fetch_schema_snapshot lists them and test_connection checks it can. The default asks SQLAlchemy's inspector (get_schema_names()).

docs.title: reflect(conn, schema, wants_table, issues) -> dict[str, ReflectedTable]
docs.text: Each table and view of schema that wants_table(name) accepts, keyed by name. A ReflectedTable (from nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy) holds columns (dicts with name, type, and optionally nullable and comment; type is a SQLAlchemy type or the database's own type name), primary_key (the column names), foreign_keys (ForeignKeyContracts) and comment. A table that cannot be read is an IndexIssue appended to issues. The default reflects with SQLAlchemy's inspector, as described above. Override it, with schema_names, when the dialect's reflection does not work on the database: DuckDB reads duckdb_tables(), duckdb_views(), duckdb_columns() and duckdb_constraints(), because duckdb-engine reuses PostgreSQL reflection, which queries pg_catalog tables DuckDB lacks.

docs.title: row_estimates(conn, schema) -> dict[str, int] | None
docs.text:
The catalog's row count of each table in schema, read from the database's statistics and never by counting. The default is None: the database keeps none. A table left out of the dictionary has no estimate.

Adapter Source PostgreSQL pg_class.reltuples (a table never analyzed has none) MySQL information_schema.tables.table_rows SQL Server sys.partitions DuckDB duckdb_tables().estimated_size SQLite none: COUNT(*) under profile: stats

docs.title: column_profile(sa_type) -> ColumnProfile
docs.text:
What a column of the reflected type gets under profile: stats: ColumnProfile(min_max, distinct, values). Its null share is always read, and values is only a permission: the scope's sample_values must be on too. The default, nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy.column_profile:

Type min_max distinct values Boolean, Uuid and the dialect types built on them (PostgreSQL uuid, SQL Server bit, uniqueidentifier) no yes no JSON (and jsonb), LargeBinary (bytea, blob), ARRAY, and a type whose name says json, blob, binary, bytea, xml or array no no no A type whose name says char, text, string or clob yes yes yes Anything else yes yes no

MIN/MAX on boolean and uuid is what PostgreSQL and SQL Server reject. A type the driver reflects without a SQLAlchemy class is profiled in full, and a query the database rejects for it is an issue. Dates, times, decimals and UUIDs a driver returns for MIN/MAX are stored as ISO strings, floats and text (as_scalar).

docs.title: render_sql(expression) -> str
docs.text: Renders the engine's finished sqlglot tree as this database's SQL. The default is sqlglot's own rendering for get_dialect(). Override it to rewrite what sqlglot cannot express for the database (SQLite rewrites date parts with STRFTIME).

docs.title: build_engine(**options) -> Engine
docs.text: Creates the SQLAlchemy engine from url(connection) with the connection's pool, on first use, and runs session_setup on every new pooled connection. Override it to pass driver settings, handing them on as super().build_engine(connect_args=...).

docs.title: session_setup(dbapi_connection)
docs.text:
The one place for session settings: it runs on every new pooled connection, before its first query, with the driver's own connection. The default does nothing. Make the session read-only and set the statement timeout here, and declare ENFORCES_READ_ONLY and ENFORCES_TIMEOUT in capabilities() only for what it really enforces.

The base keeps limits.timeout_ms but does not enforce it: SQLAlchemy has no generic statement timeout and silently ignores an execution_options["timeout"]. The built-ins:

Adapter Read-only Timeout PostgreSQL SET default_transaction_read_only = on SET statement_timeout MySQL SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY SET SESSION MAX_EXECUTION_TIME SQL Server none (it has no such setting) pyodbc's query timeout DuckDB read_only=True (a connect argument, in build_engine) interrupt() on a timer, in build_engine SQLite mode=ro in the URL a progress handler per statement, in build_engine

A setting that is per statement rather than per session (DuckDB's timer, SQLite's deadline) goes in build_engine as a SQLAlchemy event. An adapter that does neither has no statement timeout.

docs.title: classify(exc) -> str | None
docs.text:
The stage a failed test_connection failed at, or None when the error does not say. The default reads a missing driver module (driver) and the standard SQLSTATE: class 08 is network, 28 auth, 3D database, and 42501 permission. Override it to add your driver's own codes and call super() for the rest; the built-ins add MySQL's error numbers, SQL Server's, and PostgreSQL's connection messages, which carry no SQLSTATE.

test_connection connects, runs SELECT 1 and lists the schemas. A failure to connect gets classify's stage; a connection that cannot list the schemas is permission. Each stage has a fix: the install_hint for driver, "check the host, port and firewall" for network, and so on.

docs.title: is_retryable_error(exc) -> bool
docs.text:
execute() catches every SQLAlchemyError the query raises and returns it as a failed ResultFrame (query_failed(exc)), with retryable from this method (see the SDK). A message saying permission or access was denied (MySQL's "command denied" included), or that the database is read-only, is a refusal whatever else the error says. Otherwise the default reads the driver's SQLSTATE when there is one: class 42 (syntax or an unknown name) and 22 (a data or type error) are the query's fault, except 42501, insufficient privilege. With no SQLSTATE it falls back on the error's kind: ProgrammingError and DataError are retryable; OperationalError (timeouts, connections, locks) is not. The message the engine sees is the driver's first line, at most 200 characters, prefixed "The database rejected the query:"; a refusal gets a generic message instead, and the full error goes to the log. Its error_code is QUERY_REJECTED for a retryable error, QUERY_TIMEOUT for a statement stopped at limits.timeout_ms (the driver reports a timeout, a cancelled statement or an interrupt), and QUERY_REFUSED for any other refusal.

Override it when your driver reports a query mistake another way. SQLite does: it raises OperationalError with no SQLSTATE for no such column as well as for a read-only database, so SqliteAdapter reads the message.

docs.title: local_path(path) -> str
docs.text: For a file-based database. The engine passes each adapter folder, the folder of the nl2sql.yaml the datasource came from (None when the config was built in code). local_path reads a relative path from there, and leaves an absolute path and :memory: as they are. The SQLite and DuckDB adapters call it in url.

docs.title: execute_batches(request, batch_size)
docs.text: Implements the SDK's optional StreamingAdapterProtocol (see the SDK). It opens the result with stream_results=True and yields it in frames of fetchmany(batch_size) rows, each with the columns, so no more than one batch is held as Python rows. stream_results is a server-side cursor on drivers that have one (psycopg2, the MySQL drivers); the others ignore it and buffer in the driver, which is still not a Python row list. A SQLAlchemyError, before the first row or between batches, is yielded as query_failed(exc), the same failed frame execute returns. execute itself still reads the whole result with fetchall.

docs.title: probe_overlap(left, right, sample_rows) -> Overlap
docs.text:
Implements the SDK's optional ProfilingAdapterProtocol (see the SDK): of up to sample_rows distinct non-null values of left, how many exist in right. One statement in SQLAlchemy Core, a DISTINCT sample with a limit and an EXISTS on right, on the adapter's own connections, so it runs read-only and under limits.timeout_ms wherever session_setup enforces them. The value flag is computed in a subquery and only a plain column is aggregated, since SQL Server refuses an aggregate over a subquery. A failure raises RuntimeError naming the columns and the driver's error class, never the driver's message, which can quote a sampled value.

The limit caps the sample, not the read: DISTINCT usually reads all of left before the limit applies, so on a large table only timeout_ms bounds the probe.

The base has no estimate: reading a plan is the database's own. See Adding estimate.

docs.title: close()
docs.text: Disposes the connection pool, if one was made. The engine calls an adapter's close() once, from engine.close().

docs.title: SQLite Adapter
docs.text:
Simple file-based adapter for local development and testing.

Implementation

This adapter extends SQLAlchemyAdapter. It opens the file read-only and stops a statement that runs past limits.timeout_ms with a progress handler.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Type: sqlite

# datasources/my_data.yaml
type: sqlite
connection:
  database: ./my_data.db # Absolute or relative path

database is the only key (SqliteConnection); any other is an error.

A relative database is read from the folder of nl2sql.yaml when the config was loaded from a file (so nl2sql init --demo can write data/chinook.sqlite), and from the working directory when it was built in code. The DuckDB adapter does the same.

Persistence

If using Docker, avoid relative paths like ./my_data.db as they will be lost on container restart. Use an absolute path mapped to a volume, e.g., /app/data/my_data.db.

docs.title: Connection Details
docs.text:
• Driver: Built-in sqlite3.
  • URI Constructed: sqlite:///file:{database}?mode=ro&uri=true. The file is always opened read-only: the driver refuses every write before any SQL is parsed, and a file that does not exist is an error rather than a new, empty database. There is no setting to turn it off; the engine never writes.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Implementation Note Read-only mode=ro Always; declares ENFORCES_READ_ONLY. Timeout A progress handler per statement See Statement Timeout. Declares ENFORCES_TIMEOUT. Connection stages The message A file that cannot be opened is database. Estimates None Does not declare ESTIMATES_COST: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN has no row estimates. A cost rule treats every SQLite query as unknown. Row counts COUNT(*) SQLite keeps no estimate, so rows are counted under profile: stats, and there is no row count under catalog. Stats One query per column See Reading a schema.

docs.title: Statement Timeout
docs.text: SQLite has no statement timeout: its own timeout is how long to wait for a lock. So when limits.timeout_ms is set, each statement installs a progress handler with its own deadline. SQLite calls it every 10,000 steps of its virtual machine, while the statement runs and while its rows are fetched; once the deadline has passed, the handler stops the statement, which fails with "interrupted" and is reported as a timeout (QUERY_TIMEOUT) that the engine does not retry. The next statement on the connection gets a new deadline.

docs.title: Hints
docs.text: • Concurrency: SQLite is poor at high concurrency. Use for Lite Mode or single-user testing only.
