docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: engine.answers: a person's own record of "this answered my question". It stores the typed plan behind an answer, not SQL and not rows, and runs it again on request.

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/answers_api.py (AnswersAPI, internal)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/answers/ models.py (SavedAnswer, SaveReport), store.py (the owner check), service.py (the logic)

docs.title: Public Surface
docs.text:
Every method takes user_context keyword-only and required. A missing caller, or one with no user_id, is a TypeError, not an anonymous owner.

Method Returns Notes save(*, trace_id, conversation_id, step, user_context, note=None) SaveReport Keeps the answer of an ask step of the caller's conversation and rates its run up. list(*, user_context, datasource_id=None) List[SavedAnswer] Newest first. get(id, *, user_context) SavedAnswer delete(id, *, user_context) None run(id, *, user_context, llm_override=None, approvals=None) QueryResult Runs the plan again as the caller, with no model call (answer=False, as a tile), so it works with no key.

SavedAnswer has id, tenant_id, user_id, question, datasource_id, plan (a ChartPlan, as a dashboard tile holds), chart (auto by default), created_at and trace_id. SaveReport has answer, proposed, proposal_id and not_proposed_reason.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Owner only. An answer is read, run, deleted and listed only by its owner. Another caller, an admin included, gets AnswerNotFound (ANSWER_NOT_FOUND, 404).
  • save takes the plan from the stored step, the helper AddTile uses, so no model text becomes a plan. The step must have answered and kept a plan, and trace_id must be that step's run: otherwise NotSavable (NOT_SAVABLE, 422). A conversation that is not the caller's is ConversationNotFound.
  • It rates the run up through engine.feedback, which also files the run's verified_query proposal when it can (origin thumbs_up). The answer is saved either way: proposed is False and not_proposed_reason says why (verified, multiple_statements, failed, no_sql, no_trace when the run's trace was not kept, and the other reasons skip_reason gives). note is stored on the rating.
  • A cross-database answer is filed under its first sub-query's datasource, so list(datasource_id=...) for its other datasources does not return it.
  • The cap never overflows. save counts and stores under the owner's lock; a save that meets another in flight raises LockHeld and can be retried. A verified answer whose source names no datasource is NotSavable.
  • Saving the same run twice is one answer and one proposal.
  • The cap. At most answers.max_per_user answers (default 100) per person. The next save is refused with AnswerLimitReached (ANSWER_LIMIT_REACHED, 409) before anything is rated; deleting one frees a place.
  • run is a normal run as the viewer: the plan goes through plan.after, the validator, the generator, the scope and the hooks, as for any run, and approvals are as run_query takes them. A plan the schema has outgrown comes back as a result with status error whose first error has error_code TILE_NEEDS_FIXING, as a dashboard tile reports it. The answer is kept.
  • Storage. StateStore version 6 (The state store).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: engine.conversations: model-led conversations over the database (Conversations), and engine.chat_tools (Chat tools).

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/conversations_api.py (ConversationsAPI, internal)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/conversations/ (api.py the turn and its loop, agent.py the [CONVERSATION] block and the step checks, prompts.py, store.py ownership and stored rows)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/conversations/tools.py (the chat-tool runner), report.py (the Markdown report)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/chat_tools_api.py (ChatToolsAPI, internal)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/conversations/models.py (Conversation, Turn, ToolStep, ModelStep)

docs.title: Public Surface
docs.text:
Every method takes user_context keyword-only and required. A conversation that is not the caller's is ConversationNotFound; one already running a turn is ConversationBusy. InvalidArgument (a ValueError, 422) is raised, before anything runs, for: neither or both of text and choice, a choice with nothing pending or not one of the pending options, an empty message, a conversation at max_turns (CONVERSATION_TOO_LONG), retry with no earlier question.

Method start(*, user_context, datasource_id=None, dashboard_id=None) -> Conversation ask(conversation_id, text=None, *, user_context, choice=None, execute=True, cancellation_token=None, llm_override=None) -> Turn stream(conversation_id, text=None, *, user_context, choice=None, execute=True, llm_override=None) -> Iterator[Event] retry(conversation_id, *, user_context, approvals=(), llm_override=None) -> Turn (approvals are Approval objects or granted request ids) ask_only(conversation_id, question, *, user_context, choice=None, cancellation_token=None) -> QueryResult get(conversation_id, *, user_context) -> Conversation list(*, user_context, limit=20) -> list[ConversationInfo] delete(conversation_id, *, user_context) -> None (ConversationBusy while a turn runs) tool(conversation_id, name, args=None, *, user_context) -> Turn report(conversation_id, *, user_context, turns=None, title=None, include_rows=True) -> str engine.chat_tools.list() -> list[ChatToolInfo]
  • start(dashboard_id=...) needs a dashboard the caller owns (DashboardNotFound otherwise).
  • ask returns the stored Turn: status is that of the last step that did not end ok, else answered; error holds {"code", "message"} when the loop itself ended it (MODEL_STEP_INVALID, or RUN_LIMIT_REACHED for stopped, or the PROVIDER_* code when the model provider refused a step). A cancellation_token that is cancelled ends the turn error with CANCELLED after the step in flight.
  • A timeout is not a cancel. Each ask step runs on its own token, a child of the turn's: a run that exceeds pipeline.timeout_s fails that step with error.code PIPELINE_TIMEOUT, and the loop goes on, so the model can say so in its reply (within max_tool_calls). Cancelling the turn's token still cancels the step in flight. ask_only (MCP's ask) returns the timed-out QueryResult with PIPELINE_TIMEOUT, and a stream stores the turn as usual.
  • stream ends with conversation.turn; see Streaming.
  • ask_only returns the run's QueryResult with its rows; the stored turn has none.
  • tool runs one enabled chat tool as a turn of kind tool and makes no model call. Arguments the tool's args_model rejects are an InvalidArgument and store nothing; a tool that is not enabled, raises or cannot apply is a stored step with error.code UNKNOWN_CHAT_TOOL, TOOL_FAILED or TOOL_NOT_APPLICABLE.
  • report returns Markdown for the stored answered turns (or turns, a list of turn numbers). A turn number that does not exist, or a conversation with nothing answered, is an InvalidArgument. include_rows=False leaves the row tables and chart takeaways out, which is how the report tool stores its output.
  • Every method needs a caller: user_context=None, or a context with no user_id, is a TypeError, not a shared anonymous owner.
  • engine.chat_tools.list() takes no caller: it lists the enabled tools' names.

docs.title: Dashboards API
docs.text:
Partly built

The workspaces, the dashboard store, pin, move and the manual edits work, and so do open, refresh and run_scheduled, generate and suggest_questions, and filter_values and refresh(filters=...). A conversation builds and edits a draft with the dashboard_edit and dashboard_pin chat tools.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: engine.workspaces and engine.dashboards (Dashboards).

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/workspaces_api.py (WorkspacesAPI, internal)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/dashboards_api.py (DashboardsAPI, internal)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/dashboards/models.py (Workspace, Dashboard, Tile, DashboardEdit)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/dashboards/ workspaces.py, api.py, edits.py, store.py, run.py (running the charts), schedule.py, and for the starter dashboard roles.py, templates.py and layout.py (the logic behind the two faces)

docs.title: Public Surface
docs.text: Every method takes user_context keyword-only and required, except run_scheduled, which runs each dashboard as its stored owner. Another owner's workspace or dashboard is WorkspaceNotFound or DashboardNotFound. A missing caller (user_context=None) is a TypeError, not an anonymous owner.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Private. A workspace and its dashboards belong to the (tenant_id, user_id) that made them; anyone else's is WorkspaceNotFound or DashboardNotFound, never "forbidden".
  • Workspaces. create and rename refuse an empty name and a name the owner already uses (ignoring case). delete raises WorkspaceNotEmpty while a dashboard, draft or saved, is in it. They are listed oldest first.
  • list returns one status (saved by default, or draft) and, with workspace_id, one workspace, newest first. refreshed_at is the oldest stored result of its charts (None until a refresh stores some).
  • pin saves a draft whole, in workspace_id, else the workspace the draft is in, else "General" (made on first use). There is no way to pin one chart. An empty draft, a dashboard already saved, or a blank title is a ValueError.
  • create_draft(title=None, workspace_id=None, conversation_id=None) makes an empty draft owned by the caller (title "New dashboard"; in workspace_id, else "General", made on first use) and publishes dashboard.changed (created). The dashboard_edit chat tool calls it on first use, with the conversation's id, which is stored as Dashboard.conversation_id; a conversation_id that is not the caller's is ConversationNotFound. The tool also makes a new draft when the conversation's dashboard has been deleted.
  • edit(dashboard_id, edits, conversation=None) applies a list of edits in order, each seeing the ones before, all or none. The named methods (rename, rename_tile, set_tile_chart, remove_tile, arrange, set_filters, set_schedule, move) each build one edit. None calls a model, and none takes a question or a plan: what data a chart shows changes only through a conversation step (add_tile, replace_plan) or by naming a reviewed query or the caller's own saved answer by id (add_verified_tile, add_saved_tile; a verified id that curated.list does not show the caller is "no verified query"). add_tile and replace_plan read an ask step of the conversation passed (it must be the caller's, else ValueError; the chat tool passes the one it runs in) and are a ValueError without one. The step's whole decomposition and each sub-query's plan, or the verified query that answered, become the chart's plan; it is first checked by a run that executes nothing, as the caller and under the dashboard's lock, and a plan the validator rejects or the caller may not read raises a ValueError that ends with "Nothing was saved." An unknown chart id is a ValueError. from_step.turn defaults to the conversation's latest turn. conversation is trusted: its steps are not re-read from the store, only its owner is checked against the caller, so it is for SDK code holding the caller's own Conversation and is not exposed over REST or MCP; the plan's access check still runs as the caller. The lock lasts as long as the edit's checks (one time limit per add_tile or replace_plan). Two more edits add a chart without a conversation step and call no model: add_verified_tile (datasource_id, verified_id, title, params, question) from a verified query of the curated section (an unknown id or parameter, or a missing parameter without a default, is InvalidArgument), and add_saved_tile (saved_id, title) from the caller's own saved answer (another user's is AnswerNotFound); the saved plan is copied, so later changes to the answer do not touch the chart. Both get the same access check as add_tile, and the chat tool dashboard_edit accepts them.
  • set_tile_chart with a kind the chart's last result cannot be drawn as raises a ValueError naming the kinds it can be, judged from the column kinds stored with that result (so a result last drawn as a table can still be drawn as a bar). With no stored result any kind is accepted.
  • set_schedule(every_minutes) below dashboards.min_refresh_minutes is ScheduleTooFrequent; otherwise it stores the schedule with the caller's user_id, tenant_id and roles, and None removes it. It runs only while a long-running process calls run_scheduled (nl2sql-api does, every minute).
  • Stored results. remove_tile discards that chart's stored result and set_filters (when the filters change) every chart's; renaming, redrawing, arranging, moving and scheduling keep them.
  • open(dashboard_id, refresh_due=True) checks access first: each stored plan is checked under the caller's current roles, running no query (a generated plan is validated and generated; a verified query is checked by the curated matcher). It returns DashboardView(dashboard, runs, refreshed_at, due). runs holds the stored result of each chart this open checked: as stored when the check ended ok, empty, or needs_approval with no other error; otherwise the check's result (denied, needs_fixing, error, ...) without rows. A denial wins: a chart with one query refused, or one a hook dropped, is denied. A result another process stored after the check is not served; the chart stays in due. With refresh_due, the charts with no result or one older than the schedule are then refreshed (trigger="open", as the caller, never approving); due lists the ids still due (an app that passed False, a chart waiting for approval, or a dashboard another process is refreshing).
  • refresh(dashboard_id, tile_id=None, approvals=()) runs the stored plans of one chart or all, in layout order, as the caller, and stores each result (TileRun: at, status, the chart with its rows, the column_kinds, the plain-English explanation, the error). Statuses: ok, empty, needs_fixing (a plan that no longer validates or parses; the refiner is never asked), denied, needs_approval (its requests in approvals_needed; the stored result is kept), stopped (a cap; the remaining charts are stopped and keep theirs) and error (returned, not stored: the chart keeps its last good result). It raises DashboardBusy (a ValueError) while the dashboard is being refreshed or edited, ApprovalNotFound for a request id in approvals that is unknown, waiting, denied or expired (nothing runs), and ValueError for a tile_id the dashboard does not have.
  • filters maps filter ids to values: refresh(dashboard_id, filters={"country": ["Brazil"]}). Each value is checked against the filter's kind first (number, temporal as YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS[.ffffff]] with an optional Z or +HH:MM, boolean, text; in takes 1 to 100 values, between exactly two), and a wrong one, or an id the dashboard does not have, is a ValueError naming the filter, raised before any chart runs. The predicate (between as >= and <=, with a date-only upper bound as < the next day; in as ORs; the values as plan literals) is added to each stored query that reads the filter's table (schema and name; a plan table with no schema never matches) before the plan goes to run_query; other queries run unfiltered. TileRun.filtered is true when every query of the chart got a filter and every active filter reached the chart, DashboardRun.filters holds the values and dashboard.refreshed the ids. A filtered refresh is returned, not stored, and takes no refresh lock (an unfiltered one does).
  • filter_values(dashboard_id, filter_id, *, user_context, limit=100) returns the distinct values of an in filter's column (at most limit, 1 to 1,000, in order) or [min, max] of a between one ([] when there are none), by a plan built in code and run as the caller through run_query, so the caller's scope and policies apply and no model is called. A column the caller cannot read, or an unknown filter, is a ValueError.
  • run_scheduled(now=None) has no caller: it refreshes each dashboard whose schedule is due, as its saved identity, and returns the DashboardRuns (trigger="schedule"). A schedule that fails a check stops, with state="stopped" and error={"code", "message"} on Dashboard.schedule, and dashboard.schedule_stopped. The codes are SCHEDULE_IDENTITY_EXPIRED, SCHEDULE_ROLE_REMOVED, SCHEDULE_ACCESS_DENIED (a chart the owner can no longer read) and SCHEDULE_HOOK_DENIED (a hook denied a chart; the message names the chart and the hook's reason). A now without a timezone is a ValueError.
  • generate(datasource_id, title=None, workspace_id=None, max_tiles=None, on_tile=None, cancellation_token=None) builds the no-model starter dashboard and returns (Dashboard, DashboardRun) (how it chooses). The roles come from the indexed snapshot and the glossary, only for tables the caller can read; each template chart runs as the caller (trigger="generate"); the charts whose first run is ok are kept and the others are in DashboardRun.skipped (title, status, reason). The result is saved, owned by the caller, in workspace_id or "General". Raises NotIndexed (names nl2sql index --datasource <id>), NoTiles (no table the caller reaches, or no chart answered), WorkspaceNotFound, and ValueError for max_tiles below 1. on_tile is called with a TileProgress (title, status, done, total) after each chart ran. Cancelling cancellation_token stops before the next chart and raises nl2sql.RunCancelled; the dashboard is not saved, no tile result is stored, and no draft or workspace this call made is left (a chart that already ran keeps its query trace, as any question does). suggest_questions(datasource_id, n=5) returns the questions of the first n charts generate would choose and runs and saves nothing ([] when the caller reaches no table; NotIndexed as above).
  • A verified chart keeps its datasource in ChartPlan.verified_datasource_id, required with verified.
  • Events. dashboard.changed (the edit kinds, created, pinned or deleted, and by), dashboard.schedule_set, dashboard.generated, dashboard.refreshed (the counts per status and the filter ids applied), dashboard.schedule_stopped and workspace.changed. They carry no titles, names or values.
  • Retention. engine.storage.purge() deletes drafts last edited more than conversations.max_age_days ago; saved dashboards are never purged.

docs.title: Guided builder
docs.text:
engine.dashboards.builder_options, propose_tiles and build build a dashboard from choices, not from a description. All take user_context, and the ids they offer are limited to what the caller's scope reaches.

  • builder_options(datasource_id, *, user_context) -> BuilderOptions returns curated (the datasource's verified queries with no required parameter, VerifiedQueryInfo), saved (the caller's own saved answers), metrics (glossary terms whose columns the caller may read; a term with any hidden column is left out whole), dimensions and time_columns (from the column roles) and ranges (last_7_days, last_30_days, last_90_days, last_12_months, this_year). It calls no model.
  • propose_tiles(datasource_id, *, user_context, sources, curated_ids=(), saved_ids=(), metrics=(), dimensions=(), time_range=None, text=None, llm_override=None) -> list[TileProposal] reads and writes nothing. sources is any of curated, saved, asked. Curated and saved proposals use no model. asked makes one model call for at most 3 new questions (from the chosen metrics and dimensions, the time range and the free text). The list is capped at dashboards.max_tiles. Without a key, asked raises MissingProviderKey; curated and saved still work. llm_override is the caller's own key, as for ask.
  • build(datasource_id, tiles, *, user_context, title=None, workspace_id=None, time_column=None, on_tile=None, cancellation_token=None, llm_override=None) -> BuildReport takes the ticked TileProposals (more than max_tiles is InvalidArgument) and makes a draft: curated and saved tiles through the two edits above, asked tiles as ask steps of one builder conversation joined through add_tile (that conversation is deleted afterwards). A question that cannot be answered is reported in BuildReport.skipped (question, code, message) and the rest are kept; nothing built raises NoTiles; a cancel or failure leaves nothing behind. With time_column a between filter on it is added. It then pins the draft, publishes dashboard.generated and returns BuildReport(dashboard, built, skipped). It does not run the tiles; opening refreshes them. on_tile receives a TileProgress per tile.
  • engine.curated.list(*, user_context, datasource_id=None) -> list[VerifiedQueryInfo] lists the verified queries the caller's scope reaches, with their parameters.

docs.text: Method workspaces.create(name, *, user_context), rename(workspace_id, name, *, user_context), list(*, user_context), delete(workspace_id, *, user_context) dashboards.get(dashboard_id, *, user_context), list(*, user_context, workspace_id=None, status="saved"), delete(...) dashboards.pin(dashboard_id, *, user_context, workspace_id=None, title=None), move(dashboard_id, workspace_id, *, user_context) dashboards.edit(dashboard_id, edits, *, user_context) and the named edits rename, rename_tile, set_tile_chart, remove_tile, arrange, set_filters, set_schedule dashboards.open(dashboard_id, *, user_context, refresh_due=True) -> DashboardView dashboards.refresh(dashboard_id, *, user_context, tile_id=None, filters=None, approvals=()) -> DashboardRun (approvals are Approval objects or granted request ids) dashboards.filter_values(dashboard_id, filter_id, *, user_context, limit=100) -> list dashboards.run_scheduled(*, now=None) -> list[DashboardRun] dashboards.generate(datasource_id, *, user_context, title=None, workspace_id=None, max_tiles=None, on_tile=None, cancellation_token=None) dashboards.suggest_questions(datasource_id, *, user_context, n=5) -> list[str] dashboards.builder_options(...), propose_tiles(...), build(...); edits add_verified_tile, add_saved_tile; curated.list(...)

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: engine.datasources: the engine's datasources, listed with their status, added and removed at runtime, tested, and their indexed schema; and the methods behind Connect a database: the adapter types with their connection forms, and a test of a datasource before it is added.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• List every configured datasource with its status, capabilities and masked connection.
  • List every adapter type the registry can name, installed or not, with its connection model's JSON Schema.
  • Test a configured datasource, as check() does, or a Datasource that is not added, registering nothing.
  • Find databases to connect: scan a URL, a folder and the local ports for what the adapters declare they open.
  • Add a Datasource (validated, built, not connected) and remove one.
  • Save one datasource to its datasources/<id>.yaml, secrets as references, refusing a file changed since it was loaded.
  • Return the indexed schema as the planner is given it, as one caller may see it.

docs.title: Public Surface
docs.text:
method returns meaning list(*, user_context=None) list[DatasourceInfo] Every configured datasource, in config order, failed ones included. With user_context, only the datasources its roles reach (policies.scope), so a caller never sees the sample questions of one it may not use. get(datasource_id, *, user_context=None) DatasourceInfo One configured datasource. Raises DatasourceNotFound (a ValueError) for an unknown id, or one user_context does not reach. A failed datasource's reason (the driver's text) is shown only with no user_context or to a caller holding policies.admin_roles; any other caller gets a generic sentence, in list too. types() list[DatasourceType] Every adapter the engine's registry can name, sorted by name, whether its driver is installed or not. An adapter module imports without its driver, so the connection schema is there before the driver is. A plugin that fails to import, or implements another interface version, is left out. test(datasource) DatasourceStatus See Testing a datasource. scan(folder=".", *, url=None, ports=True) list[Candidate] The databases found, as connection candidates, in this order and each once: the url (its scheme, up to any +driver, picks the adapter), database files under folder (suffixes the adapters declare; two folders down, at most 50, no hidden folder, not storage.path), and with ports the adapters' default ports on 127.0.0.1 only (0.2 s each). Every adapter in the registry takes part, installed or not, if it declares DiscoverableAdapter. Opens no database session and builds no adapter; test() connects. Candidate.connection carries the URL's password: repr and str mask it, model_dump and model_dump_json do not, so never log or serialise a Candidate. found.value of a URL has the password masked and its query and fragment dropped. add(datasource) None Validates connection against the adapter's connection model and index as an IndexScope, builds the adapter without connecting, registers it, and adds the Datasource to engine.config; its description and sample questions are what indexing reads. Raises ValueError if the id is taken, the type is unknown, a reference does not resolve, index does not validate (naming the index. field) or the adapter rejects its connection settings (ConnectionInvalid, a ValueError naming the field, with "did you mean" for an unknown key, and never a value; its problems list each as {path, message}). Index it next: engine.index.build([datasource.id]). add_demo(*, user_context=None, on_datasource=None) RebuildResult Try the demo: adds the three sample databases (read-only, from the installed package), their verified queries and the demo glossary (copied to demo-glossary.yaml in the project folder) as ordinary datasources and knowledge, skipping any already configured (a demo id that is another database raises DatasourceExists and adds nothing), saving it all in the project when the engine was loaded from a nl2sql.yaml (each added datasource under datasources/, the verified queries in the curated section's file, creating curated.yaml and its curated: line when the project has none, and the glossary as a source in the knowledge section's file), so it survives a restart; an inline section, or an engine built in code, keeps the verified queries and the glossary for that engine only. A demo id is the demo's own database only when it opens the packaged file or the project's data/<name>; another file of the same name raises DatasourceExists. Then runs index.build over them, passing on_datasource (an IndexProgress per datasource). With user_context the caller needs an admin role (NotAuthorized). The files it writes are checked first against the hashes read at load (a section file edited since is ConfigError "changed on disk", the REST 409 FILE_CHANGED), the text is appended so the file's comments stay, and a second call on an engine that is out of date with the file adds nothing. Also engine.add_demo(...). remove(datasource_id) None Takes the datasource out of routing and out of engine.config, and closes its adapter's pool. Its index entries stay until the next full index.build or index.clear. Raises ValueError for an unknown id. save(datasource_id, *, by, env_file=False) Path One datasource as datasources/<id>.yaml beside the nl2sql.yaml the engine was loaded from; returns the file. by must hold an admin role (TypeError if it is not a UserContext, PermissionError without an admin role). Every secret field (by its key, or declared secret by the adapter's connection model) is written as a reference: a literal needs env_file=True (it goes to the .env as ${env:NL2SQL_<ID>_<KEY>}) and is otherwise refused with SecretValueInConfig. Refuses (ReviewError, code FILE_CHANGED, fix "reload the engine") a file that changed on disk since the config was loaded, and a new file that already exists. Raises DatasourceNotFound (a ValueError) for an unknown id, ReviewError (NOT_WRITABLE, not a ValueError) for an engine built in code, whose datasources is not a folder, or whose folder cannot be written, and ValueError for an id that cannot be a file name (letters, digits, _, -, . only; no Windows device name), and two secrets that map to one environment variable. Written to a temporary file and renamed; publishes datasource.saved (audited). See Saving a datasource. schema(datasource_id, *, user_context) dict The indexed schema as the planner is given it, as user_context may see it: {"datasource_id", "tables": [...]}, tables sorted by name, each with name, schema, row_count, description, columns (name, type, nullable, primary_key, description) and foreign_keys (columns, references_table, references_columns). A table the caller's roles deny is left out, and so is a foreign key that refers to one; a caller whose roles do not reach the datasource gets no tables. user_context is required: there is no default view, so code that forgot it fails instead of showing everything. Pass an admin's UserContext for the whole schema. Read from the snapshot the datasource's live index build was made from, not the database; before the first index tables is empty. dialect(datasource_id) str The sqlglot dialect name of the datasource's adapter (postgres, tsql...). Used to read a verified query's SQL for diagram_for. diagram(datasource_id, *, user_context, tables=None) str The schema as a Mermaid erDiagram, drawn from schema(...), so only what user_context may see: a denied table, and every foreign key or glossary join that names one, is left out. Each table shows its primary and foreign key columns; each foreign key and each glossary join is a relationship. tables draws those tables and the ones one relationship away (a ValueError if none is a table the caller may see); without it, the whole datasource, cut to the 30 tables with the most relationships and a %% N more tables not shown comment. No colour, no %%{init} line, no model call. user_context is required, as for schema. See Diagrams.

DatasourceInfo is a frozen dataclass, exported from nl2sql:

field meaning id The datasource id. type Its type (the adapter's engine type for an adapter object). description Its description, or None. status ready once check() or test() connected to it, failed when one did not, unchecked before either ran. capabilities The capabilities its adapter declares, sorted. Empty for a failed datasource: nothing is routed to it. connection The configured connection, with every secret field masked as ***. References (${env:...}) are shown masked too. reason Why it failed, or None. sample_questions The datasource's own sample_questions, then the accepted glossary examples not already there. Not scoped to a caller.

DatasourceType is a frozen dataclass, exported from nl2sql:

field meaning name The name a datasource's type uses: postgres. title The adapter's title, for a form: PostgreSQL. installed Every one of its driver modules is found. install_hint What to install when it is not: pip install "nl2sql-engine[postgres]". connection_schema The JSON Schema of its connection model (connection_model.model_json_schema()): the form. A secret field is "format": "password", "writeOnly": true, which a form renders as a password input; a field with "group": "advanced" is folded away.

docs.title: Testing a datasource
docs.text:
test() takes a configured datasource's id or a Datasource.

  • An id connects to that configured datasource, as check() does: ready puts it back in routing, failed keeps it out. Raises DatasourceNotFound (a ValueError) for an unknown id.
  • A Datasource that is not added: builds its adapter, runs test_connection, closes the adapter, and registers nothing. It is what a Connect a database form calls before add. A failure is reported, never raised. An adapter object is tested as given and not closed: the caller owns it. The datasource's secret literals, and every secret the engine knows, are taken out of the reason and fix (***): a driver may echo the password it was given, and a form shows these words.

A failed status carries the stage, the reason and the fix:

stage When fix config The type is unknown (with the closest name), or connection does not validate against the adapter's model (the field, and "did you mean" for an unknown key; never a value) What to correct driver A module in the adapter's driver_modules is not installed The adapter's install_hint the adapter's stage test_connection failed: the ConnectionCheck's stage (network, auth, database, permission), or connect where the adapter does not say The ConnectionCheck's fix, or a generic one 
from nl2sql import Datasource

{t.name: t.installed for t in engine.datasources.types()}   # {'duckdb': True, 'mssql': False, ...}
form = next(t for t in engine.datasources.types() if t.name == "postgres").connection_schema

candidate = Datasource(id="sales", type="postgres",
                       connection={"host": "db.internal", "database": "sales", "user": "nl2sql",
                                   "password": "${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD}"})
status = engine.datasources.test(candidate)   # registers nothing
if status.status == "ready":
    engine.datasources.add(candidate)
else:
    print(status.stage, status.reason, status.fix)

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, Datasource, UserContext

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")
engine.check()
[(d.id, d.status) for d in engine.datasources.list()]   # [('shop', 'ready'), ('hr', 'failed')]
engine.datasources.get("hr").reason
engine.datasources.schema("shop", user_context=UserContext(roles=["analyst"]))["tables"]

engine.datasources.add(Datasource(id="ledger", type="sqlite", connection={"database": "ledger.db"}))
engine.datasources.test("ledger").status                 # 'ready'
engine.index.build(["ledger"])

To add every datasource of another nl2sql.yaml:

from nl2sql import load_config

for datasource in load_config("other/nl2sql.yaml").datasources:
    engine.datasources.add(datasource)

See Datasources for the Datasource fields, and When a datasource fails to start for running degraded.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: engine.index: build the vector index that retrieval and grounding read, report its health, clear it, prune other embedding models' indexes, inspect one search of it, and measure schema drift.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Build the index for some or every datasource, beside the live entries.
  • Report each datasource's progress as it goes, for a console or a job.
  • Report the index's health, clear it, and run one inspected search (and say what that search uses by default).
  • Compare each live database with the schema its build was made from, and read the stored versions and the diffs between them, as the caller may see them.

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/indexing_api.py (IndexAPI, internal)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/types.py (IndexProgress)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/rebuild.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/orchestrator.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/retrieval.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/health.py
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/storage/chroma.py

docs.title: index.build
docs.text:
Signature: build(datasource_ids=None, *, on_progress=None, on_datasource=None, cancellation_token=None) -> RebuildResult

name meaning datasource_ids Only these datasources; every configured one when None. on_progress Called with a sentence before each step. on_datasource Called with an IndexProgress as each datasource starts, is done or fails. cancellation_token A CancellationToken. Cancel it to stop between datasources: the one in flight finishes, the rest are not touched.

Returns a RebuildResult: ok (every requested datasource's new entries are live), stats (one dict per indexed datasource: datasource_id, schema_version and the entry counts), empty, errors (datasource_id, error) and cancelled (the token stopped the build; ok is then false and the datasources before the stop are live).

IndexProgress is a frozen dataclass, exported from nl2sql, that serves a console line and a job's status record alike:

field meaning datasource_id The datasource. state started, then done or failed. A datasource that is unavailable or not configured is failed without started. counts With done: the entries written, by kind. reason With failed: why. 
from nl2sql import IndexProgress

def show(progress: IndexProgress) -> None:
    print(progress.datasource_id, progress.state, progress.counts or progress.reason or "")

result = engine.index.build(["shop"], on_datasource=show)

A failure of one datasource never raises: it is in errors, and that datasource keeps its previous build and schema version. A build calls no model.

docs.title: index.refresh
docs.text:
Signature: refresh(datasource_ids=None, *, on_progress=None, on_datasource=None) -> RebuildResult

Writes the entries of datasource_ids (every datasource when None) again after a glossary or curated.yaml change. It reads no schema and calls no model: each entry's text is rendered from the live build's stored snapshot, the current verified queries and the current knowledge, an entry whose text and metadata did not change keeps its stored vector, and only the others are embedded. The pointer keeps its schema version and records the new knowledge_hash and curated_hash, so health() stops reporting the index stale. A datasource that was never indexed (or whose stored snapshot is gone) fails with the command to run. The result is a RebuildResult as for build. nl2sql index --refresh calls it.

The build goes into the namespace of the configured embedding model. Each datasource's new entries are written under a new build id, and its build pointer (the build id and the schema version it was made from) is switched to them when all are written: that switch is the commit. The build it replaces is kept for runs in flight, which pinned the pointers when they started; older builds are deleted. Other datasources' entries are never touched. A changed embedding model needs no special build: its namespace starts empty.

docs.title: index.health
docs.text:
Signature: health(*, user_context=None) -> dict

Health of the configured embedding model's index: status (ok, empty, stale, missing), total, counts by entry type, built_at, embedding_model, namespace, one entry per registered datasource (entries, index_version, the schema version its live build was made from, and built_at), problems and warnings. missing when the model has no namespace yet (never indexed, or the model changed): run nl2sql index. A datasource that failed to start is a warning: "Datasource 'x' is unavailable: ". check() reports its status.

Without user_context it is the whole report. With one that holds none of policies.admin_roles (and no allow_all), only the datasources its roles reach are listed, a failed one is named without the driver's text, and a warning about a preferred table (it names a table the scope may hide) is left out; status and counts stay the whole index's.

docs.title: index.clear
docs.text:
Signature: clear() -> None

Drops the configured embedding model's namespace, for every datasource. Every question fails at the resolver until the index is built again; to refresh an index, build it instead, which never leaves it empty.

docs.title: index.prune
docs.text:
Signature: prune() -> list[str]

Drops the index namespace of every other embedding model, including 0.5's nl2sql_store collection, which this version never reads, and returns their names. The current model's namespace is kept. nl2sql index prune calls it.

docs.title: index.inspect
docs.text:
Signature: inspect(query, k=8, lambda_mult=None, types=None, datasource_id=None, *, user_context) -> dict

One MMR search of the live index, as the engine runs it: the candidate pool with scores, the picks in order and what was dropped. types limits the entry types (schema.table, ...). It reads index metadata only and needs no LLM.

user_context is required (a missing one is a TypeError): the pool holds only the entries the caller's scope reaches. A denied table's entries, a glossary term knowledge.show would hide from the caller, an entry whose text names a denied table, and every entry of a datasource the caller cannot reach or that is not indexed are left out; verified-query entries are never shown. The hiding happens after the search, from a pool four times larger than usual, so a caller for whom most matches are hidden can get a short pool. The playground and REST API take the role from the request without verifying it; see the security model.

docs.title: index.check
docs.text:
Signature: check(datasource_ids=None, *, user_context) -> list[DriftReport]

Compares each datasource's live database (reflected with its index scope, catalog only, no profiling) with the snapshot its live build was made from. Each DriftReport has datasource_id, status (unchanged, drifted, not_indexed, failed), live_version, checked_at, and for drifted the diff (a SchemaDiff, to_version None) and its impact (a DriftImpact: verified queries, policy rules, preferred tables and glossary items it breaks); error (redacted) for failed. Drift publishes schema.drifted, once per drift and engine. Nothing is stored and nothing is rebuilt. user_context is required: the caller sees drift only in tables its scope may read, a datasource it cannot reach is left out (or, named, is a DatasourceNotFound (a ValueError) like an unknown one). See Schema Drift.

docs.title: index.versions
docs.text:
Signature: versions(datasource_id, *, user_context) -> list[SchemaVersionInfo]

The datasource's stored schema versions, newest first: schema_version, fingerprint (of the schema without the tables the caller may not read), live (the live build pointer names it) and has_diff (a build stored the diff that introduced it, with something the caller may read).

docs.title: index.diff
docs.text:
Signature: diff(datasource_id, schema_version=None, *, user_context) -> SchemaDiff | None

The stored diff that introduced schema_version (the live one by default), as the caller may see it; None for a first build, a version whose structure did not change, or drift only in tables the caller may not read.

docs.title: index.inspect_defaults
docs.text:
Signature: inspect_defaults() -> dict

What inspect searches with when not told otherwise, which is what the pipeline's own retrieval uses: k (8 picks), lambda_mult (1 is relevance only, 0 is difference only), fetch_multiplier (the candidate pool is k times it) and types, every entry type the index holds (schema.datasource, schema.datasource_example, schema.table, schema.column, schema.relationship, schema.metric, knowledge.term). The playground's Retrieval inspector starts from it.

docs.title: Execution Lifecycle
docs.text:
• Fetch schema via adapter.
  • Store the schema snapshot and its version (nothing reads it yet).
  • Build the chunks (the schema's, the knowledge's and the verified queries'), embed them, write them as a new build, and switch the datasource's build pointer to it, recording the knowledge_hash and curated_hash.

docs.text: engine.llm: the model each agent runs on, and replacing them at runtime.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• List each agent and the provider and model it runs on (list, get).
  • Report the prices every call is costed with (prices).
  • Replace the engine's whole llm section at runtime (replace).

docs.title: AgentConfig
docs.text:
One agent's resolved settings, as LLMRegistry builds a client from them. agents_from_config(llm) (llm/registry.py) makes one per agent from the config's llm section (LLM configuration).

Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/llm/models.py

Fields: | name | type | required | meaning | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | provider | str | yes | Provider name: openai, anthropic, openai_compatible, its presets openrouter and ollama, or one a plugin registers. | | model | str | yes | Model identifier. | | temperature | Optional[float] | no | Sampling temperature (default 0.0). None (null in YAML) sends no temperature parameter, for models that accept only their default. | | api_key | Optional[SecretStr] | no | API key or secret reference. Masked in repr, str and JSON dumps. None reads the provider's standard variable. | | base_url | Optional[str] | no | Endpoint override; defaults to the provider preset (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 for openrouter, http://localhost:11434/v1 for ollama). Required for openai_compatible. | | structured_output | Optional[str] | no | tool_calling, json_schema or json_mode. None uses the provider's default. | | parse_retries | int | no | Retries of a structured answer that does not parse (default 1). | | max_tokens | Optional[int] | no | None uses the provider's default (16,000 for anthropic, unset for the others). | | timeout_s | Optional[float] | no | Per request. None uses the client library's. | | max_retries | Optional[int] | no | Network and rate-limit retries, done by the client. None uses the client library's. | | headers | Dict[str, SecretStr] | no | Sent with every request. A value may be a ${provider:key} reference, resolved when the client is built. Values are masked in repr, str and JSON dumps, and list() shows only the header names. | | name | str | no | Agent name (default default). |

docs.title: LLMFileConfig
docs.text:
A set of agents an eval in mode full compares, one config at a time: LLMFileConfig.from_llm(llm) turns an llm section into it.

Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/llm/models.py

Fields: | name | type | required | meaning | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | default | AgentConfig | yes | The top level of the llm section. | | agents | Dict[str, AgentConfig] | no | The agents that set their own fields. |

docs.title: llm.list
docs.text:
Signature: list() -> dict

Returns each agent by its name in the llm section, default first: its provider, model, temperature and inherited (True when the agent sets nothing of its own and runs on default). An agent given a model object shows its class as model and no provider. Never a key.

engine.llm.list()["ast_planner"]
# {'provider': 'openai', 'model': 'gpt-5.5', 'temperature': 0.0, 'inherited': False}

docs.title: llm.get
docs.text:
Signature: get(agent: str) -> dict

One agent's entry from list(). Raises ValueError for a name that is not an agent, listing the agents.

docs.title: llm.recorded
docs.text:
Signature: recorded(questions: Sequence[str]) -> list[str]

The questions the replay provider can answer from its recordings, in the order asked. See the replay provider.

docs.title: llm.recorded_with
docs.text:
Signature: recorded_with() -> dict | None

{"provider", "model"} the replay provider's recordings were made with, or None when the recordings name no model. The start screen says which model its keyless answers came from.

docs.title: llm.providers
docs.text:
Signature: providers() -> list[dict]

Each LLM provider this engine can use: the built-ins whose client library is installed, and any a plugin or Registry.add_llm registered. Each has name, label, key_variable (the environment variable it reads its key from; None for one that needs no key, such as ollama), key_present (whether that variable is set), models (the verified models, [] when none are known) and key_shape (pattern, min_length and prefix of a key, for a form to check one before sending it). Never the key.

engine.llm.providers()[0]
# {'name': 'anthropic', 'label': 'Anthropic', 'key_variable': 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', 'key_present': False,
#  'models': ['claude-opus-5', 'claude-sonnet-5', 'claude-haiku-4-5'],
#  'key_shape': {'pattern': '^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}$', 'min_length': 20, 'prefix': 'sk-ant-'}}

nl2sql.provider_for_key(key) -> str names the provider a key belongs to (from its prefix), and nl2sql.provider_keys_in_environment() -> dict[str, str] maps each keyed provider whose variable is set to its key (print only a masked form). Both are top-level exports, so an app never imports nl2sql.llm.providers. So are the stateless facts a command-line tool prints before any engine exists: nl2sql.KEYED_PROVIDERS (the providers that read a key), nl2sql.env_var_for_provider(provider), nl2sql.api_key_from_env(provider) (the key, or None; print it masked) and nl2sql.ANTHROPIC_EXTRA_HINT (what to install when langchain-anthropic is missing). So are looks_like_api_key and KEY_SHAPE_MESSAGE, the config writers (default_llm, starter_config, write_env_values, write_project, check_file_name), the eval tools (LLMFileConfig, load_llm_file, resolve_llm_spec, write_records, import_records, publish_records, run_stamp), load_trace and RegistryError. The provider tables and the replay and recording tools nl2sql demo uses are not exported: that command keeps its internal imports until X1a and X1b remove them.

docs.title: llm.prices
docs.text:
Signature: prices() -> dict

The prices every model call is costed with: the engine's dated table with llm.prices applied (Prices). checked_on is the day the table was checked against the providers' pages; models maps each model name to its input, cached_input, cache_write and output rates (USD per million tokens; a config row's cache rates may be None, priced as the Prices section says), verified, source (table or config) and citation (where a table row's numbers came from; None for a config row). A model not listed is not priced: its calls' cost is null.

engine.llm.prices()["models"]["claude-opus-5"]
# {'input': 5.0, 'cached_input': 0.5, 'cache_write': 6.25, 'output': 25.0, 'verified': True,
#  'source': 'table', 'citation': 'Anthropic model table in the claude-api skill (cached 2026-06-24); ...'}

docs.title: llm.set_models
docs.text:
Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/llm_api.py

Signature: set_models(changes: Mapping[str, Optional[Mapping[str, str]]], *, by: Optional[UserContext] = None, via: str = "python") -> LLMChange

Changes the model of some agents and keeps every other llm setting. changes maps an agent's name (as in llm.list, default included) to {"provider", "model"}, or to None to drop that agent's override so it inherits default (default itself cannot be dropped). Only provider and model change: base_url, headers, prices, temperatures and the rest stay. Where an entry's provider changes, its api_key and base_url are cleared (a cleared key is the new provider's standard variable). An agent with no provider of its own follows a new default provider and keeps its own model name, key and base_url; change that agent too if they belong to the old provider. Whether a provider changed is judged against the old default, whatever the order of changes. The result goes through llm.replace, so it is validated, atomic, logged, audited, in memory only and per process.

Returns: LLMChange, as llm.replace.

Raises: ValueError for an unknown agent or default given None; ConfigError as llm.replace (nothing changes). nl2sql-api answers PATCH /api/v1/settings/llm with it.

docs.title: llm.replace
docs.text:
Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/llm_api.py (Runtime.replace_llm in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/runtime.py)

Signature: replace(llm: LLM | Mapping, *, by: Optional[UserContext] = None, via: str = "python") -> LLMChange

Parameters: | name | type | required | meaning | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | llm | LLM or a mapping | yes | The whole llm section: an LLM, or the section as written in nl2sql.yaml (a mapping, such as a request body). A mapping is checked exactly as the file is: strict keys with "did you mean", the model's validators, references kept in secret fields. A ${...} reference outside a secret field is an error rather than read, since the data did not come from the operator's file. | | by | Optional[UserContext] | no | Who is making the change; its user_id and roles are logged. | | via | str | no | The entry point making the change (python, api, playground). |

Returns: LLMChange (exported from nl2sql): by (via, and user_id and roles when by was given) and changes, each agent whose effective provider or model changed as {"old": "provider/model", "new": "provider/model"}. It holds no key.

Raises: - ConfigError for a section that does not validate, a provider that is not registered or not installed, an agent whose API key does not resolve, or, with settings.pipeline.max_cost_usd set, a model with no price. Nothing changes. nl2sql-api answers it as HTTP 422 with the same text (PUT /api/v1/settings/llm).

Side Effects: - Builds the new clients (no model call), then swaps the engine's LLMSet and engine.config.llm together under the engine's lock. Runs already in flight finish on the old set. - One INFO line on the nl2sql.llm logger and one llm.changed audit record. Nothing is written to disk.

To use the llm section of a file: engine.llm.replace(load_config(path).llm).

See LLM configuration → Replacing the LLM at runtime.

docs.title: Internals: AgentConfig and LLMFileConfig
docs.text: AgentConfig (llm/models.py) is one agent's resolved settings, as LLMRegistry builds a client from them; agents_from_config(llm) (llm/registry.py) makes one per agent from the llm section. Its fields are provider, model, temperature (None sends no temperature parameter), api_key (masked in repr, str and JSON dumps; None reads the provider's standard variable), base_url, structured_output, parse_retries, max_tokens, timeout_s, max_retries, headers (values masked like the key) and name. LLMFileConfig is a set of agents an eval in mode full compares, one config at a time (LLMFileConfig.from_llm(llm)). Neither is part of the public API.

docs.title: Behavioral Contracts
docs.text:
• The built-in providers are openai, anthropic and openai_compatible, and openrouter and ollama, which are named presets of openai_compatible with no code path of their own. They are rows of PROVIDER_PRESETS in llm/registry.py, which stays the one table of key variables, and LLM_PROVIDERS in llm/providers.py makes one LLMProvider per row. Any other provider is a plugin: a class implementing LLMProvider, interface version 2, registered with registry.add_llm or the nl2sql.llms entry point group. An unregistered name raises ValueError: Unsupported LLM provider, naming the valid ones.
  • LLMProvider version 2 has interface_version, label, api_key_env, requires, install_hint, structured_output (the method an agent that sets none is asked with) and create(agent: ResolvedAgent). ResolvedAgent carries the agent's name, model, temperature, resolved api_key, base_url, structured_output (the agent's, else the provider's), max_tokens, timeout_s, max_retries and resolved headers; neither the key nor a header value is in its repr. A provider of another version is rejected when it is loaded.
  • Each preset names a wire type (ProviderPreset.wire), and the client is built by that wire's adapter in llm/wires/ (WIRES[preset.wire].build_client). The Wire protocol (llm/wires/base.py) is build_client(model, temperature, **kwargs), structured_output_method, mark_cache(payload) and read_usage(response). wires.structured(llm, schema) is how every node asks for structured output, with the agent's structured_output method, which the registry records on the client it builds (tool_calling is LangChain's function_calling); for json_mode it adds the schema to the prompt, since JSON mode alone does not carry it. An answer that does not parse is sent back with its validation errors, up to the agent's parse_retries times (recorded on the client too), and then wires.StructuredOutputError(agent, schema, attempts, errors) is raised, which failures.provider_error() reports as MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID. wires.streaming_structured(llm, schema) is the same with the first answer streamed; a retry is not streamed. A model object given in the config uses its wire's structured_output_method and one retry. wires.wire_of(llm) picks the adapter from the client. See LLM configuration → Providers and wire types.
  • openai, openai_compatible, openrouter and ollama are on the openai wire, served by ConfiguredChatOpenAI (llm/wires/openai.py). openai uses the client's own default endpoint. openai_compatible has no endpoint of its own: without a base_url its agent raises a ValueError asking for one. openrouter defaults to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 and ollama to http://localhost:11434/v1; a config-supplied base_url overrides either.
  • anthropic is on the anthropic wire, served by CachingChatAnthropic (llm/wires/anthropic_client.py), a langchain-anthropic ChatAnthropic whose requests go through the adapter's mark_cache (a cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"} breakpoint on the last system block), with max_tokens=16000 unless the agent sets max_tokens, and whose tool calls go through the adapter's repair_tool_calls (arguments Claude nested under a single key the schema does not declare -- input, query, ... -- are unwrapped). It needs the nl2sql-engine[anthropic] extra; without it get_llm() raises a ValueError naming the extra. See LLM configuration → Anthropic.
  • openai, anthropic and openrouter require an API key (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY). openai_compatible and ollama do not: without an api_key their preset supplies the placeholder key ChatOpenAI insists on. openai_compatible never reads OPENAI_API_KEY.
  • max_tokens, timeout_s, max_retries and headers reach the client when set (ChatOpenAI's and ChatAnthropic's max_tokens, timeout, max_retries and default_headers); unset, the client's own default holds.
  • The engine's LLM is one immutable LLMSet (each agent's settings and client), built when the engine is created and on every replace, without a model call. A run reads it once, when it starts (LLMRegistry.begin_run), so a run never mixes two sets.
  • Clients come from the engine's LLMClientCache, an LRU of 16 keyed on the agent's resolved settings with the API key and each header value only as a SHA-256 digest. Agents with equal settings share one client, and swapping back reuses cached clients. A client that falls out of the cache is closed (its close(), when it has one) once no set in use holds it; engine.close() closes them all.
  • A provider that needs a key and cannot resolve one does not stop the engine being built: check() reports it (missing_keys()), and get_llm() for that agent raises a ValueError naming the agent, the provider and the environment variable to set - not the raw openai.OpenAIError: Missing credentials.
  • Ollama is supported at the transport level. The pipeline calls with_structured_output (including the recursive PlanModel in the AST planner), so results depend on the chosen local model's structured-output capability.
  • LLMRegistry.get_llm() falls back to default if the name is missing, and raises ValueError naming the missing agent when no default is registered either.
  • Embeddings are not routed through LLMRegistry: each engine builds one embedder from its embeddings section, through the registry's embeddings providers (openai, which needs an OpenAI key even when chat runs through OpenRouter, or local, the key-free ONNX model bundled with chromadb), or uses the Embeddings(instance=...) it is given. Two engines never share one.
  • Determinism: every OpenAI-protocol client is built with seed=42 (Anthropic has no seed parameter), and every client with the agent's configured temperature, or none when it is null (see LLM configuration → Temperature).
  • A provider's HTTP 400 rejecting temperature is re-raised as a ValueError naming the model and agent and telling you to set temperature: null.
  • LLMRegistry.register_llms (internal) registers each agent under its key in the mapping, whatever its name field says.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: engine.policies: who may read what. The roles, what a caller may read in a datasource, whether a caller may read a table, and whether the patterns match the datasources.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• List the configured roles.
  • Give the Scope a caller has in one datasource, and check one table with it.
  • Check that every pattern matches a datasource the engine has.

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/policy_api.py (PoliciesAPI, internal)
  • packages/sdk/src/nl2sql_sdk/policy.py (UserContext, Grant, PolicyCheck)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/policies/scope.py (PolicyEngine, Scope)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/policies/check.py (building a policies.check block)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/policies/patterns.py (the pattern rules)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/config/models.py (Policies, Role)

docs.title: UserContext
docs.text:
Exported from nl2sql; defined in nl2sql_sdk.policy, so a policy check needs only the SDK. Fields: user_id (optional), tenant_id (optional) and roles (a list).

method returns meaning roles() dict[str, Role] The configured roles by id: each one's description, allow and deny patterns. Empty with allow_all. scope(user_context, datasource_id) Scope What user_context may read in datasource_id: the same Scope a run decides with. allows(user_context, datasource_id, table, schema=None) bool Whether user_context may read table. schema defaults to the datasource's default schema. validate() PolicyValidationReport Every pattern checked against the engine's datasources: one entry per pattern (role, target -- Allow: <pattern> or Deny: <pattern> --, status -- OK, MISSING, UNAVAILABLE -- and details), and ok. The patterns' own shape was checked when the config loaded. nl2sql policy validate prints it.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
method returns meaning reaches_datasource() bool Whether any role reaches the datasource (one of its allow patterns can match inside it) and, with a policy check, the check's grant does too. allows(schema, table) bool Whether schema.table may be read; a None schema is the default schema. rule_for(schema, table) str or None Why it may not be read (the deny pattern, or the missing allow, of a role or of the policy check), for the log; None when it may.

datasource_id and default_schema are attributes.

from nl2sql import UserContext

analyst = UserContext(roles=["analyst"])
engine.policies.allows(analyst, "shop", "customers")   # True
scope = engine.policies.scope(analyst, "shop")
scope.rule_for("main", "orders")   # "no allow pattern of role(s) 'analyst' matches 'shop.main.orders'"
engine.policies.roles()["analyst"].description

docs.title: Behavioral Contracts
docs.text:
• Patterns are *, datasource or datasource.schema.table, each part a glob, matched regardless of case; deny beats allow within a role, and roles add up. See Policies.
  • Unknown roles grant nothing, and an empty roles list does too (unless default_role is set); neither raises. An unknown role beside a known one is ignored.
  • Scope is the only access decision: the datasource resolver, the curated matcher, the schema retriever (which hides denied tables), the logical validator (which refuses), the executor's value check and allows() all ask it. Nothing outside nl2sql/policies/ matches a pattern; the architecture test test_every_access_decision_goes_through_scope holds it.
  • Inside a run, PolicyEngine.scope builds each datasource's scope once and returns the same one, so every step of the run decides the same way.
  • With a policy check, the check's Grant is intersected with the roles, it is asked once per caller and datasource per run (and on every scope() call outside a run), and any exception from it denies the datasource. See A policy check.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Provide one entry point: NL2SQL is built from one Config, owns everything it builds (its Runtime), and is the only thing an application talks to. Questions are top-level methods; everything else is a namespace.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Build the engine from a Config, resolving every name through a Registry.
  • Connect, and report what is ready, only when asked (check()).
  • Release what it opened (close()).
  • Answer questions (run_query, stream_query) and group the rest by subject (engine.datasources, engine.index, ...).

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/public_api.py: the facade
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/runtime.py: Runtime.from_config, what one engine builds
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/check.py: CheckReport, DatasourceStatus, EngineNotReady

docs.title: Creating an engine
docs.text:
Every way builds the same Config (see Configuration). Names in it (type: postgres, provider: anthropic) are resolved through a Registry; Registry.default() is used when none is passed.

constructor meaning NL2SQL(config, *, registry=None) Loads and validates: resolves every name, imports only the components the config uses, checks interface versions and driver modules, builds the secret manager, the adapters (not connected), the LLM settings (no model call), the embedder and the stores under storage.path. Raises one ConfigError listing every problem. It never connects to a datasource or calls a model. NL2SQL.from_config(path=None, *, registry=None) NL2SQL(load_config(path), registry=registry). path defaults to $NL2SQL_CONFIG, then ./nl2sql.yaml. engine.add_demo(*, user_context=None, on_datasource=None) Try the demo on an existing engine: adds the sample databases, their verified queries and the demo glossary, then indexes them (the provider is not changed); returns the build's RebuildResult. See datasources.add_demo. NL2SQL.demo(*, llm=None, path=".nl2sql-demo") The demo: the three bundled SQLite databases, opened read-only from the installed package, with the demo roles and verified queries. Without llm, the first provider whose key variable is set is used with its default model; with none set, a ConfigError names the variables. 
from nl2sql import NL2SQL, Config, Datasource, Embeddings, LLM, Policies, Storage, load_config

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")

engine = NL2SQL(Config(
    datasources=[Datasource(id="shop", type="sqlite", connection={"database": "shop.db"})],
    llm=LLM(provider="anthropic", model="claude-sonnet-5-5"),
    embeddings=Embeddings(provider="local"),
    policies=Policies.allow_all(),
    storage=Storage(path=".nl2sql"),
))

cfg = load_config("nl2sql.yaml").with_datasource(
    Datasource(id="hr", type="sqlite", connection={"database": "hr.db"}))
engine = NL2SQL(cfg)

What one engine builds belongs to it alone: its secret manager (resolving ${provider:key} references through the providers in secrets), its embedder (from embeddings, or the instance given), and its stores:

store location Vector index <storage.path>/index/ Schema snapshots, plan cache, feedback, the index lock the state store, <storage.path>/state.db by default Run traces <storage.path>/traces/ Result files <storage.path>/results/ (see Artifact Store)

A relative storage.path, and a relative SQLite or DuckDB file in a datasource's connection, are read from the folder of nl2sql.yaml when the config was loaded from a file, and from the working directory when it was built in code. engine.config is the current frozen Config, with secrets as references only; datasources.add, datasources.remove, llm.replace and llm.set_models are the calls that change it.

Each engine owns its config: nothing is process-global and nothing writes the environment, so two engines in one process share nothing. The CLI, nl2sql-api and the playground build their engine from nl2sql.yaml and call check() at startup.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
with NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml") as engine:
    report = engine.check()
    if not report.ok:
        print(report)
    result = engine.run_query("Top 5 customers by revenue")
# close() ran: pools disposed, stores closed
method meaning check() -> CheckReport Connects to each datasource and records it ready, or failed with the stage the adapter found (config, driver, network, auth, database or permission; none when it cannot tell), the reason and a fix. A ready datasource whose adapter does not declare ENFORCES_READ_ONLY carries a warning in warnings: its session can write. A failed datasource is marked unavailable and left out of routing: the engine runs degraded, and a query that targets it fails with the reason. It also reports each agent whose API key does not resolve (no model is called) and the index status from index.health(). Raises EngineNotReady if a required: true datasource fails, or if datasources are configured and none is ready; the error carries the report. Safe to call again: a datasource that connects on a later call is routed to again. close() Disposes each adapter's connection pool (an adapter's optional close()) and closes the state store and the vector store client. run_query, stream_query and check raise afterwards. Calling it twice is fine. serve_mcp(identity, *, http=False, host=None, port=None) Serves the engine to an MCP client (the mcp extra): over stdio until the client closes the stream, or with http=True over HTTP until stopped. identity is the stdio caller's UserContext; over HTTP with mcp.auth: api_keys it is None and each caller comes from its key. host and port override mcp.http. Raises ImportError without the extra. nl2sql mcp calls it. clear_plan_cache() -> int Removes every cached plan from the state store and returns how many there were. Schema snapshots and feedback stay; the next run of each question calls the planner. nl2sql cache clear calls it. with NL2SQL(...) as engine: __exit__ calls close(). config The current frozen Config. closed Whether close() ran.

CheckReport has datasources (one DatasourceStatus each: id, status, required, stage, reason, fix), llm (agent to reason, for each key that does not resolve), index, and ok, true when every datasource is ready, every key resolves and the index is built. str(report) is a readable summary.

Two methods judge a report for a caller that serves traffic (GET /ready, nl2sql doctor):

  • ready(*, keys_optional: bool) -> bool: every required datasource is ready and at least one is, every key resolves unless keys_optional (a caller brings its own key, or every agent is on replay), and the index is ok or stale (a glossary changed since the build; it still answers). A failed optional datasource does not make the engine not ready.
  • problems() -> list[str]: one line per failed datasource (its id and stage), per agent whose key does not resolve, and the index status unless ok or stale. Safe to show an administrator: it never carries a reason's text, which can echo a connection string or a key.

Building an engine is cheap and has no side effects outside storage.path, so it suits tests and notebooks. Startup policy belongs to the entry point: call check() straight after building the engine, refuse to start on EngineNotReady, and start degraded, printing the report, when an optional datasource fails.

docs.title: The shape
docs.text:
engine.run_query(question, *, datasource_id=None, execute=True, user_context=None, cancellation_token=None)
engine.stream_query(question, *, datasource_id=None, execute=True, user_context=None, cancellation_token=None)
engine.check(); engine.close(); engine.config; engine.about(); engine.clear_plan_cache()

engine.datasources   # list, get, types, test, add, remove, schema
engine.index         # build, health, clear, inspect, inspect_defaults
engine.llm           # list, get, providers, prices, replace, set_models
engine.policies      # roles, allows, allowed, validate
engine.curated       # validate, test
engine.results       # manifest, page, csv
engine.feedback      # record, list, stats, export, clear
engine.traces        # get, replay
engine.storage       # info, purge
engine.events        # subscribe, catalog
engine.evals         # load, run, regenerate, scorers
engine.knowledge     # sources, show, export, reload, profile; save_choice
engine.proposals     # list, get, current, accept, reject, export, apply (the review queue)
namespace reference run_query, stream_query, results Query API datasources Datasource API index Indexing API llm LLM API policies Policies API curated Curated answers → Checking them feedback below, and Feedback and signals traces, about() below events Events evals Evals knowledge Knowledge: sources, show, export, reload and profile (Schema Profiler). save_choice(choice, *, user_context, term=None) files a clarification pick as a term proposal (Asking again). Each read takes user_context as a required keyword. proposals The review queue: list, get, current, accept, reject, export and apply. Each read takes user_context as a required keyword; deciding takes by, a caller with an admin role.

The namespace classes are internal: reach them through the engine, never by importing them. Each is built on first use.

The CLI, the playground and nl2sql-api are callers like any other: they use only these methods and namespaces, never the runtime behind them. test_the_cli_the_playground_and_the_api_use_only_the_public_api in tests/architecture/test_boundaries.py holds them to that, and test_the_playground_the_demo_command_and_the_api_import_only_the_public_nl2sql holds the playground, nl2sql demo and nl2sql-api to importing from the top-level nl2sql only (the old playground keeps a short, named list of exceptions in that test, each with the reason and the change that removes it; nl2sql demo is now a launcher that imports nothing from the engine but nl2sql_cli).

docs.title: About
docs.text:
engine.about() describes the engine and its pipeline: version (of nl2sql-engine), git_sha (when running from a checkout, else None), python, and steps, one dict per step of a run in the order a run takes them. Each step has its node (the name usage and timings are recorded under), label, what it does, its kind (model when a model decides it, code otherwise) and its parent (sql_agent for the steps nested in the SQL agent). A model step also has its agent and the provider and model it is configured to run on; never a key. The playground's Pipeline page reads it.

about = engine.about()
[(s["node"], s["model"]) for s in about["steps"] if s["kind"] == "model"]
# [('curated_matcher', 'gpt-5.4'), ('datasource_resolver', 'gpt-5.4'), ...]

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text:
Ratings of answered runs, and the guardrail rates over recorded runs. They live in the state store (<storage.path>/state.db by default); the rates also read the traces in <storage.path>/traces. nl2sql feedback and the playground's thumbs up and down are built on it. See Feedback and signals for what is stored.

method does list(limit=None) -> list[dict] Every rating, newest first. record(trace_id, rating, *, user_context, note=None) -> dict Rate one run, "up" or "down", with an optional note (280 characters). The engine reads the run's own trace as user_context, so only the caller who asked the run can rate it; another caller's run, an unknown id or a run whose trace was not kept (settings.traces.mode) is TraceNotFound (a LookupError, 404). The stored row (question, roles, status, SQL, datasources, error codes, counters, models, engine version; never rows or the answer) comes from the trace. A thumbs-up on a qualifying answer also files a verified_query proposal. TypeError for a missing user_context. stats(*, traces=None) -> dict Rates over the ratings plus the traces in traces (default: the engine's traces folder): feedback, refusals, refiner retries, validator failures, errors, and the plan cache's hit rate. export(path) -> dict Write the thumbs-up runs to path as draft gold entries for review; {"written", "skipped"}. Raises ValueError for the gold set's own path. clear() -> int Delete every rating; returns how many. correct(trace_id, *, sql=None, plan=None, question=None, note=None, user_context, as_operator=False) -> Proposal Correct a run with exactly one fix: sql (one read-only query) or plan (a PlanModel or its JSON). The run is rated down with note unless it already is; the fix is checked as user_context and filed in the review queue as a verified_query proposal (origin correction). Only the run's asker can correct it: another user's run is refused as no_run. as_operator=True (for operator tools such as nl2sql feedback correct; an app never passes it) reads any run, and still overwrites the asker's rating with down. Raises CorrectionRefused (a ValueError, with code and messages) when a check fails. See Correcting an answer. 
result = engine.run_query("How many customers are there?", user_context=user)
engine.feedback.record(result.trace_id, "up", user_context=user)
engine.feedback.stats()["feedback"]   # {'up': 1, 'down': 0, 'up_rate': 1.0, 'down_rate': 0.0}

docs.title: Traces
docs.text: engine.traces.get(trace_id, *, user_context=None) returns one recorded run's trace document, or None when none was kept. A trace records who asked the run (owner, as a result manifest does); with a user_context, only that asker reads it, and another caller's run (or a trace with no recorded asker) is None. With no user_context, the caller is the trusted in-process operator and reads any run, as nl2sql trace does; the REST API, MCP and the terminal app always pass the caller. Which runs are kept is settings.traces.mode, and for how long the trace store's max_age_days. It reads through the trace store, storage.traces (the files store reads only <storage.path>/traces), and the id must be a plain token (letters, digits, - and _), so no id can name a file elsewhere: anything else raises ValueError, as does a file in another trace format.

docs.title: Approvals
docs.text: engine.approvals keeps the approval requests a needs_approval run raised and their grants: list(*, user_context, status="pending"), grant(request_id, *, by), deny(request_id, *, by, reason=None). The asker's re-run names a granted id in approvals= of run_query, stream_query, conversations.retry and dashboards.refresh. See Query API → Approval.

docs.title: Saved answers
docs.text: engine.answers keeps a person's own answers: save(*, trace_id, conversation_id, step, user_context, note=None), list(*, user_context, datasource_id=None), get(id, *, user_context), delete(id, *, user_context) and run(id, *, user_context, llm_override=None, approvals=None). See Saved answers.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
engine.storage.info() returns each store slot's type and location (and max_age_days for the traces and results stores that have it) and the current index namespace. engine.storage.purge() deletes the traces and results older than their store's max_age_days, and the audit observer's day files older than its own, and the review queue's decided proposals older than settings.review.max_age_days, and the stored approvals older than settings.approvals.max_age_hours, and returns the counts, {"traces": 3, "results": 12, "proposals": 4, "approvals": 0, "audit": 1}, which it also publishes as retention.purged. See Storage → Retention.

engine.traces.replay(trace) re-runs a recorded question, answering every LLM call from the trace document (no model is called), on a runtime of its own so the engine's config and LLMs never change. It returns a ReplayReport: the replayed result, how many recorded calls were served, the divergence (where the replay asked for a call the recording does not have) and the differences from the recorded result. It raises LookupError when a datasource the trace used is not configured here or does not answer; the message names each one and why. nl2sql trace replay is built on it (see Debugging).

engine = NL2SQL.demo()
admin = UserContext(roles=["admin"])                         # the schema is always one caller's view
engine.datasources.schema("chinook", user_context=admin)["tables"][0]["name"]   # 'Album'
engine.index.health()["status"]                              # 'ok'
engine.index.inspect("top customers", k=4, user_context=admin)["picks"]

docs.title: Top-level exports
