The list is fixed by tests/unit/test_public_surface.py: adding or removing a name is a semver decision. The REST API (nl2sql-api) is held to importing only from nl2sql by an architecture test.

docs.title: NL2SQL.run_query
docs.text:
Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/public_api.py, packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/query_api.py

Signature: run_query(question: str, *, datasource_id: Optional[str] = None, execute: bool = True, user_context: Optional[UserContext] = None, cancellation_token: Optional[CancellationToken] = None, plan: Optional[SuppliedPlan] = None, approvals: Optional[Sequence[Approval]] = None, clarify: bool = True, choice: Optional[ClarificationChoice] = None, answer: bool = True, llm_override: Optional[LLMOverride] = None) -> QueryResult

Every argument after the question is keyword-only. run_query passes the runtime's artifact store to result_from_state, so each sub-query carries a capped row sample alongside its artifact reference.

Parameters: | name | type | required | meaning | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | question | str | yes | The question, in plain language. | | datasource_id | Optional[str] | no | Datasource override; otherwise resolved. | | execute | bool | no | Whether to execute SQL against datasource. | | user_context | Optional[UserContext] | no | RBAC context. Omitted (or None), the run starts with an empty UserContext, a caller with no roles, and RBAC treats it exactly as it treats any roles list it has no policy for. Pass one with a role to be granted anything. | | cancellation_token | Optional[CancellationToken] | no | A token (from nl2sql import CancellationToken) the caller cancels from another thread to stop the run. No further step and no further model call starts once it is cancelled; the step in flight finishes, and the result carries one CANCELLED error. The playground cancels it when the browser drops the request. | | plan | Optional[SuppliedPlan] | no | A plan the caller holds (from nl2sql import SuppliedPlan): a whole run (decomposition and plans), or a verified query (verified and verified_datasource_id). See Running a plan you hold. A datasource_id passed with it must be the datasource of every sub-query of the plan, or the call raises ValueError before anything runs. | | approvals | Optional[Sequence[Union[Approval, str]]] | no | Approvals for an earlier run's approvals_needed: Approval objects, or request ids granted through engine.approvals. See Approval. | | clarify | bool | no | Default True: a question the planner reads two or three ways ends needs_clarification with the options instead of running the most likely one. False runs the most likely reading and lists the others as assumptions. The prompts are the same either way. See Clarification. | | choice | Optional[ClarificationChoice] | no | The caller's pick from an earlier run's clarification (from nl2sql import ClarificationChoice: request, option_id). Ask the same question as the same caller: the chosen option's plan runs through the validator and the generator without routing, decomposing or planning. See Asking again. Not with plan or approvals. | | answer | bool | no | Default True. False skips the answer synthesizer: the run ends at the aggregator, final_answer is None and no model is called to write prose. With plan= that is a run with no model call at all, which is how a dashboard refresh re-runs a stored plan. The rows, the SQL and the explanation are the same. See Running without an answer. | | llm_override | Optional[LLMOverride] | no | The caller's own keys and models for this one call (from nl2sql import LLMOverride: keys, a provider to the caller's key, and models, an agent name to (provider, model)). See Per-request keys and models. A model whose provider has no key in keys raises MissingProviderKey before anything runs. |

docs.title: Running a plan you hold
docs.text:
run_query(question, plan=SuppliedPlan(...)) runs a plan without routing or planning: the curated matcher, the datasource resolver, the decomposer and the planner's model call are skipped. A SuppliedPlan is a whole run, shaped on the pinned run the approval re-run uses, and is exactly one of:

  • decomposition (a DecomposerResponse, its combine groups and post-combine steps included) and plans, the plan of every sub-query keyed by its id; or
  • verified (a VerifiedRef: the verified query's id and its bound params) and verified_datasource_id.

SuppliedPlan.for_sub_query(sub_query, plan) is the common case, one sub-query run standalone. A plan missing for a sub-query, a plan for a sub-query that is not there, or both forms at once is a ValidationError when the SuppliedPlan is built. What is not skipped:

  • Every datasource of the decomposition is checked against user_context's scope, as the resolver would; a datasource the caller may not read ends the run with SECURITY_VIOLATION before anything runs.
  • The plan passes the plan.after hooks, the logical validator (so a table outside the caller's scope is refused) and the generator, like any plan.
  • It is never written to the plan cache, and a validator failure ends the sub-query with the validator's error: the refiner is never asked for a different plan. A database error is not retried either.

The sub-query's plan_source is "supplied". The question is still asked: the answer is written for it (unless answer=False). The same entry serves the approved re-run ("approved") and a plan the asker chose ("chosen").

A supplied verified query is run by the curated matcher with its values, and it never falls back to a model run (a dashboard refresh uses no tokens). The call raises ValueError, before anything runs, when no curated file with a verified query is loaded, or datasource_id is not verified_datasource_id. With execute=False the matcher checks the query (the caller's scope, its values, every table it reads) and runs nothing: the run ends plan_only, or with the error below (a dashboard's access check). Where an approved pin would fall back to generation, a supplied one ends the run with an error and makes no model call: SECURITY_VIOLATION (the role may not read the datasource or a table the query reads), EXECUTION_FAILED (the query failed) or INVALID_STATE (an unknown query id, or a value that is missing or out of bounds).

docs.title: Running without an answer
docs.text:
run_query(question, plan=plan, answer=False, user_context=...) is a run with no model call. It is how a stored plan is re-run to refresh a chart: the graph is built without the answer synthesizer, so the run ends at the aggregator and final_answer is None (a stopped or timed-out run too: it has no stop text), timings has no answer_synthesizer and a streamed run emits no answer.delta. answer is recorded in the trace's request, so a replay runs the same graph. On its own, answer=False still routes, decomposes and plans with the models; pair it with plan= for a run that calls none.

Hooks still apply. While a hook is attached at answer.after, a model-free step runs it with final_answer=None, so a Deny withholds the rows and the result manifest as it does after an answer, and stream_query sends the result.manifest event only once the hook has allowed it.

docs.title: Approval
docs.text:
A hook at execute.before may answer NeedsApproval(reason). The run then ends with status: "needs_approval", the error NEEDS_APPROVAL and one ApprovalRequest per pending sub-query in approvals_needed: the question, the asker's user_id and tenant_id, the hook, the datasource, the run's decomposition, the sub-query and its plan (or, on the verified path, the verified query's id and values), the SQL and its SHA-256, the reason, and the roles that may approve (for display). Its id is a SHA-256 over a fixed list of those fields (REQUEST_ID_FIELDS: all but the reason and the roles), each without the values it holds at their defaults, so an edit shows, the same request always has the same id, and a field added in a later version keeps the ids of requests an app stored before.

An approver re-runs the question as the asker:

result = engine.run_query(question, user_context=asker)
if result.status == "needs_approval":
    approvals = [Approval(request=r, by=approver) for r in result.approvals_needed]
    result = engine.run_query(question, user_context=asker, approvals=approvals)

Request ids are the other way, for an approver and an asker who are different callers at different times (over HTTP). A run that ends needs_approval stores each request; an approver grants it by id, and the asker's re-run names the id:

result = engine.run_query(question, user_context=asker)          # needs_approval, requests stored
[record] = engine.approvals.list(user_context=approver)          # status="pending" by default
engine.approvals.grant(record.id, by=approver)                   # NotAuthorized without an approver role
result = engine.run_query(question, user_context=asker, approvals=[record.id])

list(*, user_context, status="pending") shows the requests the caller's roles may approve and the caller's own, within the caller's tenant (another tenant's id is ApprovalNotFound in list, grant and deny, and APPROVAL_NOT_GRANTED as a run's id); grant(request_id, *, by) and deny(request_id, *, by, reason=None) return the ApprovalRecord (id, status, request, created_at, updated_at, decided_by, reason, own: whether the caller asked it, set by list, grant and deny; the approver's roles stay inside the engine); a request already decided is returned as it is, and an unknown or expired id is ApprovalNotFound. A grant is reusable for any re-run of that request (same question, asker, plan and SQL) until it expires (settings.approvals.max_age_hours, 24, counted from the last change). An id that is unknown, still waiting, denied or expired ends the run with APPROVAL_NOT_GRANTED before the graph runs. stream_query, conversations.retry and dashboards.refresh take ids the same way (a refresh with a bad id raises ApprovalNotFound before any chart runs).

The engine, not the hook, checks each approval. An approval pins nothing when its request was edited (its id no longer matches), its sql is not the SQL of its sql_sha256 (the SQL an approver reads is the SQL whose hash is checked), it is for another question or another asker, its hook is not configured, or by holds none of that hook's approver roles. Then the run plans as usual and the hook asks again. Otherwise the re-run takes the request's decomposition and plan (plan_source: "approved", no resolver, decomposer or planner call) and validates and generates the SQL again. At execute.before the approval counts as the hook's Allow only when it is for that hook and datasource, the hash of the SQL just generated equals the request's (and, on the verified path, the values are the same), and by holds one of the hook's configured approver_roles (by default policies.admin_roles), never the roles the request lists. Then the next hook still runs. Anything else asks again: the run ends needs_approval with a new request. An Approval object is not stored, signed or expired by the engine (request ids are stored and expire: see above): it is trusted as far as the user_context a caller passes. See Hooks.

Returns: QueryResult, built from the pipeline graph state by result_from_state.

Raises: No exceptions are raised by run_query; errors are returned in QueryResult.errors.

Side Effects: - Pipeline execution, LLM calls, optional database execution.

Idempotency: - Not guaranteed; execution can depend on external systems and time.

docs.title: Execution Lifecycle
docs.text:
• Use the caller's CancellationToken, or create one per run, and install signal / Ctrl+X handlers bound to it.
  • Pass the graph a callback that raises RunCancelled at the next node start or model call once the token is cancelled.
  • Build LangGraph pipeline from build_graph.
  • Execute graph in thread pool with timeout.
  • On timeout/cancel, return PipelineError with appropriate ErrorCode.

docs.title: QueryResult
docs.text:
Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/query_api.py

Fields: | name | type | required | meaning | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | sub_queries | List[SubQueryResult] | no | One entry per decomposed sub-query. | | final_answer | Optional[Dict[str, Any]] | no | Answer synthesizer payload (summary, format_type, content, warnings, and truncated: True when a result was cut at the row limit). | | errors | List[Dict[str, Any]] | no | Pipeline errors (node, message, error_code, severity, provider, provider_response). provider and provider_response are set for a PROVIDER_* code and null otherwise; see provider failures. | | trace_id | str | no | Trace identifier. | | reasoning | List[Dict[str, Any]] | no | Reasoning events/logs. | | warnings | List[RunWarning] | no | What the answer should say without failing the run. See Warnings. | | artifact_refs | Dict[str, ArtifactRef] | no | Result artifact references keyed by execution node id. | | status | Optional[RunStatus] | no | "success", "plan_only", "error", "needs_approval", "stopped", "needs_clarification", or None when nothing ran and nothing failed. See below. | | timings | Dict[str, float] | no | Wall-clock seconds per graph node, plus LangGraph for the whole run. | | usage | QuestionUsage | no | LLM calls, tokens and model time per node and for the whole question. See below. | | trace_path | Optional[str] | no | Where this run's trace file was written, or None when TRACE_MODE did not write one. See Debugging a Run. | | truncated | bool | no | True when any sub-query's result reached its row limit, so rows may be missing. See sub_queries[].truncated. | | result_manifest | List[ResultSummary] | no | The run's saved results, one per terminal DAG node (node_id, columns, row_count, truncated, column_kinds): the manifest the aggregator writes beside them. column_kinds maps a column to its type category (number, text, temporal, boolean, other); the aggregator fills it from the saved file's column types, so engine.results.chart can choose a chart without reading rows. Never the rows; see Reading a run's saved results. Empty when nothing was saved. | | source | AnswerSource | no | Where the answer came from: type "verified" with the verified query's id, datasource_id and the params it ran with, or type "generated" with the other fields None. See Curated answers. | | stop | Optional[RunStop] | no | Set when status is "stopped": the limit the run reached (max_llm_calls or max_cost_usd), its configured value, and what was spent. | | approvals_needed | List[ApprovalRequest] | no | Set when status is "needs_approval": one request per sub-query a hook asked a person to approve, with the SQL, its SHA-256, the reason and the asker. Re-run the question with an Approval for each. | | clarification | Optional[ClarificationRequest] | no | Set when status is "needs_clarification": the phrase, and two or three readings, each a label, a validated plan and its explanation. See Clarification. | | explanation | Optional[Explanation] | no | The run's plan in plain English, rendered from the typed plans with no model call: one step per sub-query with its tables, joins, filters, groupings, measures, order, glossary terms, rules and assumptions; a verified answer is one step naming the verified query. Only steps that passed validation are explained (a success or plan_only run's, and the successful steps of a partly failed one); None when no step did, when a hook ended the run, or when it cannot be rendered. See Explanation. | | decomposition | Optional[DecomposerResponse] | no | The run's whole decomposition (sub-queries and combine groups), set on every run that has one and withheld, like the data, when a hook ended the run. With each sub-query's plan it rebuilds the run: a dashboard chart stores both. |

errors holds the ERROR and CRITICAL entries, and the one INFO entry NEEDS_CLARIFICATION of a run that asked which reading was meant; WARNING-severity pipeline errors are appended to warnings as RunWarnings.

A sub-query that succeeded contributes nothing to errors: the errors of the attempts it recovered from are in warnings with detail.recovered true, and its warnings with an empty detail, each with its sub_query_id. The run trace and subgraph_outputs[<id>].errors keep every attempt's errors for debugging. A sub-query that failed without a blocking error of its own (it ended with no SQL on warnings alone) adds a MISSING_SQL error, so the run reports "error".

status is derived: "needs_approval" when a hook asked for approval (approvals_needed), "stopped" when the run reached a per-question limit (stop), "needs_clarification" when the run asked which reading was meant (clarification), otherwise "error" when any blocking error is present, otherwise "plan_only" when no sub-query produced rows or an artifact (an execute=False run), otherwise "success". A state with no sub-queries and no errors leaves it None. Hooks, approval and the caps that produce "needs_approval" and "stopped" arrive with release 0.7.

Only a capped sample of the rows is inlined, in sub_queries[].rows. The full result set lives in artifact storage, addressed through artifact_refs; each combined result is listed in result_manifest and read back by the run's trace_id with the methods below.

docs.title: Clarification
docs.text:
When the planner reads a phrase of the question in more than one way that changes the result ("sales": the invoice total or the invoiced amount), it names the phrase and gives up to two other readings beside its most likely one. The clarifier step, after the logical validator, runs each other reading through the validator's own checks with the caller's scope and drops any that fail, so an option never names a table the caller cannot read, then merges readings that render to the same SQL. When two or three readings remain, the question has exactly one sub-query, clarify is on and settings.clarify.enabled is on (the default), the run ends before the generator: nothing is executed, aggregated or synthesized.

result = engine.run_query("What were sales last year?", user_context=ana)
if result.status == "needs_clarification":
    for option in result.clarification.options:
        print(option.id, option.label, option.explanation.text)

The result then has:

  • status "needs_clarification" and one errors entry, NEEDS_CLARIFICATION (INFO, never retried);
  • final_answer a fixed sentence: "This question can be read more than one way. Choose one: Sales: total of invoice total; Invoiced amount.";
  • clarification, a ClarificationRequest (from nl2sql import ClarificationRequest): id (SHA-256 of every other field, 32 hex, so a mixed-up or edited request is recognised), question (as passed, before any run.before hook), asker_user_id, asker_tenant_id, phrase, datasource_id, schema_version, knowledge_digest, sub_query and options;
  • each option a ClarificationOption: id ("a" is the most likely reading, then "b", "c"), label, plan (the plan as JSON) and explanation (an ExplainedStep, as in Explanation). The planner gives no label for its most likely reading, so a is named by the glossary term its plan reads, else its first measure, filter or table;
  • explanation None, and the sub-query's status "needs_clarification" with no SQL: nothing ran, so the options carry the explanations.

Otherwise the most likely reading runs, and the readings that passed the checks are listed as assumptions in its explanation step ("'sales' was read one way; it could also mean Invoiced amount."). That happens with clarify=False, with more than one sub-query, when only one reading passed, and on a re-plan after an attempt already executed (a sanity check's retry), so the answer is never the flagged attempt's rows. clarification.requested (sub_query_id, phrase, options) is published on the engine's bus when a run asks; it is an operator event, not on the stream. Evals run with clarification off, so a case measures the most likely reading; a case may expect clarify, and the clarify suite does.

docs.title: Asking again
docs.text:
choice = ClarificationChoice(request=result.clarification, option_id="b")
answer = engine.run_query("What were sales last year?", user_context=ana, choice=choice)

The re-ask is stateless: the caller holds the request and sends it back, and nothing is stored. The engine checks, before anything runs:

Check Failure The request's id is the hash of its content; its question is the question as passed now (before any run.before hook); its asker is this caller; option_id is one of its options CLARIFICATION_INVALID (CRITICAL). The id is an unkeyed hash, a check against mixed-up requests, not tamper evidence: the validator, run on the chosen plan with the caller's scope, is the guard against an edited plan The datasource is in the caller's scope, the request's schema_version is the live one and its knowledge_digest the live glossary's CLARIFICATION_STALE (ERROR, never retried): the data or the glossary changed since the options were offered; ask again No approvals come with it CLARIFICATION_INVALID: pass the approval alone

A refused choice ends the run with that one error (status "error") and calls no model. A plan or a pinned passed with a choice is a ValueError at the call. Otherwise the run enters at pinned entry with one sub-query, standalone: no resolver, decomposer or datasources.after. The planner step returns the chosen plan with plan_source "chosen" and no model call; then it is an ordinary run: plan.after, the validator with the caller's scope, the generator, execute.before. A chosen plan is one person's reading and is never cached. The sub-query's plan_source is "chosen" and its explanation says "You chose: Invoiced amount".

If a hook (the cost guard, say) answers needs_approval on the chosen plan, the run ends needs_approval with an ApprovalRequest for the chosen plan; the approver's re-run passes approvals only.

engine.knowledge.save_choice(choice, user_context=ana) files the pick as a term proposal, so an admin can make the phrase part of the glossary: see the review queue.

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text:
QueryResult.warnings is a list of RunWarning (from nl2sql import RunWarning):

name type meaning code str An ErrorCode value, such as VALUE_NOT_FOUND, JOIN_FAN_OUT, ALL_NULL_COLUMN, JOIN_KEY_UNCONVERTED, RESULT_TRUNCATED or HOOK_DENIED; CURATED_FALLBACK when a verified query failed and the question was generated instead. node str The node that found it. message str What the answer says. sub_query_id Optional[str] The sub-query it is about, when it is about one. detail Dict[str, Any] What a program may branch on: recovered: true for an earlier attempt's error a retry replaced; the column, counts and type of a JOIN_KEY_UNCONVERTED. Never result rows or sample values.

The answer sanity checks (a missing filter value, a join that repeated the rows an aggregate counted, a column with no value) add theirs, and the answer synthesizer says them; see the executor's sanity checks. settings.pipeline.sanity_checks: false turns those checks off.

0.7 changed this shape: a warning was a dict with error_code and severity, and is now a RunWarning with code, and detail.recovered where severity said ERROR. A run's state is never kept across an upgrade (a run that ended needs_approval is asked again, not resumed), so no older warning is ever read back.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text:
QueryResult.explanation answers "why this answer" for a business reader. It is rendered by nl2sql/explain/ when the result is assembled (result_from_state), from each sub-query's typed plan, the knowledge its prompt carried (sub_queries[].knowledge_used), the planner's readings it did not ask about, the row cap and the run's warnings. No model is called, and the same plan and knowledge always give the same words. The answer synthesizer is not given it: the explanation describes the query, the answer describes the rows.

Only a sub-query that passed validation is explained. A plan the validator or a hook refused, and a dropped sub-query, get no step: their tables, and their glossary descriptions, would confirm what the refusal withholds. A run a hook ended (HOOK_DENIED, HOOK_FAILED, NEEDS_APPROVAL, COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) has no explanation, as it has no rows. An explanation never fails a run: one that cannot be rendered (a stored plan an older version wrote, say) is None, and the error is logged.

The glossary that names tables and tells a glossary join from a declared key is the caller's: every caller of result_from_state (run_query, stream_query, evals, trace replay and the trace itself) passes the knowledge filtered by the caller's scope (caller_knowledge in nl2sql/knowledge/scope.py), so a description that mentions a table the caller cannot read never reaches the explanation. It is the knowledge and snapshot the run pinned (run_with_graph hands back its pinned runtime as pinned_runtime), so a reload during the run does not change the words.

Explanation has steps (one ExplainedStep per sub-query, in the decomposition's order) and combined: how the steps' results were put together ("The results of a and b were joined on country."), or None for a single step. An ExplainedStep:

name type meaning sub_query_id Optional[str] The sub-query it explains. datasource_id str Its datasource. source str Where the plan came from: generated (the planner), cache, supplied (run_query(plan=...)), approved, chosen (a clarification pick) or verified (a verified query, with no plan). tables List[str] Each table, qualified as the plan names it, with its glossary description's first clause when there is one: "Invoice: one row per customer invoice (glossary)". joins List[str] Each join and the relationship it used: "each InvoiceLine to its Invoice, on InvoiceId (declared key)", or (glossary) for a join the glossary declares. filters List[str] Each condition of the WHERE, then each of the HAVING as "for each group, ...". groupings List[str] "by Customer country". measures List[str] Each aggregate the plan selects, by its alias: "revenue: total of InvoiceLine unit price times InvoiceLine quantity". order Optional[str] "highest revenue first, top 10". terms List[TermUse] The glossary terms sent with the step whose columns the plan reads: term, definition, source. rules List[str] The business rules sent with the step, by text. assumptions List[str] What the answer took for granted, all deterministic: a reading not chosen when an ambiguity was not asked about; a filter value the column did not have ('Brasil' is not in Customer country; 'Brazil' was used instead. when the final plan filters on a suggested value, else ...; the question was planned again.); the sanity checks' warnings (VALUE_NOT_FOUND, JOIN_FAN_OUT, ALL_NULL_COLUMN, JOIN_KEY_UNCONVERTED), and the row cap when the result was cut. planner_note Optional[str] The plan's own reasoning: model text, kept apart and labelled as the planner's. It appears in no other field. text str The step in two to four sentences: what it shows, what it reads and filters, which groups it keeps, and its order.

Names are the glossary description's first clause when there is one, else the name split into words (InvoiceDate on Invoice is "Invoice date"); a table the plan reads twice is named with its alias ("Track (t3)"). Each expression kind has a phrase (= "is", IN "is one of", LIKE "matches", IS NULL "is empty", SUM "total of", COUNT with distinct "number of different", DATE_PART('year', d) "the year of d", a case "depending on: ..."); a function without one is written as its name and arguments.

result_from_state(state, ..., knowledge=None) takes knowledge, a mapping from datasource id to its glossary (DatasourceKnowledge) as the caller's scope filters it; without it, names are the split names and every join is a declared key. A run on the Chinook suite's gold plans renders as the files in packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/explain/golden/, which are compared on every test run, so a change to the wording is a reviewed diff.

docs.title: NL2SQL.stream_query
docs.text:
Source: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/query_api.py, step events in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/events.py, the allow-list in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/events/catalog.py

Signature: stream_query(question: str, *, datasource_id: Optional[str] = None, execute: bool = True, user_context: Optional[UserContext] = None, cancellation_token: Optional[CancellationToken] = None, plan: Optional[SuppliedPlan] = None, approvals: Optional[Sequence[Approval]] = None, clarify: bool = True, choice: Optional[ClarificationChoice] = None, answer: bool = True, llm_override: Optional[LLMOverride] = None) -> Iterator[Event]

The same run as run_query, with the same parameters, yielded as it happens: the run's own events on the engine's bus (Events), from the caller-safe allow-list. nl2sql run shows its live progress from them.

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, UserContext

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")
for event in engine.stream_query("Which genre sells the most tracks?",
                                 user_context=UserContext(roles=["admin"])):
    if event.name == "node.finished":
        print(f"{event.data['node']} took {event.data['seconds']} s")
    elif event.name == "answer.delta" and event.data["field"] == "summary":
        print(event.data["text"], end="", flush=True)
    elif event.name == "run.finished":
        result = event.data["result"]   # run_query's QueryResult, as JSON

An Event (nl2sql.Event, from nl2sql_sdk.events) has a name, at (UTC), the run's trace_id, its tenant_id and a JSON-ready data dict; event.sse() is the event as one Server-Sent Event (event: <name>, and the whole event as JSON on the data line), which is how nl2sql-api and the playground send it.

name data when run.started question, user_id, tenant_id, roles, datasource_id, execute The run began. Always first. node.started node, sub_query_id A pipeline step began (the SQL agent's steps once per sub-query, and again on a retry). sub_query_id is None outside a sub-query. node.finished node, sub_query_id, seconds, ok The step ended; ok is False when it raised. result.manifest results The aggregator saved the results: results is the run's result_manifest and the event's trace_id its request_id, so engine.results.page can be called before the answer is written. answer.delta field, text The next piece of final_answer.summary or final_answer.content, as the answer model writes it. sanity.flagged, run.limit_reached see Events Published by the sanity checks and the caps when they arrive. run.finished the run's summary (status, duration_s, usage, error_codes, source, datasources, tables, result_manifest, user_id, roles) plus result The run finished. result is exactly what run_query returns, as JSON; it is on the stream's copy only, never on the bus. A refusal, a provider failure, a timeout or a cancel is a run.finished with status: "error", as run_query returns it. run.failed message, error_code The run could not start or finish (an exception outside the pipeline, such as a missing API key when the graph is built).

Every stream ends in exactly one run.finished or run.failed. Operator events (policy.decision, hook.decision, llm.call, plan_cache.lookup) are never on it: a denial would tell a denied caller which table exists, and the rest are operator data. An operator reads them with engine.events.subscribe.

How it works:

  • The run goes on a thread of its own, started on the first next(); the caller's context goes with it, so request-scoped keys (nl2sql.llm.request_key) reach the graph as they do in run_query.
  • Every run (streamed or not) has a RunScope, and QueryAPI.open_scope attaches a RunEvents to it: a LangChain callback the graph gets with the scope's callbacks, which publishes through the scope. A node's own run (its name is its langgraph_node) is a node.started / node.finished; the runnables inside a node are not events. The aggregator's end publishes result.manifest. The stream subscribes to its scope's events from the allow-list (nl2sql.events.STREAM_EVENTS), so it yields exactly what the bus carries, in publish order, and then its own run.finished with the result.
  • run_with_graph(stream_answer=True) asks the answer synthesizer to stream: its chain is streaming_structured (nl2sql.llm.wires) instead of structured, the same request with stream on. Each piece of the answer's tool call reaches on_llm_new_token; RunEvents parses the arguments so far as partial JSON and publishes what summary and content gained as answer.delta. The pieces are joined into one message before the parser sees it, so the answer, and the token usage the call reports, are the unstreamed call's. On the Anthropic wire the joined message gets the same tool-call repair as an unstreamed one.
  • Closing the iterator before the last event (a client that went away) cancels the run's token, so it stops before its next step or model call.

Token by token, per wire: both the OpenAI wire (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and the Anthropic wire stream the answer's forced tool call, so the answer streams on every provider; how finely is the provider's choice, and one that sends the whole answer at once gives one answer.delta per field. The other model steps return a typed object the next step needs whole, and are not streamed. FakeLLMServer streams both wires, a word at a time, so replay mode and the keyless tests stream too.

docs.title: Reading a run's saved results
docs.text:
The aggregator saves each terminal result of a run as <tenant_id>/<request_id>/result_<node_id>.parquet and writes manifest.json beside them (see Artifact Store → The result manifest). While a hook is attached at answer.after, the manifest is written only once those hooks allowed, so a run's results are not readable before that, and never for a run a hook ended (What withholding guarantees). engine.results reads them back by the run's trace_id (its run_id, the request_id of the REST routes). They read lazily from the parquet file: a page reads only its slice, and the CSV export reads and yields a slice at a time (CSV_CHUNK_ROWS, 10,000 rows), so neither holds the whole result in memory.

method returns meaning results.manifest(run_id, *, user_context) ResultManifest request_id, owner (the asker's tenant_id and user_id, and an anonymous asker's sorted roles) and results: List[ResultSummary], the same entries as QueryResult.result_manifest. results.page(run_id, result_id, offset=0, limit=100, *, user_context) ResultPage Rows offset to offset + limit of the result whose node_id is result_id. limit above MAX_RESULT_PAGE_SIZE (1,000) is cut to it, and the page's limit says so. A page past the end has no rows. next_offset is where the next page starts, None at the end. A negative offset or a limit below 1 raises ValueError. results.csv(run_id, result_id, *, user_context) Iterator[bytes] The whole result as UTF-8 CSV, header first, one chunk per slice. The ids are checked before the iterator is returned, so a missing result raises before any byte is sent.

ResultPage has request_id, result_id, columns, rows (rows[i] is row offset + i), offset, limit, total_rows and next_offset.

Scope: a run is readable only by the caller who asked it, passed as the required user_context (Who can read a run); no caller is a TypeError. Results are read from the engine's own TENANT_ID folder, the tenant every run of this engine writes under. Each of these raises ResultNotFound (a LookupError, exported from nl2sql): an unknown run_id, a run another user or another tenant asked, a manifest that records no asker, a result_id the run's manifest does not list, and an id that is not a plain token (letters, digits, _, -; at most 128 characters). Ids are checked before any path is built, and the parquet path is rendered from the artifact template, never read from the manifest, so no id reaches a file outside the run's folder.

ann = UserContext(user_id="ann", roles=["admin"])
result = engine.run_query("List every genre.", user_context=ann)
[saved] = result.result_manifest                   # node_id, columns, row_count, truncated
page = engine.results.page(result.trace_id, saved.node_id, offset=0, limit=20, user_context=ann)
with open("genres.csv", "wb") as out:
    for chunk in engine.results.csv(result.trace_id, saved.node_id, user_context=ann):
        out.write(chunk)

nl2sql-api serves these as GET /api/v1/results/{trace_id}/{result_id} and .../{result_id}.csv; the playground serves the same two under /api/query/....

docs.title: SubQueryResult
docs.text: name type required meaning id str no Sub-query identifier. intent str no Semantic intent of the sub-query. sql str no SQL generated for the sub-query (subgraph_outputs[<id>].sql_draft). datasource_id str no Datasource the sub-query targets. schema_version str no Schema version used for planning. plan Optional[Dict[str, Any]] no The validated PlanModel, dumped. validation List[ValidationCheck] no name, passed, message per validation gate. rows Optional[RowSample] no Capped row sample; None when nothing executed or the artifact could not be read. status str no "success" or "error" for this sub-query, from its final attempt: "success" when it ended with SQL and, if executed, a result; otherwise "error". A retry that recovers reports "success". "dropped" when a hook denied it with scope="sub_query": the run went on without it. retry_count int no Plan/SQL refinement attempts made. plan_source "llm" \| "cache" \| "verified" \| "supplied" \| "approved" \| "chosen" no "cache" when the plan came from the plan cache (no planner LLM call; still validated, generated and executed), "verified" when a verified query answered (no plan; sql is the verified query's own), "supplied" for a plan passed as run_query(plan=...), "approved" for an approval's pinned plan ("chosen" is reserved), otherwise "llm". Only an "llm" plan is ever cached. See Determinism → The plan cache. row_cap Optional[int] no The row limit that bounded this sub-query's SQL (the datasource's row_limit, bounded by RESULT_ROW_LIMIT), or None when the plan's own LIMIT was smaller. truncated bool no True when the result has row_cap rows: it was cut at the limit and may be missing rows. A result of exactly row_cap rows may be whole; it is counted as cut. knowledge_used Optional[KnowledgeUsed] no The glossary terms and rules this sub-query's prompts carried, and what the block's cap dropped. Only items within the caller's scope: none names a table the caller cannot read. Filled by the schema retriever; None when no term or rule matched, and for a plan served from the plan cache, which sent no prompt. estimate Optional[Estimate] no The database's estimate of the rows this sub-query reads, when the cost rule asked for one. rows is what the query is expected to read; cost is the database's own units, for display. None when the cost rule asked for none: no policies.cost limit applies to the caller, or the run did not reach execute.before. Present too when the rule then refused or asked for approval.

docs.title: RowSample
docs.text: name type required meaning columns List[str] no Column names, in result order. rows List[List[Any]] no At most sample_rows rows (default 50). total_rows int no Row count of the whole result, not of the sample.

docs.title: State mapping
docs.text:
result_from_state normalises the raw graph state (LangGraph may return dicts or model instances for nested values):

QueryResult field Graph state source sub_queries[].sql subgraph_outputs[<id>].sql_draft sub_queries[].id / .intent / .datasource_id / .schema_version subgraph_outputs[<id>].sub_query sub_queries[].plan / .validation / .status / .retry_count / .plan_source / .row_cap / .truncated subgraph_outputs[<id>] usage.plan_cache_hits count of sub_queries[] with plan_source == "cache" sub_queries[].rows artifact_store.read_result_frame(subgraph_outputs[<id>].artifact) final_answer answer_synthesizer_response.final_answer source verified_match (set by the curated matcher on a verified answer; absent means generated) errors, reasoning, warnings, trace_id, artifact_refs, timings, usage top-level state

errors are projected onto a client-safe summary; stack_trace and details are deliberately not exposed.

result_from_state(state, artifact_store=None, sample_rows=50) reads rows only when an artifact store is supplied. A failed read is not fatal: rows stays None and a warning is appended.

timings is collected by NodeTimingCallback (packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/timing.py), a LangChain callback handler that run_with_graph always attaches. It keys on metadata["langgraph_node"] where LangGraph provides it, so the keys are node names such as ast_planner, logical_validator, generator and executor.

docs.title: Usage: tokens, calls and model time
docs.text:
usage is collected by TokenUsageCallback (packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/services/callbacks/token_handler.py), which run_with_graph attaches to every run, so the Python API, the REST API, the CLI and the demo playground all report it. It is also filled in, with whatever had been recorded, on a timed-out or cancelled run.

QuestionUsage:

name type meaning total UsageTotals The whole question. nodes Dict[str, UsageTotals] Keyed by graph node: datasource_resolver (the answerability check), decomposer, ast_planner, refiner, answer_synthesizer. calls List[LLMCallUsage] Every model call in order, with its node and model. plan_cache_hits int Sub-queries whose plan came from the plan cache. A hit makes no planner call, so it adds no ast_planner calls or tokens; a question answered entirely from the cache has no ast_planner entry in nodes.

UsageTotals:

name type meaning calls int LLM calls. The planner and refiner run once per retry, so a sub-query retried once shows ast_planner.calls == 2. input_tokens Optional[int] Prompt tokens, including cached ones. cached_input_tokens Optional[int] Input tokens served from the provider's prompt cache (a subset of input_tokens). cache_write_input_tokens Optional[int] Input tokens written to the prompt cache (Anthropic reports these; OpenAI does not, so it is null there). output_tokens Optional[int] Completion tokens, including reasoning ones. reasoning_tokens Optional[int] Reasoning ("thinking") tokens (a subset of output_tokens). total_tokens Optional[int] As the provider reports it; input + output if it does not. latency_s float Seconds spent waiting on the model, summed over calls. The node's wall-clock time, which includes its non-LLM work, is in timings. cost Optional[float] Dollars, when every call counted here has a cost; otherwise null. Each call is priced from llm.prices, then the dated price table: cache reads at cached_input, cache writes at cache_write (Claude's are 1.25x input), the rest of input_tokens at input and output_tokens at output; see Prices.

A token count in UsageTotals is the sum of what the calls reported, and null when no call reported it: an unknown count is never 0.

LLMCallUsage has the same token fields plus node, model (the model the provider says served the call, e.g. gpt-4o-2024-08-06), latency_s, cost, usage_reported and error.

Tokens are read by the adapter of the wire type that served the call (read_usage in nl2sql/llm/wires/openai.py or anthropic.py), picked by the model_provider the client stamps on the response; TokenUsageCallback only asks it. Both read LangChain's AIMessage.usage_metadata (input_token_details.cache_read, input_token_details.cache_creation, output_token_details.reasoning) into the same fields, and differ where their providers differ, as below. A detail the provider did not report is null, never 0. A call whose result carried no usage at all is recorded with every count null and usage_reported: false; a failed call is recorded the same way, with its latency and error.

For OpenAI through langchain-openai (verified against the pinned 1.6.x by packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_fake_llm_server.py): prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens and completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens all arrive. OpenAI's chat completions API reports no cache-write count, so cache_write_input_tokens is null there.

For Claude through langchain-anthropic (provider: anthropic; verified against the fake Anthropic endpoint by packages/nl2sql/tests/unit/test_llm_wire_contract.py, which runs the same usage tests against both wires), Anthropic's usage maps as follows:

Anthropic usage field here cache_read_input_tokens cached_input_tokens cache_creation_input_tokens, or its per-TTL split cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens + ephemeral_1h_input_tokens cache_write_input_tokens input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens input_tokens output_tokens output_tokens

Anthropic's own input_tokens counts only the uncached tail of the prompt; langchain-anthropic adds the cache reads and writes back, so input_tokens here is the whole prompt, counted once, and both cache fields stay subsets of it. When the write is reported per TTL, langchain-anthropic sets the generic cache_creation detail to 0 and puts the tokens under the TTL keys, which are summed here.

Cost is (input - cached - cache_write) * input_price + cached * cached_input_price + cache_write * cache_write_price + output * output_price, per million tokens; a cache count the provider did not report is not split out of input. Prices are looked up in llm.prices by the served model name, then by the configured one, and only then in the dated table by either, by exact match only, so a gpt-4o price never prices gpt-4o-mini. A call with no price, or no input or output count, has a null cost. See Prices.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: engine.results: the results a run saved, read back by its trace_id, and the chart their data is drawn as. Readable only by the caller who asked the run.

docs.title: Key Modules
docs.text:
• packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/results_api.py (ResultsAPI, internal)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/execution/artifacts/results.py (ResultManifest, ResultOwner, ResultPage, ResultReader)
  • packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/charts/spec.py (ChartSpec)

docs.title: Public Surface
docs.text:
Method What it does manifest(run_id, *, user_context) -> ResultManifest Which results the run saved: per result its node id, columns, row count and truncated flag, and who asked (owner). Never the rows. page(run_id, result_id, offset=0, limit=100, *, user_context) -> ResultPage Rows offset to offset + limit of one saved result, read lazily from its parquet file. csv(run_id, result_id, *, user_context) -> Iterator[bytes] The whole result as UTF-8 CSV, a slice at a time. chart(result, result_id=None, *, user_context, kind=None) -> ChartSpec The chart the result is drawn as (Charts): a ChartSpec chosen by rules from the saved result's column kinds, with no model call. result is a QueryResult (a single sub-query's plan refines the kinds, and its intent titles the chart) or a trace_id. result_id may be left out when the run saved one result. kind forces line, bar, big_number or table; one the data cannot draw is a ValueError naming those it can. Raises ResultNotFound as page does, and also when a QueryResult has an empty result_manifest (a run a hook withheld) or its result_id is not in it: the chart is drawn only from results the caller was given. A trace_id alone is checked like page, by caller and run id; a run a hook withheld is ResultNotFound for every read, as manifest, page and csv also raise it.

The first three are described with run_query in Query API.

The run's trace is bound to the same asker: it records owner (the same ResultOwner), and engine.traces.get(trace_id, *, user_context=None) answers only that asker, with None for any other caller's run. No user_context is the trusted in-process operator (nl2sql trace), which reads any run. engine.feedback.record(trace_id, rating, *, user_context) reads the run's trace as the caller and raises TraceNotFound for another caller's run (Feedback).

docs.title: Who can read a run
docs.text:
Every run writes manifest.json beside its results, and the manifest records who asked: a ResultOwner, the caller's tenant_id (else the engine's settings.tenant_id) and user_id, and for an anonymous caller its roles, sorted. Every read goes through the manifest, and every method takes the caller as a required keyword, user_context:

  • A named user who asked reads the run: the same user_id and the same tenant, whatever their roles are now.
  • An anonymous caller (no user_id) reads a run asked anonymously in the same tenant with the same set of roles.
  • Any other caller is ResultNotFound, exactly as for a run that does not exist: another user of the same tenant, the same user id in another tenant, an anonymous caller reading a named user's run, or an anonymous caller with other roles. A trace id appears in events, traces and the audit log, so it is never the access check.
  • No caller is a TypeError (user_context missing, None, or not a UserContext). There is no default caller, as for conversations and dashboards: failing open would let anyone read a run whose trace id they saw.
  • A manifest that records no asker (one written before 0.9) is ResultNotFound for every caller. There is no legacy path; run the question again.

Anonymous callers. A run asked with no user_id (a UserContext with only roles, or run_query with no user_context) is owned by its tenant and its sorted roles. It is readable by any caller of that tenant who also has no user_id and has the same roles, and by no named user. So a viewer holding an admin run's trace id reads nothing, while anonymous callers with the same roles share each other's results, because nothing else tells them apart.

The REST API has no per-user identity yet: its static or header role (and the playground's role picker) build a UserContext with roles only. So every REST run is anonymous, and readable by any REST caller of the same tenant with the same roles. API keys carry a user_id, but only to the MCP server; REST does not take them. To keep callers' results apart, call the engine in process with a user_id from your own auth.

Operator tools. nl2sql run, nl2sql trace, nl2sql eval, the replay provider and the feedback tools read the result they were just given, traces and recordings, never engine.results, so they are unchanged. In-process code is trusted with the UserContext it passes: an operator who needs a past run's rows reads them as its asker, a UserContext with that caller's user_id and tenant_id.

from nl2sql import UserContext

ann = UserContext(user_id="ann", roles=["analyst"])
result = engine.run_query("Revenue by month", user_context=ann)
page = engine.results.page(result.trace_id, result.result_manifest[0].node_id, user_context=ann)
engine.results.page(result.trace_id, "combine_g1", user_context=UserContext(user_id="bob"))  # ResultNotFound

docs.title: REST API (FastAPI)
docs.text: This section documents the nl2sql-api FastAPI package that exposes the core engine over HTTP. Implementation lives in packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/.

docs.title: Application lifecycle
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/main.py

  • lifespan configures logging, builds one engine with NL2SQL.from_config() (the file NL2SQL_CONFIG names, else ./nl2sql.yaml) and calls engine.check() before it serves. A required datasource that fails, or no datasource ready at all, raises EngineNotReady: the API logs the report and starts anyway, so a restart loop never hides the reason. GET /ready then answers 503 not_ready and an admin reads each failing datasource and its stage under problems; an optional one that fails leaves the others serving. Any other failure of check() closes the engine and stops the start. The engine is stored in app.state.engine and closed at shutdown. Logs are text, or JSON lines with NL2SQL_LOG_FORMAT=json.
  • Retention: the lifespan calls engine.storage.purge() once before it serves and then once a day (purge_daily, every PURGE_INTERVAL_S seconds), so traces and results older than their store's max_age_days are deleted (see Storage → Retention). A failed purge is logged and never stops the server.
  • Dashboard schedules: the lifespan starts a runner that calls engine.dashboards.run_scheduled() every minute (run_schedules, every SCHEDULE_INTERVAL_S seconds), so a dashboard with a schedule refreshes as its owner while the server runs (see Dashboards). A failed run is logged and never stops the server.
  • The package imports the engine only through the top-level nl2sql namespace (from nl2sql import NL2SQL, QueryResult, UserContext, configure_logging, ...), never an engine submodule. packages/api/tests/test_architecture.py enforces it.
  • create_app(config_path=None) builds the app: one router module per namespace (health, query, approvals, conversations, dashboards, workspaces, answers, datasources, datasource, index, indexing, knowledge, evals, settings, llm, web) under /api/v1 (web at the root), and errors.install for the error envelope. nl2sql_api.main:app is create_app() for uvicorn nl2sql_api.main:app.
  • CORS is restricted to the origins in api.cors_origins (see CORS origins); with none configured, no cross-origin browser access is allowed.

docs.title: Dependency injection
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/dependencies.py

  • get_engine(request) returns the singleton NL2SQL instance.
  • Routes are thin over the engine's namespaces (engine.datasources, engine.index, ...); there are no service classes between them.
  • identity.caller (in nl2sql_api/identity.py) returns the caller's UserContext; see Identity.
  • identity.admin guards the routes that change datasources, LLMs or the index; see Admin routes.

docs.title: Interactive docs
docs.text:
FastAPI serves Swagger UI at /docs, ReDoc at /redoc and the OpenAPI schema at /openapi.json, with a summary, description and tag on every route. Start the server on a config:

nl2sql-api serve --config nl2sql-demo/nl2sql.yaml --port 8000   # one worker, 127.0.0.1; then open http://localhost:8000/docs

docs.title: API Index
docs.text:
API Router Path Purpose Health routes/health.py Liveness (/health), readiness (/ready, from the engine's own check), /meta (mode, auth source, request_llm; with a caller also the datasources and what is recorded) and /about. Query routes/query.py Execute natural language queries, whole or streamed as Server-Sent Events, with a clarification choice or granted approval_ids, and a request's own keys and models. Results routes/query.py A run's manifest, pages, CSV and chart (/results/{trace_id}/...). Traces and feedback routes/query.py A run's trace, ratings, and corrections as proposals. Approvals routes/approvals.py List, grant and deny the approvals a hook asked for. Conversations routes/conversations.py Conversations: start, list, read, delete, send a turn (whole or streamed), retry, run a chat tool, report. Datasources routes/datasources.py Connect a database, list datasources, read a schema or its diagram. Settings and API keys routes/settings.py The agents' models (/llm, /llm/providers), replace the LLM (PUT /settings/llm), change models only (PATCH /settings/llm), API keys (/api-keys) and the event catalog. Evals routes/evals.py, routes/jobs.py The configured suites and the scorers; the eval job. Indexing routes/index.py, routes/jobs.py Index status, drift check, retrieval inspector, the index job. Knowledge routes/knowledge.py, routes/jobs.py The merged knowledge, proposals, the profile job. Saved answers routes/answers.py Save, list, read, delete and run a person's own answers. Dashboards routes/dashboards.py, routes/workspaces.py Dashboards and workspaces: open, refresh, edit, pin, move, delete; the starter questions. Errors errors.py The one error envelope and the request id.

The router web is empty for now: a later row fills it. The committed contract is packages/api/openapi.json; test_openapi_snapshot_is_current fails when a route changes without it (rewrite it with python packages/api/tests/test_openapi_snapshot.py).

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Every non-2xx response is the error envelope, {"error": {"code", "message", "fix", "details", "request_id"}}. Only the facade's own NL2SQLError (and its named subclasses) is mapped to its status; anything else, a built-in ValueError, KeyError, PermissionError or a pydantic ValidationError included, is a 500 that names a request id and never the exception's text. Routes carry no except Exception.

POST /api/v1/query still returns pipeline errors as a normal HTTP 200 inside QueryResult.errors.

Route handlers that call blocking engine code are declared with def rather than async def, so Starlette runs them in its threadpool instead of blocking the event loop.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The REST API is configured by the same nl2sql.yaml as the engine. Beyond the runtime server options of nl2sql-api serve (--config, --host, --port, --demo, --dir, --hosted, --questions-per-minute, --questions-per-session; one worker, no reload; see Hosted demo), its own settings are the api section of that file (see The api section), and the admin roles are policies.admin_roles. The engine validates the api section and never reads it.

docs.title: CORS origins
docs.text:
api.cors_origins lists the browser origins allowed to call the API cross-origin. Each entry is a full origin (scheme, host and, if non-default, port).

# api.yaml
cors_origins: [https://bi.corp.example, http://localhost:3000]

With one or more origins configured, only those origins are accepted and credentialed requests (cookies, Authorization) are permitted.

With none, no origins are allowed and credentials are disabled. That is the intended default, not a misconfiguration: a browser page served from another origin cannot call the API until you opt it in. The list is read from the engine's config, which is loaded at startup, so changing it requires restarting the server.

This setting governs the browser same-origin policy only. Non-browser clients -- curl, server-side callers, the Python SDK -- do not send an Origin header and are unaffected by it; use authentication and network controls to restrict those.

docs.title: Identity
docs.text:
The engine enforces RBAC; the API decides who is asking. api.auth picks one source, and every request resolves one UserContext through the identity.caller dependency. The request body is never read for it.

api.auth Identity No identity api_keys Authorization: Bearer <key>, verified by engine.api_keys.verify: the key's user, tenant and roles. 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer proxy The api.proxy.user_header, tenant_header (else settings.tenant_id) and roles_header (comma-separated), honoured only from a peer in api.proxy.trusted_from. 401 (also for a peer outside trusted_from, whose headers are ignored) static One role, api.static_role, for every request, with no user id. 401 when static_role is unset none (default) The local operator: user_id: "local" with the policies.admin_roles. 403 unless the request is made straight to localhost

Under none, nl2sql-api serve refuses to bind a host that is not loopback, and a request whose Host is not localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], or that carries X-Forwarded-For, Forwarded or X-Real-IP, is a 403, so a reverse proxy on the same host or a DNS-rebinding page is not taken for the operator.

# api.yaml behind an authenticating proxy at 10.0.0.5.
auth: proxy
proxy: { trusted_from: [10.0.0.5/32] }

A test or an embedding app overrides identity.caller and identity.admin with app.dependency_overrides.

docs.title: Admin routes
docs.text:
The routes that change the running process need an admin role, checked by the identity.admin dependency:

  • POST /api/v1/datasources and DELETE /api/v1/datasources/{datasource_id}
  • The Connect routes GET /api/v1/datasource-types and POST /api/v1/datasources/test
  • PUT and PATCH /api/v1/settings/llm and the /api/v1/api-keys routes
  • Every /api/v1/evals route, POST /api/v1/jobs/eval and POST /api/v1/jobs/demo
  • POST /api/v1/jobs/index, POST /api/v1/jobs/profile, DELETE /api/v1/index and GET /api/v1/index/check
  • POST /api/v1/knowledge/reload and every /api/v1/proposals route
Key Default Meaning policies.admin_roles [admin] The roles that may call the admin routes.

A caller whose roles include one in policies.admin_roles is let through; one with roles but none of them admin is HTTP 403; one with no identity is HTTP 401. The check uses admin_roles alone, so policies.allow_all does not make a caller an admin.

The read-only routes (/health, /ready, /meta, GET /datasources, GET /llm, which never returns API keys, and GET /index) need no role.

# The proxy sets X-NL2SQL-Roles; only "ops" may change datasources and the index.
# api.yaml
auth: proxy
# policies.yaml (with the roles)
admin_roles: [ops]

docs.title: Saved answers
docs.text:
A person's own record of "this answered my question": the typed plan behind a chat answer, run again on request. It is the REST face of engine.answers; Code: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/answers.py.

A saved answer belongs to its owner alone. Another caller's answer is a 404 ANSWER_NOT_FOUND, an admin's call included, and no route acts as the in-process operator. On the hosted demo the owner is the visitor.

Route Does POST /api/v1/answers Body {trace_id, conversation_id, step: {turn?, step}, note?}. 200 with a SaveReport: {answer, proposed, proposal_id, not_proposed_reason}. The plan is read from the stored step. Saving the same run again returns the same answer. GET /api/v1/answers The caller's SavedAnswer list, newest first. Optional datasource_id. GET /api/v1/answers/{id} One SavedAnswer: id, question, datasource_id, plan, chart, created_at, trace_id. DELETE /api/v1/answers/{id} 204. POST /api/v1/answers/{id}/run Optional body {approval_ids}. A QueryResult, run again as the caller (their data scope, hooks and approvals apply). No model call, so it works with no key. A plan the schema has outgrown is a result with status: "error" whose first error is coded TILE_NEEDS_FIXING.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Status Code When 404 ANSWER_NOT_FOUND No such answer, or not the caller's. 409 ANSWER_LIMIT_REACHED The caller is at answers.max_per_user (default 100). 422 NOT_SAVABLE The step did not answer, kept no plan, or is not the run named. 409 CONFLICT Two saves by the same owner raced; the second can try again at once. 422 INVALID_REQUEST A body that does not validate.

See Errors for the envelope.

docs.title: Approvals API
docs.text:
When a hook holds a run for approval, the run ends with status: "error", an approvals_needed entry, and a stored request. An approver (a caller holding one of the roles the hook names) grants or denies it; the asker then re-asks the same question with approval_ids. Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/approvals.py.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Asker
    participant API
    participant Approver
    Asker->>API: POST /query
    API-->>Asker: error, approvals_needed
    Approver->>API: GET /approvals
    Approver->>API: POST /approvals/{id}/grant
    Asker->>API: POST /query with approval_ids
    API-->>Asker: the answer

docs.title: GET /api/v1/approvals
docs.text: The requests the caller asked, plus those their roles may decide. status (pending by default, granted or denied; anything else is a 422) filters them. Each is an ApprovalRecord: the request (its question, sql, reason, hook and the approver_roles who may decide), its status, and when and by whom it was decided. Who granted it, with the roles they held, is the engine's record and is not returned. Each record also has own: true when the caller asked it (same tenant, same user_id), set by the server so a page never compares ids; grant and deny return it the same way. own says nothing about who may decide: the engine answers that on the call.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/approvals/{request_id}/grant
docs.text: Grant the request, as the caller. A caller holding none of the approver roles gets 403 FORBIDDEN; an unknown id, or another tenant's request, is a 404. Returns the updated ApprovalRecord.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/approvals/{request_id}/deny
docs.text: Deny it. The optional body {"reason": "..."} is kept on the record. Same 403 and 404 as grant.

docs.title: Retrying
docs.text: POST /api/v1/query with {"question": ..., "approval_ids": ["<request_id>"]}, the same question, as the same asker. An id that is unknown, pending, denied, or another asker's ends the run with an APPROVAL_NOT_GRANTED error in the result (HTTP 200, status: "error"), and the pipeline does not run. See the query API.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: packages/api/tests/test_approvals_routes.py covers the list scoping, a grant by an approver and the asker's retry, the APPROVAL_NOT_GRANTED ending, a denial with and without a reason, and the 403 and 404 cases, over the real facade.

docs.title: Conversations API
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/conversations.py, models/conversations.py, sse.py, overrides.py.

A thin layer over engine.conversations and engine.chat_tools: each handler passes the caller as user_context= and serves the facade's own models (Conversation, ConversationInfo, Turn, ChatToolInfo; see Conversations). The model decides what a turn does, so there is one turns route. A conversation is the caller's own: another user's is a 404.

Route Does POST /api/v1/conversations Start one, 201 with the Conversation. Body {datasource_id?, dashboard_id?}; with dashboard_id the chat edits that dashboard (404 if it is not the caller's) GET /api/v1/conversations The caller's conversations, newest first (limit, 1 to 100, default 20), as ConversationInfo[] GET /api/v1/conversations/{id} The Conversation: its turns and, when the last turn asked one, the pending clarification DELETE /api/v1/conversations/{id} Delete it, 204 POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/turns One turn, the stored Turn POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/turns/stream The same turn as Server-Sent Events POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/retry Run the last question again as a turn of kind retry POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/tools/{name} Run one chat tool as a turn of kind tool, with no model call GET /api/v1/conversations/{id}/report The answered questions as Markdown (turns numbers, title) GET /api/v1/chat-tools The enabled chat tools: name, description and the JSON Schema of their arguments (ask is not listed)

docs.title: Bodies
docs.text:
Every body is strict: an unknown field is a 422.

Body Fields TurnRequest text or choice (exactly one), execute (default true) RetryRequest (optional) approval_ids: the granted request ids after a needs_approval turn, passed straight to the facade ToolRequest (optional) args: the tool's arguments, validated by its args_model

A pipeline outcome is not an error. A turn's status is answered, needs_clarification (answer it with choice in the next turn), needs_approval, stopped or error. A tool that is not enabled is a stored step with an error code, not an error status.

docs.title: Statuses
docs.text:
Status When 404 The conversation is not the caller's, or does not exist; on retry, also an id in approval_ids that is unknown, waiting, denied or expired (ApprovalNotFound) 409 The conversation is already running a turn (ConversationBusy) 422 The body does not validate, or the facade refused an argument (INVALID_ARGUMENT: blank text, a choice that is not an option, nothing to retry, bad tool arguments, a report with nothing answered; CONVERSATION_TOO_LONG at max_turns)

All use the error envelope. The turn routes also take the X-NL2SQL-* key and model headers (Jobs); they apply to the whole turn.

docs.title: The stream
docs.text:
POST .../turns/stream sends the run events of each question the model asks, a conversation.step after each step, and conversation.turn last, whose data.stored is the stored Turn. A : keep-alive comment is sent every 15 seconds. A refusal (not the caller's, a bad body, a busy conversation) answers with the envelope and its status before the stream begins; once it has, a failure is one last run.failed event: a named engine error keeps its error_code and message, any other is UNKNOWN_ERROR with a fixed message, never the exception text.

Closing the connection cancels the turn and stores nothing. A step that is running finishes first, so the turn ends when the step in flight returns.

docs.title: Dashboards and workspaces API
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/dashboards.py, routes/workspaces.py, models/dashboards.py and the generate job in routes/jobs.py.

These routes are thin over engine.dashboards and engine.workspaces (see Dashboards): each handler passes the request's caller and calls one named method, and none calls a model. A dashboard is built as a draft in chat (dashboard_edit) and saved whole by pin; a workspace is a named group of the caller's own dashboards. Both are private to their owner: another caller's dashboard or workspace is a 404, the same answer as one that does not exist. A request body is strict: an unknown field is a 422. Responses are the engine's own models (Dashboard, DashboardView, DashboardRun, Workspace), served as they are.

There is no route that edits what data a chart shows (add_tile, replace_plan) and none that shares a dashboard: those exist only in chat, and dashboards stay private.

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text:
Route Does GET /api/v1/dashboards The caller's dashboards, newest first. Query workspace_id and status (saved, the default, or draft). Returns DashboardInfo[]. GET /api/v1/dashboards/{id} Opens one: a DashboardView with the stored TileRuns, refreshed_at and due. It only reads. Nothing is refreshed and no query runs; call the refresh route for the charts in due. A chart the caller can no longer read is denied, one whose plan no longer validates is needs_fixing, both with no rows. POST /api/v1/dashboards/{id}/refresh Re-runs the stored plans as the caller. Body {tile_id?, filters?, approval_ids?}, all optional. tile_id limits it to one chart; filters maps a filter id to its values and the result is returned, never stored; approval_ids are request ids of approvals granted through /approvals. Returns a DashboardRun. Synchronous: it makes no model call. A dashboard someone else is refreshing is a 409; an id in approval_ids that is unknown, waiting, denied or expired is a 404 and nothing runs. GET /api/v1/dashboards/{id}/filters/{filter_id}/values The distinct values of an in filter's column, or [min, max] of a between one, as the caller may read them. Query limit (1 to 1,000, default 100). Returns a list. PUT /api/v1/dashboards/{id}/title Body {title}. Returns the Dashboard. PUT /api/v1/dashboards/{id}/tiles/{tile_id}/title Body {title}. PUT /api/v1/dashboards/{id}/tiles/{tile_id}/chart Body {chart}: auto, line, bar, big_number or table. A kind the chart's last result cannot be drawn as is a 422 CHART_NOT_SUPPORTED naming the kinds it can. DELETE /api/v1/dashboards/{id}/tiles/{tile_id} Removes the chart and its stored result: how a needs_fixing chart is taken off. PUT /api/v1/dashboards/{id}/layout Body {arrangements: [{tile_id, x, y, w, h}]} on the 4-column grid (x + w at most 4). PUT /api/v1/dashboards/{id}/filters Body {filters: [{id, label, column, kind, op}]}, op being in or between. PUT /api/v1/dashboards/{id}/schedule Body {every_minutes}; null stops the schedule (the field is required). Below dashboards.min_refresh_minutes is a 422 SCHEDULE_TOO_FREQUENT. POST /api/v1/dashboards/{id}/pin Saves a draft whole. Optional body {workspace_id?, title?}; without a workspace, the one the draft is in, else "General". A saved dashboard or an empty draft is a 422 NOT_PINNABLE. POST /api/v1/dashboards/{id}/move Body {workspace_id}: one of the caller's workspaces. DELETE /api/v1/dashboards/{id} Deletes it, its stored results and its schedule. 204.

Every edit returns the updated Dashboard. An edit or refresh of a dashboard that is being refreshed is a 409 CONFLICT.

docs.title: Generate a starter dashboard
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/jobs/dashboard is a job: it answers 202 with the queued Job. Body:

{"datasource_id": "chinook", "title": "Sales", "workspace_id": "w1", "max_tiles": 8}

Only datasource_id is required. The runner calls engine.dashboards.generate as the caller (no model is called), so only the tables and columns the caller can read are charted. progress has one step per chart (tile 3 of 8), the job can be cancelled between charts, and result is {dashboard, run}: the saved Dashboard and its first DashboardRun. Any caller may start one, and the dashboard is theirs. No index is a 422 NOT_INDEXED and a datasource with nothing to chart a 422 NO_TILES, both as the job's error.

docs.title: Build a dashboard from chosen tiles
docs.text:
The guided builder is three calls. None runs a tile; the job does.

GET /api/v1/dashboard-builder/options?datasource_id=chinook returns what the caller may tick, with no model call:

{"curated": [{"id": "v_revenue", "question": "Revenue by month?", "datasource_id": "chinook"}],
 "saved": [{"id": "a1", "question": "Top countries?", "datasource_id": "chinook"}],
 "metrics": [{"term": "revenue", "columns": ["chinook.main.invoices.total"], "definition": null}],
 "dimensions": [{"label": "Country", "column": "chinook.main.customers.country", "table": "customers"}],
 "time_columns": [{"label": "Invoice date", "column": "chinook.main.invoices.date", "table": "invoices"}],
 "ranges": [{"id": "last_30_days", "label": "last 30 days"}]}

POST /api/v1/dashboard-builder/proposals takes the chips and returns the tiles to tick (a 200 list of TileProposal: source, ref, question, title, chart, ticked). Only datasource_id and sources (one or more of curated, saved, asked) are required; the rest default to empty:

{"datasource_id": "chinook", "sources": ["curated", "saved", "asked"], "curated_ids": ["v_revenue"],
 "saved_ids": ["a1"], "metrics": ["revenue"], "dimensions": ["chinook.main.customers.country"],
 "time_range": "last_30_days", "text": "by country"}

Curated and saved ids become tiles with no model call. asked makes one model call and needs a key: the server's, or one sent in headers as for POST /query; without one it is a 422 MISSING_PROVIDER_KEY, and the hosted keyless demo refuses it the same way. Nothing is saved.

POST /api/v1/jobs/dashboard-build is a job (202, the queued Job). Body: datasource_id and tiles (the reviewed TileProposal list, unticked ones may be left out) are required; title, workspace_id and time_column (from the options; adds a date filter) are optional. progress has one step per tile (tile 2 of 5), the job can be cancelled between tiles (nothing is saved), and result is a BuildReport: {dashboard, built, skipped}, where skipped lists {question, code, message} for tiles that could not be built. A tile limit overflow is a 422 INVALID_ARGUMENT, and nothing buildable a NO_TILES error, both as the job's error. Only the owner reads the job's result. Request keys are passed to the build as to a question.

docs.title: Starter questions
docs.text: GET /api/v1/datasources/{id}/starter-questions?n=5 returns the questions of the first n charts the starter dashboard would build, as the caller may read the datasource, without running or saving anything. The list is empty when the caller reaches no table; a datasource with no index (or one the caller cannot reach) is a 422 NOT_INDEXED. It needs a caller: no identity is a 401.

docs.title: Workspaces
docs.text: Route Does GET /api/v1/workspaces The caller's workspaces, oldest first. POST /api/v1/workspaces Body {name}. 201 with the Workspace. Names are unique per owner, ignoring case. PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/name Body {name}. DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{id} An empty workspace only; one that still holds dashboards is a 422 WORKSPACE_NOT_EMPTY. 204.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Status When 404 NOT_FOUND No such dashboard or workspace, or one that belongs to someone else; on refresh, also an unknown, waiting, denied or expired approval id. 409 CONFLICT The dashboard is being refreshed or edited. 422 NOT_PINNABLE, CHART_NOT_SUPPORTED, UNKNOWN_TILE, UNKNOWN_FILTER, SCHEDULE_TOO_FREQUENT, WORKSPACE_NOT_EMPTY, NOT_INDEXED, NO_TILES, MISSING_PROVIDER_KEY, INVALID_ARGUMENT, or INVALID_REQUEST for a body that does not validate.

See Errors for the envelope.

docs.title: Request/Response Models
docs.text: Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/models/datasources.py

docs.title: DatasourceTestRequest
docs.text:
field type required meaning config Dict[str, Any] yes One datasource, in the shape of a datasources entry of nl2sql.yaml: id, type, connection, and optionally description, limits, preferred_tables, sample_questions, required. See Datasources.

A key the model does not know is an error, so a typo is found, not ignored. The body never carries the caller.

docs.title: DatasourceRequest
docs.text:
DatasourceTestRequest and:

field type required meaning save bool no Also write the datasource to datasources/<id>.yaml (default false).

docs.title: DatasourceResponse
docs.text: field type required meaning success bool yes Operation status. message str yes Result message. datasource_id Optional[str] no Datasource ID. file Optional[str] no With save, the file written, relative to the project (datasources/sales.yaml).

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: The three Connect routes (GET /datasource-types, POST /datasources/test, POST /datasources) are what a Connect a database form calls, in that order. They are admin only and are thin over engine.datasources.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/datasource-types
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/datasources.py

Admin only: see Admin routes.

Response: {"types": [...]}, engine.datasources.types(): every adapter the engine can name, installed or not, sorted by name, each with name, title, installed, install_hint (what to install when a driver is missing) and connection_schema, the JSON Schema of its connection model. A secret field is "format": "password", "writeOnly": true; a field in the advanced group carries "group": "advanced".

docs.title: POST /api/v1/datasources/test
docs.text:
Request model: DatasourceTestRequest

Admin only: see Admin routes.

Execution flow: - Validates config as a Datasource and delegates to engine.datasources.test(datasource): the adapter is built, its connection tested and closed. Nothing is registered, written or indexed.

Response: the status, {"id", "status", "required", "stage", "reason", "fix", "warnings"}. A failure is a 200 with status: "failed", the stage it failed at (config, driver, network, auth, database or permission), the reason and the fix. No value is echoed: the datasource's secret literals (a plugin's secret fields included) and every secret the engine knows are replaced by *** in the driver's words, and only those exact values: a validation message such as connection.password: Field required stays readable.

Errors: - A body that does not validate -> HTTP 422, as for POST /api/v1/datasources.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/datasources
docs.text:
Request model: DatasourceRequest

Response model: DatasourceResponse

Admin only: see Admin routes.

Execution flow: - Validates config as a Datasource and delegates to engine.datasources.add(...): the adapter is built (not connected) and the datasource joins engine.config. Nothing is indexed. - With "save": true, then engine.datasources.save(id, by=caller, env_file=...) writes datasources/<id>.yaml beside nl2sql.yaml (see Saving a datasource). A secret is never written into the YAML. A reference (${env:VAR}, ${vault:path}) is written as it is. A literal is written to the .env beside nl2sql.yaml as ${env:NL2SQL_<ID>_<KEY>} only when api.auth is none, which answers only a request made straight to localhost (a Host that is not loopback, or an X-Forwarded-For, Forwarded or X-Real-IP header, is already a 403).
