Under any other api.auth a literal secret with save: true is a 422 that asks for a ${env:...} reference. If the save fails, the datasource is taken out again: nothing is left running that was not saved. The one exception is a read-only config (Docker's mounted config): 403 NOT_WRITABLE, and the datasource stays registered until the server restarts.

Errors: - Every error is the error envelope. No identity -> HTTP 401; a role not in policies.admin_roles -> HTTP 403. - A body that does not validate, a typo included -> HTTP 422 and error.details is a list of {"loc": ["config", "sampel_questions"], "msg": "Extra inputs are not permitted"}, one per problem, each naming its place in the body and never a value. That includes a body that is not a JSON object or not JSON at all ([{"loc": [""], "msg": "The body must be a JSON object."}], no input echoed), and a connection that does not validate against the adapter's model (config.connection.passwrd, config.connection.port). - A literal secret that cannot be written (SecretValueInConfig) or a connection the adapter rejects (ConnectionInvalid) -> HTTP 422 with the engine's message and fix. An id that is already taken, or two secrets that map to one environment variable, is the engine's own named error, with its status and code. - An unknown id on a /datasources/{id} route, or one the caller's scope hides -> HTTP 404 NOT_FOUND. - save found datasources/<id>.yaml changed on disk since the engine loaded it, or a new file that already exists -> HTTP 409; reload the engine and try again. - Any other failure -> HTTP 500 INTERNAL naming a request id. The exception, which can hold the connection string, is logged server-side under that id and never returned.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/datasources
docs.text: Response: a list of DatasourceInfo from engine.datasources.list(user_context=caller): the datasources the caller's scope reaches, each with id, type, description, status (ready, failed with a reason, or unchecked; the reason is the driver's text for an admin and a generic sentence for anyone else), capabilities, connection with every secret masked, and sample_questions. No role needed.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/datasources/{datasource_id}
docs.text: Response: one datasource, as the list shows it. An unknown id, or one the caller cannot reach -> HTTP 404.

docs.title: DELETE /api/v1/datasources/{datasource_id}
docs.text:
Admin only: see Admin routes.

Delegates to engine.datasources.remove(...): the datasource leaves routing and engine.config, and its connection pool is closed. Nothing is written to the config files, and its index entries stay until the next full index. Response: {"success": true, "message": "...", "datasource_id": "..."}. An unknown id -> HTTP 404.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/datasources/{datasource_id}/schema
docs.text: The tables and columns as the caller may see them: a table or column the caller's scope denies is left out. An unknown or hidden datasource -> HTTP 404.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/datasources/{datasource_id}/diagram
docs.text: The schema as a Mermaid erDiagram, as text/plain. Repeat the tables query parameter to draw those tables and the ones one relationship away; leave it out for the whole datasource (cut to the 30 with the most relationships). tables that match no table the caller may see -> HTTP 422 INVALID_ARGUMENT.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Every non-2xx response from nl2sql-api is one envelope (packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/errors.py):

{"error": {"code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": "No datasource 'sales'.", "fix": "List the datasources with GET /api/v1/datasources.",
           "details": [], "request_id": null}}
Field Meaning code A stable name: the facade exception's own code (APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND, DASHBOARD_BUSY, ...), or one of the API's own: UNAUTHENTICATED, FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, INVALID_REQUEST, INTERNAL. message One sentence a person can act on. fix What to do about it, when there is something to do. details 422 only: one {"loc": [...], "msg": "..."} per problem. A rejected value is never echoed, because it may be a password. request_id 500 only: the id the server logged the cause under.

Every response, error or not, carries the id in the X-Request-ID header.

docs.title: What becomes which status
docs.text:
• An NL2SQLError (the base of every named facade exception) is answered with its own status and code: for example NotAuthorized 403, ApprovalNotFound 404, DashboardBusy 409, InvalidArgument 422.
  • LockHeld (another save or run holds the same lease; it is not an NL2SQLError) is 409 CONFLICT, and the caller may retry.
  • A route or dependency that refuses on its own raises RequestRefused(status, code, message, fix=..., details=...), with a message it wrote.
  • A body or parameter that does not validate is 422 INVALID_REQUEST with details.
  • An unknown route is 404 NOT_FOUND; a wrong method is 405.
  • Anything else is 500 INTERNAL: "Something failed on the server. Request id: <id>". A built-in ValueError, KeyError, LookupError or PermissionError, or a pydantic ValidationError, is never mapped to a 4xx, because its text may hold a connection string. The exception is logged with the id.

In an OpenAPI route, declare the envelope with responses={404: ERROR_RESPONSE} (from nl2sql_api.errors), or use identity.AUTH_RESPONSES and identity.ADMIN_RESPONSES.

A conversation that is running a turn is a 409 (ConversationBusy); a refused conversation argument is a 422. POST /api/v1/query is the exception for a pipeline failure: it is 200 with the errors in QueryResult.errors.

docs.title: Evals API
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/evals.py, routes/jobs.py

Both routes below are admin only (see Admin routes): a report holds every role's cases, plans and SQL. Running the suites is a job, POST /api/v1/jobs/eval.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/evals/suites
docs.text: The suites evals.suites names, in order: {"name", "path", "cases", "approved"}, where path is as configured, cases is the number in the file and approved the number that run. An empty list when none is configured.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/evals/scorers
docs.text: The registered scorer names: the built-ins and every plugin's, as a list of strings.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/jobs/eval
docs.text:
Starts an eval run as a job. Body (all optional):

Field Meaning suites Suites to run, each by its file or its name as evals.suites lists it (GET /evals/suites). Every configured suite when left out. A name that is not configured is a 422: a caller never names a file. mode full (default), plans or retrieval. plans and retrieval call no model. cases Case ids or tags to run. max_cost_usd The cost cap for full.

full calls the server's model, never a caller's, so it needs a cap: max_cost_usd, else evals.max_cost_usd; with neither it is a 422. Answers 202 with the queued Job; progress is one step per case (case <id>); the result is an EvalReport.

docs.title: Traces and feedback API
docs.text: A run's trace, a rating of its answer, and a correction that becomes a proposal for a verified query. All three act on a run the caller asked: another caller's run is a 404, and feedback/correct is always checked as the caller (the route never takes the trusted in-process operator path the CLI has). Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/query.py.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/traces/{trace_id}
docs.text: The run's trace document: its request, every node's input and output, and the result. An unknown trace, another caller's, or an id that is not a plain token is a 404. The operator's settings block is left out, and llm.configured keeps only each agent's provider, model and temperature (no endpoint or header names). When a hook withheld the run's results (answer.after denied them, or they were never released) the trace also has none of their rows (rows, terminal_results) and none of its LLM calls' prompts or answers, which carry preview rows; the asker reads those rows only through the results routes, which refuse such a run.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/feedback
docs.text: Body {"trace_id", "rating": "up" | "down", "note"?}. The question, SQL and answer are read from the run's trace, never the body. Returns the stored rating. An unknown or another caller's run is a 404; a bad rating, a trace_id that is not a plain token (letters, digits, -, _), or an unknown body field, is a 422.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/feedback/correct
docs.text:
Body {"trace_id", "sql" | "plan", "question"?, "note"?} with exactly one of sql and plan. Returns a Proposal for a verified query (origin: "correction"); nothing is saved until a reviewer accepts it.

status code when 404 NOT_FOUND no such run for this caller 422 INVALID_REQUEST a trace_id that is not a plain token, or not exactly one of sql and plan 422 CORRECTION_REFUSED the fix is not read-only, reads what the caller may not, fails validation, or a hook denies it; details is one {code, msg} per reason

docs.title: GET /api/v1/feedback
docs.text: Every rating, newest first (limit caps it). Admin only: it spans all callers.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: packages/api/tests/test_feedback_routes.py, over the real facade with a run of one caller read by another: the trace, the rating, the correction and its refusals, that as_operator is never passed, and that another caller's run can neither be rated nor corrected.

docs.title: Health API
docs.text: Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/health.py. /health and /ready need no caller, nor does /meta (a caller adds fields), and /about needs one.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/health
docs.text: Liveness. Returns {"status": "ok", "version": {"engine": "<nl2sql-engine>", "api": "<nl2sql-api>"}}.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/ready
docs.text: Readiness, from the engine's own check() (kept for 10 seconds, so a poll every few seconds does not connect to every datasource each time). Ready means every required datasource and at least one datasource is up, every agent's key resolves (unless api.request_llm is on, or every agent is on the replay provider) and the index is ok or stale. 200 {"status": "ready"} or 503 {"status": "not_ready"}, to everyone. A caller who is an admin also gets problems: each failing datasource and its stage, each agent whose key does not resolve and the index status, never a secret. The API starts even when a required datasource cannot connect; this route says so.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/meta
docs.text: Without a caller: {"mode": "demo" | "your_data" | "hosted", "auth": "api_keys" | "proxy" | "static" | "none", "request_llm": false, "start": "choose" | "hosted" | null}, what a page needs before it has an identity. start tells the web app which start screen to show: choose when the project has no datasource yet and the caller is an administrator (try the demo or connect a database; anyone else gets null, so the route does not tell them the project is empty), hosted on the hosted demo, and null once a datasource exists. With a caller, also datasources, each one the caller may reach as {id, description, sample_questions, recorded} (recorded is the sample questions the replay provider can answer with no key), and recorded_with, the provider and model those recordings came from, or null. It also names the caller as caller: {"user_id": "...", "admin": true | false}. admin is whether the caller holds a role in policies.admin_roles, which is the check every admin route makes. user_id is the key's owner under api_keys, the proxy's user header under proxy, static under static and local under none; on the hosted demo it is visitor- and a one-way hash of the session cookie, never the cookie itself. Nothing else about the caller (roles, tenant) or any other user is returned, and whether the caller may approve a request is not here: each hook names its own approvers, so the approvals routes decide.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/about
docs.text: engine.about(): the engine version and its pipeline steps. Needs a caller.

docs.title: Indexing API
docs.text: Indexing a datasource is a job: it outlives its request. The routes here read the index, clear it, check it for drift and inspect retrieval. DELETE /api/v1/index and GET /api/v1/index/check are admin only (see Admin routes); GET /api/v1/index and the inspector are open to any caller, and GET /api/v1/index is scoped to the caller: an admin sees the whole report; anyone else sees only the datasources their roles reach, a failed one by name without the driver's text, and no warning that names a table.

docs.title: Start an index build
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/jobs/index (admin, 202). Body: {"datasource_ids": ["chinook"]}; leave datasource_ids out to index every configured datasource. Unknown keys are a 422.

It delegates to engine.index.build(datasource_ids, on_datasource=..., cancellation_token=...): the new entries are written beside the live ones and switched in when all are written. No model is called: a build embeds the schema, the glossary and the verified queries. Progress is one step per datasource (done of total); a datasource that failed is the step <id> (failed) and keeps its previous entries. Its reason goes to the server log, never the job.

The job's result (owner only) is {"ok": bool, "stats": [...], "empty": [...], "failed": ["<id>", ...]}.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/index
docs.text:
engine.index.health(user_context=...) (see Indexing API), the report the index panel shows.

{
  "status": "ok",
  "total": 162,
  "counts": {"schema.column": 121, "schema.table": 20},
  "built_at": "2026-09-22T12:35:42+00:00",
  "embedding_model": "local/all-MiniLM-L6-v2",
  "namespace": "nl2sql__local-all-minilm-l6-v2__384",
  "datasources": [
    {"datasource_id": "chinook", "entries": 87, "index_version": "20260922123542_ceed8",
     "built_at": "2026-09-22T12:35:42+00:00"}
  ],
  "problems": []
}

status is ok, empty, stale (a datasource has no live build, or its build's snapshot is gone) or missing (the configured embedding model has no index yet); problems says what is wrong and how to fix it.

docs.title: DELETE /api/v1/index
docs.text: Admin. engine.index.clear(); answers {"success": true, "message": "..."}.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/index/check
docs.text: Admin. engine.index.check(datasource_ids, user_context=caller) compares each datasource's live schema with what was indexed. Repeat datasource_id to name some; leave it out for every datasource. Response: a list of DriftReport (datasource_id, status, live_version, checked_at and what changed). An unknown datasource is a HTTP 404.

docs.title: The retrieval inspector
docs.text: GET /api/v1/index/inspect returns the defaults (k, lambda_mult, fetch_multiplier, types). POST /api/v1/index/inspect takes {"query": "...", "k": 8, "lambda_mult": null, "types": null, "datasource_id": null} (query required, k at least 1, unknown keys a 422) and returns the candidate pool, the picks and what was dropped, for the caller's scope.

docs.title: Jobs API
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/jobs.py, jobs.py, sse.py, overrides.py.

A job is one facade call (an index build, a profile, an eval, a dashboard) that outlives its request. One worker thread in the server takes jobs in submission order, so two index builds never race on the index. The last 100 jobs are kept in memory; a restart loses them, and what they produced (an index, proposals, a dashboard) stays in the engine's stores. nl2sql-api serve therefore runs one Uvicorn worker and has no --workers option.

A caller with a job queued or running gets a 409 naming it when it starts another, so one caller cannot stall the queue. Another user's job is a 404; an admin sees every caller's jobs, but never their result: it can hold rows read under the owner's data scope, so it is the owner's alone (in GET /jobs, GET /jobs/{id}, DELETE /jobs/{id} and the job.finished event an admin gets result: null).

docs.title: The Job
docs.text: Field Holds id 22 url-safe characters kind index, profile, eval, dashboard or demo status queued, running, succeeded, failed or cancelled params The request body that started it, typed per kind created_by The caller's user id created_at, started_at, finished_at Timestamps progress [{at, step, done, total}], one per item (a datasource, a case, a tile) result Typed per kind once succeeded: IndexResult, ProfileReport[], EvalReport or {dashboard, run}; null when the viewer is an admin looking at another caller's job error The error envelope's body once failed; never an exception's text

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Route Does GET /api/v1/jobs The caller's jobs, newest first GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id} One job DELETE /api/v1/jobs/{job_id} Cancel: a queued job is removed; a running one stops between items. Returns the job GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/events Progress as Server-Sent Events Route Starts POST /api/v1/jobs/dashboard A starter dashboard for one datasource, as the caller; any caller. See Dashboards. POST /api/v1/jobs/dashboard-build A dashboard from the guided builder's ticked tiles, as the caller; any caller. See Dashboards. POST /api/v1/jobs/index Build the index for datasource_ids (every datasource when left out); admin. Progress is one step per datasource, <id> (failed) for one that failed; the result is {ok, stats, empty, failed}. See Indexing. POST /api/v1/jobs/profile Profile datasource_ids into proposals (draft, max_cost_usd), on the server's key only; admin. The result is a list of profile reports. See Knowledge.

| POST /api/v1/jobs/eval | Run the configured eval suites (suites, mode, cases, max_cost_usd), on the server's model; admin. mode: full needs a cost cap. Progress is one step per case (case <id>); the result is an EvalReport. See Evals. | | POST /api/v1/jobs/demo | Add the sample databases, their verified queries and the demo glossary, then index them (engine.add_demo()), as the caller; admin. Progress is one step per datasource; the result is an IndexResult. No body. |

Each POST /api/v1/jobs/<kind> answers 202 with the queued Job and a 409 when the caller already has a job queued or running.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
GET /jobs/{id}/events sends one job.progress event (a JobProgress as data) for every step so far, then for each new one, then job.finished (the whole Job) and closes. A : keep-alive comment is sent every 15 seconds. The wire is the one every stream uses:

event: job.progress
data: {"at": "...", "step": "chinook", "done": 1, "total": 3}

event: job.finished
data: {...the Job...}

The stream waits without holding a thread.

docs.title: Per-request keys and models
docs.text: Where api.request_llm: true, a request may carry X-NL2SQL-Api-Key-<provider> (one provider's key per header) and X-NL2SQL-Models ({"ast_planner": "anthropic:claude-opus-5"}, no secret). They become the engine's LLMOverride. With request_llm off they are a 403. A model on a provider the same request sent no key for is a 422 MISSING_PROVIDER_KEY, even when the server holds that provider's key. A key is never logged or echoed.

docs.title: Knowledge API
docs.text: What the engine knows about each datasource, and the proposals that change it. Thin over engine.knowledge and engine.proposals; reads pass the caller, so a datasource the caller's scope hides is a 404. Every /proposals route is admin only (a proposal can name a table the caller's scope hides, and accepting one writes a file); see Admin routes. Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/knowledge.py.

docs.title: Knowledge
docs.text: Route Does GET /api/v1/knowledge The merged knowledge per datasource the caller may see (datasource_id narrows it): each item with where it came from, and the problems (names that do not resolve, joins whose types cannot be compared). GET /api/v1/knowledge/sources Each knowledge source (yaml, ...): counts per datasource, checksum, load time, last reload error. POST /api/v1/knowledge/reload Admin. Load every source again and swap atomically; a failing source keeps its previous knowledge and says why in error. POST /api/v1/knowledge/choices Body {"choice": <ClarificationChoice>, "term": null}. Files the caller's clarification pick as a term proposal and returns it; nothing changes until an admin accepts.

docs.title: Proposals
docs.text:
Route Does GET /api/v1/proposals Newest first. Filters kind, status (default proposed), datasource_id, limit (1 to 500). GET /api/v1/proposals/{proposal_id} One proposal. POST /api/v1/proposals/accept Body {"ids": [...], "edits": {"<id>": {...fields merged over the change}}}. Writes each file once; returns AcceptReport (accepted, files_written, warnings, refused by id). POST /api/v1/proposals/reject Body {"ids": [...], "reason": "..."}. A rejected change is never proposed again. POST /api/v1/proposals/examples Body {"datasource_id": "...", "questions": [...]}. Files each question as an example proposal.

Unknown keys in a body are a 422. Errors are the error envelope: an unknown proposal is 404 NOT_FOUND, a file that changed on disk is 409 FILE_CHANGED, a config with no writable knowledge file is 403 NOT_WRITABLE.

docs.title: Start a profile
docs.text: POST /api/v1/jobs/profile (admin, 202). Body: {"datasource_ids": null, "draft": false, "max_cost_usd": null} (max_cost_usd above 0; unknown keys a 422). It runs engine.knowledge.profile(...) as a job, one step per datasource, and files what it finds as proposals. It always uses the server's key: a key typed in a browser never pays for drafts. The job's result (owner only) is a list of profile reports.

docs.title: Request/Response Models
docs.text: Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/models/query.py

docs.title: QueryRequest
docs.text:
field type required meaning question str yes The question. (It was natural_language; that name is now a 422.) datasource_id Optional[str] no Datasource override. execute bool no Execute SQL against datasource (default true). choice Optional[ClarificationChoice] no The option picked from an earlier clarification_request: send {"request_id", "option_id"} with the same question to answer it. approval_ids List[str] no Ids of approvals an approver granted, from an earlier run a hook held. choice and approval_ids together are a 422 CLARIFICATION_INVALID, before the engine is called.

The body is strict: a field it does not name is a 422, so a misspelt or removed field is never silently ignored.

docs.title: SubQueryResult
docs.text:
The engine's own nl2sql.SubQueryResult, served as is.

field type required meaning id str no Sub-query identifier. intent str no Semantic intent of the sub-query. sql str no SQL generated for the sub-query. datasource_id str no Datasource the sub-query targets. schema_version str no Schema version used for planning. plan Optional[Dict[str, Any]] no The validated plan, dumped. validation List[ValidationCheck] no Validation checks (name, passed, message). rows Optional[RowSample] no Capped row sample (columns, rows, total_rows). status str no "success" or "error" for this sub-query, from its final attempt: "success" when it ended with SQL and, if executed, a result; otherwise "error". A retry that recovers reports "success". "dropped" when a hook denied it with scope="sub_query": the run went on without it. retry_count int no Plan/SQL refinement attempts made. plan_source "llm" \| "cache" \| "verified" \| "supplied" \| "approved" \| "chosen" no "cache" when the plan came from the plan cache (no planner call; still validated and executed), "verified" when a verified query answered (there is no plan; sql is the verified query's own, with its :name placeholders), "supplied" or "approved" for a pinned plan (see Query API → Running a plan you hold), otherwise "llm". row_cap Optional[int] no The row limit that bounded this sub-query's SQL, or null when the plan's own LIMIT was smaller. truncated bool no True when the result reached row_cap, so rows may be missing.

docs.title: QueryResult
docs.text:
The engine's own nl2sql.QueryResult, served as is: the route's response_model is that class, so the HTTP response cannot drift from what the engine returns.

field type required meaning sub_queries List[SubQueryResult] no One entry per decomposed sub-query, each with its SQL. final_answer Optional[Dict[str, Any]] no Answer synthesizer payload (summary, format_type, content, warnings, truncated). errors List[Dict[str, Any]] no Pipeline errors (node, message, error_code, severity, provider, provider_response). provider and provider_response are set for a PROVIDER_* code and null otherwise; see provider failures. trace_id str no Trace identifier. reasoning List[Dict[str, Any]] no Reasoning events/logs. warnings List[RunWarning] no What the answer should say without failing the run: code, node, message, sub_query_id, detail. See Warnings. artifact_refs Dict[str, ArtifactRef] no Result artifact references keyed by execution node id. status str no "success", "error" or "plan_only" for the run. timings Dict[str, float] no Wall-clock seconds per graph node. usage QuestionUsage no LLM calls, input/cached/output/reasoning tokens and model time per node (nodes) and for the question (total), plus every call (calls) and the number of plans served from the plan cache (plan_cache_hits). The same model as QueryResult.usage; see the core query API. trace_path Optional[str] no Where the run's trace file was written on the server, or null. See Debugging a Run. truncated bool no True when any sub-query's result was cut at its row limit. result_manifest List[ResultSummary] no The run's saved results, one per terminal DAG node: node_id, columns, row_count (the whole result's), truncated (a sub-query feeding it was cut at its row limit) and column_kinds (each column's type category: number, text, temporal, boolean or other, read from the saved file's column types). Never the rows: read those with the two result routes below, result_id being the node_id. Empty when nothing was saved (execute: false, or the run failed before aggregation). source AnswerSource no Where the answer came from: {"type": "verified", "id", "datasource_id", "params"} when a verified query from curated.yaml answered, with the values it ran with; {"type": "generated"} (the other fields null) otherwise. The last event of POST /query/stream carries it too.

Only a capped sample of the rows is inlined, in sub_queries[].rows. The full result set is written to artifact storage and addressed through artifact_refs (uri, format, row_count, columns). The run's combined results are listed in result_manifest and read back, a page at a time or as CSV, with the results routes.

An errors[] entry for a key the provider rejected:

{
  "node": "datasource_resolver",
  "message": "OpenAI rejected the API key.",
  "error_code": "PROVIDER_AUTH_FAILED",
  "severity": "ERROR",
  "provider": "OpenAI",
  "provider_response": "HTTP 401 (invalid_api_key): Incorrect API key provided: [redacted key]. You can find your API key at https://platform.openai.com/account/api-keys."
}

Branch on error_code, show message, and keep provider_response for a "provider response" disclosure. The codes are listed under provider failures.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/query
docs.text:
Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/query.py

Request model: QueryRequest

Response model: QueryResult

Execution flow: - The identity.caller dependency supplies the caller's UserContext (see Identity); with no identity it answers HTTP 401 before the engine runs. - Delegates to engine.run_query(...), which returns a QueryResult. - Returns that QueryResult unchanged; there is no field mapping.

The handler is declared with def, not async def: the pipeline performs blocking LLM and database calls, so Starlette runs it in its threadpool instead of on the event loop.

Keys and models in the request: where api.request_llm is on, a request may send X-NL2SQL-Api-Key-<provider> headers (one provider's key each) and X-NL2SQL-Models (a JSON object of agent name to "provider:model", no secret) for this run only. A model is honoured only on a provider the same request sent a key for, so it can never move a step onto the operator's account, even if the server has a key for it (422 MISSING_PROVIDER_KEY). With request_llm off the headers are a 403. A key is never logged, stored in a trace or echoed in a response. The stream route takes the same headers.

Errors: - Pipeline failures are a normal HTTP 200 carrying errors; they are not HTTP failures. - Genuinely unexpected failures return HTTP 500 with a generic detail; the traceback is logged server-side rather than returned to the client. - No role for the request returns HTTP 401 with a message naming the settings. - An invalid request body returns HTTP 422 (FastAPI validation).

Example response:

{

    {
      "id": "sq-1",
      "intent": "top customers by revenue",

      "datasource_id": "warehouse",

    "format_type": "text",

    "warnings": [],
    "truncated": false
  },
  "errors": [],

  "reasoning": [],
  "warnings": [],
  "artifact_refs": {

  },

(Illustrative numbers. usage.calls is shortened to one entry; a real response lists all three.)

docs.title: POST /api/v1/query/stream
docs.text:
The same run as POST /api/v1/query, reported as it happens, as Server-Sent Events (Content-Type: text/event-stream). The request body, the caller role and the 401 are exactly those of /query. Delegates to engine.stream_query(...) (see the core query API).

The events are the engine's own run events (Events), from the caller-safe allow-list. Each is an event: line naming it and one data: line holding the whole event as JSON: name, at (UTC), trace_id (the run's, its trace_id in the result routes), tenant_id and data. The table lists each event's data:

event data when run.started question, user_id, tenant_id, roles, datasource_id, execute The run began. Always first. node.started node, sub_query_id A pipeline step began. The SQL agent's steps (ast_planner, logical_validator, generator, executor) come once per sub-query, and again on a retry. node.finished node, sub_query_id, seconds, ok The step ended; ok is false when it raised. result.manifest results The aggregator saved the run's results. results is the result_manifest the final response will carry, so a client can start paging the rows (with the event's trace_id) before the answer is written. answer.delta field, text The next piece of the answer's summary or content, as the answer model writes it. Joined in order, the pieces of a field are that field of final_answer. sanity.flagged, run.limit_reached see Events A sanity check's finding; a cost or call cap reached. run.finished the run's summary, plus result: the QueryResult The last event of a run that finished: result is exactly what /query returns for it. A refusal or a provider failure is a run.finished with status: "error", as /query returns it. run.failed message (a key in it is redacted), error_code; and user_id, roles when the engine ended the run The last event of a run that could not finish (an unexpected failure; the traceback is logged on the server).

Every stream ends in exactly one run.finished or one run.failed. Policy denials, hook decisions and model calls are never on it; they are an operator's, through engine.events.subscribe.

event: run.started
data: {"name": "run.started", "at": "2026-10-15T09:12:03.120Z", "trace_id": "0f1c...", "tenant_id": null, "data": {"question": "Who are the top 5 customers by revenue?", ...}}

event: node.started
data: {"name": "node.started", ..., "data": {"node": "datasource_resolver", "sub_query_id": null}}

event: node.finished
data: {"name": "node.finished", ..., "data": {"node": "datasource_resolver", "sub_query_id": null, "seconds": 0.41, "ok": true}}

...

event: result.manifest
data: {"name": "result.manifest", ..., "trace_id": "0f1c...", "data": {"results": [{"node_id": "sq_1", "columns": ["customer", "revenue"], "row_count": 5, "truncated": false, "column_kinds": {"customer": "text", "revenue": "number"}}]}}

event: answer.delta
data: {"name": "answer.delta", ..., "data": {"field": "summary", "text": "Acme leads "}}

...

event: run.finished
data: {"name": "run.finished", ..., "data": {"status": "success", "duration_s": 6.2, ..., "result": {"sub_queries": [...], "final_answer": {...}, "status": "success", ...}}}

curl -N -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/query/stream \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $NL2SQL_KEY" \
  -d '{"question": "Who are the top 5 customers by revenue?"}'

What streams token by token: only the answer. The answer model is asked to stream on this route (and on this route only; /query is unchanged), on both wires: OpenAI's (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) streams the answer's tool call as argument pieces, Anthropic's as input_json_delta pieces, and the engine reads summary and content out of them as they grow. How finely the text arrives is the provider's choice: a provider or a local server that sends the whole answer in one piece gives one answer.delta per field. The other model steps (resolver, decomposer, planner, refiner) return a typed object the next step needs whole, so they are not streamed; their progress is their node.started and node.finished. A streamed answer reports the same token usage as an unstreamed one (stream_options.include_usage is sent on the OpenAI wire).

The route answers Cache-Control: no-cache and X-Accel-Buffering: no, so a proxy passes each event on as it comes. Closing the connection cancels the run before its next step or model call.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: packages/api/tests/test_query_routes.py, test_query_stream_route.py and test_query_response_shape.py cover these routes with FastAPI's TestClient, a stubbed engine (get_engine override) and a stubbed caller, so no datasource, LLM or network access is required. packages/api/tests/test_identity.py covers the identity sources and the 401. packages/nl2sql/tests/e2e/test_stream_fake_llm.py streams a question on the demo databases through the stream route with no key. The results, traces, feedback and approvals routes have their own pages and test files.

docs.title: Results API
docs.text:
The rows of a run, read after the fact. A run's result_manifest (in the /query response, and in the stream's result.manifest event) names its saved results; these routes list them, page through them, download them and draw them. trace_id is the run's trace_id; result_id is a node_id from the manifest.

Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/query.py

docs.title: ResultPage
docs.text: field type meaning request_id str The run's trace_id. result_id str The result's node_id from result_manifest. columns List[str] Column names, in row order. rows List[List[Any]] rows[i] is row offset + i of the result. offset int The first row returned, from 0. limit int The page size used, after the cap of 1,000. total_rows int Rows in the whole result. next_offset Optional[int] Where the next page starts, or null when this page reaches the end.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/results/{trace_id}
docs.text: The run's manifest: per result its node_id, columns, row_count, truncated, column_kinds and who asked (ResultManifest). Never rows.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/results/{trace_id}/{result_id}
docs.text:
One page of a run's saved result.

parameter in default meaning trace_id path The run's trace_id. result_id path A node_id from the run's result_manifest. offset query 0 First row, from 0. Negative is HTTP 422. limit query 100 Rows per page, at least 1 (else HTTP 422). Above 1,000 it is cut to 1,000; limit in the response says which.

Response model: ResultPage. Delegates to engine.results.page(...), which reads the rows lazily from the result's parquet artifact: only the slice asked for is read. A page past the end has no rows.

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $NL2SQL_KEY"   "http://localhost:8000/api/v1/results/0f1c.../combine_g1?offset=100&limit=100"

{"request_id": "0f1c...", "result_id": "combine_g1", "columns": ["customer", "revenue"],
 "rows": [["acme", 42], ["globex", 40]], "offset": 100, "limit": 100,
 "total_rows": 102, "next_offset": null}

docs.title: GET /api/v1/results/{trace_id}/{result_id}.csv
docs.text: The whole of a run's saved result as text/csv (UTF-8, header first), sent as an attachment named <trace_id>_<result_id>.csv. Delegates to engine.results.csv(...), which reads the parquet artifact a slice at a time and streams each slice out, so the result is never built in memory on the server.

docs.title: Errors and scope
docs.text:
• Both need a role, as /query does: no role is HTTP 401.
  • A run is readable only by the caller who asked it: the request's caller (from the auth settings) is passed to engine.results as user_context, and must match the run's recorded asker. Results are read from the engine's own tenant folder (TENANT_ID, the <tenant_id> of the artifact path) and nowhere else. An unknown trace_id, another user's run, a run of another tenant, a result_id the run's manifest does not list, and an id that is not a plain token (letters, digits, _ and -, so no /, . or ..) are all HTTP 404, so a caller cannot tell one from the other or reach a path outside the run's folder.
  • A caller with a user_id (an API key, or a proxy that sets the user header) reads only its own runs. A static caller has roles and no user_id, so its runs are anonymous: readable by any caller of the same tenant with the same roles, and by no caller with other roles: a viewer holding an admin run's trace id gets HTTP 404. See Who can read a run.
  • The request body never names the caller: user_context is not a field of POST /query.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/results/{trace_id}/{result_id}/chart
docs.text:
The chart the saved result is drawn as, chosen from its column kinds by five fixed rules with no model call (engine.results.chart(...)).

parameter in default meaning kind query rules choose Force line, bar, big_number or table. Anything else is a 422; a kind the data cannot draw is a 422 CHART_NOT_SUPPORTED (the engine's own code) naming the kinds it can. format query spec spec is the engine's ChartSpec (kind, encodings, the rows in data, a one-line reason, a takeaway). vega-lite is a Vega-Lite v5 document, rows inline and no colour set, ready to render. A table has no Vega-Lite form: format=vega-lite on one is a 422. 
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $NL2SQL_KEY"   "http://localhost:8000/api/v1/results/0f1c.../combine_g1/chart?format=vega-lite"

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: packages/api/tests/test_results_routes.py covers these routes over the real facade and a local artifact store: the manifest, paging, the cap, HTTP 422 for a bad offset, limit, kind or format, the chart and its Vega-Lite form, the complete CSV, HTTP 404 for unknown, foreign and crafted ids and for an anonymous run read with other roles, and HTTP 401 without a role.

docs.title: REST API routes
docs.text:
The nl2sql-api package serves the engine over HTTP with FastAPI. At startup it loads the .env next to nl2sql.yaml (never overriding a variable already set), builds one engine with NL2SQL.from_config() (NL2SQL_CONFIG, else ./nl2sql.yaml) and calls engine.check() before it accepts a request: a required datasource that cannot connect stops it from starting.

pip install nl2sql-api
cd nl2sql-demo                               # ./nl2sql.yaml is the config
nl2sql-api serve --port 8000        # 127.0.0.1, one worker
# or: NL2SQL_CONFIG=nl2sql-demo/nl2sql.yaml uvicorn nl2sql_api.main:app --port 8000

Its own settings are the api section of nl2sql.yaml, which the engine ignores:

# api.yaml (included from nl2sql.yaml as  api: { file: api.yaml })
auth: static                    # api_keys | proxy | static | none (default none)
static_role: admin              # one static role for every request
cors_origins: []                # browser origins allowed to call the API

Full interactive docs at http://localhost:8000/docs (Swagger UI), with ReDoc at /redoc and the schema at /openapi.json. Browser access from other origins is off unless listed in api.cors_origins.

api.auth picks who is asking, and the request body never carries the caller:

api.auth Identity api_keys Authorization: Bearer <key> from nl2sql keys create. proxy The user, tenant and roles headers of a proxy that connects from api.proxy.trusted_from. static api.static_role for every request. none (default) The local operator, for a request made straight to localhost only; nl2sql-api serve refuses to bind any other host.

With no identity the routes answer HTTP 401 (HTTP 403 under none for a request that is not the local operator). Every error is one envelope, {"error": {"code", "message", "fix", "details", "request_id"}}.

The routes that change the process (POST /api/v1/datasources, DELETE /api/v1/datasources/{id}, and the Connect routes GET /api/v1/datasource-types and POST /api/v1/datasources/test, PUT and PATCH /api/v1/settings/llm, the /api/v1/api-keys and /api/v1/evals routes, POST /api/v1/jobs/index, POST /api/v1/jobs/profile, POST /api/v1/jobs/eval, POST /api/v1/jobs/demo, DELETE /api/v1/index, GET /api/v1/index/check, POST /api/v1/knowledge/reload and every /proposals route) also need a role listed in policies.admin_roles (default [admin]), else HTTP 403.

Method Path Purpose POST /api/v1/query Ask a question; returns the plan, checks, SQL, a row sample, the result manifest, answer, errors and usage POST /api/v1/query/stream The same run as Server-Sent Events: each step as it starts and ends, the result manifest, the answer as it is written, then the /query response GET /api/v1/results/{trace_id}/{result_id} One page of a run's saved result (offset, limit up to 1,000) GET /api/v1/results/{trace_id}/{result_id}.csv The whole of a run's saved result as CSV, streamed GET /api/v1/results/{trace_id} The run's saved results: columns, row counts, never rows GET /api/v1/results/{trace_id}/{result_id}/chart The chart a result is drawn as (?format=vega-lite for a Vega-Lite v5 spec) GET /api/v1/traces/{trace_id} The trace of a run the caller asked POST /api/v1/feedback Rate a run the caller asked, up or down POST /api/v1/feedback/correct Turn the caller's fixed SQL or plan into a proposal for a verified query GET /api/v1/feedback Every rating, newest first (admin) GET /api/v1/approvals Approval requests the caller asked or may decide (status) POST /api/v1/approvals/{request_id}/grant Grant a request (an approver role) POST /api/v1/approvals/{request_id}/deny Deny a request, with an optional reason POST /api/v1/conversations Start a conversation GET /api/v1/conversations The caller's conversations, newest first GET /api/v1/conversations/{conversation_id} One conversation with its turns DELETE /api/v1/conversations/{conversation_id} Delete a conversation POST /api/v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/turns Send a message (text or a choice); returns the stored turn POST /api/v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/turns/stream The same turn as Server-Sent Events, ending with the stored turn or a run.failed frame POST /api/v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/retry Run the last question again, with approved request ids POST /api/v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/tools/{name} Run one chat tool with its arguments GET /api/v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/report The conversation as a Markdown report GET /api/v1/chat-tools The chat tools a conversation can use GET /api/v1/health Liveness check GET /api/v1/ready Readiness from the engine's check, kept 10 s: 200 ready or 503 not_ready (an admin also gets problems) GET /api/v1/meta The mode, the identity source and whether callers may send their own LLM; needs no caller. With a caller: the datasources, which questions are recorded, and recorded_with GET /api/v1/about What the engine is: version and pipeline steps GET /api/v1/events/catalog Every event the engine publishes, with its data's JSON Schema GET /api/v1/llm/providers The LLM providers: key present, verified models, the shape a key must have GET /api/v1/api-keys List API keys, revoked ones included, never a token (admin) POST /api/v1/api-keys Create a key for a user and roles; the token is returned once (admin, 201) DELETE /api/v1/api-keys/{key_id} Revoke a key (admin, 204) GET /api/v1/evals/suites The configured eval suites and their case counts (admin) GET /api/v1/evals/scorers The registered scorer names (admin) POST /api/v1/jobs/eval Start an eval run (admin, 202): suites, mode, cases; full needs a cost cap POST /api/v1/jobs/demo Start the demo job (admin, 202): add the sample databases and index them GET /api/v1/jobs The caller's background jobs, newest first (an admin sees all, without their results) GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id} One job: status, progress, result or error DELETE /api/v1/jobs/{job_id} Cancel a queued or running job GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/events A job's progress as Server-Sent Events, ending with job.finished POST /api/v1/jobs/dashboard Queue a job that builds the no-model starter dashboard for a datasource (202) POST /api/v1/jobs/dashboard-build Queue a job that builds a dashboard from the guided builder's ticked tiles (202) GET /api/v1/dashboard-builder/options The guided builder's chips for a datasource: curated queries, saved answers, metrics, dimensions, time ranges POST /api/v1/dashboard-builder/proposals The tiles to tick, from the chosen sources and chips; only asked calls a model POST /api/v1/answers Save the answer of a chat step as the caller's own, and propose it for review GET /api/v1/answers The caller's saved answers, optionally those of one datasource GET /api/v1/answers/{answer_id} One saved answer (another caller's is a 404) DELETE /api/v1/answers/{answer_id} Delete a saved answer (204) POST /api/v1/answers/{answer_id}/run Run a saved answer's plan again as the caller; no model call GET /api/v1/dashboards The caller's dashboards, saved or draft, optionally in one workspace GET /api/v1/dashboards/{dashboard_id} A dashboard and the stored results of its charts; reads only, runs no query DELETE /api/v1/dashboards/{dashboard_id} Delete a dashboard, its stored results and its schedule POST /api/v1/dashboards/{dashboard_id}/refresh Re-run the stored plans of one chart or all of them as the caller; no model call GET /api/v1/dashboards/{dashboard_id}/filters/{filter_id}/values The values a filter offers, as the caller may read them PUT /api/v1/dashboards/{dashboard_id}/title Rename a dashboard PUT /api/v1/dashboards/{dashboard_id}/tiles/{tile_id}/title Rename a chart PUT /api/v1/dashboards/{dashboard_id}/tiles/{tile_id}/chart Choose how a chart is drawn DELETE /api/v1/dashboards/{dashboard_id}/tiles/{tile_id} Remove a chart and its stored result PUT /api/v1/dashboards/{dashboard_id}/layout Place the charts on the 4-column grid PUT /api/v1/dashboards/{dashboard_id}/filters Store the filter definitions PUT /api/v1/dashboards/{dashboard_id}/schedule Set or stop the refresh schedule POST /api/v1/dashboards/{dashboard_id}/pin Save a draft whole into a workspace POST /api/v1/dashboards/{dashboard_id}/move Move a dashboard to another workspace GET /api/v1/datasources/{datasource_id}/starter-questions The questions of the charts the starter dashboard would build; nothing runs GET /api/v1/workspaces The caller's workspaces, oldest first POST /api/v1/workspaces Create a workspace (201) PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/name Rename a workspace DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id} Delete an empty workspace (204) GET /api/v1/datasource-types The adapters the engine can name, installed or not, each with its connection schema (the Connect a database form) POST /api/v1/datasources/test Connect to a datasource that is not added and report the stage that failed and the fix; registers nothing POST /api/v1/datasources Register a datasource in the running process; config has the shape of one datasources entry (id, type, connection, ...). save: true also writes datasources/<id>.yaml, with every secret as a reference; a read-only config answers 403 NOT_WRITABLE and keeps it registered until restart. A body that does not validate is a 422 listing each problem by path GET /api/v1/datasources List the datasources the caller reaches: type, description, status (ready, failed, unchecked), capabilities, masked connection, sample questions GET /api/v1/datasources/{datasource_id} One datasource, as the list shows it DELETE /api/v1/datasources/{datasource_id} Take a datasource out of the running process GET /api/v1/datasources/{datasource_id}/schema The tables and columns the caller may see GET /api/v1/datasources/{datasource_id}/diagram The schema as a Mermaid erDiagram (plain text); repeat tables to draw some and their neighbours GET /api/v1/index Index health: status, entries by type, embedding model and problems per datasource DELETE /api/v1/index Clear the vector store GET /api/v1/index/check Drift check: compare each datasource's live schema with what was indexed (admin) GET /api/v1/index/inspect The retrieval inspector's defaults POST /api/v1/index/inspect Run a retrieval and show the pool, the picks and what was dropped POST /api/v1/jobs/index Start the index job (admin, 202): index every datasource or datasource_ids; progress per datasource POST /api/v1/jobs/profile Start the profile job (admin, 202): profile datasources into proposals, on the server's key; draft, max_cost_usd GET /api/v1/knowledge The merged knowledge per datasource, with where each item came from and its problems GET /api/v1/knowledge/sources Each knowledge source, its counts, checksum, load time and last error POST /api/v1/knowledge/reload Reload every knowledge source and swap atomically (admin) POST /api/v1/knowledge/choices File a clarification pick as a term proposal GET /api/v1/proposals List proposals by kind, status, datasource_id and limit (admin) GET /api/v1/proposals/{proposal_id} One proposal (admin) POST /api/v1/proposals/accept Accept proposals by id, with optional edits; writes each file once (admin) POST /api/v1/proposals/reject Reject proposals by id, with a reason (admin) POST /api/v1/proposals/examples File starter questions as example proposals (admin) PUT /api/v1/settings/llm Replace the whole llm section in the running process (the body is the section as JSON; a bad one is a 422) PATCH /api/v1/settings/llm Change only the provider and model of named agents; every other llm setting stays (admin) GET /api/v1/llm Each agent and the model it runs on 
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/query \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"question": "How many customers are there?"}'

The response has status, sub_queries, final_answer, errors, warnings, reasoning, timings, usage, artifact_refs, trace_id and trace_path. Each sub-query carries id, intent, datasource_id, schema_version, plan, validation, sql, rows, status, retry_count and plan_source. rows is a capped sample with the true total; the full result set lives in artifact storage, addressed by artifact_refs. A pipeline failure, a refusal included, comes back as HTTP 200 with status: "error" and the reason in errors. Per-area reference: REST API.

docs.title: Settings and API keys
docs.text: Source: packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/routes/settings.py

docs.title: PUT /api/v1/settings/llm
docs.text:
Replaces the engine's whole llm section in the running process, through engine.llm.replace (see LLM API → llm.replace).

Admin only: see Admin routes.

Request body: the llm section as JSON, the same shape as llm.yaml (see LLM configuration).

{
  "provider": "openai",
  "model": "gpt-5.4",
  "api_key": "${env:OPENAI_API_KEY}",
  "agents": {"ast_planner": {"model": "gpt-5.5"}}
}

Execution flow: - The body is checked exactly as llm.yaml is: strict keys with "did you mean", the section's validators, and the providers resolved through the engine's registry. A ${provider:key} reference is kept in a secret field (api_key) and resolved by the engine's secret manager, so the body can name a variable or a secret rather than carry a key. A reference anywhere else is an error: the server's environment is never read into the config. - Every agent's API key must resolve. No model is called. - The new clients are built, then swapped in with engine.config.llm as one step. Questions already running finish on the old LLM. - The change is logged (one INFO line on nl2sql.llm) and audited, naming the caller's roles, via: "api", and each agent's old and new provider and model. Nothing is written to disk: a restart reads llm.yaml again.

Response (200): the change, never a key.

{
  "by": {"user_id": null, "roles": ["admin"], "via": "api"},
  "changes": {
    "default": {"old": "openai/gpt-5.4", "new": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"},
    "ast_planner": {"old": "openai/gpt-5.4", "new": "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5"}
  }
}

Errors: - No role -> HTTP 401; a role not in policies.admin_roles, or a remote client with no role source configured -> HTTP 403. - A section that is not valid, a provider that is not installed, or a key that does not resolve -> HTTP 422, whose detail is the config error's text. Nothing changes.

HTTP 422
{"detail": "LLM has 1 problem:\n\n  LLM → llm.agents.ast_planer\n    Unknown key. Did you mean 'ast_planner'?"}

docs.title: PATCH /api/v1/settings/llm
docs.text:
Changes the provider and model of the named agents and nothing else, through engine.llm.set_models (see LLM API → llm.set_models). Admin only. In memory and per process, like PUT: with more than one worker, a save reaches only the one that answered, and a restart reads llm.yaml again.

Request body: an agent's name, as GET /llm lists it (default included), mapped to {"provider", "model"}, or to null to drop that agent's own model so it runs on default.

{"default": {"provider": "openai", "model": "gpt-5.4"}, "ast_planner": {"provider": "openai", "model": "gpt-5.5"}, "refiner": null}

base_url, headers, prices, temperatures and every other setting stay. Where an agent's provider changes, its api_key and base_url are cleared, so it uses the new provider's standard key variable. Response (200): the same change as PUT, never a key.

Errors: 401 and 403 as for PUT. A provider or model the server cannot use, a key that does not resolve, an unknown agent, or default: null -> HTTP 422 with the fixed message "That provider and model cannot be used on this server."; nothing changes.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/llm
docs.text: Any caller. Response: {"llms": {...}}, engine.llm.list(): each agent by its name in the llm section (default first) with its provider, model, temperature and inherited (True when it sets nothing of its own). Never a key. There is no GET /llm/{agent}: the list holds every agent.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/llm/providers
docs.text: Any caller. engine.llm.providers(): each provider the engine can name, with its name, key_variable, key_present, the verified models and the key_shape (prefix, min_length) a key must match, so a form can check one before sending it. Never a key.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/api-keys
docs.text: Admin only. Every key, newest first, revoked ones included: id, label, user_id, tenant_id, roles, created_by, created_at, and revoked_at/revoked_by once revoked. Never a token or its hash.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/api-keys
docs.text: Admin only. Body {"user_id": "ann", "roles": ["analyst"], "tenant_id": null, "label": "ci"}. Answers 201 {"key": {...}, "token": "nl2sql_<id>_<secret>"}. The token is in this response only: the server stores a hash. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>. An empty user, or a role that is not one of policies.roles, is a 422 INVALID_REQUEST.

docs.title: DELETE /api/v1/api-keys/{key_id}
docs.text: Admin only. Revokes the key; it stops verifying at once. Answers 204. An unknown id is a 404.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/events/catalog
docs.text: Any caller. Every event the engine publishes (engine.events.catalog()): name, description, whether a run has it (run), whether a caller's stream carries it, whether the audit observer writes it, and its data's JSON Schema (data_schema).

docs.title: Terminal app
docs.text:
nl2sql chat is the chat of the web app in a terminal: ask a question, follow up, see why the answer is what it is, chart it, approve a query that needs it. It uses the keyboard only and is part of the nl2sql-cli package (Textual is a normal dependency of it), so pip install nl2sql-cli is all it takes.

nl2sql chat                            # the project in ./nl2sql.yaml (or --config PATH)
nl2sql chat --demo                     # the demo project in ./nl2sql-demo, answered from recordings when there is no key
nl2sql chat --as analyst --user ana    # ask as a role and a user
nl2sql chat --datasource chinook       # one datasource only
Option Meaning --demo, --dir Chat on the demo project in --dir (default nl2sql-demo); it is written and indexed on first use, as nl2sql demo does --as ROLE The caller's role. The default is the project's policies.default_role; with none, the caller has no role --user NAME The caller's user id. The default is the operating-system user --datasource ID Start conversations on this datasource and offer only its starter questions

The app takes its keys from the environment and the project's .env, like every command; it never asks for one. Every call it makes names the caller. The role is the one you name with --as (as with nl2sql run --role, it is self-asserted: this is a local tool for the person at the keyboard), and the policy of that role applies. While a turn runs, Ctrl+N, /new and opening another conversation wait until it ends.

docs.title: The screen
docs.text:
Conversations are on the left, the transcript in the middle and the question box at the bottom. A side panel on the right is hidden until you ask for it.

Key Does Enter Send the question (or run the /command) Tab In the question box, fill the next starter question of the datasource; elsewhere, move the focus F2 Show or hide why this answer: the plan in plain words F3 Show or hide the SQL that ran PageDown Read the next page of rows into the table Ctrl+O Move to the list of conversations; Enter opens one Ctrl+N Start a new conversation Esc Back to the question box Ctrl+Q Quit

A turn streams: a status line shows the node or tool that is running, then the answer, any warnings, and the rows as a table (the first page; PageDown reads on). When the model took several steps, each is listed before the reply.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Type these in the question box.

Command Does /chart [line, bar, big_number or table] Chart the last result. A line is one sparkline per series with its first and last value, a bar is one row of block characters per category, a big_number is the figure /diagram Show the Mermaid text of the schema diagram (a terminal cannot draw it) /report, /save FILE Show the conversation as a report; write it to a file /approvals List the approval requests waiting for your role /remember After picking a reading of an ambiguous phrase: save the pick as a proposal for review /new, /help New conversation; the keys and commands

Any other /name runs the chat tool of that name.

docs.title: Clarifying and approving
docs.text:
• A phrase that can be read two ways opens a list of the readings. Pick one with the arrow keys and Enter; the question runs again with your choice. /remember then saves the choice as a proposal; it reaches the glossary only when a reviewer accepts it.
  • A query that needs approval shows the reason and the SQL. If your role is one of the approvers, Approve and run grants the request and retries the turn; otherwise the app says which roles can approve. An approver can list what is waiting with /approvals.

docs.title: Where it lives
docs.text: nl2sql-cli/src/nl2sql_cli/chat/ holds the app (app.py), its widgets and the drawing of a chart as text (charts.py); the command is nl2sql_cli/commands/chat.py. Only that folder imports textual, and it imports only the top-level nl2sql, like the rest of the CLI. import nl2sql and the other commands load no Textual.

docs.title: Web app
docs.text:
The web app is the browser front end of NL2SQL. It lives in nl2sql-ui/ at the repository root, is built into the API package, and talks to nothing but the REST API through nl2sql-ui/src/api/http.js. Anything the page can do, an SDK or REST caller can do the same way.

Pages are reached by hash route: #/chat, #/approvals, #/settings, #/retrieval, #/pipeline, #/evals. A route nobody serves opens Home.

docs.title: Chat
docs.text:
#/chat (and #/chat/<conversation id>) is a conversation with the model-led chat. The model decides which steps to take; the page shows what it did.

The list and the transcript. The left column lists your conversations (GET /conversations), with New conversation and a delete button on each. The transcript shows one block per stored turn. A new conversation starts on the first question, so the address bar names it from then on and a reload comes back to the same place. A new conversation also offers the datasource's starter questions and, with more than one datasource, a choice of which one to ask.

A turn streams. A question is sent to POST /conversations/{id}/turns/stream. While it runs, the page shows the run spine (the pipeline stations lit as each one finishes) and the answer text as it arrives. The rows appear with the stored turn, not before. The last event carries the stored turn, which replaces the live view, so what stays on the page is exactly what the server saved. Stop cancels the stream; during a tool or retry call, which cannot be cancelled from the page, the button reads Working and is disabled. A second turn sent while one is running is refused by the server with 409, and the page says so.

What an answered turn shows. The answer text and the rows come first. Below them, in this order:

  • warnings about the result (truncated rows, withheld columns, and so on);
  • Why this answer, a fold with the sections of the explanation (how the question was read, which tables and curated answers were used, what the planner chose; the planner's note is marked as the model's own words);
  • SQL and Plan, the typed plan and the query it produced;
  • Trace and cost, the run's stations, timings and token use;
  • Did this answer it?, a light bar with Yes and Not quite. Yes keeps the answer in My answers (POST /answers; the server also rates the run up) and says so, adding "sent for review" only when a proposal was filed. A full My answers (100), a save racing another ("try again") and an answer that cannot be kept are shown in place. Not quite rates the run down and opens a note and a corrected SQL that Send for review files (POST /feedback, POST /feedback/correct). A one-line hint explains both until the first click; that it was seen is a browser-local flag only.

Only the last turn is live. A clarification pick answers the conversation's pending question, and Run it now re-runs the last question, so those buttons show on the last turn only. Earlier turns keep their text. If you open another conversation while a turn is running, its result is added to the conversation it was sent for, not to the one on screen.

Clarification. When the model needs a decision, the turn shows its question and an option for each reading. Use this reading sends {choice: option id} as the next turn. Remember this meaning also files the pick, with an optional term, as a proposal for review (POST /knowledge/choices).

Approvals. When a plan needs approval, the turn lists what is waiting. Once every request is granted, Run it now calls POST /conversations/{id}/retry with the approval ids. Check again reads the requests' state; a denied request says so and the turn stays stopped.

More with this answer. Buttons under a turn run the conversation's tools (GET /chat-tools, POST /conversations/{id}/tools/{name}): Chart, Diagram, Report, and Pin to dashboard when the conversation belongs to a dashboard. A tool the model offers in its reply gets a button too. Tool arguments use 1-based turn and step numbers. Report calls POST /conversations/{id}/tools/report, which stores the report as a turn output (the markdown is in output.body); the GET /conversations/{id}/report download is not used by the page.

docs.title: Approvals
docs.text: #/approvals lists the requests waiting for a decision (GET /approvals?status=pending), each with the question, who asked, the plan, the SQL it would run and why it stopped. Grant and Deny call the matching routes. The list also holds requests you asked yourself; those show no buttons, since only an approver may decide them, and the nav count leaves them out. The server marks them (own on each record), so the page compares no ids; it never decides who may approve, and the server refuses a decision that is not yours, with its reason shown.

docs.title: Charts, diagrams, reports
docs.text:
A chat answer can carry outputs. Each is drawn from data the API already holds, by the renderer for its kind (src/outputs/Output.jsx picks it from the ToolOutput). A body the page cannot read is shown as text, never dropped.

Output What you see Chart A line, bar, big number or table from the engine's ChartSpec, drawn as SVG sized to its card. Bars run horizontally so long labels stay readable. A Table switch shows the rows behind the chart, the takeaway sits under it, and a note says when only the first rows are drawn. Download Vega-Lite saves the same chart as a Vega-Lite file (not offered for a table). Diagram A Mermaid diagram. The library loads on the first diagram only, in its own file, and follows the page theme (light or dark). Source shows the text. Report The Markdown the report tool wrote: headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, code and collapsible sections. Links open in a new tab; raw HTML is never rendered. Download .md saves the text. Rows The result table, paged from /results/{trace_id}/{result_id}, with CSV download.

Charts use up to four series colours and then a neutral grey; every chart with two or more series has a legend, and each mark has a hover title with its full value. The series colours keep 3:1 contrast against the card in both themes (src/outputs/palette.test.js). Downloads are fetched with the page's own request headers, so they work with the same keys and identity as every other call.

docs.title: Dashboards and workspaces
docs.text:
The Dashboards page (#/dashboards, and #/dashboards/{id} for one dashboard) shows whole dashboards, which the chat builds as drafts and a person pins into a workspace. It calls the dashboards and workspaces routes and never a model.

  • Workspaces are listed on the left: create, rename, and delete (an empty one only; the server's sentence is shown otherwise). The chosen workspace lists its saved dashboards; Drafts lists those not yet pinned.
  • Opening a dashboard only reads: each chart appears with its stored result and how old it is ("Refreshed 10 min ago"). The charts the server reports as due are then refreshed one at a time. Refresh re-runs every chart.
  • Charts are drawn with the same chart card as the chat. A chart that cannot show says why: needs fixing (what broke, with Remove this chart), denied (you may not read its data), needs approval (the reason, a link to Approvals, and Run again: it names the request, then runs the chart with it once it is granted, or says it is still waiting), or no rows.
  • Filters apply values to every chart: a list of a column's values for an in filter, two ends for a between filter. Apply shows the filtered result and stores nothing; Clear brings back the stored results (it opens the dashboard again). A chart a filter does not reach is marked "Not filtered". The header's age is that of the oldest result shown.
  • Schedule sets how often the dashboard refreshes itself, or stops it. An interval under the server's minimum is refused with its own sentence.
  • Edit turns on, per chart: rename, chart type (automatic, line, bar, big number, table; the chart runs once so the new type shows), move earlier or later, wider or narrower, taller or shorter, and remove. It also renames the dashboard, moves it to another workspace (or pins a draft into one; with no workspace yet, Pin makes "General"), removes a filter, and deletes the dashboard. The grid has four columns; charts are packed in order, so an arrangement never overlaps. What data a chart shows is changed in chat, not here.
  • Generate a starter dashboard (at the top of the page) builds one for a datasource from what the project already knows, with no model and no key. Pick the datasource, and optionally a title, the workspace to save into (the chosen one by default) and how many charts. Progress shows as "tile 3 of 8" and can be cancelled; when it is saved the new dashboard opens. Only one job per person runs at a time: the form locks while the start request is in flight, a job already running (after a reload, say) comes back with its progress and Cancel, and leaving the page stops following it without opening anything.
  • Build a dashboard (a fold under Generate, which stays) makes a dashboard from questions you choose. Four steps: Sources (Curated, My saved answers, Tell us what matters; mix them), What to ask (chips from GET /dashboard-builder/options: curated questions, your saved answers, and for the model source the metrics, breakdowns and period, plus a line in your own words; at most 3 new questions are written), Review (POST /dashboard-builder/proposals: tick, untick or reword each chart, and optionally set the title, the workspace and a date column) and Build (POST /jobs/dashboard-build, shown as "tile 3 of 8" and cancellable). A question that could not be answered is listed as "Couldn't answer ..." with the reason, and you open the dashboard from there; with none skipped it opens by itself. "Tell us what matters" needs a model key: on the hosted demo without one it is disabled with a note pointing to Settings, and a missing key from the server reads the same way. The other two sources call no model.

My answers. A fold at the top of the Dashboards page lists the answers you kept with Yes in chat (GET /answers): the question, its datasource and the day it was kept. Run answers the saved plan again as you (POST /answers/{id}/run): your data scope, hooks and approvals apply, and no model is called; the rows show in the usual result table. An answer the schema has outgrown says it needs fixing, and one waiting for an approval offers Run again once it is granted. Delete forgets it (DELETE /answers/{id}). The list is yours alone.

docs.title: Connect and review
docs.text:
Connect (#/connect) adds a datasource to the running server.

  1. Pick a type. The form is built from that adapter's own connection schema, so a third-party adapter gets a form with no change to the app. An adapter that is not installed shows its install hint.
  2. Fill in the connection. Secret fields are password inputs: type an ${env:NAME} reference, not the secret itself. Less common settings sit under Advanced.
  3. Test connection reports Connected, or the stage that failed (configuration, driver, network, sign-in, database, permissions) with the reason and the fix.
  4. Add registers the datasource. Tick "Save to the project config" to write it to nl2sql.yaml. Where the config is read-only (the Docker image), the datasource is added but not saved: it works until the server restarts, and you add it to the mounted config to keep it.
  5. After Add the page offers Index, Profile (optionally drafting descriptions with the model, under a spending cap you set) and Suggest starter questions, which are filed as proposals for review. Each job shows its progress and can be cancelled.

Removing a datasource asks first. Once a datasource is added, secrets typed into the form are cleared. Connect needs an administrator. GET /meta says whether you are one (caller.admin), so on the hosted demo, and for anyone who is not an administrator, the page says it is off instead of showing a form. If /meta is unavailable the page asks the server, and a 403 from it turns the page off the same way.

Knowledge (#/knowledge) shows, for one datasource:

  • What the engine knows: terms, rules, joins, tables and columns. Tables and columns are marked with where their description or role came from (a knowledge file, the database, or derived). Any problems found while loading, and the schema.
  • Waiting for review (administrators; the page does not ask for these unless /meta says you are one, and a 403 still hides them): the proposals from profiling and starter questions, grouped by kind. Each shows everything accepting would write (a role, a unit, code values, text), and the counts and checks that back it, never rows of data. Accept or reject one or many; "Edit and accept" lets you change a proposal's text first. Accepting writes to the knowledge files; the page names the files and shows any proposal the server refused and why.
  • Drift (administrators): Check for drift compares each live database with its index and lists what changed (tables, columns, types, foreign keys) and what the change may break: verified queries, glossary items, policy rules and preferred tables. To bring a drifted index up to date, run nl2sql index.

docs.title: Evals
docs.text:
Evals (#/evals) runs the suites named in evals.suites on the server and shows the report. It is for administrators: a report holds every role's cases, plans and SQL, so GET /meta (caller.admin) decides whether the page is listed: until /meta names the caller, or when it names none, the page is not listed. A caller who opens it anyway is told it is off.

  1. Pick a mode. Plans only and Retrieval only call no model. Full asks every case end to end, spends money, and needs a cost cap in dollars (the run stops when its model calls reach it).
  2. Tick the suites to run (all by default; each shows how many of its cases are approved).
  3. Run starts POST /jobs/eval. The job shows its progress and can be cancelled.

The report shows, for each configuration: accuracy with its interval, the generated path's accuracy, cost, latency (p50 and p95) and planner retries; accuracy by source (curated or generated) and the pass, fail, error and skip counts by role; and every case that did not pass, with its question, the reason each scorer gave and its SQL. A run that stopped at its cost cap, or was cancelled, says so, and a model call with no known price is counted so the cost reads as a floor.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Settings (#/settings) holds up to four cards, depending on the server and on who you are.

  • API key and Model for each step appear when the server lets a request bring its own model (api.request_llm, which GET /meta reports). The key and the choices stay in this browser tab (sessionStorage) and travel as headers with each question; nothing is written on the server. A step put on a provider needs a key for it in the same tab, or the question is refused. The providers, their models and the steps come from GET /llm/providers and GET /llm.
  • The server's model (administrators) edits the default model and the model of each step, and saves with PATCH /settings/llm, which sends only the models you changed. Everything else in the server's llm section (base_url, headers, prices, temperatures, a key held in a custom variable) stays as it was; where a step's provider changes, its key and base_url are cleared and the new provider's standard key variable is used. A provider whose key the server does not have is labelled "(no key)". The change is in memory and in this server process only, so with more than one worker a save reaches just the one that answered; llm.yaml is read again on a restart. The page no longer warns about models that ignore temperature 0, because GET /llm/providers does not say which they are.
  • API keys for this server (administrators) lists the keys the server issues, and creates one from a user id, roles, an optional tenant and an optional label (POST /api-keys). The new key's token is shown once and never again. Revoke ends a key (DELETE /api-keys/{id}).

A caller who is not an administrator, on a server that does not take a key with a question, sees that there is nothing to set.

docs.title: Home, Pipeline and Retrieval
docs.text:
Home says what the engine does (the five steps a question travels, a clip of each page) and, while the project has nothing to ask yet, shows the start screen above that story. GET /meta decides it with start:

start When What Home shows choose The served project has no datasource and the caller is an administrator Two cards. Try the demo (administrators) runs POST /jobs/demo, shows its progress, then opens Chat on a sample question. Connect your database opens the Connect page. Anyone else gets no start at all. hosted The hosted demo Ask a sample question opens Chat. Connect your database only explains: the hosted server connects nothing, so it shows the steps to run nl2sql yourself (install and nl2sql demo, or Docker Compose) and links the self-hosting guide. No route is called. null A datasource exists No start screen.

Try a sample question asks the first guided question that has a recorded answer, so it works without a key. The guided questions and the recordings come from each datasource in GET /meta (sample_questions, recorded); the recording's model is recorded_with.

Pipeline (#/pipeline) lists every step of a run from GET /about, and marks which a model decides. A page answers from recordings (it says so on each model step) when the visitor is on the hosted demo with no key, or when every model step in /about runs on the replay provider.

Retrieval (#/retrieval) searches the live index with no model and no key: GET /index/inspect gives the defaults (k, lambda, the entry types) and POST /index/inspect runs one search as the caller, so it shows only what the caller's scope reaches. The datasource list comes from /meta. With no datasource it says there is nothing to search yet.

Hosted first run. A hosted visitor without a key sees the guided questions replay recorded runs. A question with no recording comes back as a REPLAY_MISS error, and Chat then points to Settings to add a key. Chat labels a recorded answer Recorded run when every model call in its usage reports no token count and names the recording's model.

docs.title: Source map
docs.text: Path What it holds src/api/chat.js Every conversation, approval, feedback and trace call src/chat/spine.js Folds stream events into the live run spine src/chat/turns.js Reads a stored turn: answer, steps, pending questions, tool buttons src/pages/Chat.jsx The page: list, transcript, composer, streaming src/pages/Approvals.jsx The approvals queue src/api/evals.js, src/pages/Evals.jsx, src/evals/report.js Run a suite and read the report src/api/settings.js, src/pages/Settings.jsx, src/lib/settings.js The tab's keys and models, the server's model, API keys

docs.title: Screenshots
docs.text:
Captured from the playground on the demo project, asking about Chinook, with recorded model responses (so token counts are placeholders).

An answer: the question, the plan the model wrote, the validator's checks, the generated SQL and the rows.

Debug: LLM calls, tokens and time per node in execution order. Open a node to see what it read and returned, the retrieval it ran, and each prompt and raw model response.

Pipeline: every step of a run in order, with the seven a model decides marked and the deterministic ones left quiet. Before a question it shows the model each step is set to use; after one, the model that answered, that step's tokens and its time.

Settings: save an API key per provider and choose a provider and model for each LLM step. Written to the demo project's .env and llm.yaml.

Retrieval inspector: run the engine's vector search for any text against the live index, with k, lambda, entry types and datasource as knobs, and see what MMR picked and what it dropped, as the role you chose, so entries it may not read are not shown. No LLM call.
