docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Purpose: plan, validate, generate, and execute SQL for a single sub-query.
  • Why it exists architecturally: isolates SQL-capable execution into a reusable subgraph that can be scheduled per scan node in the global execution DAG.
  • When it is invoked: when layer_router resolves a datasource with SUPPORTS_SQL capability and sends a scan-layer payload.

Defining function: build_sql_agent_graph() Source file path: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/subgraphs/sql_agent.py

docs.title: Boundary Definition
docs.text: This subgraph encapsulates the SQL planning and execution loop for a single SubQuery. It does NOT perform cross-subquery aggregation, answer synthesis, or datasource resolution; those responsibilities are owned by the main pipeline graph and upstream nodes.

docs.title: Entry Conditions
docs.text:
Required state: - SubgraphExecutionState.trace_id - SubgraphExecutionState.sub_query (must include id, datasource_id, and intent)

Preconditions: - sub_query.datasource_id must map to a registered adapter/executor. - Schema store and vector store may be used if configured; otherwise schema retrieval falls back to full schema snapshot.

Triggering parent graph: - layer_router in the main pipeline graph sends build_scan_payload() to the subgraph via wrap_subgraph().

docs.title: Exit Conditions
docs.text:
Successful completion criteria: - Reaches END after executor and produces executor_response. - Or reaches END after clarifier, which asked which reading of the question was meant (NEEDS_CLARIFICATION, INFO): no SQL is generated or run, and the wrapper reports the sub-query with status needs_clarification.

Failure exits: - check_retriever returns end when schema_retriever returned a non-retryable error: retrieval failed and there was no snapshot to fall back to (SCHEMA_RETRIEVAL_FAILED, CRITICAL). The planner is never called. - check_planner returns end when planner output is missing and retries are exhausted or errors are non-retryable. - check_logical_validation returns end when validation errors are non-retryable or retries are exhausted. - check_execution returns end after executor unless the database rejected the query as wrong (EXECUTION_FAILED) and retries remain: a success, a refusal (DB_EXECUTION_ERROR: permission, timeout, connection) and any other executor error all end the subgraph. - Cancellation forces end in router checks and in the retry handler. The run's CancellationToken is read from the RunnableConfig (configurable.cancellation_token); when no token is present the subgraph behaves as not cancelled.

Partial completion behavior: - If planner or logical validation errors are retryable and retry budget remains, execution loops via retry_handler → refiner → ast_planner. - So does a query the database rejected as wrong (an unknown column or table, a type mismatch, bad syntax): the adapter marks the error retryable and the executor reports it as EXECUTION_FAILED, with the database's own first line as the message.

docs.title: Internal Node Composition
docs.text:
Execution order (nominal path): - schema_retriever — SchemaRetrieverNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/schema_retriever/node.py — retrieve relevant schema tables/columns. - ast_planner — ASTPlannerNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/ast_planner/node.py — create SQL AST plan. - logical_validator — LogicalValidatorNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/validator/node.py — validate plan correctness and policy constraints. - clarifier — ClarifierNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/clarifier/node.py — validate the planner's alternative readings and, when two or three remain, end the sub-query by asking which was meant. See ClarifierNode. - generator — GeneratorNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/generator/node.py — generate SQL text from AST. - executor — ExecutorNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/executor/node.py — execute SQL and produce artifacts. - retry_handler — retry_node() — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/subgraphs/sql_agent.py — apply exponential backoff and increment retry count. - refiner — RefinerNode — packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/refiner/node.py — generate feedback for the planner.

Mermaid diagram (sql_agent only): 

flowchart TD
    schema_retriever -->|ok| ast_planner
    schema_retriever -->|end| END
    ast_planner -->|ok| logical_validator
    ast_planner -->|retry| retry_handler
    ast_planner -->|end| END
    logical_validator -->|ok| clarifier
    clarifier -->|ok| generator
    clarifier -->|end| END
    logical_validator -->|retry| retry_handler
    logical_validator -->|end| END
    retry_handler --> refiner --> ast_planner
    generator --> executor
    executor -->|retry| retry_handler
    executor -->|end| END

docs.title: State Contract
docs.text:
State model: SubgraphExecutionState (packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/state.py).

Field ownership, reducers, and lifecycle are defined in ../graph_state.md.

docs.title: Step-by-Step Execution Flow
docs.text:
1. schema_retriever builds a semantic query from sub_query and retrieves relevant schema context; if none found, or the search fails, it falls back to full schema snapshot. A table cut to the searched columns keeps its keys, join columns and label. check_retriever routes end when retrieval failed with no snapshot (a non-retryable SCHEMA_RETRIEVAL_FAILED), else ok.
  2. ast_planner runs an LLM planning chain to produce PlanModel.
  3. check_planner routes:
  4. ok if a plan exists.
  5. retry if errors are retryable and retry budget remains.
  6. end if errors are non-retryable or retries exhausted.
  7. logical_validator validates the plan for structural and policy compliance.
  8. check_logical_validation routes:
  9. ok when no blocking errors exist.
  10. retry when retryable errors exist and retry budget remains.
  11. end when errors are non-retryable or retries exhausted.
  12. clarifier passes straight through when the planner gave no alternative readings. Otherwise it runs each alternative through LogicalValidatorNode.check (the static checks and the caller's scope), drops those that fail, merges those that render to SQL another option has, and keeps the rest on ast_planner_response.alternatives. check_clarifier routes end when it asked (two or three options, a named phrase, state.clarify and settings.clarify.enabled on), else ok. Every path from the planner to the generator still passes the validator.
  13. generator converts the plan to SQL for the target datasource dialect.
  14. executor runs SQL via the datasource adapter and returns artifacts/errors. check_execution routes retry when every executor error is a retryable EXECUTION_FAILED and retry budget remains, otherwise end. It also routes retry when the query returned no rows on a filter value the column does not have but a close one exists (VALUE_NOT_FOUND ERROR, raised once per sub-query; see ExecutorNode), and when a COUNT counted rows a join repeated (JOIN_FAN_OUT ERROR, raised once per sub-query; see ExecutorNode). Only a finding of this attempt (its details.attempt) routes retry.
  15. If routed to retry: retry_handler waits with exponential backoff and jitter, then increments retry_count.
  16. refiner uses LLM feedback to enrich error context, then loops back to ast_planner. Both are told about the latest attempt only, as {node, error_code, message} (nl2sql.pipeline.retry_feedback): never an earlier attempt's errors again, never a stack trace or details.
  17. Subgraph terminates at END.

docs.text: Determinism guarantees and non-determinism sources are documented in ../determinism.md.

docs.title: Error Propagation
docs.text: Failure domains, retry scope, and recovery limitations are centralized in ../failure_recovery.md.

docs.title: Retry + Recovery
docs.text: See ../failure_recovery.md for retry scope and recovery behavior.

docs.title: Performance Characteristics
docs.text:
• Blocking LLM calls: ASTPlannerNode and RefinerNode.
  • External I/O: vector store retrieval and schema store access in SchemaRetrieverNode; datasource execution in ExecutorNode.
  • CPU-bound steps: SQL generation via sqlglot in GeneratorNode.
  • Retry loop introduces sleep-based delays on failures.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
• Node-specific loggers are used (schema_retriever, planner, logical_validator, generator, executor, refiner).
  • trace_id is stored in state and forwarded to executor requests; logging context is not explicitly set.
  • No explicit metrics or tracing spans are emitted by the subgraph code.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Read from the runtime's settings.pipeline.retries when the subgraph is built:

  • max (default 3)
  • base_delay_s (default 1.0)
  • max_delay_s (default 10.0)
  • jitter_s (default 0.5)

docs.title: Extension Points
docs.text:
• Modify build_sql_agent_graph() to insert, remove, or rewire nodes and edges.
  • Add new subgraphs by constructing them in build_graph() and extending resolve_subgraph() with their required capabilities.
  • Replace node implementations via dependency injection in Runtime.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• Generator errors are not routed into the retry loop; a failure proceeds to executor, which reports MISSING_SQL, and terminates at END.
  • No subgraph-specific metrics or trace spans are emitted.
  • The executor retries only what the adapter marks retryable. An adapter that raises instead of returning a failed ResultFrame ends the sub-query with EXECUTOR_CRASH.

Because the generator has no retry edge, the invariant the loop depends on is that logical_validator rejects every plan generator would refuse to build. LogicalValidatorNode._validate_buildable() enforces it by running the generator's own _build_query() — see Buildability. Without it, a plan whose tables are not joined reached generator and ended the sub-query with a terminal SQL_GEN_FAILED.

docs.title: Charts
docs.text:
An answer's rows become a chart without a model call. engine.results.chart(result, user_context=caller) reads the saved result, as the caller who asked it, and returns a ChartSpec: our own small typed chart (a line, a bar, a big number or a table), which to_vega_lite() exports for a browser. See Results API.

spec = engine.results.chart(result, user_context=caller)   # a QueryResult, or a trace_id
spec.kind, spec.reason, spec.takeaway
vega = spec.to_vega_lite()                   # None for a table

docs.title: The spec
docs.text: Field Meaning kind line, bar, big_number or table title The question that ran (a run with one sub-query: its intent; a trace_id alone: Result) x, y, series, value Encodings (field, kind, a humanised title) the kind uses: x the time or category, y one or more measures, series a category split into lines, value the big number data ChartData: trace_id, result_id, columns, rows (at most charts.max_points), truncated takeaway One sentence from a template, or None for a table reason Why this kind, for example "one date column and 1 number"

docs.title: Column kinds
docs.text: The artifact writer records each column's kind in the run's manifest from the saved file's types: integer, decimal and float are number; date, time and timestamp temporal; string text; bool boolean; anything else other. When the run had one sub-query, its plan refines them: a DATE_TRUNC select item is temporal, a grouped DATE_PART('year', x) is temporal (a year axis), an aggregate is a measure, and a number that is grouped on is a dimension. In a plan that has an aggregate, a plain column that is not grouped on (an id) is a dimension too. With several sub-queries or no plan, every number is a measure and everything else a dimension.

docs.title: The five rules
docs.text:
First match wins.

# Shape of the result Chart 1 One row, one measure, at most one text column big_number 2 One temporal dimension, one to max_series measures, at least two rows line, x ascending 3 One temporal and one text dimension (at most max_series distinct values), one measure line with series 4 One text or boolean dimension, one to three measures, two to max_categories rows bar, in the plan's order if it ordered, else by the first measure descending 5 Anything else table

At most max_points rows are read. When the result has more, or was cut at the datasource row limit (ResultSummary.truncated), data.truncated is true and the chart is a table, so no point is dropped silently. kind= forces a kind the data can draw; any other is a ValueError naming the ones it can.

docs.title: Takeaways
docs.text:
Chart Sentence line "Revenue went from 100 in 2024-01-01 to 150 in 2024-03-01 (+50%)." For a series, the one with the largest last value. No change is given when an end is null or the start is zero. bar "Books has the highest sales: 50." (the category is written as the data has it) After a SUM or COUNT with no negative value: "..., 50% of the total shown." big_number "Total: 1,234.5." table none

Numbers have thousands separators and at most three digits after the point.

docs.title: Vega-Lite
docs.text: to_vega_lite() returns a Vega-Lite v5 spec with the rows inline (data.values): a line or bar mark, a temporal, ordinal (whole-number years, times of day) or nominal x, a quantitative y, several measures folded with a fold transform and told apart by a color field, and a color field for series. It sets no colour, scheme, font or size: the renderer's theme decides.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
# settings.yaml
charts:
  max_points: 1000
  max_categories: 20
  max_series: 5

docs.title: The chart chat tool
docs.text: In a conversation the chart tool charts the rows of an answer: turn (the latest turn with an answer when absent), step (the nth answer of the turn, from 1), result_id and kind. Its output is a chart whose body is the ChartSpec as JSON, titled with the question. It raises ToolNotApplicable when there is no answer with data, or its rows have expired.

docs.title: Diagrams
docs.text: Two Mermaid views, written to read the same on a light or a dark page: no %%{init} line, no style, classDef, linkStyle or click, no colour. Emphasis is carried by shape and grouping, and the reader's page picks the theme. Neither view calls a model.

docs.title: The answer view
docs.text:
import nl2sql

text = nl2sql.diagram_for(result)      # a QueryResult; a pure function
text = nl2sql.diagram_for(result, dialect_of=engine.datasources.dialect)   # verified SQL in its own dialect

A flowchart LR of the tables the answer read, taken from each sub-query's plan and nothing else: no row of the result, and no database. One node per table (schema.table, or the table alone when the plan names no schema), and one edge per join labelled with its columns (customer_id = id). A table read twice (a self-join) is one node.

  • Several datasources get a subgraph each, and where the decomposition joins or compares two sub-queries from different datasources, an edge between the subgraphs carries the join keys.
  • A verified query has no plan. Its SQL is parsed and the tables it reads are listed, unconnected. With dialect_of (a datasource id to its adapter's dialect, as the diagram chat tool passes) the SQL is read the way the verified-query checks read it, so TOP, [dbo].[orders] and backticks work; without it, or for a datasource the engine no longer has, in sqlglot's generic dialect. SQL that does not parse gives an empty diagram rather than an error.
  • No tables gives a single node, No tables.
flowchart LR
    t0["public.orders"]
    t1["public.customers"]
    t0 ---|"customer_id = id"| t1

docs.title: The schema view
docs.text:
engine.datasources.diagram("shop", user_context=me)                    # the whole datasource
engine.datasources.diagram("shop", user_context=me, tables=["orders"]) # orders and its neighbours

An erDiagram of the live index snapshot, drawn from engine.datasources.schema, so it shows exactly the tables the planner would be given for that caller: a table the caller's roles or policy check deny is left out, and so is every foreign key and glossary join that names one. The caller is required; there is no default view.

Each table is an entity with a generated id (e0, e1...) and its schema.table name as a quoted label, so two names that Mermaid would read alike (order-items and order_items) stay two tables. It lists its primary and foreign key columns. Each foreign key is a relationship (e0 ||--o{ e1 : "id = customer_id") and each glossary join the caller may see is one too, with its cardinality. A reference resolves to schema.table exactly; a bare name resolves only if one table has it or, for a foreign key, if the referencing table's own schema does. Anything else is left unlinked rather than drawn to the wrong table.

  • tables limits the diagram to those tables and the ones one relationship away. A name that matches no table the caller may see is a ValueError, so a hidden table and a missing one look the same.
  • More than 30 tables are cut to the 30 with the most relationships (the tables you asked for first, then their neighbours), and a comment, %% 41 more tables not shown, says how many (it names none).
erDiagram
    e0["public.customers"] {
        INTEGER id PK
    }
    e1["public.orders"] {
        INTEGER id PK
        INTEGER customer_id FK
    }
    e0 ||--o{ e1 : "id = customer_id"

docs.title: Safe to show
docs.text: Table, column and datasource names come from a database or a model, so none is trusted. A label keeps letters, digits, spaces and . , : $ = - and is always quoted; an identifier is ASCII letters, digits and _ and never starts with a word Mermaid reads (style, click, classDef, or the key markers PK, FK, UK) or with a digit. A name cannot hold a newline, so it cannot start a line of its own. The text can be put straight into a Markdown fence or a Mermaid renderer.

docs.title: In a conversation
docs.text: The diagram chat tool draws either view as a mermaid output. view is answer (the default; turn and step pick the answer, the latest by default) or schema (datasource_id, and tables if wanted), drawn for the conversation's caller. The model reads the diagram's text, which holds table names and join columns but no data.

docs.title: REST API (api)
docs.text:
The api section of nl2sql.yaml holds nl2sql-api's own settings. It is optional. The engine validates it like every other section (strict keys, ${env:...} references) and never reads it; nl2sql-api reads engine.config.api.

# nl2sql.yaml
api: { file: api.yaml }

# api.yaml
auth: none                      # api_keys | proxy | static | none (default none)
proxy:                          # auth: proxy only
  trusted_from: [127.0.0.1/32, "::1/128"]
  user_header: X-Forwarded-User
  tenant_header: null           # null: settings.tenant_id
  roles_header: X-NL2SQL-Roles
static_role: null               # auth: static only
request_llm: false              # callers may send their own key and models
cors_origins: [https://app.example.com]

These fields are validated by the engine. The engine validates them now; nl2sql-api starts reading them when its identity replaces auth.py, which also deletes role_header, role and trust_body_role.

auth: none                      # api_keys | proxy | static | none (default none)
proxy:                          # auth: proxy only
  trusted_from: [127.0.0.1/32, "::1/128"]
  user_header: X-Forwarded-User
  tenant_header: null           # null: settings.tenant_id
  roles_header: X-NL2SQL-Roles
static_role: null               # auth: static only
request_llm: false              # callers may send their own key and models
Field Default Meaning auth none How a caller is identified: api_keys, proxy, static or none. proxy.trusted_from loopback CIDRs the proxy connects from; its headers are honoured only from these. proxy.user_header, proxy.tenant_header, proxy.roles_header X-Forwarded-User, none, X-NL2SQL-Roles The headers the proxy sets. static_role none The one role of every request under auth: static. request_llm false Whether callers may send their own provider key and models per request. Field Default Meaning auth none How a caller is identified: api_keys, proxy, static or none. See Identity. proxy.trusted_from loopback CIDRs the proxy connects from; its headers are honoured only from these. proxy.user_header, proxy.tenant_header, proxy.roles_header X-Forwarded-User, none, X-NL2SQL-Roles The headers the proxy sets. static_role none The one role of every request under auth: static. request_llm false Whether callers may send their own provider key and models per request. cors_origins [] Browser origins allowed to call the API. Empty, no cross-origin request is allowed.

The 0.9 fields role_header, role and trust_body_role are gone, and the engine rejects them as unknown keys. Use auth: proxy (the roles header is proxy.roles_header), auth: static with static_role, and nothing for the body role: a request body never carries the caller.

docs.title: Admin routes
docs.text: The routes that change datasources, LLMs or the index need one of the roles in policies.admin_roles (default [admin]), which is a policy, so it lives in the policies section, not here. A request with another role is a 403. Under auth: none the caller is the local operator, who holds the admin roles. See Admin routes.

docs.title: Starting nl2sql-api
docs.text:
nl2sql-api serve builds its engine from --config (else NL2SQL_CONFIG, else ./nl2sql.yaml), after loading the .env next to that file without overriding a variable already set. It calls engine.check() before it accepts requests: a required datasource that fails, or datasources configured and none ready, raises EngineNotReady: the API logs the report and starts anyway, and GET /api/v1/ready answers 503 not_ready (an admin sees problems); an optional one that fails leaves it serving the others. See Startup.

nl2sql-api serve --config /etc/nl2sql/nl2sql.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
# or: NL2SQL_CONFIG=/etc/nl2sql/nl2sql.yaml uvicorn nl2sql_api.main:app

--demo prepares and serves the demo project, and --hosted makes it the public demo; NL2SQL_MODE or the mode: key picks the mode when no flag does (see Hosted demo).

serve loads the .env beside nl2sql.yaml (never overriding a variable already set), except for a hosted server, which never loads one. uvicorn nl2sql_api.main:app loads no .env: export the variables first. It also refuses to start over a config with mode: hosted, which needs nl2sql-api serve.

serve runs one worker, and with auth: none it refuses to bind any host but loopback, naming api.auth in the message.

The NL2SQL_API_* variables of 0.4 are not read; see From 0.4.

docs.title: Curated Answers (curated.yaml)
docs.text:
The curated section of nl2sql.yaml, usually its own curated.yaml, is where a data team writes verified queries: SQL they have already written and reviewed, with typed parameters, and the questions each query answers.

What works today

The section is loaded and checked (at startup and with nl2sql curated validate), every query can be run once with nl2sql curated test, its questions are indexed with nl2sql index, a question is matched to a verified query and answered by it (see What happens at question time), and the playground badges such an answer Verified. The demo ships six verified queries (In the demo). Preferred tables (below) and proposals from thumbs-up feedback (From feedback to verified queries) are built too. Business metrics are parsed but not used yet.

docs.title: Where it lives
docs.text:
# nl2sql.yaml
curated: { file: curated.yaml }

The section is optional. Present, curated answers are on; absent, they are off, and nothing else changes. To turn them off, remove the line from nl2sql.yaml (the file can stay). A file: that does not exist is an error, and so is a section that is broken: building the engine (NL2SQL(config), nl2sql run, the REST API, the playground) fails with a ConfigError that names every problem, as a broken datasource does.

The matching knobs are in the settings section:

Setting Default Meaning settings.curated.match_top_k 5 Verified query candidates a question's search returns and the model is shown, one per query. settings.curated.match_floor 0.6 Cosine similarity the best candidate must reach before the model is asked to choose one. Below it the question is answered as if there were no curated section, with no model call. Calibrated on the local embedding model; see Curated answers.

docs.title: Writing the file
docs.text:
One section covers every datasource, keyed by the datasource id. This is one of the demo's verified queries (nl2sql init --demo writes all six):

# curated.yaml
datasources:
  chinook:
    verified_queries:
      - id: top_customers_by_revenue
        description: "Customers ranked by invoiced revenue in a calendar year"
        questions:
          - "Who are our top {n} customers by revenue in {year}?"
          - "Best {n} customers in {year}"
        params:
          n:    { type: int, default: 10, min: 1, max: 100 }
          year: { type: int, min: 2000, max: 2100, example: 2012 }
        sql: |
          SELECT c.CustomerId,
                 c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS customer,
                 c.Country,
                 ROUND(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 2) AS revenue
          FROM Customer c
          JOIN Invoice i      ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
          JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
          WHERE CAST(strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) = :year
          GROUP BY c.CustomerId, customer, c.Country
          ORDER BY revenue DESC, c.CustomerId
          LIMIT :n
    metrics: []

docs.title: A verified query
docs.text: Key Required Meaning id yes A slug: lower-case letters, digits and _, starting with a letter. Unique within its datasource. description yes What the query returns, in a sentence. questions yes, at least one Phrasings the query answers. {name} marks where a parameter goes. params no The parameters, by name. sql yes The query, in the datasource's own SQL dialect.

docs.title: A parameter
docs.text: Key Meaning type int, float, string or date (YYYY-MM-DD). default The value used when the question gives none. A param with no default is required. min, max Bounds, for int, float and date. choices The allowed values, for string. example A typical value, used where a value is needed and there is no default.

docs.title: The SQL
docs.text:
• Write it in the dialect of the datasource it belongs to: the SQLite example above uses strftime, a Postgres datasource would use EXTRACT. It is parsed with the dialect the datasource's adapter declares.
  • Exactly one statement, and a query: a SELECT, a set operation such as UNION, or a WITH around one. No INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, CREATE, DROP, ALTER, SELECT ... INTO or statements the parser cannot type (VACUUM, PRAGMA), anywhere in the tree, a CTE included.
  • Parameters are :name placeholders, and they are exactly the declared params: no placeholder without a param, no param the SQL does not use. Positional ? placeholders are refused. Values are always bound, never pasted into the text, so a value cannot change the shape of the query.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
metrics: (a list of name, description, expression, table) is accepted and checked for shape so the format is fixed, but nothing uses it yet.

Every key is checked: a misspelt one (descripton:) is an error, not ignored.

docs.title: Checking the file
docs.text:
nl2sql curated validate                              # ./nl2sql.yaml, or NL2SQL_CONFIG
nl2sql --config prod/nl2sql.yaml curated validate

Building the engine runs every startup check; a section that fails one exits 1 with the ConfigError. The command then adds the one that needs the index: every table a query reads (CTE names aside) is in its datasource's latest indexed schema, compared case-insensitively. A datasource that has not been indexed yet is skipped for that check, with a note. The command prints a table, one row per query, and exits 1 on any error, so it can run in CI:

                         Verified Queries
┏━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
┃ Datasource ┃ Query                    ┃ Status ┃ Details                            ┃
┡━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
│ chinook    │ top_customers_by_revenue │ OK     │ Verified against the indexed schema │
└────────────┴──────────────────────────┴────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘
Check At startup curated validate YAML parses and every key is known yes yes Every datasource key is a configured datasource yes yes Query ids unique within a datasource yes yes Every {placeholder} in a question is a param, every param is in a question yes yes Defaults, examples, bounds and choices agree with the type yes yes SQL is one read-only query in the datasource's dialect yes yes SQL :name placeholders are exactly the params yes yes Tables the SQL reads are in the indexed schema no yes, when indexed

engine.curated.list(user_context=...) returns the verified queries a caller can reach (used by the dashboard builder).

From Python, the same check is engine.curated, on the engine's own config:

from nl2sql import NL2SQL

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")
report = engine.curated.validate()
if not report.ok:
    for error in report.errors:
        print(error)
    for entry in report.entries:
        print(entry.datasource_id, entry.query_id, entry.status, entry.details)

docs.title: Testing the queries
docs.text:
validate reads the SQL; it does not run it, so a column renamed under a query passes it. nl2sql curated test runs every verified query once against its database:

nl2sql curated test
nl2sql --config prod/nl2sql.yaml curated test

It reads the same config as validate. Each param is bound to its default, else its example; a param with neither fails its query without running it, so give every required param an example. A query that fails the static checks (not read-only, placeholders that do not match the params) is never run. The rest run read-only through their datasource's adapter, the same path a matched question takes, with the values bound and only the first batch of rows fetched. It prints one row per query and exits 1 if any fails, so it can run in CI after a schema change:

                                     Verified Queries
┏━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
┃ Datasource ┃ Query                    ┃ Status ┃ Params          ┃ Details                                      ┃
┡━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
│ chinook    │ top_customers_by_revenue │ PASS   │ n=10, year=2012 │ 10 rows in 0.00 s                            │
│ chinook    │ revenue_by_year          │ FAIL   │                 │ The database rejected the query: no such     │
│            │                          │        │                 │ column: Total                                │
└────────────┴──────────────────────────┴────────┴─────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

From Python it is engine.curated.test(), which returns a report like validate()'s: ok, errors, and one entry per query with its status (PASS or FAIL), params, row_count and details.

docs.title: Indexing the questions
docs.text:
nl2sql index embeds every phrasing of every verified query, and its description, beside the datasource's schema entries. Placeholders are filled first with the param's example, else its default: "Best {n} customers in {year}" is indexed as "Best 10 customers in 2012". The SQL is never indexed.

After editing the curated section, re-index its questions:

nl2sql index --refresh                       # every datasource
nl2sql index --refresh --datasource chinook  # one

--refresh writes the entries again from the stored snapshot and embeds only those whose text changed (here, the verified queries): it reads no schema and makes no model call, so it takes seconds. The datasource must have been indexed once with plain nl2sql index. A plain nl2sql index also picks up the file, and a schema re-index always keeps the verified queries.

Until you re-index, nl2sql doctor and the index status (engine.index.health(), GET /api/v1/index) warn:

Warning: curated.yaml changed for 'chinook' since it was indexed; run `nl2sql index --refresh --datasource chinook`.

It is a warning, not a failure: the index stays ok, because the stale entries still name queries that exist.

docs.title: What happens at question time
docs.text:
With the file loaded and at least one verified query in it, every question that executes starts at the curated matcher (node reference):

  1. It searches the indexed phrasings of the verified queries of the datasources the caller's role may read (only the pinned datasource when a request names one), and keeps the best settings.curated.match_top_k queries.
  2. If the best one's similarity is below settings.curated.match_floor, the question goes to the normal pipeline. No model call is made.
  3. Otherwise one model call sees those candidates: each one's datasource.id, description and params (type, bounds, choices, default). Never the SQL. The model picks the one that answers the whole question and gives its parameter values, or answers none_of_these.
  4. Code checks the values against the param specs. A param the question does not give takes its default; a required one missing, or a value out of bounds, sends the question to the normal pipeline.
  5. Every table the SQL reads must be allowed for the role by the policies section. If one is not, the question goes to the normal pipeline, which refuses it the way it always does. The user is never told a verified query exists.
  6. The SQL runs with the values bound by the driver, through the same executor as generated SQL. The row limit is the datasource's row_limit (capped by settings.results.row_limit): the executor stops reading there and marks the result cut, rather than adding a LIMIT to your SQL. The result is saved, paged and exported like any other, and the answer is written from it, told what the numbers mean by the query's description.

A verified answer costs two model calls (the choice and the answer). When anything above does not hold, the run continues as if there were no curated section, and the answer is generated.

Every answer says where it came from, in QueryResult.source (and the REST response):

{"type": "verified", "id": "top_customers_by_revenue", "datasource_id": "chinook", "params": {"n": 5, "year": 2012}}

or {"type": "generated", ...} with the other fields null. The sub-query of a verified answer has plan_source: "verified", its sql is your SQL with its :name placeholders, and its plan is null.

In the playground a verified answer carries a green Verified · top_customers_by_revenue label beside the question, with the bound values in its tooltip. The Plan station says no plan was written and lists the query and its values, the Checks station shows the matcher's three checks (read-only, params, role), and the SQL station shows your SQL as Verified SQL, with its placeholders. A generated answer looks as it always has.

Why a question was not matched is in the run trace: the curated_matcher node's curated_match record lists the candidates and their similarities, the floor, the model's choice and reason, the checked values, and one reason code: not_configured, no_candidates, below_floor, none_of_these, model_failed, unknown_query, param_invalid, param_missing, policy_denied, capability_missing or execution_failed. A verified query that fails to run also adds a warning to the result.

The model for the choice is the curated_matcher agent in the llm section, falling back to the top level.

Parameters are bound by the datasource's adapter. Every built-in adapter binds them; a third-party adapter has to declare SUPPORTS_BOUND_PARAMETERS (SDK), and a verified query with params on one that does not is never run (capability_missing).

docs.title: In the demo
docs.text:
nl2sql init --demo (which nl2sql demo runs the first time) writes curated.yaml with six verified queries on Chinook and includes it from nl2sql.yaml; nl2sql demo indexes their questions with the schema:

Query One of its phrasings Params top_customers_by_revenue "Who are our top {n} customers by revenue in {year}?" n (default 10), year (example 2012) revenue_by_year "What is the total revenue per year?" none monthly_revenue "What was the monthly revenue in {year}?" year (example 2013) sales_by_country "What are total sales by country?" none best_selling_genres "Which genre sells the most tracks?" n (default 5) top_artists_by_tracks_sold "Who are the top {n} artists by tracks sold?" n (default 10)

Two of the guided questions, "What is the total revenue per year?" and "Which genre sells the most tracks?", are phrasings of these, so with a key they come back verified. Check and run them with nl2sql --config nl2sql-demo/nl2sql.yaml curated validate and nl2sql --config nl2sql-demo/nl2sql.yaml curated test.

The keyless demo (a hosted Space with no key, or nl2sql demo replaying recordings) answers from recorded model answers, and those include the matcher's VerifiedQueryChoice for every guided question. So without a key, "What is the total revenue per year?", "Which genre sells the most tracks?", "How many customers do we have, by country?" and "How many purchases were there per month in 2013?" come back verified, and the rest generated.

docs.title: Preferred tables
docs.text: Preferred tables are not in the curated section: they are a preferred_tables list on a datasource, naming views or tables (built by the data team, never by the package) the planner should reach for first. See Datasources: preferred tables.

docs.title: From feedback to verified queries
docs.text:
A thumbs-up on a generated answer is a candidate verified query: a real question, and SQL a person said was right. engine.feedback.record(trace_id, "up", user_context=...) files it in the review queue as a verified_query proposal; it reaches the curated section only when an admin accepts it. Rating needs a kept trace, so on the default settings.traces.mode: on_failure only failed runs can be rated; set always to rate successful ones.

nl2sql review list --kind verified_query --as admin
nl2sql review show <id> --as admin
nl2sql review accept <id> --as admin

The proposal's change is an entry in the curated section's shape, for the datasource the run used:

id: how_many_customers_are_in_brazil
description: 'TODO: say what this query returns. ...'
questions:
- How many customers are in Brazil?
sql: |
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM Customer WHERE Country = 'Brazil'
  • id comes from the question: lower case, words joined by _, at most 60 characters, q_ in front when it would start with a digit.
  • questions holds the question as it was asked, as the one phrasing.
  • sql is the run's generated SQL, exactly as it ran. Every value in it is literal ('Brazil' above): the proposal has no params.
  • description is a placeholder.

The same question and SQL is one proposal however often it is rated; a new SQL for the same question supersedes the open one. These file nothing: thumbs-down ratings, answers that came from a verified query already, runs that did not succeed, runs with no SQL or more than one statement, runs on more than one datasource, and ratings recorded before the feedback table kept the datasource (see Feedback and Signals).

Accepting is the approval. Before accepting, a reviewer checks the SQL answers the question and, with edits (or by editing the change in a review file), writes the description, turns the values a reader would change into {params} in the question and :params in the SQL with a params: entry, drops the row-cap LIMIT the generator added unless the question asks for it, and adds other phrasings. Accept then runs the curated checks on the edited section, rewrites the section's own file (curated: {file: curated.yaml}) in canonical form, swaps the engine's curated answers and refreshes that datasource's curated index entries, so the next question can match it. An inline section, or a config built in code, is never written: export the proposals and edit by hand. See The review queue.

Accept rewrites curated.yaml

The rewrite is canonical: keys in the models' order, datasources and params sorted by name, SQL as literal blocks, under a fixed header. Comments in curated.yaml are not kept; write remarks in a query's description. A file edited since the engine loaded it is never overwritten: accept refuses with FILE_CHANGED.

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:

  • The section in the config: Curated in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/config/models.py
  • Index entries and the change hash: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/curated.py
  • Startup check: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/runtime.py
  • Facade: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/api/curated_api.py
  • Command: nl2sql-cli/src/nl2sql_cli/commands/curated.py
  • The demo's verified queries: CHINOOK_VERIFIED_QUERIES in packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/datasets/chinook.py
  • The playground badge: verifiedSource() in nl2sql-ui/src/outputs/results.js

docs.title: Datasource Configuration
docs.text:
The datasources section of nl2sql.yaml lists the databases the engine can query. nl2sql init writes it as a folder, one file per datasource, so each team can own its own database's file:

# nl2sql.yaml
datasources: { file: datasources/ }

# datasources/sales.yaml   (the id defaults to the file name: "sales")
type: postgres
description: Orders, customers and revenue for the EU shop.
connection:
  host: db.internal
  port: 5432
  database: sales
  user: nl2sql
  password: "${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD}"
limits: { row_limit: 1000, timeout_ms: 8000, max_bytes: 10485760 }
index:
  exclude_tables: ["*.*_audit"]
preferred_tables: [public.revenue_daily, v_monthly_sales]
domains: [revenue, customers, orders]
sample_questions:
  - What was revenue by region last quarter?
  - Which customers placed the most orders this year?
required: true

The section can also be a file holding the list (datasources: {file: datasources.yaml}), or the list written inline in nl2sql.yaml. An empty list is valid: the apps add datasources at runtime.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Default Meaning id the file name in a folder, otherwise required The datasource's id. In a folder, if it is given it must equal the file name. type required The adapter: sqlite, duckdb, postgres, mysql, mssql, or an adapter a plugin registers. A misspelt or uninstalled one is a ConfigError with "did you mean" and the install hint. description none What is in the database. The resolver's answerability check reads it, so write one. connection {} The adapter's connection settings, validated against its connection model; see Connection. Every value may be a ${provider:key} reference and keeps it until the adapter is built. A relative SQLite or DuckDB database is relative to nl2sql.yaml. limits none row_limit, timeout_ms, max_bytes; see Limits. index everything What of the database is indexed; see Index. preferred_tables [] Tables or views the planner should reach for first. See Preferred tables. sample_questions [] Questions the datasource answers. Each is indexed as an entry of its own (schema.datasource_example), one of the signals routing votes with. domains [] A routing hint written by people. Routing does not read it yet. required false engine.check() fails (EngineNotReady) when this datasource cannot connect, and the CLI and the demo refuse to start. nl2sql-api starts anyway and /ready answers 503 not_ready. See Startup.

In Python, Datasource(id=..., adapter=MyAdapter(...)) passes a built adapter object instead of type.

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
Each adapter declares its connection keys in a connection model, and the keys are strict: a key the model does not have is an error when the engine is built, with the field it was probably meant to be.

datasources[0].connection: connection.hostname: unknown key 'hostname'. Did you mean 'host'?
Adapter Keys sqlite database (the file) duckdb database (the file, or :memory:) postgres host, port (5432), database, user, password, sslmode (disable, prefer (default), require, verify-full) mysql host, port (3306), database, user, password mssql host, port (1433), database, user, password, driver (the newest ODBC Driver N for SQL Server installed), trusted_connection (false), encrypt (true), trust_server_certificate (false)

postgres, mysql and mssql also take pool, the connection pool:

connection:
  host: db.internal
  # ...
  pool: { size: 5, max_overflow: 0, timeout_s: 30, recycle_s: 1800 }   # the defaults
Key Default Meaning size 5 Connections kept open max_overflow 0 Extra connections allowed under load timeout_s 30 How long a query waits for a free connection recycle_s 1800 A connection older than this is replaced

With no overflow, size is also the most queries NL2SQL runs against that database at once, so it cannot overload a production server. A SQLite or DuckDB file has no pool.

In Python, connection may also be the adapter's model, used as given:

from nl2sql.adapters.postgres.adapter import PostgresConnection

Datasource(id="sales", type="postgres",
           connection=PostgresConnection(host="db.internal", database="sales", user="nl2sql",
                                         password=os.environ["SALES_DB_PASSWORD"]))

The model's JSON Schema (PostgresConnection.model_json_schema()) describes the form for connecting that database; a password is "format": "password".

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
limits:
  row_limit: 1000       # the most rows one sub-query returns
  timeout_ms: 8000      # the longest one statement may run
  max_bytes: 10485760
  • timeout_ms: every built-in adapter enforces it (SQL Server rounds up to whole seconds; SQLite stops a statement with a progress handler). Every session is read-only where the database allows it, with no setting; SQL Server cannot, and check() warns. See each adapter page for how.
  • row_limit: unset, it is settings.results.row_limit (100,000); set higher, settings.results.row_limit still bounds it. A result that reaches it is flagged as truncated and the answer says so. It is applied before results are combined, so a join input that reaches it is refused (RESULT_TRUNCATED) and a union input that reaches it is flagged with a warning; see row cap before a combine.
  • max_bytes: passed to the adapter.

There is one place for each limit: the 0.4 options: bag and the top-level spellings are gone.

docs.title: Index
docs.text:
index says what of the database is indexed. Every key is optional, and an unknown key is an error.

index:
  include_schemas: [public, reporting]
  exclude_tables: ["*.*_audit", "public.tmp_*"]
  exclude_columns: ["public.customers.email"]
Key Default Meaning include_schemas every schema but the database's system schemas Schema globs exclude_schemas none Schema globs, applied after include include_tables, exclude_tables all, none schema.table globs; a pattern with no schema is an error with the fix ('*.tmp_*') exclude_columns none schema.table.column globs: the column is neither indexed nor profiled. This is not access control: use policies. profile stats catalog: names, types, keys, comments and the catalog's row estimates, with no query against table data. stats: also each column's null share, distinct count and min/max. sample_values false Store each text column's values: every one when there are 50 or fewer distinct, otherwise the five most frequent. Off by default, since values reach the index, the prompts and the model provider. The demo (NL2SQL.demo(), nl2sql init --demo) turns it on. max_profile_rows 1,000,000 A table estimated above this is profiled from the catalog only, and the index build reports it

Every glob ignores case, and an exclude wins over an include. A SQLite database has one schema, main.

The scope is applied before any query that reads a schema, so an excluded schema costs nothing. A row count is the catalog's estimate where the database keeps one (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, DuckDB); otherwise, under stats, the rows are counted. What a table or column was indexed without (a statistics query the database rejected, a table over max_profile_rows) is an issue: nl2sql index prints it, and engine.index.build() returns it in the datasource's stats under issues. See SQLAlchemy adapters for how the built-in adapters read a schema.

docs.title: Preferred tables
docs.text:
The package never creates a view. The data team creates it in the database, lists it under preferred_tables, and runs nl2sql index; every built-in adapter snapshots views as well as tables (PostgreSQL materialized views are not read). At question time the schema retriever lists preferred tables first and marks them "preferred": true in the schema the planner sees, and the planner is told to plan against a preferred table when it answers the question:

  • When the whole schema is sent (settings.retrieval.full_snapshot_max_tables tables or fewer), every preferred table is in it, first.
  • Otherwise the retrieved tables are re-ordered so preferred ones come first, and a preferred table the search scored but did not pick is added when its similarity is within 0.05 of the least similar pick.

RBAC is unchanged: a preferred table the role may not read loses its data like any other table, and the validator refuses a plan that reads it.

A name that is not in the indexed schema is a warning, not an error: nl2sql doctor and the index status (engine.index.health(), GET /api/v1/index) print "Preferred table 'v_x' of 'chinook' is not in the indexed schema". The usual cause is a view created after the last index; re-index the datasource.

docs.title: When a datasource fails to start
docs.text:
A datasource the engine cannot build (an unknown type, a missing driver, an invalid connection config, a ${...} reference that does not resolve) stops it: building the engine raises one ConfigError that names every such datasource and the reason. Building never connects, so this needs no database.

A datasource that cannot connect is found by engine.check() (see Public Facade → Lifecycle), and does not stop the engine unless it is required. The others stay routed, and the broken one is marked unavailable:

  • the log has an error: Datasource 'sales' is unavailable: <reason>;
  • check() reports it failed at stage connect, with a fix;
  • engine.datasources.list() (and GET /api/v1/datasources) shows it with status: "failed" and the reason, and nothing is routed to it;
  • the index status (engine.index.health(), GET /api/v1/index) carries the same sentence as a warning;
  • a query with datasource_id set to it, and nl2sql index or engine.index.build([...]) naming it, fail with that reason.

check() raises EngineNotReady when a required: true datasource fails, or when datasources are configured and none is ready. A later check(), or engine.datasources.test(id), that connects routes the datasource again.

nl2sql doctor prints the same check() report. After check(), engine.policies.validate() reports a role that names an unavailable datasource as UNAVAILABLE.

A secret provider that cannot start is different: it fails startup. See Secrets → When a provider fails to start.

docs.title: Saving a datasource
docs.text:
engine.datasources.add(...) changes the running engine only. To keep a datasource, save it:

engine.datasources.add(Datasource(id="sales", type="postgres", connection={"host": "db.internal",
                                  "database": "sales", "user": "app", "password": "${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD}"}))
engine.datasources.save("sales", by=admin)          # -> <folder>/datasources/sales.yaml

save writes that one datasource as datasources/<id>.yaml beside the nl2sql.yaml the engine was loaded from, and nothing else. It needs:

  • an admin by (policies.admin_roles; under allow_all any caller) - a caller without one gets PermissionError;
  • an engine loaded from a nl2sql.yaml whose datasources section is a folder (datasources: { file: datasources/ }, one <id>.yaml each, as nl2sql init writes it). An engine built in code, or with the datasources inline in nl2sql.yaml, or one whose folder cannot be written, raises ReviewError with code NOT_WRITABLE (not a ValueError; the REST API answers 403).

The file is checked before it is replaced. The engine records each datasource file's SHA-256 when it loads the config, as an accept does for the glossary. If the file changed on disk since (somebody edited it), save raises ReviewError with code FILE_CHANGED and the fix "reload the engine", and writes nothing. A datasource that is new to the engine must not have a file yet. The file is written to a temporary file beside it and renamed; it publishes datasource.saved (audited), and never connects to the database or calls a model.

A secret is never written into YAML. Every secret field is written as a reference:

Its value Written as A reference (${env:VAR}, ${vault:path}) The reference, unchanged A literal, with save(..., env_file=True) ${env:NL2SQL_<ID>_<KEY>} in the YAML and NL2SQL_<ID>_<KEY>=value in the .env beside nl2sql.yaml A literal, otherwise Refused: SecretValueInConfig naming the field, with the fix "pass ${env:VAR} or a secret provider reference"

A connection field is a secret when its key says so (password, secret, token, api_key) or its adapter's connection model declares it secret (SecretStr, "format": "password" in the schema): a plugin's private_key or credentials field goes to the .env too, whatever its name. The name is NL2SQL_ plus the datasource id and the key in upper case, every character that is not a letter or digit as _: NL2SQL_SALES_PASSWORD. Two fields that map to one name are refused with both fields named: a value is never overwritten. That covers another datasource's reference and the names the writer gives the rest of the config, so a datasource called llm with an api_key field cannot replace NL2SQL_LLM_API_KEY (the LLM's and each agent's key and headers, the embeddings key and each secret provider's settings). .env keeps every other line, is created when needed, and .gitignore is made to list it. A value that holds a line break (\n, \r, \x0b, \x0c, \x1c to \x1e, \x85, , ) is refused, as it could start a line of its own. Saves run one at a time, so two at once both keep their .env line. Nothing is read from or written to os.environ: the entry points load the .env (nl2sql.load_env_file), and it never overrides a variable that is already set.

The id becomes a file name, so it is limited to letters, digits, _, - and . (up to 128 characters, starting with a letter or digit, not ending in a dot) and may not be a Windows device name (con, prn, aux, nul, com1-com9, lpt1-lpt9, with or without an extension); anything else is a ValueError naming the id.

The same rules write a whole new project: nl2sql.config.write_project(config, folder, env_file=False) writes any data Config as nl2sql init lays it out (a file per section, datasources/<id>.yaml, knowledge.yaml and an empty glossary.yaml), with the secrets of the llm, embeddings and secrets sections and of every connection handled as above (NL2SQL_LLM_API_KEY, NL2SQL_LLM_AGENTS_AST_PLANNER_API_KEY, NL2SQL_EMBEDDINGS_API_KEY, NL2SQL_SECRETS_VAULT_TOKEN). It never overwrites a file, refuses a section that holds an object instead of data (an adapter, store, hook or chat model object) and loads what it wrote before it returns. nl2sql.config.starter_config(llm=..., path=...) is a config with no datasources, allow_all policies, local embeddings and a yaml knowledge source; nl2sql.config.write_env_values(folder, values) writes the .env.

Over REST, POST /api/v1/datasources with "save": true calls the same method; see Datasource API.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Use ${env:VAR} for environment variables, or ${provider:key} for a secret from a provider in the secrets section.
  • The keys under connection are the adapter's; see Connection.
  • From Python, engine.datasources.add(Datasource(...)) adds one to a running engine (built, not connected), engine.datasources.save(id, by=admin) writes it to datasources/<id>.yaml (Saving a datasource), and engine.datasources.remove(id) takes one out; nl2sql-api's POST /api/v1/datasources takes the same shape as JSON, and POST /api/v1/datasources/test and GET /api/v1/datasource-types are the Connect a database form's other two calls.

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
The embeddings section of nl2sql.yaml chooses how schema entries are embedded during nl2sql index, and how questions are embedded during retrieval. nl2sql init writes the key-free local provider:

# embeddings.yaml
provider: local
Field Default Meaning provider required local, openai, openai_compatible, or a provider a plugin registers. model the provider's default The embedding model. Required for openai_compatible. api_key the provider's standard variable A ${env:VAR} or ${provider:key} reference, resolved when the embedder is built. base_url none The server's URL, for openai and openai_compatible. An error for local. dimension the provider's The model's output dimension. Write it only when the provider does not know it and you want to skip the probe (see Model and dimension).

In Python, Embeddings(instance=MyEmbeddings()) passes a LangChain embeddings object instead of a provider name. Each engine builds its own embedder once.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
provider Model Dimension API key base_url local all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (ONNX, bundled with chromadb); the only model 384 none not allowed openai model, default text-embedding-3-small known for OpenAI's own models (1536, or 3072 for text-embedding-3-large) api_key, else OPENAI_API_KEY optional openai_compatible model, required dimension:, else probed api_key if the server needs one required

An openai section with no key resolving, an openai_compatible section without model or base_url, or a local section with a base_url, is a ConfigError when the engine is built, naming the problem.

Notes on the local provider:

  • No extra dependency. The model ships with chromadb, which the engine already depends on for its built-in chroma index store.
  • One-time download. The first indexing run downloads roughly 79 MB of ONNX model files into a local cache directory. Expect a pause of up to a few minutes; a log line is emitted before the download starts.
  • Embeddings only. This removes the API key requirement from the embedding step. It does not make querying key-free: answering a question still needs a chat model (see LLMs).

docs.title: openai_compatible
docs.text:
Any server with an OpenAI-style embeddings API: Azure OpenAI's v1 endpoint, Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM, LM Studio or a company gateway. There is no Azure-specific provider; Azure uses this one.

# embeddings.yaml: Ollama
provider: openai_compatible
base_url: http://ollama:11434/v1
model: nomic-embed-text
dimension: 768            # optional: skips the probe

# embeddings.yaml: Azure OpenAI's v1 endpoint
provider: openai_compatible
base_url: https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/
api_key: "${env:AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY}"
model: embed-prod          # the Azure deployment name
dimension: 1536
  • No key variable. OPENAI_API_KEY is never read: that key belongs to OpenAI, not to your server. Write api_key (usually ${env:...}) if the server needs one; without it a placeholder is sent, because the OpenAI client refuses to start without a key.
  • Text, not tokens. The text is sent as is. (The openai provider sends OpenAI's token ids, which other servers' models cannot read.)

docs.title: Model and dimension
docs.text:
The engine needs the embedder's model and dimension to know which index it reads and writes. A provider reports them as EmbeddingInfo(provider, model, dimension):

  • local and openai with OpenAI's own models know the dimension.
  • openai_compatible knows it only when you write dimension:.
  • An instance reports its model attribute (or its class name) and the dimension: of the section, if any.

When the dimension is unknown, the engine embeds the text "dimension probe" once, the first time it needs the dimension, and keeps the answer for the engine's life. Building the engine never calls the model. Writing dimension: skips that one call; it must be what the model returns.

docs.title: Writing a provider
docs.text:
A plugin implements nl2sql.embeddings.EmbeddingsProvider, interface version 2, and registers it under the nl2sql.embeddings entry point group or with registry.add_embeddings (see the registry):

from nl2sql.embeddings import EmbeddingInfo


class MyProvider:
    interface_version = 2
    default_model = "my-model"
    requires = ("my_sdk",)
    install_hint = 'pip install "nl2sql-my-embeddings"'

    def create(self, cfg):
        """The LangChain embeddings object for ``cfg``. No model call; ValueError for a bad section."""
        ...

    def describe(self, cfg):
        """What ``create(cfg)`` embeds with. None as the dimension means "probe it"."""
        return EmbeddingInfo("mine", cfg.model or self.default_model, cfg.dimension)

docs.title: Switching providers
docs.text: Switching providers or models needs a re-index, and nothing more. Different embedding models produce different vectors, so each model has its own index namespace, nl2sql__<model slug>__<dimension>. After a change the new model's namespace is empty: check() and nl2sql doctor report the index missing, and nl2sql index builds it. The old model's namespace is kept, so switching back finds it built; nl2sql index prune drops the ones you no longer need. See Storage → The index.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: A hook is your code, called at six fixed points of every run. At each point it may let the run go on, change what the run carries (before the validator only), stop it, or (at execute.before) ask for a person's approval. Hooks apply to every run: a generated answer and a verified query, from the Python API, the CLI and nl2sql-api alike. None ships built in.

docs.title: The six points
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  Q["question"] --> P1(["run.before"])
  P1 --> CM["curated matcher"]
  CM -->|"no match"| RES["datasource resolver"]
  RES --> P2(["datasources.after"])
  P2 --> DEC["decomposer"]
  DEC --> PL["planner, or the plan cache"]
  PL --> P3(["plan.after"])
  P3 --> VAL["logical validator"]
  VAL --> GEN["generator"]
  GEN --> P4(["execute.before"])
  CM -->|"verified query"| P4
  P4 --> EX["executor"]
  EX --> P5(["execute.after"])
  P5 --> AGG["aggregator"]
  AGG --> ANS["answer synthesizer"]
  ANS --> P6(["answer.after"])
Point When The hook sees (beyond question, user, trace_id) It may answer run.before Once, before the first step datasource_id, execute Allow, Modify(question=...), Deny datasources.after The resolver chose its datasources datasource_ids Allow, Modify(datasource_ids=...) (a subset only), Deny plan.after Per sub-query and attempt, on the planner's or the plan cache's plan sub_query, plan Allow, Modify(plan=...), Deny execute.before Per sub-query, before the adapter runs the SQL datasource_id, sql, params, tables Allow, Deny, NeedsApproval execute.after Per sub-query, after it ran result: columns, row count, truncated; never rows Allow, Deny answer.after The answer is written, before it is returned; with answer=False there is no answer and final_answer is None, but the point still runs final_answer, results (summaries) Allow, Deny

tables are datasource.schema.table. A field a point does not have is None. The context is frozen and holds copies of the run's plan, caller and values: a hook that changes one in place changes nothing. A hook changes the run only through Modify. ctx.conversation_id is set when the run is a conversation's turn.

Modify before the validator, deny only after. A plan a hook changed is validated like any other, so a hook can never slip in what the policies or the validator refuse. datasources.after may only remove datasources; the resolver checks what is left against the caller's role again. After the validator nothing may change the SQL, the plan or the result.

The answer sanity checks' probes are not hooked. After a sub-query runs, the executor may send small checking queries of its own (does a filter value exist, did a join repeat rows; see the executor's sanity checks). They run outside execute.before and execute.after. So when any hook is attached at execute.before, no probe runs at all: SQL a hook gates never has unseen SQL beside it. settings.pipeline.sanity_checks: false turns the checks off entirely.

Eval seeding is hooked; regenerate is not. engine.evals.seed (Benchmark your own database) runs SQL a model proposed, so each draft's SQL passes execute.before and execute.after like a question's: every hook sees it (an approval hook, a cost guard), and a deny, a hook failure or a NeedsApproval drops the draft (dropped_hooked). execute.after gets a summary of the first row only (seeding reads one row to see that the query returns any), so its row_count is a floor and truncated is true. engine.evals.regenerate runs SQL a person reviewed and approved (a suite's gold sql and alt_sql) and calls no hook.

The verified path has no routing and no plan, so only run.before, execute.before, execute.after and answer.after apply. A deny there ends the run; it does not fall back to the generated path. A plan-only run (execute=False) never reaches the execute.* points.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Order. Hooks run in the order of the hooks list. A Modify replaces the fields it sets and the next hook sees the result. The first Deny (or NeedsApproval) ends the point; later hooks are not asked.
  • A deny ends the run with the error HOOK_DENIED (never retried), whose message is the hook's reason. A run a hook ended carries none of its data: no answer, no rows, no artifact references, no result manifest, and its saved results cannot be read by its trace_id either (see What withholding guarantees).
  • Streaming. While any hook is attached at answer.after, stream_query does not stream the answer as it is written (no answer.delta events), and holds the result.manifest event until the hooks allowed the answer; on a deny it is never sent. The answer arrives whole in run.finished.
  • A sub-query deny. At a per-sub-query point (plan.after, execute.before, execute.after), Deny(reason, scope="sub_query") drops only that sub-query: the run goes on without it and the answer's warnings say what went unanswered. A sub-query that feeds a join or compare cannot be dropped alone, so its whole group is dropped. If nothing is left, the run ends with HOOK_DENIED.
  • Hooks fail closed. An exception, a return value that is not a decision, or a decision the point does not allow (a Modify at execute.before, a NeedsApproval at plan.after) is a hook error: the run ends with HOOK_FAILED, whose message names only the hook and the point; the exception's text goes to the log and to hook.decision, never to the caller. With on_error: open, an exception is logged and counts as Allow; a disallowed decision still fails, because it is a bug in the hook, not an outage.
  • Approval. NeedsApproval at execute.before (on the generated or the verified path) ends the run with status: "needs_approval", the error NEEDS_APPROVAL and an ApprovalRequest per pending sub-query in approvals_needed. Re-running the question as the asker with approvals=[Approval(request=..., by=<the approver>)] pins what was approved and generates the SQL again; the engine accepts the approval only if the request is unedited, the question and the asker are this run's, the hash of the new SQL matches, and the approver holds one of the hook's approver_roles (by default policies.admin_roles). An accepted approval counts as Allow (hook.decision with decision: "approved" and the approver), and the next hook at the point still runs. A hook also sees the run's approvals as ctx.approvals. See Query API → Approval.
  • Timeouts are the hook's own; the pipeline's timeout_s bounds the run.
  • Events. Every hook asked publishes hook.decision (hook, point, decision, reason, sub_query_id, approver, seconds).
  • The plan cache keeps the planner's plan, never a hook's change of it; plan.after runs on every cache hit, so a change applies afresh on each run and stops the moment the hook config changes.

docs.title: What withholding guarantees
docs.text:
A run a hook ended (HOOK_DENIED, HOOK_FAILED, NEEDS_APPROVAL, COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) returns none of its data, and its saved results cannot be read by its trace_id: engine.results.manifest, page, csv and chart and the REST results routes answer ResultNotFound (404), from run_query, stream_query, nl2sql eval and trace replay alike. This holds while the run is still going too, although a streaming caller has the trace_id from run.started.

Every read of a run's results goes through its manifest, and the manifest is written only once no hook can end the run any more:

  • While a hook is attached at answer.after, the aggregator saves the results but not the manifest. The node that asks answer.after writes it when the hooks allow. A run they deny, or that ends earlier, never has one. If that write fails, the run fails.
  • Without such a hook, nothing can end the run after the aggregator, so the aggregator writes the manifest itself, as soon as the results are saved.
  • A hook at any earlier point that ends the run ends it before the aggregator runs, so there is no manifest.

The parquet files of a run with no manifest stay until retention purges them, but nothing reads them. With a hook at answer.after, a run that crashed or timed out before the hooks ruled has no manifest either, and neither has a run whose answer model failed: the hooks never saw its results, so it returns no result_manifest, no artifact_refs and no rows, and stream_query sends no result.manifest event. Without such a hook that run keeps its results, as nothing was left to withhold them for. The run's trace records the error that ended it, without rows. An approved re-run is a new run with a new trace_id, read as any other.

docs.title: Built-in hooks
docs.text: One hook is built in: policy.cost, the cost rule. The engine builds it from policies.cost (or a role's cost), not from the hooks list, and puts it first at execute.before, ahead of every hook you configure, so an over-limit query never reaches your hook. Its approvers are policies.admin_roles. Its Deny ends the run with COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED rather than HOOK_DENIED, and its hook.decision events name policy.cost. Without a cost block it is not built, and execute.before is as you configured it.

docs.title: Write one
docs.text:
# corp_hooks.py: a hook that keeps the payroll database out of the afternoon.
from datetime import datetime
from typing import ClassVar

from pydantic import BaseModel

from nl2sql.hooks import Allow, Deny, HookContext


class QuietHoursConfig(BaseModel):
    datasource: str                 # the datasource it guards
    from_hour: int = 12             # local time
    to_hour: int = 18


class QuietHours:
    interface_version: ClassVar[int] = 1
    config_model: ClassVar[type] = QuietHoursConfig
    points: ClassVar[frozenset] = frozenset({"execute.before"})

    def __init__(self, cfg: QuietHoursConfig) -> None:
        self.cfg = cfg

    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg: QuietHoursConfig) -> "QuietHours":
        return cls(cfg)

    def __call__(self, ctx: HookContext):
        busy = self.cfg.from_hour <= datetime.now().hour < self.cfg.to_hour
        if ctx.datasource_id == self.cfg.datasource and busy:
            return Deny(reason=f"{ctx.datasource_id} is closed to questions until "
                               f"{self.cfg.to_hour}:00.", scope="sub_query")
        return Allow()

Register it, either in code or as an entry point in your package:

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, Registry

registry = Registry.default()
registry.add_hook("quiet_hours", QuietHours)       # or @registry.hook("quiet_hours")
engine = NL2SQL.from_config(registry=registry)

[project.entry-points."nl2sql.hooks"]
quiet_hours = "corp_hooks:QuietHours"

docs.title: Configure it
docs.text:
# nl2sql.yaml
hooks: { file: hooks.yaml }

# hooks.yaml: a list; order matters
- type: quiet_hours
  points: [execute.before]        # a subset of the hook's own points; all of them by default
  on_error: closed                # closed (the default) | open
  approver_roles: [dba]           # who may approve its NeedsApproval; default policies.admin_roles
  datasource: payroll             # the hook's own keys, checked by its config_model

A point the hook does not declare, an unknown type or a key its config_model rejects is a ConfigError when the engine is built, naming hooks[<i>]. In code, a HookConfig or any callable object works:

from nl2sql import Config, HookConfig
from nl2sql.hooks import Allow, Modify

def tag_year(ctx):
    return Modify(question=ctx.question + " (calendar year)") if ctx.point == "run.before" else Allow()

tag_year.points = frozenset({"run.before"})
Config(..., hooks=[HookConfig(type="quiet_hours", datasource="payroll"), tag_year])

An object runs at its points (all six when it has none), named by its name attribute or its function or class name.

Kind Entry point group Interface Version Built-ins hook nl2sql.hooks nl2sql.hooks.Hook 1 none configurable; policy.cost is built in from policies.cost

docs.title: Knowledge
docs.text:
The glossary is what people know about their data and the database does not say: table and column descriptions, synonyms, column roles, units, grains and code values, joins the database does not declare, business terms, prose rules and example questions. It is written in glossary.yaml and read by a knowledge source; the knowledge section lists the sources.

Release 0.8

The engine loads, merges, shows and exports knowledge from release 0.8, and the planner and refiner read it: descriptions, roles, units, grains, code values and glossary joins in the schema block, matched terms and rules in [BUSINESS_CONTEXT]. It reaches the index too: the chosen descriptions, the terms, the joins and the examples are index entries, and nl2sql index --refresh brings them up to date after an edit without reading the schema, and the schema retriever.

docs.title: The section
docs.text:
# nl2sql.yaml
knowledge: { file: knowledge.yaml }

# knowledge.yaml: a list, in precedence order
- type: yaml
  path: glossary.yaml             # relative to nl2sql.yaml
- type: corp_catalog              # a plugin; its config_model checks the rest
  url: "${env:CATALOG_URL}"

from nl2sql import Config, KnowledgeSourceConfig

Config(..., knowledge=[KnowledgeSourceConfig(type="yaml", path="glossary.yaml"), MySource()])
Rule Detail No section No knowledge: the pipeline is 0.7's. nl2sql init writes knowledge.yaml naming one yaml source and a glossary.yaml with one empty block per datasource; nl2sql init --demo writes the demo glossary. Loaded at build and on reload only Each source's load() runs when the engine is built and on engine.knowledge.reload(), never during a run. Fails closed at build A source that cannot be built or loaded, a missing glossary.yaml, or a text longer than settings.knowledge.item_max_chars is a ConfigError naming the source and the item. Fails open on reload A reload that fails keeps the previous knowledge live; the source's error says why. A config built in code A relative path is read from the current folder. Objects skip the registry A source object in code (one with load) is used as given, named by its type attribute or its class.

docs.title: glossary.yaml
docs.text:
version: 1
datasources:
  chinook:
    tables:
      Invoice:
        description: One row per customer invoice. Total includes tax.
      InvoiceLine:
        description: One row per track sold on an invoice.
        notes: Refunds are not recorded anywhere.     # for people; never sent to a model
    columns:
      Invoice.Total:
        description: Invoice total in US dollars, tax included.
        synonyms: [invoice amount, bill total]
        role: money
        unit: USD
      Invoice.InvoiceDate:
        grain: day                                   # role: date is derived from the type
      Track.MediaTypeId:
        role: enum
        values: {"1": MPEG audio file, "2": Protected AAC audio file}
    joins:
      - from: Track.MediaTypeId
        to: MediaType.MediaTypeId
        cardinality: many-to-one
    terms:
      - term: revenue
        synonyms: [sales, turnover]
        definition: Sum of InvoiceLine.UnitPrice times InvoiceLine.Quantity. Excludes tax.
        columns: [InvoiceLine.UnitPrice, InvoiceLine.Quantity]
    rules:
      - id: no_test_customers
        text: Customers whose email ends in @example.com are test accounts; leave them out of counts and sums.
        tables: [Customer]
    examples:
      - Which genres sell best in Germany?
Item Fields A table description, notes A column (table.column) description, notes, synonyms, role (identifier, enum, money, quantity, date, text), unit, grain (second to year), values (a code, written as a string, and its meaning; on role: enum only) A join from, to (table.column, or a list of them for a composite key), cardinality (default unknown), notes A term term, synonyms, definition, columns, tables A rule id (a slug, unique in its datasource), text, tables (empty: every sub-query on the datasource) An example a question

Every model is strict: an unknown key is an error. Every text is at most settings.knowledge.item_max_chars (500) characters; a longer one is a load error naming the item, so nothing is silently cut. Every name (a table, a column, a code, a rule id, a term's tables and columns) is at most 255 characters, and the yaml source reads a glossary file of at most 5 MB. notes is for people: it is shown by knowledge show and never sent to a model.

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
A table is named as preferred_tables names it: the bare name or schema.table, case ignored. A column is table.column or schema.table.column. Names are resolved against the datasource's indexed schema when the knowledge is used, not when it is loaded:

Case What happens Resolves to one table or column Used Resolves to nothing (a typo, a dropped column) Not used; a problem in knowledge show, never an error in a run A bare name matching tables in two schemas Not used; the problem says to write schema.table A join whose two sides' types cannot be compared (a date against a number or a boolean) Not used; the problem names both types

A schema drift check (engine.index.check) lists the glossary items that named a dropped table or column in its impact's glossary_items.

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text:
Several sources are merged in config order. A single value (a description, a role, a unit) is the first source's that sets it; lists (synonyms, terms, rules, joins, examples) are unioned, a duplicate (the same term name, rule id or join, case ignored) kept from the first. Each item records the source it came from.

A table or column then has at most one description, and each column one role, chosen in this order:

Origin Where it is kept Who wrote it knowledge A knowledge source, in config order A person database The table or column comment the adapter read The data owner, in the database derived Nowhere: computed from the schema. A role only: identifier for a primary or foreign key column, date for a temporal type The schema itself

Each datasource's merged knowledge has a digest (the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON), shown by knowledge show and published by knowledge.loaded.

docs.title: Who sees what
docs.text:
