The caller is answered within about a second of the limit; the run's worker thread winds down in the background (see isolation). plan_cache true Reuse a plan that already passed validation and executed, for the same normalised sub-query intent, datasource and schema version on the same run date, instead of calling the planner LLM. The cached plan is validated again on every use, so RBAC and policy changes still apply. Stored in <storage.path>/state.db; nl2sql cache clear empties it. See Determinism → The plan cache. strict_columns true Treat a column the plan names but the retrieved schema does not have as a blocking, retryable COLUMN_NOT_FOUND error, so the planner is asked again instead of the plan reaching the database. false downgrades it to a warning that lets the plan through once retries are spent. today none The date the planner and refiner are told it is, as an ISO date (2013-12-31). Unset, it is the real date in UTC. Pin it for tests and gold runs whose questions say "this year" or "the last 30 days". A trace records the date its run used, and nl2sql trace replay pins it. It is part of the plan cache key, so a plan made on another date is not reused. retries.max 3 Retry attempts for the SQL agent's refinement loop. retries.base_delay_s 1.0 Base delay between retries, in seconds. retries.max_delay_s 10.0 Longest delay between retries. retries.jitter_s 0.5 Most jitter added to a delay. max_llm_calls 60 The most model calls one question may make, parse retries included; null turns the cap off. 60 covers the largest legitimate run: the resolver, the decomposer, six sub-queries each with a planner call and three refiner and planner retries, the answer, and parse retries. See Per-question caps. max_cost_usd none The most one question may spend, in dollars; null (the default) is no cap. With a cap set, every model the llm section names must have a price, or the engine does not build. See Per-question caps. sanity_checks true The answer sanity checks after each sub-query runs (join fan-out, all-null columns, missing filter values). false turns them all off. Read from release 0.7's sanity checks.

docs.title: Per-question caps
docs.text:
Both caps are checked before each model call, by the question's budget: a call that would be the 61st, or that would start once the question has spent max_cost_usd, is never sent. The calls already in flight finish, so a question can pass the cost cap by the calls in flight: at most one per running sub-query.

A question that reaches a cap ends with status: "stopped", never as a planner error to retry: QueryResult.stop is {limit, value, spent} (limit is max_llm_calls or max_cost_usd), the one error is RUN_LIMIT_REACHED (not retryable) naming the limit and the setting, and the answer says so: "This question reached its limit of 60 model calls (settings.pipeline.max_llm_calls)." The run publishes run.limit_reached, which the caller's stream carries and the audit log records.

nl2sql.limits.Budget(max_llm_calls=..., max_cost_usd=...) is the same check for work that is not a question: make the model calls with budget.callbacks(), and a call over a cap raises LimitReached (with the RunStop in .stop) before it is sent.

docs.title: retrieval
docs.text:
Key Default Description full_snapshot_max_tables 15 When a datasource's schema has at most this many tables, the schema retriever skips vector retrieval and passes the full schema snapshot (every table, every column) to the planner. 0 always uses vector retrieval. table_k 8 Table entries the schema retriever's search keeps for a sub-query (and column entries, when no table matches). planning_k 12 Column and relationship entries of those tables the planner is shown for a sub-query. decomposer_tables 30 Table names the decomposer is shown per datasource; the rest are counted. table_selector true On a schema past full_snapshot_max_tables, one model call per sub-query picks tables from a catalog of every table the caller may read (the table_selector agent), so a table whose name is far from the question's words still arrives. false skips the call; the glossary's tables and the join-path fill still run, and no model is needed. selector_catalog_max 200 Past this many readable tables, the selector's catalog is the nearest this many by vector search, not all of them (about 15,000 tokens at 200, with column names). join_path_max_hops 4 The tables that join the chosen ones are added from the foreign keys and glossary joins when at most this many joins apart; a longer path is not added.

table_k, planning_k and decomposer_tables replace the constants the schema retriever and the resolver had before 0.7 (TABLE_K, PLANNING_K, MAX_DECOMPOSER_TABLES).

How the tables are chosen past the threshold is in the schema retriever's reference.

docs.title: routing
docs.text:
Cross-database routing: which datasources a question goes to, and how far it may spread. The resolver reads candidates, max_datasources and floor_ratio (Routing); the decomposer reads max_sub_queries.

Key Default Description candidates 3 Datasources routing keeps for the answerability check, best by fused score first. max_datasources 3 Datasources one question may use: of those the answerability check accepts, the resolver forwards at most this many, best first. max_sub_queries 6 Sub-queries one question may have. A decomposition over it ends the run with QUESTION_TOO_BROAD. floor_ratio 0.5 A candidate whose best index-entry similarity to the question is under this share of the most similar candidate's is dropped, between 0 and 1. It is on similarity, not on the fused score: with a handful of datasources every reciprocal-rank score is within a few percent of the best. 0 keeps every candidate up to candidates.

docs.title: results
docs.text: Key Default Description row_limit 100000 The most rows one sub-query returns: a resource ceiling baked into the SQL as a LIMIT. A datasource's own limits.row_limit applies when it is lower (the demo datasources set 10000). A result that reaches it is flagged as truncated (QueryResult.truncated, sub_queries[].truncated) and the answer says it was cut. fetch_batch_size 10000 Rows fetched from the database and written to the sub-query's result file at a time, for an adapter that streams (every built-in SQL adapter does). At most one batch is held in memory. See Artifact Store. preview_rows 20 Result rows the answer model sees, with the total row count and the column names. The model writes about the result; it never copies it. See AnswerSynthesizerNode.

docs.title: traces
docs.text: Key Default Description mode on_failure When to write a run trace to <storage.path>/traces/: off, on_failure (errors, a retry, or an incomplete run) or always. See Debugging a Run. sample_rows 50 Result rows kept in a trace. max_field_chars 20000 Longest string kept in a node's recorded inputs and outputs; LLM prompts and responses are never cut.

docs.title: schema
docs.text: Key Default Description max_versions 3 The newest schema snapshots kept per datasource in the state store, besides every version a build pointer names and the one a build just replaced.

docs.title: curated
docs.text:
Key Default Description match_top_k 5 Verified query candidates a question's search returns, one per query. match_floor 0.6 Cosine similarity the best verified query candidate must reach before the model is asked to choose one. Below it the question is answered by the normal pipeline with no model call. See Curated Answers.

Whether curated answers are on is not a setting: the curated section is present or absent.

docs.title: feedback
docs.text: Key Default Description enabled true Let the playground record a thumbs up or down, with an optional note, for a run. Stored in <storage.path>/state.db: question, role, status, SQL, the datasources it ran on, whether the answer was verified or generated, error codes, the model per node and the engine version, never result rows or sample values. nl2sql feedback clear empties it. See Feedback and Signals.

docs.title: knowledge, clarify, profiler and review
docs.text:
Four groups for release 0.8. They are accepted and validated now; the change named with each reads it.

Key Default Description knowledge.item_max_chars 500 The longest one glossary text may be; a longer one is a load error naming the item, so nothing is silently cut. knowledge.block_max_chars 4000 The longest the [BUSINESS_CONTEXT] block of a prompt may be; the lowest-scored terms, then rules, are dropped, and the trace records what was. knowledge.top_k 8 Matched glossary terms kept per sub-query. knowledge.match_floor 0.6 Similarity a term's index entry must reach to the sub-query's intent to match, between 0 and 1. clarify.enabled true Ask which reading was meant when the planner flags a real ambiguity, instead of guessing. profiler.sample_rows 1000 Distinct values one join-overlap probe reads. profiler.max_probes 200 Overlap probes per datasource; the remaining candidates are proposed without one. profiler.time_budget_s 60 Seconds per datasource after which no probe starts. profiler.min_overlap 0.9 A measured overlap under this drops a join candidate, between 0 and 1. profiler.enum_max_distinct 50 The most distinct values a column proposed as an enum may have. profiler.max_cost_usd 0.50 The most one profile(draft=True) call may spend drafting descriptions (profile(draft=True), nl2sql profile --draft). review.max_age_days 365 Decided proposals older than this are purged by engine.storage.purge().

docs.title: charts
docs.text:
Release 0.9. engine.results.chart reads it (Charts).

Key Default Description charts.max_points 1000 The most rows charted. A longer result is read up to this and flagged truncated; a line chart becomes a table rather than drop points silently. charts.max_categories 20 The most categories a bar chart draws; more is a table. charts.max_series 5 The most lines in one line chart (measures, or values of a category split into lines).

docs.title: approvals
docs.text:
Read by stored approval grants (engine.approvals).

Key Default Description approvals.max_age_hours 24 A stored approval request, and the grant on it, expires, and is purged, this long after its last change.

docs.title: conversations and dashboards
docs.text:
These two are sections of nl2sql.yaml of their own, not groups of settings: see Conversations, chat tools, dashboards and MCP.

Key Default Description conversations.context_turns 3 Turns of history the model sees. conversations.max_tool_calls 12 Tool calls the model may make in one turn; after the last it makes one more call with the tools off and must reply. conversations.max_turns 50 Turns in one conversation; the next is refused with CONVERSATION_TOO_LONG. conversations.max_age_days 30 Conversations, and draft dashboards, not updated for this long are deleted by engine.storage.purge(). null keeps them. dashboards.max_tiles 10 Charts in the starter dashboard. dashboards.min_refresh_minutes 15 The shortest refresh schedule; a shorter one is refused. dashboards.schedule_identity_max_age_days 30 A schedule stops when the owner identity saved with it is older than this, until the owner sets it again. answers.max_per_user 100 Saved answers one person may keep (engine.answers); the next save is refused with AnswerLimitReached.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
The storage section of nl2sql.yaml says where the engine keeps its data, and which store keeps each part of it. Only path is required:

# storage.yaml
path: .nl2sql          # or "${env:NL2SQL_DATA_DIR}" in a container

A relative path is relative to nl2sql.yaml in a file, and to the working directory when the Config is built in code. nl2sql init writes .nl2sql and adds .nl2sql/ to .gitignore.

Everything the engine writes lives under it:

Under path What Was (0.4) index/ The vector index (Chroma), one collection per embedding model: nl2sql__<model slug>__<dimension>. VECTOR_STORE, VECTOR_STORE_COLLECTION state.db SQLite: schema snapshots, the plan cache and playground feedback. SCHEMA_STORE_PATH traces/ Run traces (settings.traces.mode), kept 14 days by default. TRACE_DIR results/ Result files, <tenant_id>/<request_id>/<sub_query_id>.parquet. Kept 7 days by default. See Artifact Store. RESULT_ARTIFACT_BASE_URI

docs.title: The four stores
docs.text:
Each part of that data has a slot, and each slot a store, named by type. Every sub-block is optional; left out, a slot uses its built-in store, so the section above is the same as:

path: .nl2sql
index:   { type: chroma }    # <path>/index/
state:   { type: sqlite }    # <path>/state.db
traces:  { type: files, max_age_days: 14 }    # <path>/traces/
results: { type: local, max_age_days: 7 }     # <path>/results/
Slot Built-in Holds index chroma The vector index, one namespace per embedding model, and each datasource's live build state sqlite Schema snapshots, the plan cache, feedback traces files Run traces results local Result files

A store's other keys are its own, checked by the store when the engine is built, so a misspelt key is an error. They may be ${provider:key} references, resolved through the secret providers when the store is built:

index: { type: qdrant, url: "http://qdrant:6333", api_key: "${env:QDRANT_KEY}" }

Store names share one entry point group, nl2sql.stores, so a name is unique across the four slots. A store in the wrong slot is refused with the stores installed for that slot: "'chroma' is an index store; results needs a results store. Installed: local."

In code, a slot takes a StoreConfig or a store object, used as given:

from nl2sql import Storage, StoreConfig

Storage(path=".nl2sql")
Storage(path=".nl2sql", traces=StoreConfig(type="files", max_age_days=30))
Storage(path=".nl2sql", index=my_index_store)   # any object whose slot is "index"

The store interfaces are in nl2sql_sdk.stores. A plugin registers a store in the nl2sql.stores entry point group, or in code with registry.add_store(name, cls).

Every slot is read through its interface, so a plugin store works in any slot it fills.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
The files trace store and the local results store take max_age_days, 14 and 7 by default (at least 1). It is a key of those two stores, not of every store.

traces:  { type: files, max_age_days: 30 }
results: { type: local, max_age_days: 2 }

engine.storage.purge() deletes the traces and result files last written before that age, and the audit observer's day files older than its max_age_days (90 by default), and the review queue's decided proposals (accepted, rejected, superseded) decided more than settings.review.max_age_days (365) ago, and the conversations last updated more than conversations.max_age_days (30) ago, and the draft dashboards last edited more than that long ago (saved dashboards are never purged), and returns the counts, {"traces": 3, "results": 12, "proposals": 4, "approvals": 0, "conversations": 2, "dashboards": 1, "audit": 1} (no audit when the engine runs no audit observer, no conversations or dashboards when max_age_days is null). Open proposals are never purged. approvals counts the stored approval requests and grants last changed more than settings.approvals.max_age_hours (24) ago. It publishes the counts as the retention.purged event, which the audit observer writes. A plugin trace or results store is purged when it has a max_age_days attribute, and left alone when it does not (a bucket with its own lifecycle rule, say). Three things call it:

  • nl2sql storage purge, by hand or from cron;
  • nl2sql-api, at startup and then once a day while it serves (a failed purge is logged and tried again the next day);
  • your own code.

Feedback and schema snapshots have no age limit: feedback is cleared by hand (nl2sql feedback clear), and after each index build the snapshots nothing can read any more are deleted (see The state).

docs.title: What is where: engine.storage.info()
docs.text:
engine.storage.info()
# {"index":   {"type": "chroma", "location": ".../.nl2sql/index"},
#  "state":   {"type": "sqlite", "location": ".../.nl2sql/state.db"},
#  "traces":  {"type": "files",  "location": ".../.nl2sql/traces", "max_age_days": 14},
#  "results": {"type": "local",  "location": ".../.nl2sql/results", "max_age_days": 7},
#  "namespace": "nl2sql__local-all-minilm-l6-v2__384"}

type is the store's name, or the class name of a store object; location is its folder or file, or None for a store that does not have one.

docs.title: The state
docs.text: The state store keeps the schema snapshots (immutable, one row per version), the plan cache, the playground's feedback, and the lock that lets one index build run at a time. The engine applies the store's pending migrations when it starts; the built-in sqlite store adopts a 0.5 state.db as it is, and applies them in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, so engines or CLI runs opening a new state.db at the same moment apply each one exactly once. A store with nothing pending takes no lock, so a read-only state.db opens. See The state store.

docs.title: The index
docs.text:
The engine embeds; the index store keeps entries and vectors in a namespace per embedding model, nl2sql__<model slug>__<dimension> (for example nl2sql__local-all-minilm-l6-v2__384), filters them, and records each datasource's live build as a BuildPointer (its build_id and the schema_version it was made from). Switching a pointer is the commit, and a run reads the pointers once when it starts. See Indexing.

  • Changing the embedding model opens a new, empty namespace: check() reports the index missing, and nl2sql index builds it. Switching back finds the old namespace still built.
  • nl2sql index prune (engine.index.prune()) drops every namespace but the current model's, including 0.5's nl2sql_store collection, which 0.6 never reads. Run it once after upgrading, and after settling on a new model.
  • The chroma store opens index/ on the first build; reading a missing folder or namespace creates nothing.

docs.title: Sharing
docs.text:
Two engines with different paths share nothing. The commands that only read these stores (nl2sql cache clear, nl2sql feedback, nl2sql trace show, nl2sql storage purge) find them from the same config, so run them with the same --config.

There is no built-in S3 or ADLS results store. The ResultStore interface is four methods; Artifact Store has an S3 example.

In a container, mount a volume and point the path at it:

path: "${env:NL2SQL_DATA_DIR}"

docker run -e NL2SQL_DATA_DIR=/data -v nl2sql-data:/data ...

docs.title: Configuration System
docs.text:
nl2sql reads one config: nl2sql.yaml and the files it includes. Loading it gives one typed Config object, and building that same Config in Python gives exactly the same engine. Everything the engine needs is in it. Only the config path and the provider key variables are read directly (see Environment variables); any other value from the environment is written in the YAML as ${env:VAR}.

This page is the reference.

docs.title: nl2sql.yaml
docs.text:
nl2sql init writes a new project, with each section in its own file:

nl2sql init my-project              # an example SQLite datasource, allow_all policies
nl2sql init my-project --demo       # the demo: three sample databases, roles, verified queries
nl2sql init my-project --provider anthropic

nl2sql.yaml            # the table of contents
datasources/
  example.yaml         # one file per datasource (--demo: chinook.yaml, support.yaml, webanalytics.yaml)
llm.yaml               # provider + model; no key, the provider's standard variable is read
embeddings.yaml        # provider: local
policies.yaml          # allow_all: true            (--demo: admin, analyst, viewer roles)
storage.yaml           # path: .nl2sql
knowledge.yaml         # one yaml knowledge source: glossary.yaml
glossary.yaml          # one empty block per datasource (--demo: the Chinook glossary)
curated.yaml           # --demo only: the demo's verified queries
settings.yaml          # --demo only: the demo's tuning knobs
data/                  # --demo only: the three SQLite files, copied
.gitignore             # .nl2sql/ and .env

init refuses to overwrite a file without --force, never writes a key, and checks what it wrote with load_config.

# nl2sql.yaml
version: 2
datasources: { file: datasources/ }      # a folder, one file per datasource
llm:         { file: llm.yaml }
embeddings:  { file: embeddings.yaml }
policies:    { file: policies.yaml }
storage:     { file: storage.yaml }
curated:     { file: curated.yaml }      # optional
secrets:     { file: secrets.yaml }      # optional
settings:    { file: settings.yaml }     # optional
api:         { file: api.yaml }          # optional, read by nl2sql-api only
observers:   { file: observers.yaml }    # optional: where events, logs and metrics go
hooks:       { file: hooks.yaml }        # optional
evals:       { file: evals.yaml }        # optional
knowledge:   { file: knowledge.yaml }    # optional: where the glossary comes from (0.8)
conversations: { file: conversations.yaml }  # optional: follow-up questions (0.9)
chat_tools:  { file: chat_tools.yaml }   # optional: which chat tools are on (0.9)
dashboards:  { file: dashboards.yaml }   # optional (0.9)
mcp:         { file: mcp.yaml }          # optional: nl2sql mcp --http (0.9)

A small project can write every section inline instead. This file builds the same Config as a split layout would:

version: 2
datasources:
  - id: shop
    type: sqlite
    connection: { database: shop.db }
llm:        { provider: anthropic, model: claude-sonnet-5-5 }
embeddings: { provider: local }
policies:   { allow_all: true }
storage:    { path: .nl2sql }
Section Required Page Notes version yes 2. Anything else, or none, is an error that points to the 0.4 mapping. datasources yes Datasources A list; [] is enough. llm yes LLMs The model every agent uses, and per-agent overrides. embeddings yes Embeddings {provider: local} is a complete section. policies yes Policies {allow_all: true} is a complete section. storage yes Storage {path: .nl2sql} is a complete section. curated no Curated Answers Present means curated answers are on. secrets no Secrets The env provider is always there without it. settings no Settings Tuning knobs; every field has a default. api no REST API nl2sql-api's own settings; the engine ignores them. observers no below A list. Absent means the default observers, log and audit; [] means none. hooks no below A list, run in its order. evals no below The eval suites, scorers and regression gate. knowledge no below A list of knowledge sources, in precedence order. Absent (or []) means no knowledge. conversations no below How a model-led turn is bounded and kept. Every field has a default. chat_tools no below A list of chat tool names. Absent means chart, diagram and report, if registered; [] means none (ask stays). dashboards no below The starter dashboard's size and the refresh limits. Every field has a default. answers no below Saved answers: how many one person may keep. Every field has a default. mcp no below nl2sql mcp --http: where it listens and how it authenticates. Every field has a default.

From Python:

from nl2sql import NL2SQL, load_config

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")        # path=None: NL2SQL_CONFIG, then ./nl2sql.yaml
cfg = load_config("nl2sql.yaml")                  # the Config, to change in code first
engine = NL2SQL(cfg.model_copy(update={"settings": cfg.settings.model_copy(update={"tenant_id": "acme"})}))

See Public Facade → Creating an engine.

docs.title: file: includes
docs.text:
Rule Detail Shape A section is either inline, or exactly {file: <path>} with no other keys. Relative paths The path is relative to nl2sql.yaml, not to the working directory. One level Only nl2sql.yaml includes. An included file holds the section's body and includes nothing itself. No version Only nl2sql.yaml has version:. Datasource folder datasources: {file: datasources/} names a folder. Every *.yaml in it, sorted by name and not recursive, holds one datasource. id may be left out and defaults to the file name; if it is given, it must equal the file name. Datasource file datasources: {file: datasources.yaml} names a file whose body is the list. List sections observers, hooks, knowledge and chat_tools are lists too: their file's body is the list. Literal paths file: values are never interpolated. Each file once Including the same file twice is an error.

Other relative paths are relative to nl2sql.yaml too: storage.path, and a SQLite or DuckDB database. The engine can be run from any working directory.

docs.title: Secret and variable references
docs.text:
${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD} reads an environment variable; ${vault:apps/sales:password} reads a secret from the provider whose id is vault (see Secrets). env is built in.

Rule Detail Whole value only A reference is the entire string. "postgres://${env:U}@db" is an error, and there is no default syntax. Secrets resolve late Every api_key, the secret providers' credentials and every value under a datasource's connection keep the reference. It is resolved when the component is built, so engine.config, logs and errors never hold a plaintext secret. Everything else resolves at load Any other field, for example storage.path: "${env:NL2SQL_DATA_DIR}", is resolved by load_config. A variable that is not set is an error naming the field. Inside secrets: Only ${env:...}: one provider cannot depend on another.

docs.title: Observers, hooks and evals
docs.text:
Three sections added in release 0.7. They are accepted and validated now; the engine runs the hooks and the observers, and reads evals from the change named below. The observers are documented on their own page, Observers.

# observers.yaml: where the engine's events go
- type: log
  level: INFO
- type: audit
  max_age_days: 90
- type: otel                      # needs nl2sql-engine[otel]
  endpoint: http://collector:4317
- type: corp_siem                 # a plugin; its config_model checks the rest
  url: "${env:SIEM_URL}"

# hooks.yaml: code that sees every run at fixed points, in this order (see Hooks)
- type: corp_sql_review
  points: [execute.before]        # a subset of the hook's own points; all of them by default
  on_error: closed                # closed (the default) | open
  approver_roles: [dba]           # who may approve its needs_approval; default policies.admin_roles
  url: "${env:REVIEW_URL}"        # the hook's own keys

# evals.yaml: the suites engine.evals.run runs, and how they are scored
suites: [evals/chinook.yaml]      # relative to nl2sql.yaml
scorers: [result_match, outcome, faithfulness, retrieval_recall, routing]   # the default: all five
curated: true
max_cost_usd: 5.00                # across a run in mode full; required for it
gate:
  max_regressions: 2
  alpha: 0.05
  max_cost_increase: 0.20
Section Item Rule observers {type: <name>, ...} (ObserverConfig) or an observer object in code type names a registered observer (nl2sql.observers); its config_model checks the other keys, and keeps their ${...} references until it is built. Without the section the engine runs log and audit; observers: [] runs none. hooks {type: <name>, points, on_error, approver_roles, ...} (HookConfig) or a hook object in code points takes run.before, datasources.after, plan.after, execute.before, execute.after and answer.after; any other is an error. on_error is closed or open. The hook's config_model checks its own keys. A point the hook does not declare is an error. See Hooks. evals EvalsConfig Strict keys. suites are files of cases, read when a run asks for them, not when the engine starts. gate.alpha is between 0 and 1. See Evals. 
from nl2sql import Config, HookConfig, ObserverConfig

Config(..., observers=[ObserverConfig(type="log"), MyObserver()],
       hooks=[HookConfig(type="corp_sql_review", points=["execute.before"]), MyHook()])

docs.title: Knowledge
docs.text:
The knowledge sources the glossary comes from, in precedence order (release 0.8). The engine loads them when it is built and on engine.knowledge.reload(); see Knowledge for the glossary, precedence and who sees what.

# knowledge.yaml: a list, in precedence order
- type: yaml
  path: glossary.yaml             # relative to nl2sql.yaml
- type: corp_catalog              # a plugin; its config_model checks the rest
  url: "${env:CATALOG_URL}"
Section Item Rule knowledge {type: <name>, ...} (KnowledgeSourceConfig) or a knowledge source object in code (one with load) type names a registered knowledge source (nl2sql.knowledge_sources); its config_model checks the other keys and keeps their ${...} references until it is built. A source only reads; glossary.yaml itself is data, not a config section. 
from nl2sql import Config, KnowledgeSourceConfig

Config(..., knowledge=[KnowledgeSourceConfig(type="yaml", path="glossary.yaml"), MySource()])

docs.title: Conversations, chat tools, dashboards and MCP
docs.text:
Four sections for release 0.9. They are accepted and validated now; the change named with each reads it. Each is optional, and absent, the defaults shown apply. Chart limits are settings.charts (Settings).

# conversations.yaml (every value shown is the default)
context_turns: 3        # turns the model sees
max_tool_calls: 12      # tool calls per turn; the model then makes one last call, tools off
max_turns: 50           # the 51st turn is refused
max_age_days: 30        # null keeps conversations; also bounds draft dashboards

# chat_tools.yaml: a list of registered names (the nl2sql.chat_tools entry point group)
# absent: chart, diagram, report, dashboard_edit and dashboard_pin (those the registry has)
- chart
- report
- dashboard_edit
- dashboard_pin

# dashboards.yaml (every value shown is the default)
max_tiles: 10                        # the starter dashboard's size
min_refresh_minutes: 15              # a schedule below this is refused
schedule_identity_max_age_days: 30   # a schedule stops when its saved identity is older

# answers (every value shown is the default)
max_per_user: 100                    # saved answers one person may keep; the next save is refused

# mcp.yaml (every value shown is the default)
http:
  host: 127.0.0.1
  port: 8765
  path: /mcp
  allowed_hosts: ["127.0.0.1:*", "localhost:*", "[::1]:*", "127.0.0.1", "localhost", "[::1]"]   # Host headers accepted
  allowed_origins: []                              # browser Origins accepted
auth: api_keys            # api_keys | none (none: loopback only)
Section Rule conversations Conversations: strict keys; every count is at least 1, and max_age_days: null keeps conversations. Read by engine.conversations. The conversation agent that leads a turn is one of the LLM agents. chat_tools A list of names: none twice, each a registered chat tool (registry.add_chat_tool, or an entry point). An unknown name is an error when the engine is built (chat_tools[i] in the report), with the closest registered name; ask and a plugin whose args_model does not forbid extra keys are errors too. Absent means the default tools (chart, diagram and report) that the registry has, so an engine on Registry.empty() starts with none and needs no chat_tools: []; a name you list must be registered. [] means none; ask is the conversation's own tool and is always on. Read by engine.conversations and engine.chat_tools; see Chat tools. dashboards Dashboards: strict keys; every value is at least 1. Read by engine.dashboards. answers Answers: strict keys; max_per_user is at least 1. Read by engine.answers: the save past the cap is refused with AnswerLimitReached, never by dropping an older answer. mcp Mcp: strict keys. http.port is 1 to 65535 and http.path starts with /. auth: none is for loopback only: the server refuses to start on any other host, or when allowed_hosts lists a name that is not loopback. allowed_hosts and allowed_origins feed the MCP SDK's DNS-rebinding protection: a request whose Host or Origin is not listed is refused, so a deployment behind a proxy lists its public host name. Read by nl2sql mcp --http; see MCP over HTTP. 
from nl2sql import Config
from nl2sql.config import Conversations

Config(..., conversations=Conversations(context_turns=5), chat_tools=["chart", "report"])

docs.title: Mode
docs.text:
mode: your_data    # demo | your_data | hosted (default your_data)

What the project is for: the bundled demo, your own data, or a hosted public demo. It is a top-level key, not a section. The engine only validates it. nl2sql.resolve_mode(flag, env, file) picks the mode a process runs in: the launcher flag, else the value of NL2SQL_MODE, else this key. It is a pure function; the entry point reads the environment and passes the value in: nl2sql-api serve is the one place that reads NL2SQL_MODE, resolves it with the --demo and --hosted flags and the file, and builds the engine with the result in its Config. An unknown value is an error naming the three.

docs.title: Strict keys and errors
docs.text:
Every section forbids unknown keys and suggests the closest known one. Names resolved through the registry (type:, provider:) suggest from the installed names. load_config and NL2SQL(...) collect every problem before raising one ConfigError, each naming the file it is in (an included file, not nl2sql.yaml):

nl2sql.yaml has 2 problems:

  datasources/sales.yaml → preferd_tables
    Unknown key. Did you mean 'preferred_tables'?

  llm.yaml → provider
    'antropic' is not an installed LLM provider. Did you mean 'anthropic'?

A secret is shown as its reference, never as its value. A 0.4 file (version: 1) gets one message pointing to the mapping.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Only these are read directly:

Variable Read by Purpose NL2SQL_CONFIG load_config() with no path, the CLI, nl2sql-api Path to nl2sql.yaml. Without it, ./nl2sql.yaml. NL2SQL_MODE nl2sql-api serve demo, your_data or hosted: the mode when no flag sets it. It beats the config's mode: and loses to --demo and --hosted. NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL configure_logging() The log level when the caller passes none (DEBUG, INFO, ...). Without it, INFO. NL2SQL_LOG_FORMAT configure_logging() text or json (one JSON object per line, with its trace_id) when the caller chooses neither; the CLI's --log-format chooses for any command. Without it, text; any other value is an error (ValueError; the CLI prints it on one line and exits 1). OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY nl2sql/llm/ The fallback key when llm.api_key (or an agent's, or embeddings.api_key) is not set.

Anything else from the environment is written in the YAML as ${env:VAR}. There are no generic overrides such as NL2SQL__SECTION__KEY. Third-party libraries (the OpenTelemetry SDK) still read their own standard variables, the trace redactor scans the environment for values to mask. Nothing in nl2sql writes the environment: a key the demo is given travels in the engine's LLM config, and only the .env loading below adds variables. The architecture tests enforce both (invariants).

docs.title: .env files
docs.text:
Only the entry points load a .env file: the CLI, nl2sql-api and nl2sql demo load the .env next to nl2sql.yaml into the process environment at startup. A variable that is already set always wins; the file never overrides it. Each loads the .env before it configures logging, so a NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL written there applies (nl2sql-api serve --demo reads the demo project's .env, except with --hosted, which reads none).

The library itself never reads a .env file. A Python caller that wants one loads it before building the engine:

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from nl2sql import NL2SQL

load_dotenv("my-project/.env")   # or nl2sql.load_env_file("my-project/nl2sql.yaml")
engine = NL2SQL.from_config("my-project/nl2sql.yaml")

nl2sql init adds .env to .gitignore. Keep keys there, or in the environment, never in the YAML.

docs.title: The CLI
docs.text:
Every command reads the same config, named once, before the subcommand:

nl2sql --config prod/nl2sql.yaml index
nl2sql --config prod/nl2sql.yaml run "Top 5 customers by revenue"
NL2SQL_CONFIG=prod/nl2sql.yaml nl2sql curated validate
nl2sql run "..."                       # ./nl2sql.yaml
nl2sql --log-format json run "..."     # JSON log lines, for any command

There are no per-command path flags. Commands that query or index build the engine and call engine.check() first (see Startup). nl2sql cache, nl2sql feedback and nl2sql trace show only need the store paths under storage.path, and build no engine.

docs.title: Checking a config: nl2sql config check
docs.text:
nl2sql config check checks the whole config without starting the engine, so it fits a CI job or a pre-deploy step:

nl2sql --config prod/nl2sql.yaml config check            # files, names, drivers
nl2sql --config prod/nl2sql.yaml config check --connect  # and connect to every datasource

It does what building the engine does, short of the stores:

  • reads nl2sql.yaml and every file it includes, and resolves ${env:...};
  • loads every name the config uses through the registry (type:, provider:, the secret providers): the name is installed, implements the interface version this engine needs, and its drivers are installed;
  • builds the components, which resolves each datasource's connection references, without connecting or calling a model.

With --connect it also connects to every datasource, as engine.check() does, and a datasource that fails is a problem (required or not).

Problems are printed by the file they are in, then a line per secret:

datasources/sales.yaml
  type
    Unknown adapter 'postgress'. Did you mean 'postgres'? Registered: duckdb, mssql, mysql, postgres, sqlite.

llm.yaml
  provider
    Unknown LLM provider 'antropic'. Did you mean 'anthropic'? Registered: anthropic, ollama, openai, openrouter.

Secrets:
  ${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD} missing (datasources/sales.yaml → connection.password)

prod/nl2sql.yaml: 2 problems in 2 files.

A secret is reported as present or missing, never printed. Where the llm section names no api_key, the provider's standard variable is listed. A missing LLM key is reported but is not a problem, as for the engine: a CI job rarely holds the production key, and engine.check() reports it at startup. Any other secret that does not resolve stops the engine from building, so it is a problem.

Exit code Meaning 0 No problems. 1 One or more problems, or the config was not found. 2 A usage error: an unknown option.

The check creates no file under storage.path. From Python, the same check is nl2sql.config.check.check_config(path, registry=..., connect=...), which returns the problems, the secrets and the datasource statuses.

docs.title: Startup: check() and required
docs.text:
Building the engine never connects to a datasource or calls a model: every problem it can find without a connection is one ConfigError. engine.check() then connects to each datasource, checks that every agent's API key resolves (no model call) and reports the index status.

The CLI, nl2sql-api (in its lifespan, before it accepts requests) and nl2sql demo call check() at startup:

  • A datasource with required: true that fails, or datasources configured and none ready, raises EngineNotReady: the CLI and nl2sql demo print the report and refuse to start (the CLI exits 1). nl2sql-api logs the report and starts anyway: GET /api/v1/ready answers 503 not_ready, and an admin reads each failing datasource and its stage under problems.
  • An optional datasource that fails is printed, left out of routing, and the entry point runs degraded.
# datasources/sales.yaml
type: postgres
required: true           # without it, nothing works: the CLI refuses to start, /ready says not_ready
connection: { host: db.internal, database: sales, user: nl2sql, password: "${env:SALES_DB_PASSWORD}" }

A Python caller decides for itself. Without check(), a broken datasource fails the first query that targets it, with its reason.

docs.title: From 0.4
docs.text: 0.5 reads only nl2sql.yaml. There is no migration command: map each 0.4 file, variable and flag with these tables. nl2sql init writes a fresh layout to start from.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: 0.4 0.5 configs/datasources.yaml (DATASOURCE_CONFIG) datasources:, one file per datasource in datasources/. connection.type moves up to type; options: and the top-level limits become limits: {row_limit, timeout_ms, max_bytes}. configs/llm.yaml (LLM_CONFIG) llm:, flat: default:'s keys are the top level; agents: are keyed by node name (ast_planner, not astplanner); name: and version: are gone. configs/policies.json (POLICIES_CONFIG) policies:, in YAML; the role: field that repeated the key is gone. configs/secrets.yaml (SECRETS_CONFIG) secrets:, without version. hashi is now hashicorp. configs/curated.yaml (CURATED_CONFIG) curated:, without version. Present means on. configs/sample_questions.yaml (SAMPLE_QUESTIONS, ROUTING_EXAMPLES) sample_questions: on each datasource. .env, .env.<name> (ENV, APP_ENV, ENV_FILE_PATH) The .env next to nl2sql.yaml, loaded by the entry points only. .env.demo and configs/*.demo.* nl2sql init --demo (and nl2sql demo, which runs it): nl2sql.yaml, its files, and .env.

docs.title: Settings variables
docs.text: 0.4 variable 0.5 OPENAI_API_KEY llm.api_key / embeddings.api_key, or the fallback variable above VECTOR_STORE storage.path (the index is <path>/index/) VECTOR_STORE_COLLECTION removed (an internal constant) EMBEDDING_PROVIDER embeddings.provider EMBEDDING_MODEL embeddings.model TENANT_ID settings.tenant_id CURATED_ENABLED removed: the curated section is present or absent CURATED_MATCH_TOP_K settings.curated.match_top_k CURATED_MATCH_FLOOR settings.curated.match_floor GLOBAL_TIMEOUT_SEC settings.pipeline.timeout_s RESULT_ARTIFACT_BASE_URI storage.path (<path>/results/) RESULT_ARTIFACT_PATH_TEMPLATE removed: a fixed layout under <path>/results/ RESULT_ARTIFACT_BACKEND, RESULT_ARTIFACT_S3_*, RESULT_ARTIFACT_ADLS_* removed: results are local; the S3 and ADLS backends are deleted SCHEMA_STORE_BACKEND removed: SQLite at <path>/state.db SCHEMA_STORE_PATH storage.path (<path>/state.db, which also holds the plan cache and feedback) SCHEMA_STORE_MAX_VERSIONS settings.schema.max_versions SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH_POLICY removed: a run reads the schema version its index build was made from PLAN_CACHE_ENABLED settings.pipeline.plan_cache FEEDBACK_ENABLED settings.feedback.enabled SCHEMA_RETRIEVAL_FULL_SNAPSHOT_MAX_TABLES settings.retrieval.full_snapshot_max_tables LOGICAL_VALIDATOR_STRICT_COLUMNS settings.pipeline.strict_columns RBAC_REFUSAL_NAMES_TABLES policies.refusal_names_tables SQL_AGENT_MAX_RETRIES settings.pipeline.retries.max SQL_AGENT_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_SEC settings.pipeline.retries.base_delay_s SQL_AGENT_RETRY_MAX_DELAY_SEC settings.pipeline.retries.max_delay_s SQL_AGENT_RETRY_JITTER_SEC settings.pipeline.retries.jitter_s LLM_PRICES llm.prices TRACE_MODE settings.traces.mode TRACE_DIR storage.path (<path>/traces/) RESULT_ROW_LIMIT settings.results.row_limit RESULT_FETCH_BATCH_SIZE settings.results.fetch_batch_size ANSWER_PREVIEW_ROWS settings.results.preview_rows TRACE_SAMPLE_ROWS settings.traces.sample_rows TRACE_MAX_FIELD_CHARS settings.traces.max_field_chars NL2SQL_TODAY settings.pipeline.today OBSERVABILITY_EXPORTER an otel observer in the observers section (0.7) OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT the otel observer's endpoint (0.7)

docs.title: Other variables
docs.text: 0.4 variable 0.5 NL2SQL_API_ROLE_HEADER api.proxy.roles_header with api.auth: proxy (0.10) NL2SQL_API_ROLE api.static_role with api.auth: static (0.10) NL2SQL_API_TRUST_BODY_ROLE removed in 0.10: a request body never carries the caller NL2SQL_API_CORS_ORIGINS (comma-separated) api.cors_origins (a list) NL2SQL_API_ADMIN_ROLES policies.admin_roles NL2SQL_DEMO_HOSTED nl2sql-api serve --demo --hosted NL2SQL_DEMO_QUESTIONS_PER_MINUTE, NL2SQL_DEMO_QUESTIONS_PER_SESSION nl2sql-api serve --questions-per-minute N --questions-per-session N VAULT_ADDR, VAULT_TOKEN secrets.providers[].url / .token (write ${env:VAULT_TOKEN} to keep reading the variable) AZURE_KEYVAULT_URL secrets.providers[].vault_url ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY unchanged: the fallback key variables

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: 0.4 0.5 nl2sql setup nl2sql init [DIR] [--provider NAME] [--force]; the guided flow comes in a later release nl2sql setup --demo nl2sql init --demo [DIR] (or just nl2sql demo) --env NAME, --env-file PATH removed: the .env next to nl2sql.yaml is loaded --config PATH (the datasource file), --llm-config, --secrets-config, --policies-config, --vector-store the one global nl2sql --config PATH/nl2sql.yaml curated validate/test --curated --config --secrets nl2sql --config ... curated validate/test policy validate --config --policies --secrets nl2sql --config ... policy validate nl2sql --env demo <command> (from the demo folder) nl2sql --config nl2sql-demo/nl2sql.yaml <command>, or run it from inside nl2sql-demo/

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:
• Models and load_config: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/config/
  • init_project, write_project, starter_config, demo_config: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/config/project.py
  • Secrets written as references, write_env_values: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/config/writer.py
  • The runtime built from a Config: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/runtime.py
  • The CLI's --config: nl2sql-cli/src/nl2sql_cli/common/engine.py
  • nl2sql config check: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/config/check.py, printed by nl2sql-cli/src/nl2sql_cli/commands/config_check.py

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
The rules a change has to keep, how to set up a checkout and how to run the tests are in CONTRIBUTING.md at the repository root. The short form of the rules is CLAUDE.md; the reasoning behind each is in Invariants.

  • Testing Architecture: the test markers and what each one needs.
  • Real-Database Test Bed: the Docker Compose test bed and its cloud twin.
  • Releasing: how a release is cut, published and verified.
  • Extending NL2SQL: adapters, chunk types, the planner, execution backends.

Report a vulnerability privately; see SECURITY.md. Everyone taking part follows the Code of Conduct.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
The monorepo publishes four distributions to PyPI under unified versioning: they all carry the same version and are released together. Internal dependencies use compatible-release constraints (~=0.1), so a release only resolves for users if every package declares the same version.

Releases are automated. Nobody edits a version number and nobody edits CHANGELOG.md by hand — release-please owns both. Two steps are manual. First, the release page docs/releases/X.Y.Z.md is written with the release-notes skill and merged. A status check on the release PR stays red until it is. Second, the owner merges the release pull request. Everything after that runs on its own: the four packages go to PyPI, the API image to GHCR, the versioned docs to gh-pages, and the hosted demo on Hugging Face is rebuilt on the version just published. Each of those is checked from the outside before the release counts as done.

docs.title: The automated flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    C[Conventional Commit merged to main] --> RP[release_please.yml]
    RP --> PR[Release PR: CHANGELOG.md + version bumps]
    PR --> RN[release-notes skill: docs/releases/X.Y.Z.md<br/>merged to main in its own PR]
    RN -->|release-notes status turns green| PR2[Release PR refreshed]
    PR2 -->|the owner merges it| TAG[Tag vX.Y.Z + GitHub Release]
    TAG --> NOTES[release-notes job: page summary<br/>above the generated changelog]
    TAG -->|release_please.yml calls it with tag_name<br/>the tag itself cannot trigger it| B[publish_pypi.yaml: build 4 dists]
    B --> S{wheels install and import?}
    S -->|no| STOP[Nothing is published]
    S -->|yes| PY[PyPI via trusted publishing:<br/>one job per package,<br/>one environment each]
    PY --> GH[ghcr.io/nadeem4/nl2sql-api]
    PY --> D[mike deploy: versioned docs]
    PY --> PS[pypi-smoke: pip install the release<br/>from PyPI, boot the demo]
    PS --> SP[publish_space.yml: Space pinned to<br/>nl2sql-cli[web] == X.Y.Z]
    SP --> SS[space-smoke: the live Space<br/>reports version X.Y.Z]

The same chain runs on every pull request up to the point of publishing: the build and fresh-install jobs in test.yml build the wheels, install them the way a user does and boot the demo, and the api-image job builds the GHCR image from the root Dockerfile (without pushing it), so a release does not meet these checks for the first time.

docs.title: 1. Commit messages decide the version
docs.text:
The bump comes from Conventional Commits on main, so the commit subject is the release input:

Commit prefix Effect on the next version fix: patch feat: minor any type with ! or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer major docs:, perf:, deps:, revert: patch, and shown in the changelog refactor: no release on its own, shown in the changelog chore:, ci:, test:, build:, style: no release on their own, hidden from the changelog

Which types reach the changelog is set by changelog-sections in release-please-config.json. Miscellaneous Chores (chore:) is hidden there, and so are ci:, test:, build: and style:. A breaking change is shown whatever its type. A chore: commit carrying a Release-As: footer has still shown up under Miscellaneous Chores (release 0.2.2). If that keeps happening, put the footer on a commit of a visible type.

The project is pre-1.0: a breaking change bumps the minor

release-please-config.json sets top-level bump-minor-pre-major: true, which the schema describes as "Breaking changes only bump semver minor if version < 1.0.0". While the version is below 1.0.0, a feat!: or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer therefore moves 0.1.0 to 0.2.0 rather than to 1.0.0 — semver's rule for an unstable public API.

Without this setting the first breaking commit silently declares the project stable. That is exactly what happened before it was added: the refactor!: that collapsed the distributions made release-please propose 1.0.0.

Going to 1.0.0 is then a deliberate act: set the version explicitly with a Release-As: 1.0.0 commit (below). The flag stays true afterwards and becomes a no-op once the version is >= 1.0.0.

docs.title: 2. release_please.yml maintains a release PR
docs.text:
Every push to main runs googleapis/release-please-action@v4. It keeps a single open pull request (separate-pull-requests: false, one manifest entry for the whole repo) that contains the accumulated CHANGELOG.md entry and the version bump applied everywhere it appears:

File Updated by CHANGELOG.md the python release strategy pyproject.toml (repo root) the python release strategy packages/sdk/pyproject.toml an extra-files generic updater packages/nl2sql/pyproject.toml an extra-files generic updater packages/api/pyproject.toml an extra-files generic updater nl2sql-cli/pyproject.toml an extra-files generic updater (its version, and its nl2sql-engine and nl2sql-api pins) .release-please-manifest.json release-please

The four package manifests carry a marker comment on their version line:

version = "0.1.0" # x-release-please-version

The generic updater replaces the semver-looking value on any line carrying that annotation. The type: "generic" entry in release-please-config.json is required: without it a .toml path gets the TOML updater, which addresses a field by jsonpath and ignores the marker entirely. The comment is a plain TOML comment and has no effect on the build.

Because include-component-in-tag is false, the tag is vX.Y.Z rather than nl2sql-vX.Y.Z.

docs.title: 3. Every release needs a release page
docs.text:
Every version has a plain-language page at docs/releases/X.Y.Z.md, listed on the Releases page. The changelog lists commits. The page says what the release is for, what it does not do yet, and how to upgrade. It is written by the release-notes Claude Code skill (.claude/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md), which uses a fixed template (template.md next to it) and matches the last two pages. So every page has the same structure.

The order, once release-please has opened its PR:

  1. Run the release-notes skill. It reads the version from the release PR, gathers the commits, PRs and changelog section, writes docs/releases/X.Y.Z.md, adds it to docs/releases/index.md and the mkdocs.yml nav, runs mkdocs build --strict, and opens a PR titled docs(release): notes for X.Y.Z.
  2. Merge the notes PR to main. It cannot go on the release branch, because release-please rewrites that branch every time main changes.
  3. The gate goes green. The merge is a push to main, so release-please refreshes its PR, and the release-notes-gate job in release_please.yml checks again.
  4. The owner merges the release PR.

The gate is the release-notes commit status on the release PR's head commit. The release-notes-gate job sets it on every push to main that did not tag a release. It reads the version from the release branch's .release-please-manifest.json. Then it runs python scripts/release_notes.py check --version X.Y.Z against main. The check fails unless the page exists and has a summary block. While it fails, the status is red and its description says to run the release-notes skill.

Why a status from release_please.yml, not a pull_request check

release-please pushes its branch with GITHUB_TOKEN. GitHub opens pull_request runs for that push in the action_required state, and they never start unless someone approves each one. That is why test.yml has no runs on the release PRs. A job in release_please.yml runs on the same push that refreshes the PR, so the status always describes the PR's latest head. It needs no extra token: statuses: write on that job is enough.

The status blocks a merge only if it is required: add release-notes as a required status check in a branch ruleset for main. Until then it is a red mark that the owner reads before merging.

The page's first paragraph, between <!-- summary:start --> and <!-- summary:end -->, also goes into the GitHub Release. See the release-notes job below.

docs.title: The pre-release eval
docs.text:
Before merging a release PR, the owner runs the Chinook suite once on the real model, against the last published mode full record, and publishes the result. It spends the owner's key, so it is asked for explicitly and never runs in CI (nl2sql eval run --mode full refuses to start when CI is set):

# from a demo folder on the release PR's commit, with the key in its .env
nl2sql eval run --mode full --llm gpt-5.4 --max-cost 5 --baseline ../benchmarks
# from the repo root
nl2sql eval publish <demo folder>/eval_full.json --note "0.X.0 release"

Exit 1 is a regression to look at before releasing; exit 2 means the baseline is on another suite (the first run after a suite change starts a new series, and its record becomes the next baseline); exit 3 means the cap stopped the run. Mode full allows two flipped cases plus McNemar's two-sided test, because the model is noisy. The gate reads execution accuracy, the measure the history has always published (The regression gate). Commit the record and the regenerated pages in their own PR.

The routing suite is the release check for cross-database routing, on the same key and cap. Its board's routing scorer says whether each question went to the right databases:

nl2sql eval run --mode full --suite evals/routing.yaml --llm gpt-5.4 --max-cost 5 --out eval_routing_full.json

docs.title: 4. Merging the release PR is the gate
docs.text: This is the only manual step in a release, after the release page. Merging the pull request makes release-please create the vX.Y.Z tag and publish the GitHub Release. Until someone merges it, nothing is tagged and nothing is published. Reviewing the changelog and the version it proposes is the release decision.

docs.title: 5. The release publishes everything
docs.text:
publish_pypi.yaml runs a chain of seven jobs:

  1. build — builds sdists and wheels for all four packages, then smoke-installs them into a clean virtualenv and runs import nl2sql and nl2sql --help. These are the same commands as the build job in test.yml. The nl2sql-engine wheel carries LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md under dist-info/licenses/, from copies in packages/nl2sql/ (setuptools packs license files only from inside the project directory). Edit the root files and copy them over; tests/unit/test_packaging_metadata.py fails while the copies differ.
  2. pypi — needs: build, so a wheel that does not install or import fails the gate and this never runs. It is a matrix job with one leg per package: each leg runs in its own GitHub Environment (pypi-nl2sql-engine, pypi-nl2sql-api, pypi-nl2sql-sdk, pypi-nl2sql-cli), stages only that package's sdist and wheel into an upload/ directory and points pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish at it. One environment per package is what makes each PyPI trusted-publisher registration unique — see PyPI pending publishers.

  3. ghcr — needs: pypi, which waits for every leg of the matrix. Builds the root Dockerfile and pushes ghcr.io/nadeem4/nl2sql-api at both the tag and latest. The build context is the repository root (context: .) with the Dockerfile named explicitly (file: Dockerfile), because the Dockerfile installs the SDK, engine, API and CLI from their local sources and its COPY ./packages/... paths resolve against the build context. A context of packages/api makes them resolve to packages/api/packages/sdk, which does not exist — that is what failed on v0.1.0. A root .dockerignore keeps that context small. needs: pypi is retained so the image is only published for a release that reached PyPI, not because the image build needs PyPI. The image's FROM python:X.Y has to satisfy every package's requires-python (>=3.12): on v0.2.0 it was still python:3.11-slim, pip refused to install the SDK into it, and this job failed after PyPI and the docs had published. tests/unit/test_docker_images.py now checks every Dockerfile's base against every pyproject.toml, and the api-image job in test.yml builds this image on every pull request.

    There is no nl2sql-api:0.2.0 image

    The job builds from the tagged commit, and v0.2.0's Dockerfile cannot build, so re-running it would fail the same way. The first image built with the fix is published by the next release, 0.2.1, which moves ghcr.io/nadeem4/nl2sql-api:latest onto it.

    1. docs — needs: pypi, likewise after all four uploads. mike deploy --push --update-aliases $TAG latest adds a versioned copy of the docs to gh-pages and moves the latest alias onto it.
    2. pypi-smoke — needs: pypi. On a fresh runner, installs the release from PyPI itself, pip install "nl2sql-cli[web]==X.Y.Z", into an empty virtualenv, boots nl2sql-api serve --demo --hosted with no API key and checks the page, /api/v1/health (which must report X.Y.Z for the engine and the API), /api/v1/meta, each datasource's schema and /api/v1/index, then asks the advertised questions through POST /api/v1/query (no server error, one answered) and one turn that must end typed. Once the answers are re-recorded, add --guided-turns: every guided question and its scripted follow-up as turns. This is python scripts/fresh_install_check.py --pypi X.Y.Z, the same check the fresh-install PR job runs on the wheels. PyPI accepts an upload at once, but the CDN in front of its index serves a new version a little later, so the install is retried up to ten times, 30 seconds apart, with pip's cache off.
    3. space — needs: pypi-smoke, so the hosted demo is never built on a version that does not install from PyPI. Calls publish_space.yml with the tag, which pins the Space's image to nl2sql-cli[web]==X.Y.Z, pushes it and waits for the build. That pypi-smoke installed the version is not proof that the Hub's builder will: on v0.2.0 the Space build ran minutes later and its pip still saw only 0.1.x. So the workflow first waits, up to 20 times 30 seconds, until https://pypi.org/simple/nl2sql-engine/ lists X.Y.Z, and the Space's Dockerfile retries its install up to 10 times, 30 seconds apart, with pip's cache off. secrets: inherit carries HF_TOKEN down, from release_please.yml through this workflow into that one; without the secret the job skips green and says so.
    4. space-smoke — runs when space reports it deployed. A Space can report RUNNING on its new build while the router still sends visitors to the old one, so this checks where visitors are: it polls https://nadeem4nk-nl2sql-demo.hf.space/api/health until it reports X.Y.Z (up to 15 minutes), then checks the page and /api/meta; then the same on the Space's custom domain, SPACE_CUSTOM_DOMAIN in the workflow (https://nl2sql.codewithnk.com; empty skips it).

One more job, release-notes, runs on its own, next to the chain. It reads the summary block of docs/releases/X.Y.Z.md at the tag (python scripts/release_notes.py body). It puts that block above the changelog release-please generated for the GitHub Release (gh release edit --notes-file). A missing page or summary is a warning, not a failure: the job has continue-on-error: true and never holds up a publish. It is safe to re-run, because a summary already at the top is not added again.

A release is fully out when the seven jobs of the chain are green. A red pypi-smoke means the release is on PyPI but does not install or boot as published; yank it and ship a patch (see Package order). A red space or space-smoke leaves PyPI as it is and the Space on its previous image; fix the cause and re-run the failed jobs, or redeploy by hand (below).

Authentication is PyPI trusted publishing (OIDC, id-token: write). There is no API token anywhere in the workflow and no secret to rotate.

PEP 740 attestations are off, and must stay off

The pypi step sets attestations: false. Because release_please.yml reaches this workflow through workflow_call, OIDC auth and attestation signing disagree about which workflow "this" is: PyPI matches the token's job_workflow_ref claim, which names the called workflow (publish_pypi.yaml, the registered publisher), while Sigstore signs with the entry-point identity, putting release_please.yml in the certificate's Build Config URI. PyPI verifies the attestation against the one publisher that authenticated the request, so the two can never both match and the upload fails with 400 Invalid attestations supplied during upload. This is what broke v0.1.1. Trusted publishing is unaffected; the cost is that released artifacts carry no PEP 740 provenance. See PyPI's note on reusable workflows.

The four pypi legs run with fail-fast: false, so one package failing no longer cancels the others and skips ghcr and docs.

docs.title: Why the publish is chained to release-please, not to the tag
docs.text:
GitHub does not trigger workflows from events created with the default GITHUB_TOKEN. This is a deliberate recursion guard, and it has no opt-out short of pushing the tag with a personal access token instead. release-please tags with GITHUB_TOKEN, so a v* tag it pushes never fires publish_pypi.yaml's push: tags trigger. This is exactly what happened to v0.1.0: the tag and the GitHub Release exist, both authored by github-actions[bot], and Publish Release has no run for them.

Introducing a PAT would defeat the point of trusted publishing, so the publish is chained to release-please's own outputs instead. release_please.yml gives the action step an id, re-exports releases_created and tag_name as job outputs, and calls publish_pypi.yaml as a reusable workflow:

publish:
  needs: release-please
  if: ${{ needs.release-please.outputs.releases_created == 'true' }}
  uses: ./.github/workflows/publish_pypi.yaml
  with:
    tag: ${{ needs.release-please.outputs.tag_name }}
  permissions:
    contents: write
    packages: write
    id-token: write

A called workflow's jobs can never hold more than the calling job grants, so id-token: write has to appear on the caller for OIDC to reach the pypi legs. Publishing still lives in publish_pypi.yaml — the same filename the PyPI trusted publishers are registered against, which is what the pypi job's OIDC token is checked on — so no publisher entry changes.

publish_pypi.yaml keeps its push: tags: ["v*"] trigger as well. It costs nothing and still covers a tag a human pushes by hand.

docs.title: Publishing a release manually
docs.text:
publish_pypi.yaml also accepts workflow_dispatch with a required tag input. Use it when a release was tagged but never published — v0.1.0, or any tag pushed before the chaining above existed:

$ gh workflow run publish_pypi.yaml -f tag=v0.1.0

or Actions → Publish Release → Run workflow and type the tag.

The same dispatch is how you recover a release that tagged but never uploaded — the vX.Y.Z tag and the GitHub Release exist, but PyPI still shows the previous version and no image reached GHCR. That is what happened to v0.1.1: the pypi matrix failed and took ghcr and docs down with it. Nothing needs to be re-tagged; fix the cause on main, then dispatch the same tag:

$ gh workflow run publish_pypi.yaml -f tag=v0.1.1

The dispatch checks out the tag, so it publishes the tagged commit, not main. Only legs that never uploaded can be re-run — PyPI rejects a re-upload of a version it already has, so a partially-published release needs skip-existing or a manual publish of just the missing packages, in the dependency order below.

To redeploy only the hosted demo at a release that is already on PyPI, without touching PyPI, GHCR or the docs, dispatch the Space workflow with the tag:

$ gh workflow run publish_space.yml -f tag=v0.2.0

When the Space root for that tag is already on the Space there is nothing to push, so a run by hand asks the Hub for a factory rebuild instead and waits for it; the job fails unless the Space ends RUNNING. See Hosted demo.

Every job resolves its tag from ${{ inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}, never from the raw ref. On a dispatched run github.ref_name is the branch you dispatched from, so the fallback would silently build main instead of the release; the input is what makes every checkout, the GHCR image tag and mike deploy land on the tagged commit. Dispatching is safe to repeat only up to the PyPI upload — PyPI rejects a re-upload of a version that already exists.

docs.title: Pinning a version, and the first release
docs.text: Two settings exist only because release-please was adopted mid-project, long after the first commit. Both concern the very first release and neither is permanent.

docs.title: bootstrap-sha — where the changelog starts
docs.text:
With no tag in the repository, release-please has no marker for "the last release" and walks the whole history, so the first changelog it generated listed every feat: ever committed — 228 entries reaching back to before this phase of work.

The top-level bootstrap-sha in release-please-config.json is the fix. The manifest-releaser documentation describes it as a key that "will cause release-please to stop there for collecting changelog commits (so choose one commit earlier than the first commit you want to include)". Ours is:

"bootstrap-sha": "39d488ae9f9943ea5d9879bf2dd503c34370b24a"

That is the parent of 28687fe, the merge of the first pull request in this phase of work, so the changelog begins at that pull request and covers this phase rather than the entire project.

It is top-level on purpose: the schema does not accept it inside a packages entry, and the documentation notes it is "only applicable at top-level config".

It expires on its own

Per the documentation, "once a release-please generated PR has been merged, this config value will be ignored for all subsequent runs and can be removed." Once a real vX.Y.Z tag exists, that tag is the baseline and bootstrap-sha does nothing. Deleting it then is tidy-up, not a behaviour change.

docs.title: Release-As: — choosing an exact version
docs.text:
To publish a specific version rather than the one conventional commits imply, put a Release-As: footer in the body of a commit that lands on main:

ci: pin the first release to 0.1.0 and scope its changelog

Release-As: 0.1.0

Release-please reads Release-As: x.x.x (case insensitive) from the commit body and opens its next release pull request for exactly that version. This is how the first release was pinned to 0.1.0 instead of the 1.0.0 that the refactor!: commit would otherwise have produced.

The footer applies to one commit and expires with it — nothing has to be cleaned up afterwards.

Do not use the release-as config key instead

release-please-config.json accepts a release-as key that does the same job, and it is a trap. The schema marks the per-package form [DEPRECATED], advising "Consider using a Release-As commit instead", and the documentation warns that it is sticky:

Note: once the release PR is merged you should either remove this or update it to a higher version. Otherwise subsequent manifest-pr runs will continue to use this version even though it was already set in the last release.

A release-as left in the config does not pin one release — it pins every release, forever, to that version. The repository would stay at 0.1.0 while commits accumulated, and nobody would get an error saying so.

This repository therefore has no release-as key at all, and should not gain one. Use the commit footer, which cannot be forgotten because it does not persist.

docs.title: Troubleshooting: the release PR merges but nothing is tagged
docs.text:
Both traps below fail the same way. release_please.yml reports success, no tag appears, and the merged release pull request keeps its autorelease: pending label — so every later run refuses to open a new release PR:

There are untagged, merged release PRs outstanding - aborting

That line is a consequence, not a diagnosis. The cause is earlier in the same run, in the Building releases phase.

docs.title: The component mismatch
docs.text:
Symptom, in the Building releases phase of the run log:

PR component: undefined does not match configured component: nl2sql-engine

With separate-pull-requests: false the Merge plugin names the grouped release branch release-please--branches--main, with no component in it. When the release is built back out of that merged PR, release-please compares the branch's component against getBranchComponent() — which returns the configured component regardless of include-component-in-tag, unlike getComponent(), which honours it:

async getComponent()       { if (!this.includeComponentInTag) return ''; ... }  // ""
async getBranchComponent() { return this.component || ...; }                    // "nl2sql-engine"

A package-name on the packages entry is what supplies that component. The two disagree, the release is skipped, and no tag is created.

The fix is to carry no package-name for the root package. It was inert otherwise: the python strategy takes its project name from the root pyproject.toml (projectName = pyProject.name), not from that key, so the set of files release-please updates is unchanged.

The pullRequestTitlePattern warnings are noise, not the cause

The same run also logs, repeatedly:

pullRequestTitlePattern miss the part of '${scope}'
pullRequestTitlePattern miss the part of '${component}'
pullRequestTitlePattern miss the part of '${version}'

These fire unconditionally whenever a title pattern omits a placeholder, and the built-in grouped-PR default — chore: release ${branch}, which renders as chore: release main — omits all three. They appear on healthy runs too.

A missing ${version} in the title is not fatal. Release-please falls back to the pull request body, whose <summary> block carries the version; the documentation says it parses the version "either via the pull request title or body format".

Setting group-pull-request-title-pattern to add ${version} does not fix the mismatch above, and it breaks that body fallback for any release PR already merged under the old title (Bad pull request title: 'chore: release main'), stranding that version permanently. Reading these warnings as the cause cost a release cycle.

docs.title: Manifest seeding
docs.text:
.release-please-manifest.json records the last released version, not the next one, so it must be seeded below the first version to be shipped:

{ ".": "0.0.0" }

Seeding it at the target instead — {".": "0.1.0"} while a Release-As: 0.1.0 footer pins the same value — makes the first release a no-op: release-please treats the version it would propose as already released, so the pull request it opens rewrites CHANGELOG.md and bumps nothing. This also cost a cycle.

docs.title: Documentation versions
docs.text:
gh-pages is managed by mike, which keeps one built site per version:

Version Deployed by When dev publish_docs.yml every push to main X.Y.Z + the latest alias publish_pypi.yaml on a release, or a manual dispatch

publish_docs.yml previously ran mkdocs gh-deploy --force, which replaces the entire gh-pages root and would have wiped every released version on the next push to main. It now deploys to the dev version instead, so the two workflows write different directories. Both declare concurrency: group: gh-pages so they never push to that branch at the same time. Only the release workflow moves latest and sets the site default.

docs.title: One-time human setup
docs.text: Four things must be configured by hand before the first release. Only the last involves a secret, and it is not a PyPI one.

docs.title: PyPI pending publishers
docs.text:
Trusted publishing has to be told, once per project name, which repository and workflow it will accept uploads from. For a project that does not exist on PyPI yet this is a pending publisher, created at pypi.org/manage/account/publishing.

Add one for each of the four names — nl2sql-engine, nl2sql-api, nl2sql-sdk and nl2sql-cli. The engine publishes as nl2sql-engine because the nl2sql name on PyPI is already taken by an unrelated project; the import package is still nl2sql.

The environment name is required and differs per package

PyPI keys a pending publisher on the tuple (owner, repository, workflow, environment) and requires that tuple to be unique. All four of our projects publish from the same owner, the same repository and the same workflow file, so with the environment left blank all four tuples are identical: the first registration succeeds and the others are rejected with "A pending trusted publisher matching this configuration has already been registered for a different project name."

The environment is therefore the only field that can distinguish them, and publish_pypi.yaml gives each package its own. Fill it in exactly as below — these strings are the contract between the workflow and PyPI, and a mismatch fails the upload with an OIDC error rather than a helpful one.

Owner nadeem4, repository nl2sql and workflow publish_pypi.yaml are the same on all four entries. Only the project name and the environment differ:

PyPI Project Name Environment name nl2sql-engine pypi-nl2sql-engine nl2sql-api pypi-nl2sql-api nl2sql-sdk pypi-nl2sql-sdk nl2sql-cli pypi-nl2sql-cli Field Value Owner nadeem4 Repository name nl2sql Workflow name publish_pypi.yaml Environment name per the table above — never blank

The environments do not need to be created by hand. Referencing them in publish_pypi.yaml is enough for GitHub to create them on the first run, after which they appear under Settings → Environments and can be given reviewers or branch rules if the release should be gated further.

Once a name has published for the first time, its pending publisher becomes an ordinary trusted publisher on the project. Do not create an API token and do not add a password to the publish step — the workflow authenticates with OIDC and adding a token secret would only widen the blast radius.

Renaming publish_pypi.yaml, or renaming an environment in it, breaks publishing until the publisher entries are updated to match.

docs.title: Checklist before the first 0.5 release: nl2sql-sdk
docs.text:
Until 0.4 the SDK published as nl2sql-adapter-sdk. From 0.5 it publishes as nl2sql-sdk, a project PyPI has never seen, so it needs its own pending publisher. Do both before merging the 0.5 release PR:

  • [ ] On PyPI, add a pending trusted publisher for project nl2sql-sdk: owner nadeem4, repository nl2sql, workflow publish_pypi.yaml, environment pypi-nl2sql-sdk.
  • [ ] On GitHub, create the environment pypi-nl2sql-sdk under Settings → Environments.

Without them the SDK leg of the release fails. The pypi matrix is fail-fast: false, so the engine and API legs would still publish, and nl2sql-engine would land on PyPI depending on an nl2sql-sdk that is not there. nl2sql-adapter-sdk is not published again.

docs.title: GHCR package visibility
docs.text: The first push creates ghcr.io/nadeem4/nl2sql-api as a private package. Make it public under the repository's Packages settings if the image is meant to be pullable anonymously. The workflow itself needs no setup: it authenticates with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN and permissions: packages: write.

docs.title: Actions permission to open pull requests
docs.text:
Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → tick "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests".

Without it release_please.yml creates its release branch and commit and then fails with GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests, so the release pull request never appears and nothing can be merged or tagged.

docs.title: The Hugging Face token
docs.text: A Hugging Face access token with write permission (https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens), saved as the repository secret HF_TOKEN under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. It is what the space job pushes the Space with. Without it every release still publishes to PyPI, GHCR and the docs; the space job logs that the secret is missing and finishes green, and space-smoke is skipped. See Hosted demo.

docs.title: Package order
docs.text:
The matrix legs upload one at a time in the order below (max-parallel: 1). It matters when one leg fails and you re-publish by hand: release in dependency order so no package is ever on PyPI referencing a version of its dependency that is not.

flowchart TD
    SDK[nl2sql-sdk] --> CORE[nl2sql-engine]
    CORE --> API[nl2sql-api]
    CORE --> CLI[nl2sql-cli]
    API -.->|web extra| CLI
  1. nl2sql-sdk — no internal dependencies.
  2. nl2sql-engine — needs the SDK. Carries the engine and the dialect adapters, so its extras (nl2sql-engine[postgres] and friends) add only database drivers from PyPI and cannot be broken by publish order. It does not depend on the API.
  3. nl2sql-api — needs nl2sql-engine; its leg first checks the engine is on PyPI at the same version.
  4. nl2sql-cli — needs nl2sql-engine, and nl2sql-api for its web extra. It uploads last, after a step that checks the other two are on PyPI.

PyPI never lets a version be re-uploaded. If a release goes out broken, yank it and ship the next patch version; do not try to replace it.

Note

The repo-root pyproject.toml (nl2sql-monorepo) also carries a version. It is a workspace placeholder that is never built or published, but release-please keeps it in step with the rest so there is only ever one version in the repository.

docs.title: The real-database test bed
docs.text:
Most tests run on SQLite, DuckDB and mocks. Anything that depends on how a real server behaves (catalogs, quoting, permissions, read-only sessions, timeouts) is tested against real servers instead: PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server, each loaded with a well-known sample database and a large generated schema. One compose file, testbed/docker-compose.yml, defines all of it, and the same file runs on your machine, on GitHub's runners in CI, and on one small GCP VM started on demand.
