engine.events.catalog() lists every event: its name, description, whether a run has it (run), whether the caller's stream carries it (stream), whether the audit observer writes it (audit, narrowed by audit_only to some values of a field: of hook.decision, only deny, needs_approval, approved and error) and its data's JSON Schema (data_schema). The catalog lives in nl2sql/events/catalog.py; a name that is not in it cannot be published.

Run events (they carry the run's trace_id):

Name Data On the stream run.started question, user_id, tenant_id, roles, datasource_id, execute yes node.started node, sub_query_id yes node.finished node, sub_query_id, seconds, ok yes answer.delta field (summary, content), text yes result.manifest results: each saved result's node_id, columns, row_count, truncated, column_kinds yes sanity.flagged code, sub_query_id, retry yes run.limit_reached limit, value, spent yes run.finished a summary, never rows: status, duration_s, usage, error_codes, source, datasources, tables (datasource.schema.table), result_manifest, user_id, roles yes, with result added run.failed message (a key in it redacted), error_code, user_id, roles yes llm.call node, agent, model, the six token counts, latency_s, cost, usage_reported, error (redacted) no llm.parse_retry agent, schema, attempt (1 for the first retry), errors (the validation messages only, never the model's answer) no plan_cache.lookup datasource_id, hit no policy.decision a denial: datasource_id, schema, table (both None for a datasource), rule, step (logical_validator, curated_matcher or datasource_resolver) no hook.decision hook, point, decision, reason, ... no knowledge.used sub_query_id, datasource_id, terms (name to match score), rules (ids), dropped, digest no; not yet published clarification.requested sub_query_id, phrase, options (how many) no; published by the clarifier when a run ends needs_clarification cost.estimated datasource_id, sub_query_id, estimated_rows, cost, limit, decision (allow, confirm, refuse; the audit observer writes confirm and refuse) no; published by the policy.cost hook when a cost limit applies, once per sub-query's SQL (an approved re-run asks again)

Engine events carry no trace_id: they happen outside any question and go on the engine's bus directly.

Name Data Published when datasource.failed datasource_id, stage, message, fix a connection check fails: the engine's start, engine.check() and engine.datasources.test() (by id, or with a Datasource it builds and tests) index.started datasource_id, namespace engine.index.build starts one datasource index.column_failed datasource_id, table, column, stage, message one per issue the adapter reported (a column it could not profile, a table it could not reflect): the issue only, never the column's statistics or sample values. For the values and profile stages, whose driver message may quote a value, message is a fixed sentence and the error's type index.swapped datasource_id, namespace, build_id, schema_version, replaced_build_id, replaced_schema_version, counts (entries by type) a datasource's new build goes live (audited) index.failed datasource_id, reason one datasource's build fails; its previous build stays live schema.drifted datasource_id, from_version, to_version (None for the live database), detected_by (check or build), the whole diff's counts; never a table name engine.index.check() finds the live database differs from its build (once per drift per engine, not on every check), or a build stores a structural diff (audited). See Schema Drift retention.purged counts: what engine.storage.purge() returned (traces, results, proposals, audit) engine.storage.purge() ran (audited) llm.changed by, changes (never a key) engine.llm.replace (audited) eval.case, eval.finished see Evals engine.evals.run knowledge.loaded sources (type, counts, sha256), digests per datasource, error the engine is built with a knowledge section, and engine.knowledge.reload() (with error when the reload failed and the previous knowledge stayed live). See Knowledge profile.finished datasource_id, the report's counts, stopped_by, cost, seconds engine.knowledge.profile finished one datasource (counts only, never a name or a value). See Schema Profiler proposal.created id, kind, datasource_id, origin a new proposal entered the review queue (a thumbs-up, or another track's finding) proposal.decided id, kind, datasource_id, decision, by, wrote engine.proposals.accept or reject decided one (audited)

Release 0.9 adds the events below. They are catalogued now; the change named with each publishes it. None is on stream_query's allow-list: conversations.stream adds the two conversation events to its own. The three marked turn belong to a conversation turn, which opens a scope of its own and so has a trace_id; none carries rows, a value of an argument, or a token.

Name Data Published when conversation.started conversation_id, user_id, datasource_id engine.conversations.start conversation.step (turn) conversation_id, turn, tool, status, trace_id (an ask step's), args (argument names only) the model's loop finished one tool call conversation.turn (turn) conversation_id, turn, kind, status, trace_id, steps, stored (the stored Turn as JSON, on the conversation stream only) a turn was stored chat_tool.called (turn) tool, conversation_id, turn, ok, seconds, error_code a registry chat tool ran, in the model's loop or by name; in the turn's scope dashboard.generated dashboard_id, datasource_id, tiles, skipped engine.dashboards.generate dashboard.refreshed dashboard_id, trigger, counts (charts per status), filters (ids, never values) a refresh, an open that refreshed, or a scheduled run dashboard.changed dashboard_id, change (the edit kinds, a move being the kind move; pinned; deleted; created, a new draft), by an edit, a pin, a delete or a new draft dashboard.schedule_set dashboard_id, every_minutes, by a schedule was set; it saves a role snapshot (audited) dashboard.schedule_stopped dashboard_id, reason a schedule stopped with a visible error (audited) workspace.changed workspace_id, change (created, renamed, deleted), by engine.workspaces datasource.saved datasource_id, file, by engine.datasources.save wrote one datasource file (file is datasources/<id>.yaml; audited) api_key.created, api_key.revoked key_id, user_id, tenant_id, roles, by (on revoke, user_id is whose key it was); never the token engine.api_keys.create and revoke (audited); revoking an already revoked key publishes nothing mcp.denied reason (missing, malformed, unknown, revoked), key_id nl2sql mcp --http refused a bearer token: no header, a malformed token, an unknown key or a revoked one (audited; never the token)

The driver and exception text in datasource.failed (message, fix), index.failed (reason) and index.column_failed (message) is redacted as a trace is: every secret the engine knows of, and every secret-shaped substring, such as the password in scheme://user:password@host or user:password@host and a password=... pair, becomes [REDACTED].

policy.decision is published for denials only, and only where a refusal is enforced (the logical validator refusing a table of the plan, the curated matcher refusing a verified query, the datasource resolver refusing every datasource it was asked about). The validator publishes a refused table once per check, even when the plan names it twice. A scope asked only to filter (routing that skips some datasources, the schema retriever, the value check) publishes nothing, so the bus is not flooded with tables nobody asked for. Every catalogued event is published today except run.limit_reached, whose PR is named in its description. While a hook is attached at answer.after, a run publishes no answer.delta and sends result.manifest only after the hooks allowed the answer (never, on a deny).

docs.title: The run's stream
docs.text:
from nl2sql import NL2SQL, UserContext

engine = NL2SQL.from_config("nl2sql.yaml")
for event in engine.stream_query("Which genre sells the most tracks?",
                                 user_context=UserContext(roles=["analyst"])):
    if event.name == "node.started":
        print("running", event.data["node"])
    elif event.name == "answer.delta":
        print(event.data["text"], end="", flush=True)
    elif event.name == "run.finished":
        result = event.data["result"]   # what run_query returns, as JSON
    elif event.name == "run.failed":
        print("could not run:", event.data["message"])

The stream yields its own run's events, in the order they were published, from the allow-list: run.started, node.started, node.finished, answer.delta, result.manifest, sanity.flagged, run.limit_reached, and then exactly one of run.finished or run.failed.

  • The stream is the caller's, so it carries only what the caller may see. A policy.decision would tell a denied user which table exists, and hook.decision, llm.call and plan_cache.lookup are operator data. They reach an operator through engine.events.subscribe only.
  • The terminal event holds the result, on the stream only. The stream's run.finished is the bus event's summary plus data.result, the QueryResult as JSON. The event published on the bus never has it.
  • A failure inside the pipeline is still run.finished. A refusal, a provider error, a timeout or a cancel ends in run.finished with status: "error", exactly as run_query returns it. run.failed means the run could not start or crashed outside the pipeline.
  • Exactly one terminal event, whatever breaks. A failure the run's own run.failed could not report (an interrupt, a crash after the run's summary was published) still ends the stream with a run.failed carrying the run's trace_id.
  • Closing the iterator early cancels the run before its next step or model call.

As Server-Sent Events, each event is event: <name> and one data: line holding the whole event as JSON. That is what nl2sql-api's POST /api/v1/query/stream (REST) and the playground's /api/ask/stream send.

The allow-list is one definition: the catalog entries marked stream (nl2sql.events.STREAM_EVENTS). An event a later release adds joins the stream by its catalog entry alone.

docs.title: Subscribing: the operator's view
docs.text:
def show(event):
    print(event.at, event.trace_id, event.name, event.data)

subscription = engine.events.subscribe(show)                         # every event
denials = engine.events.subscribe(show, names=["policy.decision"])   # some
...
subscription.close()

engine.events.subscribe(fn, names=None) calls fn for every event the engine publishes, every run's and the engine's own, or for names only (a name not in the catalog is a ValueError). fn is a function of one Event, or an Observer (nl2sql.Observer): an object with on_event, whose own events choose its names when names is not given. Subscription.close() detaches it.

  • Synchronous. fn is called on the thread that published the event, which may be one of a run's worker threads, before the run goes on. A slow subscriber slows the run; an observer that keeps state locks it.
  • Fails open. An exception from fn is caught and logged once per subscriber and event name, at WARNING, on the nl2sql.events logger; it never fails a run.
  • One bus per engine. Two engines in one process share no subscriber.

The engine's own observers (log, audit, otel and plugins) subscribe the same way, from the observers section: see Observers.

docs.title: Logs carry the run's trace_id
docs.text:
Every log line written while a question runs carries its trace_id and tenant_id, on the caller's thread and on every graph worker thread, so a trace, its events and its log lines join on one id. nl2sql, nl2sql demo and nl2sql-api configure logging with the filter that adds them (--log-format json, or NL2SQL_LOG_FORMAT=json, writes them as fields). A library caller who configures logging their own way adds nl2sql.TraceContextFilter to their handler:

import logging
from nl2sql import TraceContextFilter

handler = logging.StreamHandler()
handler.addFilter(TraceContextFilter())
handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s [%(trace_id)s] %(name)s %(message)s"))
logging.getLogger().addHandler(handler)

docs.title: The trace
docs.text: A run's trace lists its events (every one but answer.delta) under events.

docs.title: Feedback and Signals
docs.text:
Nothing in the engine can tell on its own whether a live answer was right. Two small signals help: a person's rating of an answer in the playground, and the guardrail rates the engine already records for every run. nl2sql feedback reads both. Thumbs-up runs can then be exported as draft entries for the gold set, and thumbs-up generated answers as proposed verified queries.

The playground and nl2sql feedback are both built on engine.feedback (record, list, stats, export, clear, correct), which any Python caller can use too: see the public facade.

docs.title: Rating an answer in the playground
docs.text:
After a run, below Cost & time, the playground asks Was this answer right? with two buttons, 👍 Right and 👎 Wrong. A click saves the rating at once. A note is optional: pick Wrong number, Wrong table, Wrong filter or Missing rows, or type a few words (up to 280 characters), then Save note. Rating the same run again replaces the earlier rating.

The page sends only the run's trace id, the rating and the note. The server stores what it answered for that run, from its own copy of the last 200 runs, so a page cannot put a question or SQL into the table that the engine never produced. A run the playground did not answer is refused with 404.

Route Gate GET /api/feedback Whether feedback is on (and why not), the counts and the last 50 ratings. The ratings are returned only where the gate below passes. POST /api/feedback {"trace_id", "rating": "up" \| "down", "note"}. Local only, the same gate as Settings, Rebuild and the Retrieval inspector: on a non-loopback --host it answers 403 unless nl2sql demo --allow-settings, and it refuses another site's page (a foreign Origin), a non-loopback hostname and anything but JSON.

A rating needs a kept trace (engine.feedback.record reads the run's own trace), so on the default settings.traces.mode: on_failure only failed runs can be rated; set always to rate successful ones.

Feedback is available in the playground that nl2sql demo starts, and on by default. settings.feedback.enabled: false turns it off: the control then says so and POST /api/feedback answers 403.

docs.title: What is stored
docs.text:
One row per run, kept by the engine's state store (storage.state) beside the schema snapshots and the plan cache. The built-in sqlite state store keeps it in a feedback table of <storage.path>/state.db (nl2sql-demo/.nl2sql/state.db in the demo). No new service or file. The engine builds each row (nl2sql.feedback.rated_row) and hands it to StateStore.add_feedback, so a plugin state store keeps the same row.

Column Holds trace_id The run's id (primary key), the same id as its trace file. created_at Unix time of the rating. rating, note up or down, and the optional note. question, role, status The question as asked, the role it ran as, and the result status (success, plan_only, error). sql The generated SQL per sub-query, as a JSON list. Empty for a run the role was refused (SECURITY_VIOLATION). error_codes The blocking error codes, as a JSON list. Codes only, never messages. retries, validator_failures, plan_cache_hits, sub_queries The run's guardrail counters (below). models The provider and model each LLM node ran on, as JSON. engine_version The nl2sql-engine version, plus the git commit when run from a checkout. datasource_ids The datasources the run's sub-queries ran on, each once, as a JSON list. source Where the answer came from: verified (a verified query from curated.yaml) or generated.

datasource_ids and source were added after the table first shipped. A state.db from before them gains both columns, empty, through the state store's migrations when the engine next starts; the rows already in it keep their ratings and read the two as null. See The state store → Migrations.

Privacy. A row never holds result rows, the written answer, sample values, error messages or keys. It holds only what the run showed the role it ran as: the SQL of a refused run is dropped, and error messages (which can name a forbidden table) are not kept. nl2sql feedback clear deletes every row.

docs.title: Guardrail rates: nl2sql feedback stats
docs.text:
nl2sql feedback stats          # a table
nl2sql feedback stats --json   # the same numbers as JSON
nl2sql feedback stats --traces other/traces

stats counts every recorded run once, keyed by trace id: the feedback rows, plus every trace in <storage.path>/traces when settings.traces.mode kept them (the demo's config sets always). When a run has both, its counters come from the trace, which also sees a validator rejection a retry then fixed, and its rating from the row.

Signal Counted as Thumbs up / down Ratings; the rates are over rated runs. Refused, by code Runs that ended with SECURITY_VIOLATION or QUESTION_NOT_ANSWERABLE. Refiner retried Runs with at least one retry (retry_count summed over sub-queries). Validator rejected a plan Runs where the logical validator rejected a plan at least once. Errored, by code Runs with any other blocking error code. Plan cache hits Sub-queries whose plan came from the plan cache, over all planned sub-queries.

Every other rate is over all runs. From canned data (four rated runs, three more traces):

7 runs, 4 rated (feedback table plus traces in traces)

  Signal                                 Runs             Rate
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Thumbs up                                 2   50.0% of rated
  Thumbs down                               2   50.0% of rated
  Refused                                   2            28.6%
    SECURITY_VIOLATION                      1            14.3%
    QUESTION_NOT_ANSWERABLE                 1            14.3%
  Refiner retried (3 retries)               2            28.6%
  Validator rejected a plan (2 times)       2            28.6%
  Errored                                   1            14.3%
    DB_EXECUTION_ERROR                      1            14.3%
  Plan cache hits (2 of 5 sub-queries)      2            40.0%

nl2sql feedback list prints the ratings, newest first, with their notes.

docs.title: Growing an eval suite: nl2sql feedback export --good
docs.text:
nl2sql feedback export --good                     # feedback_gold_drafts.yaml
nl2sql feedback export --good --out drafts.yaml

Each thumbs-up run becomes a draft eval case, written to a suite file of its own:

  • status: draft and origin: feedback;
  • the question, the run's SQL as the sql candidate, and the datasources it read;
  • outcome set to allowed for the role it ran as;
  • no rows.

A run with no SQL, or with more than one statement, is skipped: a case's sql is one query. Drafts never replace reviewed cases. export refuses an --out that is:

  • a suite the package ships;
  • a suite evals.yaml names;
  • an existing file that holds an approved case.

A person must review every draft before it runs. A thumbs up says an answer looked right, not that its SQL is the reference answer. To promote a draft:

  1. Check that the SQL answers the question.
  2. Fill in difficulty, tags, tables, columns and outcome (add the roles that must be refused).
  3. Set status: approved.
  4. Write its rows:
engine.evals.regenerate("feedback_gold_drafts.yaml")

docs.title: Proposing verified queries: the review queue
docs.text:
A thumbs-up on a generated answer also files a verified_query proposal in the review queue: engine.feedback.record(trace_id, "up", user_context=...) keeps the rating and, when the run qualifies, proposes the question and the run's SQL for curated.yaml. Nothing is written until an admin accepts it:

nl2sql review list --kind verified_query --as admin
nl2sql review accept <id> --as admin

Runs answered by a verified query, failed runs, runs on more than one datasource, runs with no SQL or more than one statement, and rows rated before the table recorded the datasource file nothing. The same change is one proposal however often it is rated; a thumbs-up therefore influences routing only after a person accepts it. See From feedback to verified queries.

docs.title: Correcting an answer: nl2sql feedback correct
docs.text:
A thumbs-down says an answer was wrong; a correction also says what was right. engine.feedback.correct takes the run's trace id and exactly one fix, the right SQL or the right plan, and files it as a verified_query proposal (origin correction) in the review queue:

nl2sql feedback correct 7c0e2f4a-... --sql revenue.sql --note "Revenue is invoiced, not gross." --as analyst
nl2sql feedback correct 7c0e2f4a-... --plan revenue.yaml --question "What was revenue last year?" --as analyst

from nl2sql import UserContext

analyst = UserContext(user_id="bob", roles=["analyst"])
proposal = engine.feedback.correct(result.trace_id, sql="SELECT SUM(Total) AS revenue FROM Invoice",
                                   note="Revenue is invoiced, not gross.", user_context=analyst)

The fix is checked as the corrector before anything is queued, and a check that fails raises CorrectionRefused (a ValueError) with a code and the check's own messages; the command prints them and exits 1.

Only the caller who asked the run may correct it: user_context reads the trace as engine.traces.get does, so another caller's run is no_run and is never rated down, and a rating with no kept trace is not readable by a caller. nl2sql feedback correct is an operator tool and passes as_operator=True: it reads any run (and falls back to its rating), while --as still sets the scope the fix is checked against.

Step What happens Refused as The run Its kept trace gives the question (question overrides it), its datasource and its SQL; without a trace, its rating does. First, the corrector's role must reach every datasource the run read and every table its SQL read; the refusal names none of them, and the run's rating is left as it was. Then a run on several datasources is refused (a verified query answers from one), and the run is rated down with the note unless it already is. no_run, denied, multi_datasource A plan fix Runs as a pinned plan with execute=False: plan.after, the logical validator and the generator, under the corrector's scope, with no model call. The SQL is the engine's rendering. invalid_plan, with the validator's messages A SQL fix Must parse as exactly one read-only query in the datasource's dialect (the curated config's own check; a trailing ; and comment are fine), with no :name placeholders. It reads plain tables only, never a table-valued function, and calls only the functions a plan may call plus CAST, CASE, EXISTS and the current date and time. It reads only tables the corrector's role may read. not_read_only, denied The hooks The SQL passes the execute.before hooks with the corrector as the caller. A deny or a failed hook refuses it, and so does a request for approval: a correction is never run with an approval. hook_denied, needs_approval The check The SQL runs once through the adapter, as nl2sql curated test runs a verified query: read-only, under the datasource's limits, reading the first batch of rows and keeping none. An empty result is allowed. failed, with the adapter's message (an error it did not wrap is named by its type only) The proposal change is in curated.yaml's shape: an id slugged from the question, the question as its one phrasing, the SQL, and the note as its description (a placeholder without one). tables lists every table the fix and the original SQL read; evidence holds the trace id, the original SQL, ran, row_count and columns.

Nothing is written to curated.yaml (or any file a person owns) until an admin accepts the proposal, usually with edits: a better id, more phrasings, and :name params in place of the literal values. Only a caller whose scope reaches every table in tables sees the proposal. Keep traces (settings.traces.mode: always) to correct runs that succeeded and were not rated; the default keeps only failed runs' traces.

docs.title: Turning it off and clearing it
docs.text:
• settings.feedback.enabled: false stops the playground recording ratings.
  • nl2sql feedback clear deletes every rating (--yes skips the prompt). Schema snapshots and the plan cache are kept, and nl2sql cache clear never touches the ratings.

docs.title: Observability Stack
docs.text:
NL2SQL provides structured logging always, per-question token and time telemetry on every run, and events that observers turn into logs, an audit log and OpenTelemetry metrics and traces.

  • Every run reports its cost and timings in the result. run_with_graph() always attaches NodeTimingCallback (wall-clock seconds per node, into QueryResult.timings) and TokenUsageCallback (LLM calls, input / cached / output / reasoning tokens and model seconds per node and per question, into QueryResult.usage). That covers the Python API, the REST API, the CLI and the demo playground. Every call is priced from the dated price table and llm.prices (Prices), so usage.cost is the question's cost whenever every model it called has a price. See the query API.
  • Every question runs under caps. settings.pipeline.max_llm_calls (60) and max_cost_usd (none) are checked before each model call; a question that reaches one ends stopped and publishes run.limit_reached, which the audit log records (Per-question caps).
  • Everything else is an event, and observers decide where it goes. A run publishes its steps (node.*), each model call (llm.call, from TokenUsageCallback), each plan cache lookup (plan_cache.lookup) and its summary (run.finished); engine.llm.replace publishes llm.changed. The observers in the observers section receive them: by default log and audit.
  • OpenTelemetry is an observer, and an extra. An otel observer (with pip install "nl2sql-engine[otel]") records the metrics below and one span per run with a child span per step, on providers of its own, exported over OTLP (gRPC) or to the console. Without one, nothing exports to OpenTelemetry.
  • The audit log is the audit observer's. JSON lines under <storage.path>/audit/, one summary line per run plus the denials, approvals, limits and changes; 90 days by default, purged by engine.storage.purge().

docs.title: Telemetry flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Pipeline as run_with_graph()
    participant Usage as TokenUsageCallback
    participant Bus as The engine's bus
    participant Observers as log, audit, otel
    participant Result as QueryResult

    Pipeline->>Usage: always attached
    Usage->>Result: usage
    Usage->>Bus: llm.call
    Pipeline->>Bus: node.started, node.finished, run.finished
    Bus->>Observers: each event, in config order

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The otel observer records:

  • nl2sql.node.duration (histogram, seconds), attribute node, from node.finished.
  • nl2sql.token.usage (counter), attributes node, model and type: one point per LLM call for each of input, cached_input, cache_write_input, output, reasoning and total, from llm.call.
  • nl2sql.plan_cache.lookups (counter), attributes result (hit or miss) and datasource_id, from plan_cache.lookup. The per-question view is QueryResult.usage.plan_cache_hits and sub_queries[].plan_source; see Determinism → The plan cache.
  • nl2sql.run.cost (histogram, USD), attribute status, from run.finished when the run was priced.

The 0.6 datasource_id attribute on nl2sql.token.usage is gone: llm.call does not carry it. Token usage is not kept in a process-wide list; read it from QueryResult.usage.

docs.title: Audit logging
docs.text: The audit observer writes <storage.path>/audit/<date>.jsonl, one JSON line per audited event: one summary per run (run.finished or run.failed: the user, roles, datasources, tables read, status and source; never rows), and each policy.decision, hook.decision that denied, asked for or carried an approval or failed, run.limit_reached, llm.changed, index.swapped, retention.purged and schema.drifted. llm.changed names who made the change and each agent's old and new provider and model, never a key. See Observers → audit.

docs.title: Structured logging
docs.text: The library does not configure logging on import; the application entry point calls nl2sql.configure_logging after loading the .env next to nl2sql.yaml, so a NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL there applies (the REST API calls it in its lifespan, after nl2sql-api serve has loaded the .env; under plain uvicorn the variable must already be exported, the CLI before every command, nl2sql demo again once the demo project's .env is loaded). JSON lines are chosen with nl2sql --log-format json (any command) or NL2SQL_LOG_FORMAT=json (any entry point); text is the default. Every question's RunScope sets the run's trace_id and tenant_id in the context TraceContextFilter reads, inside the run's worker, so a log line written during a run carries them, on LangGraph's worker threads too.

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:
• Observers: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/observers/ (log.py, audit.py, otel.py)
  • Events: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/events/
  • Token usage: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/services/callbacks/token_handler.py
  • Logging: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/common/logger.py

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
Global options: --config PATH names the nl2sql.yaml every command reads (without it, NL2SQL_CONFIG, then ./nl2sql.yaml), and --version prints the installed version. The .env next to that nl2sql.yaml is loaded first; variables already exported in your shell win over the file. Paths inside the config are relative to nl2sql.yaml, so a command works from any folder. Every command has --help.

Command Purpose Key options nl2sql chat A terminal chat over your data (Textual): ask, follow up, F2 why this answer, F3 the SQL, /chart, /report, approve. Keyboard only --demo, --dir (default nl2sql-demo), --as ROLE, --user NAME, --datasource ID nl2sql demo Start nl2sql-api serve --demo (it writes the demo project, indexes it and serves the web app) and open the browser --dir (default nl2sql-demo), --host (default 127.0.0.1), --port (default 8765), --no-browser nl2sql init [DIR] Write a new config into DIR (default .): nl2sql.yaml plus one file per section, checked with load_config. Never writes a key and never overwrites a file without --force --demo (the three sample databases, their roles, verified queries, sample questions and settings), --provider (openai, anthropic or openrouter; default openai), --force nl2sql run "QUESTION" Ask a question and print the plan, checks, SQL, rows and answer --role (default admin), --no-exec (plan and validate only), --ds-id, --verbose/-v, --show-perf nl2sql index Index datasource schemas into the index of the configured embedding model, one datasource at a time --datasource/-d ID (repeatable), --refresh (write the entries again from the stored snapshot, the glossary and the curated section after a change; no schema read, no model call, and only changed entries are embedded), --check (re-index nothing: compare each live database with the schema its index was built from; exits 0 unchanged, 1 drifted, 2 a check failed or nothing was checked; with --role (default admin) and --json) nl2sql mcp Serve the engine to an MCP client: ask, list_datasources, describe_table. Over stdio by default, as the role given (refuses to start with no role and no policies.default_role); with --http, over HTTP behind bearer API keys, each running as its key's roles. Needs pip install "nl2sql-engine[mcp]" --role (repeatable), --user (default mcp), --http, --host, --port nl2sql index prune Drop the index of every other embedding model (and 0.5's collection); the current one is kept nl2sql config check Check the whole config without starting the engine: every file, include and ${env:...}, and every component it names (installed, right interface version, drivers present). Problems are printed by file; each secret is reported present or missing, never printed. Exits 0, or 1 on any problem. Writes nothing under storage.path --connect (also connect to every datasource; one that fails is a problem) nl2sql doctor Check Python, installed drivers and provider keys, then build the configured engine and print engine.check(): each datasource, each agent's key, the index nl2sql list-adapters List the installed datasource adapters nl2sql install NAME pip-install the driver extra for an adapter (postgres, mysql, mssql, duckdb, sqlite: the connection.type names), after a confirmation nl2sql policy validate Check the config's policies against its datasources nl2sql curated validate Check the curated section (verified queries): ids, params, read-only SQL in each datasource's dialect, tables against the index; exits 1 on any error nl2sql curated test Run every verified query once against its database, read-only, with each param's default or example bound; reports pass/fail per query and exits 1 on any failure nl2sql knowledge show The glossary as the engine uses it, each item with its origin (knowledge, database, derived); what the role cannot read is left out; problems last, exit 1 when there are any --datasource ID, --as ROLE (repeatable), --user nl2sql knowledge export The glossary items the role may see as one canonical glossary.yaml; never over a config or source file --datasource ID (repeatable), --out FILE (default: stdout), --as ROLE, --user nl2sql knowledge sources Each knowledge source: type, item counts, hash, when it loaded, its last reload error --as ROLE, --user nl2sql review list The review queue: proposed knowledge and verified queries the role may see, newest first --kind K, --datasource ID, --status S (default proposed; all), --as ROLE (repeatable), --user nl2sql review show ID One proposal, with the current glossary or curated value beside the proposed change --as ROLE, --user nl2sql review accept ID... Accept proposals as an admin role: writes the glossary and curated.yaml once each, then reloads and refreshes; exits 1 when an item is refused --all (with --kind, --datasource), --as ROLE, --user nl2sql review reject ID... Reject proposals as an admin role; a rejected change is never proposed again --reason TEXT, --as ROLE, --user nl2sql review export The open proposals the role may see as a review file, to decide in a pull request --out FILE, --kind K, --datasource ID, --as ROLE, --user nl2sql review apply FILE Read a review file as an admin role: accept each accept (with its edited change), reject each reject --as ROLE, --user nl2sql profile Profile the indexed schema and file what it finds for review, and with --draft have the model draft missing descriptions; arrives in 0.8 --datasource ID, --draft, --max-cost USD, --as ROLE, --user nl2sql launch Find a database (a file, DATABASE_URL or a local port), test it, write the project with secrets in .env, index, profile, file five starter questions and review what it found, in one sitting; also uvx --from nl2sql-engine nl2sql launch; arrives in 0.9 DIR, --provider, --as ROLE, --draft, --yes (accept nothing; write review.yaml), --no-ports nl2sql keys create Create an API key for MCP over HTTP; the token is printed once; managing keys needs an admin role (under allow_all leave out --as and --role) --user, --role (repeatable), --tenant, --label, --as ROLE nl2sql keys list The API keys, never a secret (under allow_all leave out --as) --as ROLE nl2sql keys revoke ID Revoke an API key; it stops verifying at once (under allow_all leave out --as) --as ROLE nl2sql dashboards refresh Re-run the stored plans of a dashboard, or of every dashboard that is due, with no model call; arrives in 0.9 --dashboard ID, --due, --as ROLE nl2sql trace show TARGET Print a run trace's timeline: nodes, attempts, durations, tokens, errors a trace file, or a trace id in the trace store (storage.traces) nl2sql trace replay TARGET Re-run a traced question on its recorded LLM responses, with no model calls nl2sql cache clear Empty the plan cache in <storage.path>/state.db; schema snapshots are kept nl2sql storage purge Delete traces and results older than their store's max_age_days (14 and 7 days by default), and decided proposals older than settings.review.max_age_days (365); nl2sql-api does this at startup and once a day nl2sql feedback list Playground ratings, newest first --limit (default 50) nl2sql feedback stats Ratings plus guardrail rates: refusals, refiner retries, validator rejections, errors, plan-cache hits --json, --traces DIR nl2sql feedback export --good Write thumbs-up runs as draft eval cases to a separate suite file for review --out (default feedback_gold_drafts.yaml) nl2sql feedback clear Delete every rating --yes nl2sql feedback correct TRACE_ID Rate a run down with its fix; the fix is checked as the role (validator or read-only and scope, execute.before hooks, one run) and filed in the review queue as a verified query --sql FILE or --plan FILE, --question TEXT, --note TEXT, --as ROLE, --user nl2sql eval run Run the eval suites in one mode (full: the model, priced and capped; plans: the gold plans on a fake LLM; retrieval: no model) and, with --baseline, gate the run against a report, a record or a benchmarks/ folder. Exits 1 on a regression, 2 on a usage error or a baseline it cannot compare, 3 at the cost cap; mode full refuses to run when CI is set --mode, --suite, --llm (preset, file or NAME=), --cases, --passes, --max-cost, --baseline, --out (default eval_<mode>.json next to nl2sql.yaml) nl2sql eval regenerate PATH Write a suite's expected rows: each approved case's SQL through its datasource's adapter; exits 1 when a case's SQL failed nl2sql eval seed Draft eval cases from a datasource's schema, as a role: the model writes questions with typed plans, the engine validates each, passes it through the execute hooks and runs it read-only, and the survivors are appended as status: draft for review. Exits 2 on a refusal, 3 at the cost cap or the call limit; refuses to run when CI is set --datasource, --out, --count (default 20), --role (default policies.default_role), --max-cost (default evals.yaml's) nl2sql eval publish [REPORT ...] Record each report eval run wrote under benchmarks/, then rebuild docs/benchmarks.md and the results block above; run from the repo root --note, --from DIR

The nl2sql eval group is the whole command; nl2sql eval --help lists its subcommands. Evals also run from Python, with engine.evals (Evals).

Examples, from the demo folder (cd nl2sql-demo, so ./nl2sql.yaml is the config; from anywhere else, add --config nl2sql-demo/nl2sql.yaml):

nl2sql run "How many customers do we have, by country?"
nl2sql run --role viewer "Who are the top 5 customers by total spend?"   # refused
nl2sql run --no-exec "Which artist has the most albums?"                 # plan only
nl2sql feedback stats

run and index call engine.check() before they start: a datasource marked required: true that cannot connect stops them with the report (exit 1); any other datasource that fails is printed and left out.

run exits 1 when the run ends with an ERROR or CRITICAL error (a refusal included). More: Demo guide, Debugging a Run, Feedback and Signals, Evaluation.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
• ArtifactRef: Metadata reference to persisted query results (URI, backend, schema_version).
  • Chunk: Typed, vector-indexed schema slice used for retrieval (datasource, table, column, relationship).
  • ExecutionDAG: Deterministic logical DAG of scan/combine/post operations.
  • GraphState: Shared state across the control graph pipeline.
  • SchemaContract: Canonical schema structure for a datasource (tables, columns, foreign keys).
  • SchemaMetadata: Descriptive metadata and statistics for schema elements.
  • SchemaSnapshot: Pair of SchemaContract + SchemaMetadata.
  • SubQuery: Decomposed, datasource-scoped query intent from the decomposer.
  • Subgraph: LangGraph subgraph that handles a specific execution capability (e.g., SQL agent).
  • ResultFrame: Adapter response containing rows/columns, row_count, and error metadata.
  • IndexStore: the store that keeps the index entries, in a namespace per embedding model, and each datasource's live build pointer (chroma by default).
  • Retriever: the engine's MMR searches over the index store's live builds, pinned per run.
  • RBAC: Role-based access control enforcing datasource/table permissions.

docs.title: Status and limitations
docs.text:
The packages are pre-1.0. nl2sql-sdk, nl2sql-engine, nl2sql-api and nl2sql-cli share one version and are released together (Releasing). Unreleased changes are on main; see the changelog for what is released.

Known limitations:

  • Every question needs an LLM; only indexing is key-free. The key-free demo answers nothing until you record answers or add a key.
  • Small local models often fail to produce a valid plan.
  • A question cannot span two databases: every sub-query is planned against one datasource, so the demo's three cannot be joined, however much their data lines up.
  • Read-only is enforced by SQLite when a datasource asks for it, and by nothing else (see Security Model), so a database user that can only read is still the real control. max_bytes is not enforced; row_limit is, in the generated SQL.
  • The hosted demo's rate limits are best-effort: they live in one process, and the per-session cap hangs on a cookie the visitor can clear.
  • The model's output is not reproducible; determinism is structural (fixed topology, validation before generation, plan cache) (Determinism).
  • The engine does not authenticate callers in the query path: it believes the UserContext it is given. The REST API resolves one from an API key, a trusted proxy's headers, a static role or the local operator (Security Model). run_query without a user_context raises instead of refusing.
  • OpenTelemetry metrics and traces are off unless an otel observer is configured (Observability).

Roadmap: using the engine on your own database (bring-your-own-database setup beyond the bundled demo databases) is planned. nl2sql init and the adapters exist, and nl2sql launch (Launch) walks you from a database to a working project; it does not yet cover every datasource type or every setting.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
What each release is for, in plain words. The full list of commits is in CHANGELOG.md. How a release is cut is in Releasing.

  • 0.9.1: better answers on large schemas: model-picked tables, joins across partitioned tables, date differences, split questions in the shape asked, and a fairer eval scorer.
  • 0.9.0: Wave C: model-led conversations with chat tools, automatic charts and diagrams, dashboards in workspaces with token-free refresh, nl2sql launch, and MCP over HTTP with API keys.
  • 0.8.0: Wave B: business knowledge in the index and prompts, a review queue, a schema profiler, clarifying questions, "why this answer" and a cost guard.
  • 0.7.0: Wave A: events and observers, hooks and approval, nl2sql eval with a regression gate, five-signal routing, answer sanity checks, cost caps, schema drift and an MCP server.
  • 0.6.0: a real-database test bed, adapter SDK v2 and its conformance kit, four storage slots, OpenAI-compatible providers and allow/deny policy globs.
  • 0.5.0: Configuration v2, one nl2sql.yaml, an extension registry, a namespaced Python API and per-engine config; a clean break from 0.4.
  • 0.4.1: admin-only REST routes, opt-in enrichment, schema-aware policies and a datasource that fails no longer stops startup.
  • 0.4.0: curated answers, where a question that matches a verified query runs its reviewed SQL and is labelled verified.
  • 0.3.0: results at any size, paged and downloadable, with a 20-row preview for the answer and a streamed run.
  • 0.2.4: a cached plan is reused only on the day it was made, so relative dates stay current.
  • 0.2.3: the model knows today's date and its data, and wrong or empty queries are retried or explained.
  • 0.2.2: correct answers or clear refusals for multi-sub-query questions, and the demo at nl2sql.codewithnk.com.
  • 0.2.1: the release image on Python 3.12, and a reliable Space deploy.
  • 0.2.0: the hosted demo, with or without a key, and pip install "nl2sql-engine[demo]".
  • 0.1.2: a merged release PR publishes to PyPI on its own.
  • 0.1.1: fixes for nl2sql doctor, the Docker demo, pipeline errors and the API image.
  • 0.1.0: the first release, as three packages on PyPI.

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.1.0
docs.text:
The first release: the NL2SQL engine, its REST API and the adapter SDK on PyPI as three packages that share one version.

Released 2026-08-28.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• pip install nl2sql-engine gives you the engine and the nl2sql CLI. nl2sql-api serves it over REST, and nl2sql-adapter-sdk is what a third-party database adapter builds against.
  • The model writes a typed plan, never SQL. The plan is checked against the schema and your role before any SQL is generated.
  • A DuckDB adapter joins PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and SQLite.
  • The Docker demo now starts the application as well as its databases, so it can answer a question with nothing else installed.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• A DuckDB adapter, installed with the nl2sql-engine[duckdb] extra (#57).
  • The Docker demo runs the application next to its databases. SQL Server is now opt-in, so the first start skips a 1.6 GB download (#59).
  • Releases are automated: release-please writes the changelog, and a merged release PR publishes to PyPI (#58).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Cancelling one run no longer cancels every other run in the process (#48).
  • The REST API needs its CORS origins listed. It no longer accepts any origin together with credentials (#49).
  • The minimum versions of pydantic, langgraph and chromadb are now correct (#50).
  • Importing nl2sql no longer changes your application's logging setup (#51).
  • The NL2SQL facade builds its settings API correctly (#52).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The README and architecture docs now describe only code that exists (#54), and the docs cover the three-package layout (#60).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• No API image was published to GHCR for 0.1.0, because the image build failed. 0.1.1 fixes the build.
  • The project is pre-1.0, so the API can still change between minor versions.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install "nl2sql-engine==0.1.0"

Breaking changes: nine earlier distributions are now three, nl2sql-engine, nl2sql-api and nl2sql-adapter-sdk, and the dialect adapters ship inside the engine (#56). The import name is still nl2sql.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.1.1, with fixes for the CLI, the Docker demo and the release pipeline.

Full changelog: CHANGELOG.md

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.1.1
docs.text:
A fix release for 0.1.0: nl2sql doctor, the Docker demo and pipeline errors now work as documented, and the API image builds.

Released 2026-09-07.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• nl2sql doctor, the command you run when something is wrong, no longer crashes.
  • The Docker demo can reach its databases and survives a terminal that cannot show prompts.
  • A question that no subgraph can answer ends with a clear error code, not a crash.
  • The API image builds and is published to GHCR.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• nl2sql doctor checks connectivity again instead of failing on an import (#72).
  • A secrets config with every provider commented out is read as "no secret providers", not an error (#73).
  • The Docker demo's datasources are reachable: only passwords are treated as secrets when a config is resolved (#74).
  • nl2sql setup --demo --docker no longer crashes under Git Bash on Windows (#79).
  • When no subgraph matches a question, the pipeline raises a real error (#75), and its error code reaches the caller (#78).
  • The API image is built from the repository root, which fixes the GHCR publish that failed on 0.1.0 (#70).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The docs match the code again (#77).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Tagging 0.1.1 did not publish it, because the PyPI upload failed in CI. The packages and the image went out about an hour later, by a manual re-run once the fix that shipped as 0.1.2 was on main.
  • The project is pre-1.0, so the API can still change between minor versions.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine==0.1.1"

Breaking changes: none.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.1.2, which fixes publishing to PyPI from the release workflow.

Full changelog: v0.1.0...v0.1.1

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.1.2
docs.text:
A release-pipeline fix: a merged release PR now reaches PyPI on its own. The packages are the same as 0.1.1.

Released 2026-09-07.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Merging the release PR publishes all three packages to PyPI with no manual step. On 0.1.1, that upload failed.
  • Library code has not changed since 0.1.1.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • The release workflow publishes without PEP 740 attestations. Through the called workflow, PyPI rejected them (#80).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Released packages have no PEP 740 provenance attestations. That is the cost of this fix.
  • The project is pre-1.0, so the API can still change between minor versions.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine==0.1.2"

Breaking changes: none.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.2.0, the hosted demo.

Full changelog: v0.1.1...v0.1.2

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.0
docs.text:
The hosted demo release: try NL2SQL in a browser, without a key or with your own, or run the same playground locally with pip install "nl2sql-engine[demo]".

Released 2026-10-10.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• A public demo on Hugging Face Spaces (https://nadeem4nk-nl2sql-demo.hf.space). It asks three linked sample databases in plain English and shows the plan, the checks, the SQL and the rows.
  • No key needed to start. Twenty guided questions replay real recorded answers. For anything else, bring your own key; it stays in your browser tab and is used for that one request only.
  • pip install "nl2sql-engine[demo]" and nl2sql demo run the same playground on your machine. It has a home page, an answer-first Ask page, a Pipeline page and a Retrieval inspector.
  • Claude is supported natively alongside OpenAI-compatible providers, and each step can use its own model.
  • A release now runs end to end on its own: tag, PyPI, a fresh install check, then the Space at the same version.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Hosted mode: a public demo where each visitor brings their own key and the server holds none (#165), plus the Dockerfile and Space config to run it (#168).
  • Try the hosted demo without a key, on recorded runs (#197), with real recorded answers for the 20 guided questions (#205).
  • The React playground and nl2sql demo (#93), now with a home page (#198), an answer-first Ask page (#186) and a Pipeline page (#171).
  • Support and web-analytics sample databases, linked to Chinook customers (#157).
  • Native Claude support, and a provider per pipeline step (#124). In the hosted demo, each step can use its own model, with a key per provider (#173).
  • QueryResult exposes the plan, the validation checks, a row sample, the status and timings (#88).
  • Every run can be recorded to a trace file, viewed, and replayed without the model (#104).
  • Validated plans are cached by question and schema version, and checked again on every use (#122).
  • An evaluation harness: a Chinook gold dataset (#114), a tier 1 check on every PR (#119) and a tier 2 benchmark against real models (#126).
  • Each tagged release deploys the Space, pinned to the version on PyPI (#196).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• The validator rejects a plan whose tables cannot be joined before SQL is generated, so the model can try again (#161). Only known function names are allowed in plans (#137).
  • Role checks refuse without leaking data from forbidden tables, and deny unknown or empty roles cleanly (#112).
  • API keys and connection secrets are held as SecretStr, so they never print (#113).
  • When a sub-query fails, you get a structured result, not a crash or a loop (#84). The pipeline timeout is enforced (#87).
  • The aggregator combines sub-query results correctly when join keys carry a prefix (#144, #162).
  • Many smaller fixes to the generator, the decomposer, the CLI and the demo. See the changelog below.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The README is organised around a quickstart, results, the CLI, the REST API and screenshots (#131), and links the live demo (#191).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• No API image was published to GHCR for 0.2.0: its Dockerfile used Python 3.11. The first Space deploy also failed, on a PyPI index that had not caught up. Both are fixed in 0.2.1.
  • Without a key, the hosted demo only answers the 20 guided questions it has recordings for.
  • A question that needs several sub-queries can be answered wrong without an error. 0.2.2 fixes the known cases.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.0"

Breaking changes: Chinook is now the only demo dataset. nl2sql setup --demo --lite, --demo --docker and nl2sql demo --dataset are removed, and nl2sql setup --demo sets up Chinook (#98).

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.2.1, which fixes the release image and makes the Space deploy reliable.

Full changelog: v0.1.2...v0.2.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.1
docs.text:
A release-pipeline fix for 0.2.0: the API image is built on Python 3.12, and the hosted demo deploys reliably. The library is unchanged.

Released 2026-10-10.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• ghcr.io/nadeem4/nl2sql-api is published again. 0.2.1 is the first image of the 0.2 line.
  • The Space deploy waits until PyPI serves the new version, and retries its install.
  • A Space deploy only passes when the Space is actually running.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• The release image moves to Python 3.12, which every package requires. A new PR check builds the image, so a broken Dockerfile fails before release (#208).
  • The Space deploy waits for PyPI to list the version before it pushes, and the Space's install retries up to ten times (#208).
  • A redeploy that pushes nothing asks for a rebuild, and the job fails unless the Space ends up running (#208).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• There is no nl2sql-api:0.2.0 image. Use 0.2.1 or later.
  • Without a key, the hosted demo only answers the 20 guided questions it has recordings for.
  • A question that needs several sub-queries can be answered wrong without an error. 0.2.2 fixes the known cases.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.1"

Breaking changes: none.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.2.2, with correctness fixes for questions answered from several sub-queries.

Full changelog: v0.2.0...v0.2.1

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.2
docs.text:
A correctness release: a question answered from several sub-queries now gets the right answer or a clear refusal, never a silently wrong one. The live demo also moves to https://nl2sql.codewithnk.com.

Released 2026-10-11.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Each sub-query writes its own result file. Before this, two sub-queries of one question could overwrite each other, and a join could combine a result with itself.
  • A join or compare is refused if it lost one of its inputs, for example to a role restriction, instead of being answered from the side that remained.
  • A join or compare is refused if one input was cut short by the row cap. Missing rows mean missing matches.
  • The hosted demo has its own domain, https://nl2sql.codewithnk.com.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: • The link preview and the release checks use nl2sql.codewithnk.com, the Space's custom domain (#212).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• One result artifact per sub-query, at <tenant_id>/<request_id>/<sub_query_id>.parquet. A failed aggregation now ends the run instead of asking the model to explain an empty result (#213).
  • A join or compare that lost one of its inputs is refused with PLANNER_FAILED, before any query runs. The message does not name the restricted datasource (#214).
  • A join or compare on a sub-query that hit the row cap is refused with RESULT_TRUNCATED. A union on a capped input still runs, with a warning (#215).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The README and docs link the live demo at nl2sql.codewithnk.com (#210).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Questions across several databases are not yet supported end to end. Each database answers its own sub-query and the results are joined in memory. This release makes that safer, not complete.
  • Each sub-query returns at most 1,000 rows by default (the datasource's row_limit). A join over a larger input is refused rather than answered.
  • Without a key, the hosted demo only answers the 20 guided questions it has recordings for.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.2"

Breaking changes: none. The default result artifact path gains a <sub_query_id> level. A custom RESULT_ARTIFACT_PATH_TEMPLATE keeps working: the sub-query id is added to its file name.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: cross-database queries, so one question can be answered from several databases.

Full changelog: v0.2.1...v0.2.2

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.3
docs.text:
A correctness release: the model now knows today's date, what values a column holds and where its data starts and ends, and a query that comes back wrong or empty is retried or explained instead of answered as fact.

Released 2026-10-12.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• "This year" and "the last 30 days" are resolved against today's date, not a year the model guessed. When the period falls outside the data, the planner uses the latest period the data has and says so.
  • A filter on a value the column does not hold, such as 'Metal' for 'Heavy Metal', no longer turns into a confident "none". A close match is retried once; a missing value is named as a warning in the answer.
  • A query the database rejects as wrong (an unknown column, a type mismatch, bad syntax) goes back to the refiner for another try, instead of ending the run.
  • A column the plan names but the schema does not have is caught before the query runs, and the planner is asked to fix it.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Strict column checking is on by default: an unknown column is a retryable COLUMN_NOT_FOUND. LOGICAL_VALIDATOR_STRICT_COLUMNS=false restores the old warning (#219).
  • The plan's offset is rendered, so "rows 11 to 20" no longer returns rows 1 to 10. An offset without an order is refused before generation (#221).
  • A query the database rejects as wrong is retried through the refiner. A refusal (permission, timeout, connection) still ends the run. Retry feedback carries only the latest error, with no SQL echo or stack trace (#223).
  • An empty result that filtered on a missing value is checked: a close stored value sends the plan back once, otherwise the answer carries a warning such as "There is no Genre with Name 'Polka'." (#226).
  • DATE and DATETIME leave the function allow-list, which now matches the planner prompt. STRFTIME is still accepted as a legacy name (#218).
  • The planner and refiner are told today's date. NL2SQL_TODAY pins it; unset, it is the UTC date (#220).
  • A text column with 50 or fewer distinct values keeps all of them in the index, not five samples (#222).
  • Date and numeric columns carry their data range in the prompt, with a rule for relative periods outside it (#224).
  • Two gold questions cover data ranges and value matching. The gold set is now 47 questions (#225).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • Every version has a release page, written by a skill and required in CI before a release (#216).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Each query returns at most 1,000 rows by default, and the answer model sees the whole result.
  • A cached plan for a relative-date question ("this month") can be reused on a later day. 0.2.4 fixes this.
  • "Rows 11 to 20" reaches the planner only through the question text.
  • Questions across several databases are still limited.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.3"

Breaking changes: none. Two behaviour changes: an unknown column is now a retried error rather than a warning (set LOGICAL_VALIDATOR_STRICT_COLUMNS=false for the old behaviour), and a plan calling DATE or DATETIME is refused. Re-index an existing demo folder to pick up the full column values: nl2sql setup --demo or nl2sql --env demo index.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.2.4, starting with cached plans for relative-date questions.

Full changelog: v0.2.2...v0.2.3

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.2.4
docs.text:
A cache fix: a cached plan is now reused only on the day it was made, so a relative-date question such as "the last 30 days" is never answered with an earlier day's dates.

Released 2026-10-12.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• "This year", "the last 30 days" and "yesterday" are planned against today's date, even when the same question was asked on an earlier day. Before this, the plan cache could serve an earlier day's plan with that day's dates.
  • Every cached plan carries the date it was made, not only plans that look date-relative, because nothing reliably tells which plans depend on today. A plan is reused for the rest of that day, or for as long as NL2SQL_TODAY pins the date.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • The plan cache key includes the run date (#228).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Each query returns at most 1,000 rows by default, and the answer model sees the whole result.
  • "Rows 11 to 20" reaches the planner only through the question text.
  • Questions across several databases are still limited.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.2.4"

Breaking changes: none. Plans cached before the upgrade no longer match and are planned again once.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.3.0, starting with larger results.

Full changelog: v0.2.3...v0.2.4

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.3.0
docs.text:
Results at any size: a question can now return up to 100,000 rows by default, the whole result is saved and can be paged through or downloaded as CSV, and the answer model reads a 20-row preview instead of every row.

Released 2026-10-12.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• The default row cap rises from 1,000 to 100,000 (10,000 in the demo). A result that hits the cap is flagged, and the answer says it is incomplete and asks you to narrow the question.
  • The answer model sees the first 20 rows and the total count, not the whole result, so a large result no longer fills the prompt.
  • Every run's result is saved whole. Page through it or download it as CSV from the SDK, nl2sql-api or the playground, where each result gets its own tab and every sub-query is shown.
  • A run can stream its progress and its answer as Server-Sent Events. The playground lights up each step as it finishes and writes the answer as it arrives.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• The answer model gets a 20-row preview and the row count (ANSWER_PREVIEW_ROWS). RESULT_ROW_LIMIT (default 100,000) replaces the 1,000-row cap, and a result cut at the cap is flagged in truncated and in the answer's warnings (#231).
  • Results are fetched in batches of RESULT_FETCH_BATCH_SIZE rows through a new optional StreamingAdapterProtocol; adapters without it work unchanged. Each run's combined result is saved as parquet in its artifact folder (#234).
  • A run writes a manifest.json of its results, returned as QueryResult.result_manifest. get_result_manifest, get_result_page and export_result_csv read a result back, and nl2sql-api and the playground serve the same as page and CSV routes (#235).
  • The playground pages through the saved result 100 rows at a time, shows a tab per result, downloads the full CSV and shows every sub-query in the Plan and SQL steps (#236).
  • NL2SQL.stream_query, POST /api/v1/query/stream and the playground's /api/ask/stream send a run's progress, its result manifest and its answer token by token as Server-Sent Events. The playground falls back to the non-streaming call if the stream fails (#237).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • A datasource's row_limit, statement_timeout_ms and max_bytes written beside connection, as the docs show, are now honoured; they were silently ignored. If a limit is set both there and under options, the lower wins (#233).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Anyone with a role who knows a run's id can read its saved result. There is no access check beyond the tenant's folder.
  • The downloaded CSV does not guard against spreadsheet formulas in cell values.
  • A join, sort or group-by across results may still hold its inputs in memory (as polars columns, not Python rows).
  • When a stream breaks, the playground asks the question again without streaming, so it is run a second time.
  • Questions across several databases are still limited.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.3.0"

Breaking changes: none. Three behaviour changes:

  • The default row cap is 100,000, not 1,000. To keep a lower cap, set RESULT_ROW_LIMIT or a datasource's row_limit.
  • terminal_results now holds only the 20-row preview. The full result is the saved artifact; read it with get_result_page or export_result_csv.
  • Every run writes its combined result as parquet and a manifest.json in its artifact folder. On S3 or ADLS, the manifest needs s3fs or adlfs installed.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.4.0.

Full changelog: v0.2.4...v0.3.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.4.0
docs.text:
Curated answers: a data team can write verified queries, reviewed SQL with typed parameters, and when a question matches one the engine runs that SQL with the values bound instead of generating new SQL, and labels the answer as verified. Any other question is answered by generated SQL, as before.

Released 2026-10-13.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Write verified queries in configs/curated.yaml: a description, the phrasings people ask, typed parameters and the SQL. When a question matches one, its reviewed SQL runs with the values bound by the driver, never pasted into the text.
  • An answer from a verified query says so. QueryResult.source is verified or generated in the SDK, the REST response and the trace, and the playground shows a "Verified" badge with the query's id and values.
  • Point the planner at the tables your team trusts with preferred_tables in datasources.yaml. The built-in adapters now index views as well as tables.
  • Thumbs-up feedback on generated answers can become proposed verified queries with nl2sql curated proposals export, for a person to review and commit.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• configs/curated.yaml, its settings CURATED_CONFIG and CURATED_ENABLED, and nl2sql curated validate, which checks every verified query, its parameters and its SQL against the indexed schema (#240).
  • nl2sql index indexes each verified query's phrasings, nl2sql index --curated-only refreshes only those after an edit, and nl2sql doctor warns when curated.yaml changed since the last index (#242).
  • A new first step, the curated matcher, picks a verified query and its values, checks the values and the role's access in code, and runs the saved SQL with bound parameters; anything else goes to the generated pipeline with a reason in the trace (#243).
  • preferred_tables in datasources.yaml puts those tables first in the schema the planner sees, and the SQLAlchemy-based adapters now snapshot views (#244).
  • The playground's "Verified" badge, six verified queries in the demo, and nl2sql curated test, which runs every verified query once with its defaults or examples (#245).
  • Feedback records the datasources a run used and the answer's source, and nl2sql curated proposals export turns thumbs-up feedback into proposed verified queries (#246).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The design for curated answers: verified queries, preferred tables and feedback proposals, with business metrics deferred (#239).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Matching runs once, on the whole question. A question with two parts falls back to generated SQL, even if one part matches a verified query.
  • A question missing a value a verified query needs falls back to generated SQL; it does not ask a follow-up question.
  • The match threshold (CURATED_MATCH_FLOOR) was calibrated with the local embedding model only.
  • Business metrics are parsed and checked in curated.yaml but not used yet.
  • PostgreSQL materialized views are not indexed.
  • Feedback given before this release cannot become a proposal, because it did not record its datasource.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.4.0"

Breaking changes: none. Curated answers are off unless a curated.yaml exists at the default path or CURATED_CONFIG names one. Two behaviour changes:

  • Views now appear in the schema snapshot of the built-in adapters, so a re-index picks them up.
  • If CURATED_CONFIG points at a missing or broken file, startup fails with a message naming every problem.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.5.0, questions across several databases.

Full changelog: v0.3.0...v0.4.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.4.1
docs.text:
A hardening release: the REST routes that change the server need an admin role, indexing no longer calls the model unless you ask it to, table access is checked by schema as well as table, and one broken datasource no longer stops the engine from starting.

Released 2026-10-13.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Adding or removing a datasource, changing the LLM and rebuilding the index over REST now need an admin role. With no role source configured, only clients on the same machine may call them.
  • nl2sql index and the indexing SDK calls no longer spend model tokens by default. Ask for descriptions with --enrich or enrich=True, and the comments already in your database are never overwritten.
  • Policies can name a schema: ds.schema.table and ds.schema.*. A grant on sales.orders no longer lets a plan read audit.orders.
  • A datasource that fails to start is marked unavailable and the rest keep working; a secret provider that fails to start stops startup with a message saying which one and why.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Passwords and user names with @ : / # % now work for PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server, and statement_timeout_ms is now enforced on SQL Server and DuckDB too (#249).
  • The REST admin routes require an admin role, a failed POST /datasource no longer echoes the connection string, and nl2sql-api pins the engine release it ships with (#250).
  • A secret provider that cannot start fails startup with a clear error; a datasource that cannot start is listed by list_unavailable_datasources() and in index_health() warnings instead of stopping the engine (#251).
  • Routing respects the answerability check's choice of datasources, and the decomposer now sees each datasource's description and table names (#252).
  • Enrichment is opt-in for every indexing entry point, only fills blank descriptions, logs a failure as one line, and a datasource added in code keeps its description (#254).
  • Tier 2 benchmarks run with curated answers off unless --use-curated is passed, and each case records whether its answer was verified or generated (#255).
  • Indexing profiles each column on its own, so a boolean, UUID, JSON or date column, or one failing query, no longer fails the whole datasource (#256).
  • Table access is decided on datasource, schema and table, the same way in the validator, schema retriever, executor and curated matcher (#257).
  • nl2sql setup checks and offers the right driver for bring-your-own PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and DuckDB databases, offers DuckDB as a type, and nl2sql install postgres installs the right extra (#258).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• A reverse proxy on the same host makes every request look like it comes from loopback. Set NL2SQL_API_ROLE_HEADER in that case.
  • The REST indexing routes do not take an enrich parameter, so they always index without enrichment.
  • There is no strict mode that fails startup when one datasource cannot start. Use nl2sql doctor as a deploy check.
  • The SQL Server timeout counts whole seconds, so statement_timeout_ms is rounded up.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.4.1"

Breaking changes / behaviour changes: four, each of which needs a look before you upgrade.

  • REST admin routes need an admin role (#250). POST /datasource, DELETE /datasource/{id}, POST /llm, POST /index/{id}, POST /index-all and DELETE /index now need a role listed in NL2SQL_API_ADMIN_ROLES (comma-separated, default admin). With no role source configured, only loopback clients are allowed. What to do: set NL2SQL_API_ROLE_HEADER behind a proxy, or NL2SQL_API_ROLE=admin for a single-user deployment. In Docker, requests arrive from the bridge gateway rather than loopback, so one of these is needed.
  • Indexing enrichment is opt-in (#254). index_datasource, index_all_datasources and nl2sql index no longer call the LLM unless you pass enrich=True or --enrich, and enrichment never overwrites table or column comments from the database. What to do: if you relied on generated descriptions, add --enrich or enrich=True to your indexing calls.
  • Two-part policy entries mean the default schema (#257). ds.table now grants that table in the datasource's default schema only (public on PostgreSQL, dbo on SQL Server, the connected database on MySQL, main on SQLite and DuckDB). Three-part ds.schema.table and ds.schema.* entries are supported. What to do: for a table outside the default schema, write ds.schema.table or ds.schema.*. Policies on SQLite datasources, including the demo's, mean what they did before.
  • Startup failures (#251). A configured secret provider that fails to start now stops startup with an error naming it and the reason. A datasource that fails to start no longer stops the engine; it is reported as unavailable. What to do: fix or remove a broken entry in the secrets config, and check list_unavailable_datasources(), GET /api/v1/index/status or nl2sql doctor for datasources that did not start.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.5, Configuration v2 and the extension registry.

Full changelog: v0.4.0...v0.4.1

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.5.0
docs.text:
Configuration v2: one nl2sql.yaml configures the engine, the CLI, nl2sql-api and the demo, an extension registry loads adapters, LLM, embeddings and secret providers by name, and every engine owns its config. This is a clean break from 0.4, with no compatibility layer: read Upgrading before you install it.

Released 2026-10-14.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• One config file. nl2sql.yaml replaces the 0.4 files and about 48 environment variables. It can be one file or split into datasources/, llm.yaml, embeddings.yaml, policies.yaml and storage.yaml. nl2sql init writes that layout for you (--demo adds the demo databases). nl2sql config check checks every file, name, driver and secret without starting the engine, and with --connect it also connects to each datasource. It fits a CI job.
  • An extension registry. Registry.default() finds adapters, LLM providers, embeddings providers and secret providers through entry points, and imports none of them until the config uses one. Register your own with add_adapter, add_llm, add_embeddings, add_secrets or a decorator (@registry.adapter("name")). A wrong interface version, a missing driver or a misspelled name is reported when the engine is built, with the fix. The SDK they build against is now nl2sql-sdk (import nl2sql_sdk).
  • A tidier Python API, with a model switch at runtime. run_query and stream_query stay at the top level. Everything else is in namespaces: engine.datasources, index, llm, policies, curated, results, traces and feedback, plus about(), check() and close() (or with). engine.llm.replace(...) and the admin-only PUT /api/v1/settings/llm swap the model in a running engine. Queries already running finish on the old model, and the change is logged without keys.
  • Each engine owns its config. There are no process-wide settings and nothing writes os.environ, so two engines in one process share nothing. import nl2sql takes about 15 ms instead of about 2.2 s, because it loads no heavy library.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• nl2sql-adapter-sdk is renamed nl2sql-sdk, with the import package nl2sql_sdk (#262).
  • import nl2sql loads no database driver, vector store or model library, and a test holds it under budget (#263).
  • The typed config models, load_config, file: includes, ${env:...} references, strict keys with "did you mean", and one ConfigError that lists every problem (#264).
  • The SDK defines the adapter and secret provider interfaces, with interface versions, driver lists and install hints. Secret provider settings are checked strictly (#265).
  • The extension registry: Registry.default(), add_*, decorators, and the entry point groups nl2sql.adapters, nl2sql.llms, nl2sql.embeddings and nl2sql.secrets (#266).
  • nl2sql init [DIR] [--demo] [--provider NAME] [--force] writes the split config layout and checks it (#267).
  • The engine is built from a Config: NL2SQL(config), NL2SQL.from_config(path), NL2SQL.demo(), check() and close(). Building never connects, and all results are written under storage.path (#268).
  • The pipeline reads its settings from its own engine, so two engines in one process each keep their own row limit, plan cache and model (#269).
  • engine.llm.replace, with LLM clients cached per engine, and a plan cache key that includes the planner's model (#270).
  • Indexing, tracing, replay and benchmarks run on run-scoped settings and never change the engine they run on (#271).
  • The CLI, nl2sql-api and the demo start from nl2sql.yaml with a single --config flag. nl2sql setup and every 0.4 config path are removed (#272).
  • nl2sql config check [--connect], which is also callable from Python as nl2sql.config.check.check_config (#273).
  • The namespaced facade and PUT /api/v1/settings/llm. The CLI now uses only the public API (#274).
  • engine.feedback, engine.traces.get, engine.about() and engine.llm.providers(). The playground now uses only the public API (#275).
  • The process-wide settings object is deleted. The library writes no environment variables and reads only an allow-list of them (#276).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text: • Secrets in the config are masked when it is printed, NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL set in .env takes effect, and the scripts no longer write the environment (#277).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The design for Configuration v2 and the extension registry (#260). The Configuration pages are rewritten for nl2sql.yaml in the PRs above.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Running several nl2sql-api replicas is not supported for a model switch. PUT /api/v1/settings/llm changes only the process that receives it, and the change is not saved: a restart reads llm.yaml again.
  • There is no migration command. You map 0.4 files and variables by hand, using the table.
  • Results are stored locally only. The S3 and ADLS backends are gone until the results-store interface in Phase 2.
  • nl2sql init is not interactive, and its --provider accepts openai, anthropic and openrouter only (Ollama has no default model). The guided setup flow comes in Phase 4.
