  • A datasource's connection block is checked by the adapter only, not by a typed model, and check() gives a generic reason when a connection fails. Typed connection models and connection-test stages come with SDK v2 in Phase 2.
  • After engine.datasources.remove(id), the datasource's index entries stay until the next full index.build or index.clear.
  • This release is Phase 1 of five. Phase 2 brings SDK v2, storage interfaces and policy globs, Phase 3 the event bus and evals, Phase 4 the guided setup and the web app on nl2sql-api, and Phase 5 glossaries and knowledge sources.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.5.0"

Adapter and secret provider authors: pip install "nl2sql-sdk==0.5.0" and uninstall nl2sql-adapter-sdk.

Breaking changes: many. 0.5 is a clean break with no compatibility layer, and the engine refuses a 0.4 config. Start with nl2sql init, then move your values across with the 0.4 to 0.5 mapping.

  • One config file (#264, #272). configs/datasources.yaml, llm.yaml, policies.json, secrets.yaml, curated.yaml, sample_questions.yaml and about 48 environment variables are no longer read. What to do: run nl2sql init (or nl2sql init --demo) and move each value to its new place using the mapping table. Sample questions now sit on each datasource, policies are YAML, and LLM agents are keyed by node name (ast_planner).
  • Environment variables (#276). Only NL2SQL_CONFIG, NL2SQL_LOG_LEVEL and the provider keys (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY) are read directly. What to do: write any other value in the YAML, as ${env:VAR} where it should come from the environment.
  • .env loading (#272). Only the CLI, nl2sql-api and nl2sql demo load a .env, and only the one next to nl2sql.yaml. They never override a variable that is already set. The library never reads .env. --env, --env-file, ENV, APP_ENV and ENV_FILE_PATH are gone. What to do: put .env next to nl2sql.yaml. From Python, call nl2sql.load_env_file(path) before building the engine.
  • nl2sql setup is removed (#272). What to do: use nl2sql init, or nl2sql init --demo in place of setup --demo.
  • One CLI flag (#272). nl2sql --config PATH/nl2sql.yaml <command> (or NL2SQL_CONFIG, or ./nl2sql.yaml) replaces every per-command path flag (--llm-config, --secrets-config, --policies-config, --vector-store, and the curated and policy path flags). What to do: pass --config once, before the command.
  • nl2sql-api settings (#272). The NL2SQL_API_* variables are removed. What to do: set api.role_header, api.role, api.trust_body_role and api.cors_origins (a list) in an api: section, and the admin roles in policies.admin_roles. The API image reads NL2SQL_CONFIG=/etc/nl2sql/nl2sql.yaml, so mount your config folder there.
  • REST LLM route (#274). POST /api/v1/llm is replaced by the admin-only PUT /api/v1/settings/llm, whose body is the llm section as JSON. A bad body gets a 422 with the config error. POST /api/v1/datasource takes the datasource in the nl2sql.yaml shape, and the datasource routes return DatasourceInfo. What to do: update your clients.
  • Result storage (#268). The S3 and ADLS backends and the RESULT_ARTIFACT_* settings are removed. Results are written under storage.path/results/. What to do: set storage.path and copy anything you need from a remote store yourself.
  • Secret providers (#265). hashi is renamed hashicorp, with no alias. The VAULT_ADDR, VAULT_TOKEN and AZURE_KEYVAULT_URL fallbacks are removed, and an unknown provider setting is an error. What to do: write type: hashicorp and give url and token (for example token: "${env:VAULT_TOKEN}"), or vault_url for Azure, in the provider's block.
  • The SDK package (#262). nl2sql-adapter-sdk / nl2sql_adapter_sdk is now nl2sql-sdk / nl2sql_sdk. Adapters also declare interface_version, driver_modules and install_hint (#265). What to do: rename the dependency and the imports, add the three class attributes, and register through the nl2sql.adapters entry point or Registry.add_adapter.
  • The Python facade (#274, #275). The flat methods, engine.context, engine.query, get_adapter, configure_llm, reload_llm_config, the auth, settings, policy, indexing and datasource sub-APIs, and the QueryAPI/DatasourceAPI/LLM_API/... exports are removed. NL2SQL() is built from a Config or NL2SQL.from_config(path). What to do: call the namespaces (engine.datasources.add, engine.index.build, engine.llm.replace, engine.policies.validate, ...). The public facade page lists them.
  • Hosted demo (#276). nl2sql demo --hosted refuses to start if OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set in its environment. NL2SQL_DEMO_HOSTED and NL2SQL_DEMO_QUESTIONS_* are replaced by --hosted, --questions-per-minute and --questions-per-session, and the demo's key file is <dir>/.env instead of .env.demo (#272). What to do: remove provider keys from the hosted server's environment and use the flags.
  • Startup errors (#268). Anything wrong that can be found without connecting is now a ConfigError when the engine is built. This includes an unknown datasource type and a secret that does not resolve, which in 0.4 only marked that datasource unavailable. A datasource that cannot connect still runs degraded unless it is required: true. What to do: run nl2sql config check before you deploy.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.6, datasources and adapter SDK v2, then the web app on the API and Docker Compose.

Full changelog: v0.4.1...v0.5.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.6.0
docs.text:
Phase 2: every built-in adapter is now tested against real PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server servers, adapters are built on SDK v2 with a conformance kit, storage has four pluggable stores, LLM and embeddings providers take any OpenAI-compatible server, and policies gain allow and deny globs. Several config keys and interfaces change: read Upgrading before you install it.

Released 2026-10-15.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Tested on real databases. A test bed runs PostgreSQL with Pagila, MySQL with Sakila and SQL Server with AdventureWorksLT, plus a generated schema of 1,200 tables. It runs in CI on every PR that touches database code, and on a GCP VM on demand. The VM run found three bugs that CI had hidden, all fixed in this release.
  • Adapter SDK v2 and a conformance kit. Each adapter has a typed connection model, so a misspelt key gets "did you mean". You can choose which schemas and tables to index (IndexScope). Row counts come from the database catalog. A table that cannot be read becomes an issue in the index build instead of a crash. Read-only sessions and statement timeouts are enforced where the database allows it and reported where it does not, and a failed connection test names the stage that failed. The SQLAlchemy base is public in nl2sql-sdk[sqlalchemy], and nl2sql-sdk[testing] is the kit that all five built-in adapters pass.
  • Four storage slots. storage has index, state, traces and results, each a built-in or a plugin store. The index's build pointer is now the commit, so a failed build leaves the previous index live. Each embedding model gets its own namespace. Traces and results are deleted after a set number of days.
  • Providers and policies. openai_compatible with a base_url works with any OpenAI-style server, with openrouter and ollama as presets of it. Each agent can set structured_output, max_tokens, timeout_s, max_retries and headers, and a malformed answer is retried with the error. Policies use allow and deny globs on datasource.schema.table, the planner never sees a denied table, and a PolicyCheck plugin can add your own access rules. engine.datasources.types(), test() and add() are the methods a Connect-a-database form needs.

docs.title: Real-database results
docs.text:
• The CI realdb job passed on every PR that touched database code.
  • The run on the GCP VM on 2026-10-14 (python scripts/testbed.py run -- pytest -m realdb): 110 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed. The four skips are expected. SQL Server does not declare ENFORCES_READ_ONLY (2 tests), and the 60-second target for reading the wide schema is measured on PostgreSQL only (2 tests).
  • Runs on the real VM found and fixed three problems. MySQL 8 logins needed cryptography, and SQL Server used a hard-coded ODBC driver (#303). The test bed also had Windows problems (#299, #301, #302, #304).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Embeddings providers v2: openai_compatible, base_url on the hosted providers, a known dimension for each model, and one probe call when the dimension is unknown (#281).
  • Store interfaces in nl2sql_sdk.stores, the four storage slots and the store registry kind (#283).
  • LLM providers v2: openai_compatible, with openrouter and ollama as its presets, and the agent fields structured_output, max_tokens, timeout_s, max_retries and headers. Header values are never printed (#284).
  • Policy allow and deny globs, one Scope wherever access is decided, and denied tables hidden from the planner (#285).
  • The real-database test bed: a Docker Compose file, the realdb pytest marker and a CI workflow (#286).
  • A malformed structured answer is sent back to the model with the error, up to parse_retries times. After that the run fails with MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID (#287).
  • The PolicyCheck extension point. Its grants are intersected with the YAML roles, and it denies if it fails (#288).
  • The index store: one namespace per embedding model, the build pointer as the commit, and nl2sql index prune (#289).
  • scripts/testbed.py starts, uses and stops the GCP test-bed VM through IAP (#290).
  • Adapter SDK v2: DatasourceAdapter, strict connection models with "did you mean", and IndexScope (#291).
  • Trace and result stores with max_age_days retention, engine.storage.info() and purge(), and nl2sql storage purge (#292).
  • The sqlite state store: snapshots that are never changed, migrations that adopt a 0.5 state.db, and a lock during index builds (#293).
  • The SQLAlchemy base in nl2sql-sdk[sqlalchemy]. It reads the schema once, takes row estimates from the catalog, collects sample values only when asked, and reports index issues (#295).
  • engine.datasources.types(), test(Datasource) without registering it, and add() checking the index scope (#296).
  • Read-only sessions and statement timeouts on every adapter that can enforce them, and connection tests that name the failed stage (#297).
  • The adapter conformance kit, nl2sql-sdk[testing], run on all five built-in adapters (#298).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• The SDK docs page no longer has leftover merge-conflict markers, and CI now fails on any it finds (#294).
  • DuckDB schemas are read from DuckDB's own catalog, so indexing works on SQLAlchemy 2.1 (#300).
  • nl2sql-engine[mysql] installs cryptography for MySQL 8 logins. SQL Server uses the newest installed ODBC driver, with a clear message when none is installed (#303).
  • Fixes to the test bed on Windows and on the VM: passwords, Docker start-up, SQL Server start-up, and stopping cleanly (#299, #301, #302, #304).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • The Phase 2 design: test bed, storage, providers, policies and adapter SDK v2 (#279). The test bed, storage, policies and adapter SDK pages are written or rewritten in the PRs above.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• SQL Server does not make the session read-only. check() warns about it, so connect with a login that can only read.
  • The built-in stores are for a single replica. A PostgreSQL state store and a pgvector index, for several replicas, come later.
  • There is no built-in S3 or ADLS results store. Write one as a ResultStore plugin; the Artifact Store page has an S3 example.
  • Policies go down to tables. Column denies, row filters and user attributes come later.
  • engine.datasources.types(), test() and add() are Python only. The REST routes and the Connect-a-database form come in Phase 4.
  • There are no Snowflake or BigQuery adapters yet.
  • The 60-second target for reading the 1,200-table schema is measured on PostgreSQL only. Retrieval limits as settings and incremental re-indexing come after 0.6.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.6.0"

Adapter, store and policy-check authors: pip install "nl2sql-sdk==0.6.0" (add [sqlalchemy] for the SQLAlchemy base, [testing] for the conformance kit).

Breaking changes: several. Each needs a look before you upgrade.

  • Storage sub-blocks and a new index namespace (#283, #289, #292). storage has index, state, traces and results sub-blocks. path on its own is still valid. The index now lives in one namespace per embedding model, and 0.6 never reads 0.5's nl2sql_store collection. Traces are deleted after 14 days and results after 7 by default. What to do: run nl2sql index after upgrading, then nl2sql index prune to drop the 0.5 collection. Set max_age_days on traces or results if you want them kept longer. A 0.5 state.db is adopted as it is.
  • Policy patterns (#285). allow and deny replace allowed_datasources and allowed_tables. A pattern is *, datasource or datasource.schema.table. A two-part pattern such as sales.orders is rejected when the config loads, and matching ignores case. What to do: rewrite each role, for example sales.orders as sales.<schema>.orders or sales.<schema>.*.
  • Denied tables are hidden from the planner (#285). A table a role cannot read never reaches the model. A user who asks about one sees "can't be answered from the connected data". A plan that still names a hidden table is refused by the validator. What to do: check that each role allows the tables its users need.
  • sample_values is off by default (#295). Column values are no longer collected into the index and prompts unless index.sample_values is on. The demo keeps them on. What to do: set index: {sample_values: true} on a datasource whose answers need its values, then run nl2sql index.
  • Strict connection keys (#291). An unknown key in a datasource's connection block is now an error with a "did you mean" hint. It used to be ignored. What to do: run nl2sql config check and fix what it reports.
  • Adapter interface version 2 (#291, #295). DatasourceAdapter replaces DatasourceAdapterProtocol, with no alias, and a version 1 adapter is refused when it loads. What to do: port your adapter to DatasourceAdapter, ideally on nl2sql_sdk.sqlalchemy.SQLAlchemyAdapter, and run the conformance kit. See Adapter development.
  • LLM and embeddings provider interface version 2 (#281, #284). A version 1 LLM or embeddings provider is refused when it loads. What to do: add structured_output to an LLM provider and describe() to an embeddings provider, and set interface_version = 2.
  • Deleted index arguments and setting (#289). index.build(full=..., switch_guard=...), nl2sql index --full and settings.schema.version_mismatch are gone. What to do: drop them. A failed build now leaves the previous build live, so there is nothing to guard.
  • engine.policies.allowed() is now engine.policies.scope() (#285). A flat table list cannot express a deny. What to do: call scope(user_context, datasource_id) and ask it allows(schema, table).
  • S3 and ADLS results only through a plugin (#292). What to do: implement the ResultStore interface and set it as the results store.
  • SQL Server always connects with Encrypt=yes (#303). ODBC Driver 17 did not encrypt by default. What to do: for a server with a self-signed certificate, set trust_server_certificate: true in its connection block.
  • nl2sql-engine[mysql] installs pymysql[rsa] (#303), which brings in cryptography. What to do: nothing, unless you pin dependencies, in which case allow cryptography.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: Phase 3, hooks, observers and evals.

Full changelog: v0.5.0...v0.6.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.7.0
docs.text:
Wave A of the redesign: every run publishes typed events that observers log, audit or export, hooks can change or stop a run and ask for a person's approval, evals become engine.evals and nl2sql eval with a regression gate, routing votes across five signals, and answers are checked for join fan-out and empty columns. It also adds per-question cost caps, schema drift checks and an MCP server. Several APIs and config keys change: read Upgrading before you install it.

Released 2026-10-15.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Events, observers and hooks. Every run publishes typed events on one bus: run, node, answer, LLM call, policy denial, index and drift events, each in a catalog. stream_query yields those events from a caller-safe allow-list, ready for SSE. The observers section sends them to a log, a JSON-lines audit log under storage.path, or OpenTelemetry. Six hook points let your code modify a run before the validator and deny it after, and a hook can stop a run as needs_approval until an approver re-runs it.
  • Evals as a product. engine.benchmark is now engine.evals, and nl2sql benchmark is now nl2sql eval. One case format, five scorers and three modes (full, plans, retrieval), with the Chinook gold set moved unchanged and pinned by its digest. A regression gate on execution accuracy runs in CI, a new routing suite of 78 cases covers the demo's three databases, and nl2sql eval seed drafts cases from your own database.
  • Better routing and safer answers. Each example question is its own index entry. Routing fuses five signals (description, examples, verified queries, tables, columns) by rank and drops a datasource far less similar than the best. A question that needs too many sub-queries is refused as QUESTION_TOO_BROAD. Join keys of different types are converted before a cross-database join. A count inflated by a join is caught and retried (JOIN_FAN_OUT), and a column that came back all null is flagged.
  • Cost caps, drift and MCP. settings.pipeline.max_llm_calls and max_cost_usd stop a question before the call that would cross them, with status stopped. nl2sql index --check reports schema drift and what it breaks, without re-indexing. nl2sql mcp serves the engine to MCP clients over stdio, as one role.

docs.title: Real-database results
docs.text:
• The CI realdb job passed on the PRs that touched database code.
  • The run on the GCP test bed against main at 5920d3f1: 111 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed, in 9.5 minutes.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• The foundation: the event bus and catalog, the run scope, the observer, hook and scorer registry kinds, the new config sections and settings, the RunStatus values and nl2sql --log-format text|json (#313).
  • Run events on every run, stream_query yielding Events from a caller-safe allow-list, engine.events.subscribe() and catalog(), and the run's trace_id on every log line (#314).
  • Hooks: six points (run.before, datasources.after, plan.after, execute.before, execute.after, answer.after), run in config order, failing closed unless a hook sets on_error: open (#315).
  • Routing: one index entry per example question, five signals fused by rank, a similarity floor, and the settings.routing and settings.retrieval limits (#316).
  • engine.evals: the suite format, the Chinook suite, five scorers, modes full, plans and retrieval, and regenerate through the datasource's adapter (#317).
  • The log, audit and otel observers, with llm.call and llm.changed on the bus. The audit log moves under storage.path (#318).
  • Approval: a hook can ask for one, the result is needs_approval with a request, and an approver's re-run pins the same plan. run_query(plan=SuppliedPlan(...)) runs a plan you already hold (#319).
  • nl2sql eval run, regenerate and publish, and engine.evals.gate(), a regression gate on execution accuracy, with records kept by mode and suite (#320).
  • The Phase 2 events are published: index builds, failed datasource checks, parse retries, policy denials and purges (#321).
  • A limit on sub-queries per question (QUESTION_TOO_BROAD), join keys converted to one type before a cross-database join, and a validator check for join keys of incompatible types (#322).
  • The routing suite of 78 cases over the demo's three databases, and its gate on top-1 and shortlist recall in CI (#323).
  • Answer checks for join fan-out and all-null columns, closest values from the index's sample values, and typed RunWarnings (#324).
  • nl2sql mcp, an MCP server over stdio with ask, list_datasources and describe_table, all limited to the caller's role (the new mcp extra) (#325).
  • The dated price table in llm/prices.py, every LLM call priced, engine.llm.prices(), the per-question caps and a Budget you can use outside a question (#326).
  • Schema drift: engine.index.check(), versions() and diff(), nl2sql index --check, and the verified queries and policy rules a change affects (#327).
  • engine.evals.seed() and nl2sql eval seed: draft eval cases from your own datasource, as typed plans the engine validates and runs read-only, under a cost cap (#328).
  • SQL Server connections take encrypt: false for a local server without TLS. Encryption stays on by default (#307).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
• The Wave A design (#308), and the designs for Waves B, C and D (#310, #311, #312). New pages: Events, Observers, Hooks, Evals, Seeding, Schema drift and MCP.
  • Two rules in CLAUDE.md corrected to match the code (#306).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Routing is not perfect. On the routing suite, top-1 is 76 of 78 and the shortlist 77 of 78. "Which customers complained most about refunds?" and "How many purchases were there per month in 2013?" go to Chinook first.
  • Approvals are not stored. The caller keeps the request and sends the approval back with the re-run. Stored approvals come with the REST API in Wave D.
  • needs_clarification is a reserved status. Nothing returns it until Wave B.
  • MCP runs over stdio only, as one role. MCP over HTTP with API keys comes in Wave C.
  • Schema drift is measured, not acted on. Nothing re-indexes or fixes a verified query by itself.
  • When a hook is attached at execute.before, the value and fan-out checks run no probe query. Only the all-null check runs.
  • While chromadb is a core dependency, it brings OpenTelemetry with it, so the otel extra installs nothing new yet.
  • Seeded drafts have no rows. Run nl2sql eval regenerate after you approve them.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.7.0"

Add [otel] for the OpenTelemetry observer and [mcp] for nl2sql mcp. Third-party store authors: pip install "nl2sql-sdk==0.7.0".

Breaking changes: several. Each needs a look before you upgrade.

  • engine.benchmark is now engine.evals, and nl2sql benchmark is now nl2sql eval (#317, #320). There is no alias. The gold files are now suites/chinook.yaml with renamed keys (expected is outcome, gold_sql is sql, alt_gold_sql is alt_sql), and the gate reads execution accuracy. What to do: call engine.evals.run() and gate(), or nl2sql eval run. Move your own gold files to the case format. A 0.6 record starts a new series in the gate.
  • QueryEvent is gone; stream_query yields Events (#314). The stream carries run.started, node.*, answer.delta, result.manifest, sanity.flagged, run.limit_reached, then one run.finished (with the QueryResult in data.result) or run.failed. Policy, hook and LLM call events never reach it. Each SSE data line of POST /api/v1/query/stream is now the whole event: name, at, trace_id, tenant_id and data. What to do: read events by name, and take the result from run.finished. See Events.
  • QueryResult.warnings are typed RunWarnings (#324). Each is {code, node, message, sub_query_id, detail}. Over REST, error_code is now code, and severity is gone: an earlier attempt that a retry replaced has detail.recovered: true. What to do: read code instead of error_code, and detail.recovered instead of severity.
  • QueryResult.status is a RunStatus (#313, #319, #326). Beside success, plan_only and error, a run can now end needs_approval (with approvals_needed) or stopped (with stop, at a cost or call cap). What to do: handle the two new values.
  • engine.datasources.schema() requires user_context (#325), and drops the tables the caller may not read. engine.index.check(), versions() and diff() take it too (#327). What to do: pass the caller's UserContext.
  • settings.observability is gone; use the observers section (#313, #318). A config that still sets it fails to load. By default the engine runs the log and audit observers, and the audit log is now <storage.path>/audit/<date>.jsonl, not logs/audit_events.log. What to do: move exporter and otlp_endpoint to an otel observer. See Observers.
  • OpenTelemetry is the otel extra (#318). It has left the core dependencies, and an otel observer without it is a ConfigError. What to do: pip install "nl2sql-engine[otel]" if you export to a collector.
  • TABLE_K, PLANNING_K and MAX_DECOMPOSER_TABLES are settings (#313, #316): settings.retrieval.table_k, planning_k and decomposer_tables, with the same defaults. What to do: if you patched the constants, set the settings instead.
  • Routing changed (#316). settings.routing.candidates now defaults to 3, a datasource far less similar than the best is dropped (floor_ratio, 0.5), and Retriever.route() replaces retrieve_datasource_candidates. What to do: run nl2sql index after upgrading, so each example question gets its own entry. Until you do, routing has no example votes.
  • A question needs at most settings.routing.max_sub_queries sub-queries (#322), 6 by default. More ends the run with QUESTION_TOO_BROAD. What to do: raise the setting if your users ask wider questions.
  • Store interface version 2 (#327). StateStore gains put_schema_diff and get_schema_diff, and a version 1 store is refused when it loads. The built-in sqlite store migrates itself. What to do: third-party state stores add the two methods and set interface_version = 2.
  • The price table moved to nl2sql/llm/prices.py (#326). nl2sql.evaluation.prices is gone, with no alias. A model the table does not know now costs None, not 0, and a token count the provider did not report is None. What to do: import from nl2sql.llm.prices, price your own models with llm.prices, and handle None in usage and cost. With max_cost_usd set, an unpriced model is a ConfigError.
  • The mcp extra (#325). nl2sql mcp needs pip install "nl2sql-engine[mcp]".

New, not breaking: run_query(plan=SuppliedPlan(...)) runs a plan you hold, through plan.after and the validator, with no planning (#319).

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.8, Wave B: business knowledge, the schema profiler, clarifying questions and a cost guard.

Full changelog: v0.6.0...v0.7.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.8.0
docs.text:
Wave B of the redesign: business knowledge (a glossary and other knowledge sources) now reaches the index and the prompts, a review queue holds every proposed change until someone accepts it, a schema profiler proposes joins, roles and drafted descriptions, ambiguous questions can be re-asked with a choice, every answer can say why, and a cost rule can refuse or confirm an expensive query. A few APIs and flags change: read Upgrading before you install it.

Released 2026-10-28.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Business knowledge. Knowledge sources (the yaml glossary first) are merged, filtered by the caller's scope and shown or exported with engine.knowledge. Descriptions, synonyms, roles, units, joins and rules now go into the index and into the planner's prompt, and a changed glossary marks the index stale. nl2sql index --refresh re-renders the entries from the stored snapshot with no schema read and no model call.
  • A review queue and a profiler. Every proposed change (a profiler finding, a thumbs-up, a correction, a chosen reading) is filed in one queue, and accepting it is the only way anything is written. engine.knowledge.profile() proposes joins and column roles from bounded probes, and with draft=True the profiler model drafts missing descriptions under a cost cap (nl2sql profile --draft --max-cost).
  • Clarifying questions, and why an answer is what it is. A question that can be read more than one way ends as needs_clarification with up to three options, each explained. run_query(choice=) runs the chosen plan, and a pick can be saved as a glossary term proposal. Every successful answer carries an explanation, written from the typed plan, not from model text.
  • A cost guard and corrections. policies.cost is enforced: over the limit, a query is allowed, held for approval or refused as COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, using a rows-read estimate from PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and DuckDB. engine.feedback.correct() checks a fixed plan or SQL and files it as a verified-query proposal.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• The shared shapes for knowledge, review, profiler, clarify, explain and cost, and store interface version 3 (#329).
  • Adapters: estimate (rows read) on PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and DuckDB, and probe_overlap on all five built-ins (#332).
  • explanation on QueryResult: why this answer, rendered from the typed plan (#335).
  • Knowledge sources, merge, scope filter, show and export, and the yaml source with a checked, atomic writer (#336).
  • The review queue: one way to file a proposal, accept as the only writer, and thumbs-up proposals (#337).
  • The clarifier and the needs_clarification result (#339).
  • Knowledge in the planner's prompts, and the terms and rules used on each answer (#340).
  • engine.feedback.correct(): a checked fix filed as a verified-query proposal (#341).
  • The cost rule, enforced by the built-in policy.cost hook (#342).
  • The profiler: join and column-role proposals from bounded probes (#343).
  • The glossary in the index, index --refresh, and no model text written into the index (#344).
  • Clarifications: choice= on run_query and stream_query, save_choice, settled phrases, a prompt in nl2sql run on a terminal, and choice on the MCP ask tool (#345).
  • Drafted descriptions under a cost cap, filed for review (#347).
  • The retrieval inspector shows only what the caller's scope reaches (#348).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• The playground and the REST API trust the caller-supplied role. See the security model.
  • The retrieval inspector over-fetches to apply a caller's scope, so a caller for whom most matches are hidden can see a short list (#348).
  • Business metrics are still deferred. A glossary term with columns is the prose half of a metric.
  • SQLite has no cost estimate, so the cost rule treats its queries as unknown.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.8.0"

Third-party store authors: pip install "nl2sql-sdk==0.8.0".

Breaking changes: a few. Each needs a look before you upgrade.

  • nl2sql index --enrich, --curated-only and their enrich= and curated_only= parameters are gone (#344). The index no longer calls the model to write descriptions, and the playground's "write descriptions with the LLM" option is gone. What to do: use nl2sql profile --draft for drafted descriptions, which are filed for review, and nl2sql index --refresh after a glossary change.
  • engine.index.inspect() requires user_context (#348), and shows only the entries that caller's scope reaches. The playground's /api/retrieval takes a role. What to do: pass the caller's UserContext.
  • Store interface version 3 (#329). StateStore gains five proposal methods. What to do: third-party state stores add them and set interface_version = 3.
  • A new QueryResult.status, needs_clarification (#339), and a new error code, COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (#342). What to do: handle both. nl2sql run exits 4 when it needs a choice and has no terminal.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: 0.9, Wave C: conversations, chat tools, charts, dashboards, the launchpad, and MCP over HTTP with API keys.

Full changelog: v0.7.0...v0.8.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.9.0
docs.text:
Wave C of the redesign: a conversation led by the model that can ask, chart and draw, dashboards you build in chat or by hand and refresh with no model call, a launcher that takes you from a database to a working project, and MCP over HTTP with API keys. Saved results are now readable only by the caller who asked, so read Upgrading before you install it.

Released 2026-10-29.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Conversations that use tools. engine.conversations keeps a conversation per user. The model reads the history and either replies or calls a tool (ask, a chart, a diagram, the dashboard tools), one call per step. It never writes SQL and never sees rows. A conversation report shows what happened on each turn.
  • Charts and diagrams. Every result gets an automatic chart chosen from its column kinds, and a Mermaid diagram can be drawn of an answer or of a schema.
  • Dashboards. Dashboards live in workspaces and are pinned whole. A refresh re-runs the stored plans with no model call, under the viewer's current access, and can run on a schedule. Filters are typed predicates added before the validator. generate builds a starter dashboard from the schema and glossary with no model call, and the conversation can build and edit dashboards too.
  • From a database to a project. nl2sql launch finds a database (a file, DATABASE_URL or a local port), tests the connection, and writes a project with every secret in .env and only ${env:...} references in YAML. nl2sql mcp --http serves the MCP tools over HTTP behind API keys, each request running as its key's user, tenant and roles.
  • Results belong to their asker. A run's saved rows can be read only by the caller who asked it, and a run a hook withheld is never readable.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Shared models, config, error codes, events and state store interface version 4 for the wave (#354).
  • SuppliedPlan for a whole run, the answer= flag on run_query and stream_query, and the stubs the parallel tracks fill (#355).
  • Model-led conversations with ask, retry and ownership (#358).
  • Chat tools in the conversation loop, and the conversation report (#363).
  • Automatic charts from a result's column kinds (#357).
  • Mermaid diagrams of an answer and a schema (#366).
  • Scan a folder, a URL or local ports for datasources (#359).
  • Writers for a project and a datasource, with secrets written as environment references, and the Connect routes in nl2sql-api (#364).
  • nl2sql launch, from a database to a working project (#373).
  • API keys with hashed tokens, revoke and verify (#360).
  • MCP over HTTP with API keys (#367).
  • Workspaces, the dashboard store and manual edits (#361).
  • Token-free refresh, stored results and schedules for dashboards (#365).
  • Dashboard filters as predicates before the validator (#372).
  • A starter dashboard from the schema and glossary (#370).
  • Chat builds and edits dashboards (#371).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• A run that a hook withheld (HOOK_DENIED, NEEDS_APPROVAL, COST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and the others) stays unreadable by its trace id; the result manifest is now written last (#362).
  • Results are readable only by the caller who asked (#369).
  • A plan that counts rows with COUNT(*) or selects t.* now runs instead of failing at the database; a star in any other position (for example COUNT(t.*) or SUM(*)) is refused at validation with a retry hint (#374).
  • A pipeline timeout fails the step, not the whole conversation turn (#376).
  • Schema retrieval keeps key and label columns, and falls back to the caller's whole visible schema when search fails (#377).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
• The Wave C design: model-led chat, dashboards pinned whole, workspaces, refresh (#352).
  • One Built-note slot per row in the Wave C design (#368).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• The web app and the REST routes for conversations and dashboards are Wave D. In this release you use them from Python, the CLI and MCP.
  • The REST API has no per-user identity yet, so its callers who share a tenant and roles share their results.
  • Dashboards are private to their owner. Sharing one across a tenant, and publishing, come later.
  • On schemas with more than 15 tables, retrieval picks tables by search and can miss the one a question needs. In the smoke test it missed payment, so the planner asked which revenue proxy to use rather than summing payments. A glossary term (for example, revenue = SUM(payment.amount)) avoids it. Better table recall is planned.

docs.title: Pre-release check
docs.text:
An end-to-end smoke test against the Pagila database (29 tables, Postgres, on the GCP test bed) with a real model.

  • Run 1 found three bugs, all fixed before release. Retrieval dropped key columns (#377). A pipeline timeout was reported as a cancelled turn (#376). A retrieval failure left the planner with an empty schema (#377).
  • Run 2, on main at 04e3c275.
  • nl2sql launch built a working project.
  • Chat answered the first two turns (rentals per month; top 5 categories by rental revenue). On the third ("for just the top category, which 5 films brought in the most revenue?") it asked a clarifying question instead of answering; see Known limits.
  • A dashboard built from chat refreshed and reopened with zero model calls.
  • MCP over HTTP refused a request without an API key (401) and answered with a key.
  • The run took about 3 minutes and $0.89 of model spend.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine[demo]==0.9.0"

Third-party store authors: pip install "nl2sql-sdk==0.9.0".

Breaking changes: several. Each needs a look before you upgrade.

  • engine.results.manifest, page, csv and chart require user_context= (#369), and the REST results routes check the caller. Any other caller gets ResultNotFound. Runs saved before 0.9 have no recorded asker and are refused. What to do: pass the asker's UserContext, and re-run a question whose old result you still need.
  • Result manifests gain column_kinds and an owner (#357, #369). What to do: code that reads a manifest should accept the new fields.
  • SuppliedPlan is now a whole run (#355): a decomposition plus plans, or a verified query with its datasource. The old fields are gone, with no alias. What to do: use SuppliedPlan.for_sub_query(sub_query, plan) for the one-sub-query case.
  • chart() no longer takes tenant_id (#369). It takes the caller's user_context instead.
  • State store interface version 4 (#354). A 0.8 file is migrated in place by migration 6. What to do: third-party state stores add the conversation, workspace, dashboard and API key methods and set interface_version = 4.
  • The playground's results routes take ?role=, the role of the run being read (#369).
  • The MCP ask tool's choice is now an option id sent with conversation_id, replacing {request, option_id} (#367). What to do: update MCP clients that answer a clarification.
  • A new conversation agent (#358). What to do: a config that pins every agent's model should add it. A small model is enough.
  • MCP's build_server(engine, identity) gains a keyword-only over_http=False (#367). The positional arguments are unchanged; with over_http=True the server is set up for streamable_http_app(), and its identity callable is asked on every request. What to do: nothing for stdio; HTTP embedders pass over_http=True and wrap the server with nl2sql.mcp.http.build_app.
  • init_project now writes through write_project (#364). It writes the same files. What to do: nothing, unless you patched or replaced the file writing inside init_project.
  • POST /api/v1/datasource answers a bad body with 422, not a 500 (#364).

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: Wave D, the apps.

Full changelog: v0.8.0...v0.9.0

docs.title: NL2SQL 0.9.1
docs.text:
Better answers on large schemas: the right tables reach the planner, joins across partitioned tables work, a split question comes back as one result in the shape you asked for, and the eval scorer reads what a real database returns.

Released 2026-10-30.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Large schemas find their tables. Past 15 tables, a model now picks the tables a question needs from a catalog, glossary terms bring in their tables, and the tables that join them are filled in from the foreign keys. The 0.9.0 smoke question on Pagila ("top 5 films by revenue in the top category") now reaches payment. On the keyed Pagila suite, answers passing went from 0 of 8 to 11 of 11.
  • Joins that work on real databases. A partitioned Postgres table takes its partitions' foreign keys. A rejected join names the joins that are declared between its tables, or the shortest declared path, and a declared join is accepted with its sides in either order. Plans can also take the days between two dates, compiled for each database.
  • A split question comes back as one result. The answer's columns follow the question, a column name shared by both joined sides is rejected before it can silently break the sort, and the decomposer splits only when one query cannot do the job. Answers quote figures exactly as the rows hold them.
  • A fairer eval scorer, and a Pagila suite. The scorer reads Decimal and date values, accepts extra columns and reordered columns, and scores a split question on its combined result. A new Pagila suite runs on CI with a model-free retrieval gate.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• A able_selector agent and a join-path fill for schemas past ull_snapshot_max_tables, with the glossary's tables sent too ((#378)).
  • A Pagila table-recall suite with gold tables and SQL ((#379)), its expected rows and a keyed recall run ((#382)).
  • A model-free Pagila retrieval baseline that CI gates ((#383)).

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• A partitioned Postgres table takes its partitions' foreign keys, a rejected join names the allowed joins, and a declared join is accepted in either operand order ((#386)).
  • Plans can use DATE_DIFF('day', start, end), compiled per dialect; another unit or a - between two date columns is rejected at validation ((#387)).
  • The decomposer splits only when needed, and the answer quotes exact figures ((#388)).
  • The eval scorer reads Decimal cells and dates, accepts extra columns, derived differences and percentages, and the preview count ((#384)).
  • A split question is scored on its combined result ((#391)).
  • The decomposer rejects a column name both joined sides share ((#392)).
  • A split answer's columns follow the question ((#393)).
  • esult_match accepts reordered columns ((#394)).
  • The decomposer keeps the columns that say what the answer is about, and no prompt example is taken from an eval question; a guard test checks every prompt module ((#395)).

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: • Wave D start screen: demo or your own database, with the multi-project platform deferred ((#381)).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: • Full-name alternatives, as reviewed lt_sql, for Pagila 002, 003 and 011 ((#389), (#390)).

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Some questions need a planner retry for an invented join, which roughly doubles their latency. This is tracked.
  • A plan is one flat SELECT per sub-query: no subqueries, CTEs or window functions. A question like "the top category, then its top 5 films" still takes two sub-queries.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade "nl2sql-engine==0.9.1"

Breaking changes: none.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
Next: Wave D, the apps.

Full changelog: v0.9.0...v0.9.1

docs.title: Schema Drift
docs.text:
A database changes after it is indexed: a column is added, a table dropped, a type widened. The engine keeps answering from the schema its build was made from until the next nl2sql index. Schema drift is measured, not acted on: nothing here re-indexes, schedules a build or changes what a question reads. You decide when to rebuild.

There are two measures:

  • A check: the live database against its live build, now (engine.index.check(), nl2sql index --check).
  • The stored diffs: what each build changed against the one it replaced (engine.index.versions(), engine.index.diff()).

docs.title: The check
docs.text:
nl2sql index --check                  # every datasource
nl2sql index --check -d shop --json   # one, as JSON

For each datasource it reflects the live database with the datasource's index scope and no profiling (only the catalog is read), and compares its structural fingerprint with the fingerprint of the snapshot the live build was made from. It writes nothing.

Exit code Meaning 0 Nothing drifted (a datasource never indexed is reported and does not change the code) 1 At least one datasource drifted 2 At least one check failed (the database could not be read, or the config did not load), or nothing was checked (no datasource is configured, or the role reaches none); wins over 1

So a cron job or a CI step can act on it. --role (repeatable, default admin, as nl2sql run) is the role the check runs as; drift shows only in the tables it may read. A role that reaches no datasource checks nothing and exits 2, so a gate never passes on a check that did not run. --json prints the reports.

From code:

from nl2sql import UserContext

for report in engine.index.check(user_context=UserContext(roles=["admin"])):
    print(report.datasource_id, report.status)
    if report.status == "drifted":
        print(report.diff.counts(), report.impact)

Each DriftReport has:

Field Meaning datasource_id The datasource status unchanged, drifted, not_indexed (no build yet) or failed live_version The live build's schema_version checked_at When (UTC) diff With drifted: a SchemaDiff from the live build (from_version) to the live database (to_version is None) impact With drifted: what the diff breaks (below) error With failed: why, redacted (a password in a connection string never shows)

docs.title: The diff
docs.text:
SchemaDiff (nl2sql_sdk.schema, also exported from nl2sql) compares exactly what the fingerprint covers:

Field Meaning tables_added, tables_dropped TableRefs. A table added or dropped is listed once, without its columns columns_added, columns_dropped ColumnRefs, in tables on both sides columns_changed ColumnChange: table, column, changes such as {"type": ["INTEGER", "BIGINT"]}; the keys are type, nullable and pk foreign_keys_added, foreign_keys_dropped ForeignKeyRef: table, columns, referred_table, referred_columns engine_type (old, new) when the datasource's engine type changed (its type), else None

diff.counts() is the number of each, and diff.is_empty() is true exactly when the two fingerprints are equal. Statistics, descriptions and sample values are not structure: a build whose statistics alone changed has no diff.

A rename is a drop and an add. Nothing can tell a renamed column from a dropped one and a new one without asking someone, so the diff does not guess.

docs.title: Stored diffs
docs.text:
When a build's new snapshot differs in structure from the version it replaces, the diff between them is stored beside the new version in the state store (see Schema Store) and schema.drifted is published with detected_by: "build". It is pruned with its snapshot.

Method Returns engine.index.versions(datasource_id, *, user_context) Each stored version, newest first: schema_version, fingerprint (of the schema as the caller may see it), live, has_diff engine.index.diff(datasource_id, schema_version=None, *, user_context) The diff that introduced the version (the live one by default), or None

Reading these is the measurement: how often a datasource's structure changes between builds, and how far the live database is from the build at a check.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text:
A drifted report's impact (DriftImpact) lists what the diff breaks, from data the engine already has:

Field What verified_queries Each verified query (datasource_id, query_id, reasons) whose SQL reads a dropped table, a dropped column, or a column whose type changed. A column is matched by its table (its qualifier's alias, or the only table read); an unqualified column in a query of several tables is reported as one it may read policy_rules Each role's allow or deny pattern (role, kind, pattern) that matched a dropped table and now matches nothing preferred_tables The datasource's preferred_tables that were dropped glossary_items Each glossary item (tables.orders, columns.orders.note, terms.revenue, rules.pay_private, joins.a.id->b.id) that named a dropped table or column, of those the caller may see

The plan cache needs no entry: it is keyed on the schema version, so a rebuild already makes its old plans unreachable.

docs.title: Who sees what
docs.text:
user_context is required on all three methods. A caller sees drift only in the tables its scope may read:

  • A table its roles deny is left out of the diff, and so is a foreign key that refers to one; the impact is computed from what is left, against the tables it may read.
  • The fingerprint versions() shows is of the schema without the denied tables, so a change only to a denied table looks like a statistics-only rebuild.
  • Drift only in denied tables is unchanged for that caller, and such a stored diff reads as None (has_diff false).
  • A datasource it cannot reach is left out of check(); named, it is a ValueError worded exactly like an unknown datasource.

schema.drifted is an operator event: it is on the engine's bus (engine.events.subscribe) and in the audit log, never on a caller's stream_query. It carries the versions and the whole diff's counts, and no table names. A check publishes a drift once: while the same drift of the same build stays, later checks (by any caller) publish nothing, so a check every few minutes writes one audit line per change. This is remembered in memory per engine, so a new process publishes it once more. A build publishes each diff it stores. See Events.

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:
• The diff and what a caller sees of it: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/schema/diff.py
  • The check, versions and stored diffs: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/schema/drift.py
  • Impact: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/schema/impact.py
  • The models: packages/sdk/src/nl2sql_sdk/schema.py
  • Storing a build's diff: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/orchestrator.py

docs.title: Schema Profiler
docs.text:
After a datasource is indexed, the profiler reads its live snapshot, asks the database a bounded number of cheap questions through the adapter, and files what it finds as proposals. It is deterministic: no model runs unless you ask for drafted descriptions (draft=True, or nl2sql profile --draft). Nothing it finds or drafts reaches a prompt, the index or a file until a person with an admin role accepts it.

nl2sql index                        # the profiler reads the live build's snapshot
nl2sql profile --as admin           # file joins and column roles for review
nl2sql profile --as admin --draft --max-cost 0.25   # also draft descriptions with the model
nl2sql review list --as admin
nl2sql review accept --all --kind column --as admin   # writes glossary.yaml once

nl2sql index --profile --as admin indexes and then profiles the same datasources. From Python:

reports = engine.knowledge.profile(user_context=UserContext(roles=["admin"]))

profile(datasource_ids=None, *, user_context, draft=False, max_cost_usd=None, on_datasource=None, cancellation_token=None) returns one ProfileReport per datasource the caller reaches. on_datasource is called with each report as its datasource finishes, and cancelling cancellation_token stops before the next datasource (the one in flight finishes) and returns the reports so far:

Field Meaning datasource_id, schema_version What was profiled; the proposals carry the same schema_version proposals Proposals created or updated, by kind (join, column, table) probes Overlap probes run skipped_by_budget Join candidates proposed without a probe because a bound was reached drafted Descriptions the model drafted (draft=True only) cost What the drafting calls cost in USD; None when nothing was drafted stopped_by done, max_probes, time_budget, or cost_cap (drafting reached max_cost_usd) issues A probe that failed, a draft that could not be used, no model for drafting, an unavailable datasource, or "not indexed yet" seconds How long it took

max_cost_usd (--max-cost) without draft=True (--draft) is a ValueError.

The caller is required and has no default. The profiler reads and probes only the tables the caller's scope reaches, so a table the role denies is never probed and is named in no proposal. A datasource that was never indexed is reported with an issue and skipped: the profiler never reflects on its own. Each finished profile publishes profile.finished (counts only).

docs.title: What it proposes
docs.text: Nothing is proposed for what the glossary already says, what the database already declares (a foreign key is not proposed as a join), or what the schema proves. A primary or foreign key is an identifier and a temporal type a date: those roles are derived when the knowledge is shown, with origin derived, and never filed.

docs.title: Joins
docs.text:
For each column that is not part of a foreign key, the profiler looks for a single-column primary key (or the only column named id) in another table that it may point to. A pair of tables with a declared foreign key between them, or a column pair the glossary already joins, is skipped.

  1. Names. The column's name equals the key's (not when the key is a bare id), or it is the key table's name, singular or plural, followed by id or key. Case and underscores are ignored: customer_id finds customers.id, CustomerId finds Customer.CustomerId.
  2. Types. Both columns fall in the same category: number, text, temporal or boolean. A mismatch drops the candidate, and a type the profiler cannot place never matches. This is stricter than the query-time join-key check, which coerces a number against text: a proposed join should hold without coercion.
  3. Overlap. probe_overlap takes up to profiler.sample_rows distinct non-null values of the left column and counts how many exist in the key column. An overlap under profiler.min_overlap (0.9), or an empty sample, drops the candidate.
  4. Cardinality. many-to-one when the key is a primary key, else unknown. Two primary keys of one name (film.film_id, film_text.film_id) are one one-to-one pair, not two.

A join proposal's change is the glossary's join (from, to, cardinality) and its evidence is the name rule that matched (same_name or table_name_key), both types, the shared category, and sampled, matched and overlap (counts, never values). A candidate the budget did not reach, and one on an adapter without probe_overlap (the five built-ins have it), is proposed with overlap: null. A probe that fails (a timeout, a driver error) is an issue on the report, and its candidate is proposed with overlap: null too. An accepted join is a relationship: the schema retriever lists it beside the foreign keys, so the validator accepts a plan that uses it.

docs.title: Column roles
docs.text:
Proposed When enum A text or integer column, not an identifier and not named like a key (..._id), with at most profiler.enum_max_distinct (50) distinct values. values lists them with empty meanings for the reviewer to fill, only when the snapshot holds all of them (index.sample_values on) money A decimal column named like price, amount, total, cost, revenue, salary, fee or balance; unit from a _usd, _eur or _gbp suffix quantity An integer or decimal column named like qty, quantity, count or units, or with a _kg, _ms or _pct suffix, which is the unit date on text A text column whose smallest and largest values are ISO dates (SQLite keeps dates as text) A refined grain month or year when every value of a date column is the first of a month or of a year (needs all the column's values in the snapshot)

A role, unit, grain or set of values the glossary already has is not proposed again. The word lists are English only. The rules are one table in nl2sql/profiler/roles.py, with a test per row. On a wide schema (every key and temporal column is derived) this is a few hundred proposals at most, and nl2sql review accept --all --kind column --datasource ID --as admin writes the glossary once.

docs.title: Drafted descriptions
docs.text:
draft=True has the profiler agent (see Per-node models) describe what nobody has: a table or column with no description in the glossary (or a knowledge source) and none from the database. It is asked about those items only, one call per table the caller reaches, and shown that table's evidence (types, statistics, sample values, foreign keys). It never sees a table the caller's scope denies. Each answer is cleaned (unknown tables and columns dropped, text trimmed, duplicates removed), and a draft longer than knowledge.item_max_chars is dropped with an issue, since the glossary would refuse it on accept.

  • A table's draft is a table proposal (change: {description}).
  • A column's draft is merged with its role: one column proposal per column carries role, unit, values and the drafted description and synonyms together, because the queue keeps one open proposal per target. Its origin is draft when it carries a description, profiler when it carries only a role.
  • Nothing drafted is written into the schema snapshot or the index. It reaches a prompt only after a person accepts it into the glossary.
  • An item with an open drafted description in the queue counts as described: a repeat draft=True run does not ask the model about it again or replace the row. A run that finds only the same role for such a column (a plain profile, a run stopped at the cost cap) leaves the open row alone; a changed role still files and supersedes it.
  • A foreign key to a table the caller's scope denies is left out of the evidence, so the model never sees that table's name.

Cost. Drafting is capped at max_cost_usd for the whole call, across datasources (the argument, else profiler.max_cost_usd, 0.50). A model with no price in llm.prices is refused before any call (UnknownPriceError). A run that reaches the cap stops, files what it drafted so far, and reports stopped_by: cost_cap. With no model configured for the agent, nothing is drafted and the report says so in issues; the joins and roles are still filed.

docs.title: Bounds
docs.text:
# settings.yaml
profiler:
  sample_rows: 1000     # distinct values one overlap probe reads
  max_probes: 200       # overlap probes per datasource
  time_budget_s: 60     # per datasource; no probe starts after it
  min_overlap: 0.9
  enum_max_distinct: 50
  max_cost_usd: 0.50    # drafting, per profile call (profile(draft=True), --draft)

Probes run one at a time, strongest candidate first (an exact key-name match before a table-name match), each under the datasource's timeout_ms. The limit caps the sample, not the read: DISTINCT usually reads the whole column first, so on a large table the timeout is what bounds a probe. When max_probes or time_budget_s is reached the remaining candidates are proposed with overlap: null and the report says which bound stopped it.

A probe that measures an overlap under min_overlap also supersedes the profiler's own earlier open proposal for that join (one filed with overlap: null when a bound stopped the probes), so a reviewer cannot accept a join the profiler has since found wrong.

docs.title: Proposals are idempotent
docs.text: A proposal's id hashes its kind, datasource, target and change, so profiling twice updates the same open rows' evidence rather than adding rows. A rejected change is never proposed again, and an accepted one is in the glossary, which the next profile reads.

docs.title: Schema & Metadata Layer
docs.text:
The schema layer provides authoritative, versioned snapshots and structured retrieval to ground planning. It is split into:

  • Schema contracts: structural schema (tables, columns, foreign keys).
  • Schema metadata: the database's own comments and statistics.
  • The state store: immutable, versioned snapshots, and the diffs between them, kept by storage.state.
  • Schema retrieval: staged lookup via schema chunks.

docs.title: Schema contracts and metadata
docs.text:
Schema contracts are defined in nl2sql_sdk.schema:

  • SchemaContract: datasource_id, engine_type, tables
  • TableContract: table ref, column contracts, foreign keys
  • ColumnContract: name, type, nullability, primary key flag
  • ForeignKeyContract: constrained/referred columns, cardinality, business meaning

Metadata complements contracts:

  • SchemaMetadata: datasource description/domains, table metadata
  • TableMetadata: table description, row_count, column metadata
  • ColumnMetadata: description, stats, synonyms, PII flag
  • ColumnStatistics: distinct counts, min/max, sample values (for a text column: every distinct value when there are at most 50, else the five most frequent; most frequent first, ties by value). A column the adapter could not profile has no statistics and an index issue; values are kept only with the datasource's index.sample_values. See Reading a schema

docs.title: The state store
docs.text: Snapshots are kept by the engine's state store, the storage.state slot (see Storage). The built-in one is sqlite, a file at <storage.path>/state.db; any store implementing nl2sql_sdk.stores.StateStore can take its place. The same store holds the plan cache, the playground's answer ratings, the review queue, conversations, workspaces, dashboards with their last chart results, API keys and the index build lock. The interface is version 6.

docs.title: Snapshots are immutable
docs.text:
put_snapshot(snapshot) stores a snapshot as a new row and returns its schema_version, YYYYMMDDhhmmss_<hash8> (the time it was stored, and a hash of its contract and metadata). A stored snapshot is never changed: in the sqlite store a trigger refuses any UPDATE of the schema_snapshots table.

  • Storing a snapshot whose contract and metadata are identical to a stored one returns that version, and writes nothing.
  • A snapshot with the same structure but new metadata (statistics, descriptions) is a new version. A run that pinned the old version keeps reading exactly the snapshot its index build was made from.

The structural fingerprint (nl2sql.schema.generate_schema_fingerprint: datasource ID, engine type, sorted tables, columns and foreign keys) is still stored beside each row, and eval reports and records use it to identify a database.

docs.title: Schema diffs
docs.text: When a build stores a snapshot whose structure differs from the version it replaces, the orchestrator stores the diff between them beside the new version (put_schema_diff(diff), keyed by datasource and diff.to_version; get_schema_diff(datasource_id, schema_version) reads it back) and publishes schema.drifted. A version whose statistics alone changed gets no diff. The diff (nl2sql_sdk.schema.SchemaDiff) and how to read it are in Schema Drift. These two methods are why the store interface is version 2.

docs.title: Which snapshots are kept
docs.text:
After each build of a datasource, indexing calls keep_snapshots(datasource_id, keep), which deletes every other snapshot of the datasource, the plans cached on them and their diffs. keep is:

  • every version a build pointer names, in every index namespace, so switching back to an earlier embedding model still finds its snapshot;
  • the version the build just replaced, which runs in flight may have pinned;
  • the newest settings.schema.max_versions (default 3).

Nothing else deletes a snapshot; there is no age limit.

docs.title: The plan cache and feedback
docs.text:
The plan cache holds validated, executed plans keyed by (normalised sub-query intent, run date, planner model and knowledge digest, datasource_id, schema_version) (get_plan, put_plan). Deleting a snapshot deletes its cached plans; nl2sql cache clear (engine.clear_plan_cache()) deletes them all and keeps the snapshots. See Determinism → The plan cache.

The playground's answer ratings are kept too (add_feedback, list_feedback, clear_feedback): one row per rated run, questions and SQL, never rows. nl2sql feedback clear empties them and nothing else. See Feedback and Signals.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text: The sqlite store records each migration it has applied in a nl2sql_meta table, and the engine applies the pending ones when it starts (StateStore.migrate()). Migration 1 creates 0.5's three tables (schema_snapshots, plan_cache, feedback) if they are missing, so a 0.5 state.db is adopted as it is; migration 2 adds the feedback columns that came later; migration 3 adds the immutability trigger and the locks table; migration 4 adds the schema_diffs table; migration 5 adds the proposals table, the review queue; migration 6 adds five tables, below; migration 7 adds the approvals table and migration 8 the saved_answers table, below. A 0.8 state.db is migrated in place and keeps its rows.

docs.title: Conversations, dashboards and API keys
docs.text:
Release 0.9. StateStore version 4 adds these methods. Each takes and returns a plain JSON document (dict), because the SDK holds none of the engine's models; the document carries the fields the store filters on. The engine methods that use them are in the conversations, workspaces and dashboards services.

Table (migration 6) Methods Filtered on Notes conversations put_conversation, get_conversation, list_conversations(tenant_id, user_id, limit), delete_conversation, purge_conversations(older_than) owner, updated_at One document per conversation, rewritten each turn, read whole. Stored without result rows. None is an owner of its own in list_*, not a wildcard. workspaces put_workspace, get_workspace, list_workspaces(tenant_id, user_id), delete_workspace owner, created_at Listed oldest first. A put on an existing id keeps its created_at, so renaming a workspace does not move it. dashboards put_dashboard, get_dashboard, list_dashboards(tenant_id, user_id), delete_dashboard, purge_dashboards(drafts_older_than), list_scheduled_dashboards() owner, status, updated_at, whether it has a schedule purge_dashboards deletes drafts only; saved dashboards are never purged. list_scheduled_dashboards serves the scheduler across owners. tile_runs put_tile_runs(dashboard_id, docs), get_tile_runs(dashboard_id), delete_tile_runs(dashboard_id, tile_ids) dashboard, chart (tile_id), at The last result of each chart, rows included. put_tile_runs replaces only the charts it lists and delete_tile_runs deletes only those it lists (an edit that changes what a chart shows discards its result). Deleted with the dashboard. api_keys add_api_key, revoke_api_key(key_id, revoked_at), get_api_key, list_api_keys id, hash, revoked_at A hash, never a secret. add_api_key is a plain insert and raises ValueError when the id exists, so a clash never replaces another holder's key. revoke_api_key sets revoked_at and nothing else; it returns False for an unknown id.

Stored chart results hold rows, so they sit in the owner's private state store and open only after the access check.

Each document's timestamps are ISO 8601; a stamp with no zone is read as UTC.

docs.title: Approvals
docs.text:
StateStore version 5 adds the approval methods, one JSON document per approval request, in the approvals table that migration 7 creates (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so it is safe to run again).

Table (migration 7) Methods Filtered on Notes approvals put_approval(doc), get_approval(request_id), list_approvals(status=None), decide_approval(request_id, status, *, by, at=None), purge_approvals(older_than) id (the request id), status (pending, granted, denied), created_at, updated_at list_approvals is newest (created_at) first. decide_approval changes only a pending request, under the store lock, so a late deny never overwrites a grant; it returns the stored document, or None for an unknown id. purge_approvals deletes by updated_at whatever the status.

docs.title: Saved answers
docs.text:
StateStore version 6 adds the saved-answer methods, one JSON document per answer, in the saved_answers table that migration 8 creates (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS).

Table (migration 8) Methods Filtered on Notes saved_answers put_saved_answer(doc), get_saved_answer(answer_id), list_saved_answers(tenant_id, user_id), delete_saved_answer(answer_id) owner (tenant_id, user_id), created_at list_saved_answers is newest first. The engine checks the owner on every read; a document holds a typed plan, never rows.

docs.title: The lock
docs.text:
lock(name, ttl_s) is a lease held for a with block: in the sqlite store, a locks row taken in a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, with an expiry. Every engine.index.build() holds the index lock, so nl2sql index is safe to run while nl2sql-api serves the same storage.path: a second build started meanwhile fails at once and says until when the lease runs. The lease expires after an hour, so a build that died cannot block forever.

The sqlite store opens its file on first use, never when it is built, and is safe to share between threads: each use of its one connection holds a lock.

docs.title: Which version is live
docs.text: There is no "latest snapshot" to read. Indexing stores a datasource's snapshot first and its index entries second; the index store's BuildPointer for the datasource then records the schema_version the live build was made from, and switching that pointer is the commit. The pointer also records the curated_hash and the knowledge_hash the build was made with, so health can tell that curated.yaml or the glossary has changed since. A snapshot holds only what the database said: model-drafted descriptions are proposals, and a person's words live in the glossary (see Indexing). Every reader (the resolver, the schema retriever, the curated matcher, engine.datasources.schema(), engine.curated.validate()) resolves the version through the pointer and reads get_snapshot(datasource_id, schema_version). A run reads the pointers once, when it starts. A snapshot stored by a build that then failed is named by no pointer, so nothing reads it. See Indexing → The build pointer is the commit.

docs.title: Retrieval and authority
docs.text:
Schema retrieval resolves authoritative tables/columns from the state store, not from the index. Index entries are only used to identify candidates; final schema is resolved via the snapshot the live pointer names. If retrieval yields no candidates, the retriever falls back to the full snapshot. The entries and the snapshot come from the same build, so their versions cannot disagree.

See ../architecture/indexing.md for retrieval stages, chunk types, and vector store behavior.

docs.title: Source references
docs.text:
• Contracts and metadata: packages/sdk/src/nl2sql_sdk/schema.py
  • Fingerprinting: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/schema/fingerprint.py
  • Diffs and drift: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/schema/diff.py, drift.py, impact.py
  • The StateStore interface: packages/sdk/src/nl2sql_sdk/stores.py
  • The sqlite state store: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/storage/sqlite.py
  • Which snapshots are kept: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/orchestrator.py
  • The index lock: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/indexing/rebuild.py
  • Schema retriever: packages/nl2sql/src/nl2sql/pipeline/nodes/schema_retriever/node.py

docs.title: API keys
docs.text:
An API key authenticates a client of MCP over HTTP. It carries the user, tenant and roles its holder runs as, so a key per person or per app is the unit of revocation. Nothing is inferred from the client. 

nl2sql keys create --as admin --user ana --role analyst --tenant acme --label laptop
nl2sql keys list --as admin
nl2sql keys revoke <id> --as admin

On a project with policies.allow_all (the starter, nl2sql launch) no roles exist: leave out --as and --role, as in nl2sql keys create --user ana. Any --as or --role is refused as an unknown role.

create prints the token once. Keep it in the client's secret store: only its hash is kept here, so a lost token is replaced by a new key, not recovered.

docs.title: The token
docs.text: nl2sql_<id>_<secret>: id is 8 hex characters, shown in lists, logs and events; secret is 32 random bytes, URL-safe (43 characters). The state store keeps sha256(secret) and the key's fields, never the token. SHA-256 with no salt is deliberate: the secret is 256 bits of randomness, so there is nothing to guess and a slow hash would only cost time on every request. The comparison uses hmac.compare_digest.

docs.title: From Python
docs.text:
from nl2sql import NL2SQL, UserContext

admin = UserContext(user_id="root", roles=["admin"])

key, token = engine.api_keys.create(user_id="ana", roles=["analyst"], by=admin, tenant_id="acme", label="laptop")
engine.api_keys.list(by=admin)            # [ApiKey, ...], newest first, revoked ones included; no secret
engine.api_keys.revoke(key.id, by=admin)  # stops verifying at once
engine.api_keys.verify(token)             # UserContext(user_id="ana", tenant_id="acme", roles=["analyst"]) or None
engine.api_keys.check(token)              # KeyCheck(user=..., reason=None, key_id="...") or KeyCheck(reason="revoked", ...)
Method Behaviour create(*, user_id, roles, by, tenant_id=None, label="") Returns the ApiKey and its token, once. roles must be configured in policies.roles; user_id must not be empty. An id that is already taken is retried with a new one and never replaces another key. Publishes api_key.created. list(*, by) Every key, newest first. ApiKey has no secret and no hash. revoke(key_id, *, by) Sets revoked_at; revoking a revoked key changes nothing. An unknown id is a ValueError. Publishes api_key.revoked. verify(token) The key's UserContext, or None for a malformed, unknown or revoked token, or a wrong secret. It takes no caller: it is how a caller is found. check(token) As verify, saying why: a KeyCheck with the user of a good token, else a reason (malformed, unknown, revoked). The secret is compared before a key is called revoked, so a right id with a wrong secret is unknown, and an id alone never reveals a key's state. key_id is set only when the secret matched. record_denied(reason, key_id=None) Publishes mcp.denied for a request a server refused (missing, malformed, unknown or revoked). It takes a reason, never a token.

by is required and has no default. A call without one is a TypeError, a by that is not a UserContext is a TypeError, and a by holding none of policies.admin_roles is a PermissionError. Under policies.allow_all every caller is an admin, as for the rest of the engine, but a key still cannot carry a role name: with no roles defined, roles=[] is the only value, and a role name is a ValueError. Keys outlive the policy, so an admin key minted under allow_all would become a real admin key once roles are configured. A key with no roles reads everything under allow_all and nothing once roles are configured; create new keys then.

docs.title: Events and logs
docs.text: api_key.created and api_key.revoked carry key_id, user_id, tenant_id, roles and by, and the audit observer keeps both. mcp.denied carries a reason (missing, malformed, unknown, revoked) and the key_id of a revoked key (only a request that proved the secret names a key), and the audit observer keeps it too. Neither the token nor any part of the secret appears in an event, a log line or an error. See Events.

docs.title: On the wire
docs.text: nl2sql mcp --http takes the key from Authorization: Bearer <token>. A missing header, another scheme, a malformed token, an unknown key or a revoked key is a 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer and an mcp.denied event; a good key runs the request as the key's user, tenant and roles. See MCP over HTTP.

docs.title: What a key does and does not give
docs.text: A key proves that the holder has the token; it does not prove who the holder is, and it does not expire. Revoke a key when a person leaves or a token leaks. A key's roles are checked against the policies at every request, so removing a role from policies.roles stops what the key can read, though not the key.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• What reaches the LLM provider: the question; the schema the planner needs (table and column names, types, keys, relationships, descriptions); sample column values for tables the role may read; and the result rows, which the answer writer summarises. With settings.traces.mode on, run traces store prompts, responses and sample rows on disk.
  • RBAC is strict. A plan that touches a table the role may not read is refused before any SQL exists, never answered from the tables the role can see. Sample values and statistics of forbidden tables are stripped from the prompt and the trace. An unknown role grants nothing. There is no column masking and no row-level security.
  • Read-only is a database setting, not something the executor checks. The plan type only allows SELECT and the generator only builds one, but the executor does not inspect the SQL. A SQLite datasource is always opened read-only at the driver level (SQLite's mode=ro URI), so a write is refused by SQLite itself. No other dialect opens read-only yet, so on PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server or DuckDB, give the engine a read-only database user.
  • No authentication in the CLI or REST API. The CLI takes the role from the caller. The REST API takes it from a trusted proxy header or a static setting, never from the body unless a dev flag is on; put your own auth in the proxy and derive the role from it.
  • settings.pipeline.timeout_s bounds how long the caller waits, not how long the work runs; the graph runs in-process with no sandbox.

Details are below and in Execution Isolation.

Authorization is enforced at planning time, by the logical validator, before any SQL exists. That is the one security property this engine provides. It is not authentication, it is not containment, and it is not row- or column-level security.

docs.title: The role is supplied by the caller
docs.text:
There is no authentication in the query path; the engine believes the UserContext it is given. The one exception is an API key, which a transport may verify to find that context. Where the role comes from depends on the client:

  • CLI: nl2sql run --role <id>, defaulting to admin.
  • Python API: UserContext(roles=[...]), whatever the calling code passes.

  • REST API: the identity.caller dependency (packages/api/src/nl2sql_api/identity.py) resolves one UserContext from the source api.auth names: an API key (api_keys), the user, tenant and roles headers of a proxy that connects from api.proxy.trusted_from (proxy), one role for everyone (static) or the local operator (none, the default). It answers HTTP 401 when there is no identity, and never reads the request body. Headers from a peer outside trusted_from are ignored. With auth: none the request must be made straight to localhost (a connecting peer that is not loopback, such as a published container port, a Host that is not loopback, or an X-Forwarded-For, Forwarded or X-Real-IP header, is a 403, so a same-host proxy or a DNS-rebinding page is not the operator), and nl2sql-api serve refuses to bind a non-loopback host. The routes that change datasources, LLMs or the index also need one of the roles in policies.admin_roles (default [admin]), else HTTP 403. See Identity and Admin routes.

  • API keys: engine.api_keys makes bearer tokens that each carry the user, tenant and roles their holder runs as, and verify(token) turns a token back into that UserContext. This is the one place the engine itself checks who is asking; MCP over HTTP (nl2sql mcp --http) is the first transport to use it, and the other clients above still do not. Every request there needs a valid key, and runs as that key's user, tenant and roles. See API keys and MCP over HTTP.

  • Playground: the page sends the role chosen in "Ask as" with each request (/api/ask, and /api/retrieval for the Retrieval inspector), and the server believes it.
